danishChanges.before: Having read with great pleasure a pamphlet, which you have lately published, on National Education, I dedicate this volume to you, the first dedication that I have ever written, to induce you to read it with attention; and, because I think that you will understand me, which I do not suppose many pert witlings will, who may ridicule the arguments they are unable to answer. But, sir, I carry my respect for your understanding still farther: so far, that I am confident you will not throw my work aside, and hastily conclude that I am in the wrong because you did not view the subject in the same light yourself. And pardon my frankness, but I must observe, that you treated it in too cursory a manner, contented to consider it as it had been considered formerly, when the rights of man, not to advert to woman, were trampled on as chimerical. I call upon you, therefore, now to weigh what I have advanced respecting the rights of woman, and national education; and I call with the firm tone of humanity. For my arguments, sir, are dictated by a disinterested spirit: I plead for my sex, not for myself. Independence I have long considered as the grand blessing of life, the basis of every virtue; and independence I will ever secure by contracting my wants, though I were to live on a barren heath.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har med stor glæde læst Deres nyligt udgivne skrift om undervisningen i landet og tilegner Dem derfor denne bog — den første tilegnelse, jeg nogensinde har skrevet — for at få Dem til at læse den opmærksomt. Jeg gør det også, fordi jeg tror, De vil forstå mig, hvilket jeg ikke venter af de mange næsvise vittighoveder, der måske vil latterliggøre argumenter, de ikke kan besvare. Men min respekt for Deres forstand rækker videre endnu: Jeg er overbevist om, at De ikke vil lægge mit værk fra Dem og forhastet slutte, at jeg tager fejl, blot fordi De ikke selv har set emnet i samme lys. Tilgiv min åbenhed, men jeg må bemærke, at De behandlede det for overfladisk og nøjedes med at se på det, som man tidligere gjorde, da menneskets rettigheder — for slet ikke at tale om kvindens — blev trådt under fode som fantasier. Derfor opfordrer jeg Dem nu til at overveje det, jeg har fremført om kvindens rettigheder og den fælles undervisning, og jeg gør det med medmenneskelighedens faste stemme. Mine argumenter er nemlig, min herre, båret af en uselvisk ånd: Jeg taler mit køns sag, ikke min egen. Uafhængighed har jeg længe anset for livets største velsignelse, grundlaget for enhver dyd, og jeg vil altid sikre min uafhængighed ved at begrænse mine behov, selv hvis jeg måtte leve på en gold hede.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is, then, an affection for the whole human race that makes my pen dart rapidly along to support what I believe to be the cause of virtue: and the same motive leads me earnestly to wish to see woman placed in a station in which she would advance, instead of retarding, the progress of those glorious principles that give a substance to morality. My opinion, indeed, respecting the rights and duties of woman, seems to flow so naturally from these simple principles, that I think it scarcely possible, but that some of the enlarged minds who formed your admirable constitution, will coincide with me.
danishChanges.after: Det er altså kærlighed til hele menneskeheden, der får min pen til at løbe hurtigt hen over papiret til støtte for det, jeg anser for dydens sag. Den samme bevæggrund får mig inderligt til at ønske, at kvinden får en stilling, hvor hun kan fremme, i stedet for at hæmme, de herlige principper, som giver moralen indhold. Mine synspunkter om kvindens rettigheder og pligter følger efter min mening så naturligt af disse enkle principper, at jeg knap kan forestille mig andet, end at nogle af de vidsynede mennesker, der udformede Deres beundringsværdige forfatning, vil være enige med mig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In France, there is undoubtedly a more general diffusion of knowledge than in any part of the European world, and I attribute it, in a great measure, to the social intercourse which has long subsisted between the sexes. It is true, I utter my sentiments with freedom, that in France the very essence of sensuality has been extracted to regale the voluptuary, and a kind of sentimental lust has prevailed, which, together with the system of duplicity that the whole tenor of their political and civil government taught, have given a sinister sort of sagacity to the French character, properly termed finesse; and a polish of manners that injures the substance, by hunting sincerity out of society. And, modesty, the fairest garb of virtue has been more grossly insulted in France than even in England, till their women have treated as PRUDISH that attention to decency which brutes instinctively observe.
danishChanges.after: I Frankrig er kundskaber uden tvivl mere udbredte end noget andet sted i Europa, og det tilskriver jeg i høj grad det selskabelige samvær, som længe har eksisteret mellem kønnene. Ganske vist — jeg siger åbent, hvad jeg mener — har man i Frankrig udvundet sanselighedens reneste essens til nydelsesmenneskets fornøjelse, og en slags sentimental vellyst har hersket. Sammen med den dobbelthed, som hele det politiske og civile styres væsen har lært folk, har den givet den franske karakter en skummel form for skarpsindighed, passende kaldet finesse, og en poleret optræden, som skader indholdet ved at fordrive oprigtigheden fra samfundet. Og blufærdigheden, dydens smukkeste klædning, er blevet grovere krænket i Frankrig end selv i England, indtil franske kvinder har stemplet den sans for anstændighed, som selv dyr instinktivt viser, som SNERPET.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Manners and morals are so nearly allied, that they have often been confounded; but, though the former should only be the natural reflection of the latter, yet, when various causes have produced factitious and corrupt manners, which are very early caught, morality becomes an empty name. The personal reserve, and sacred respect for cleanliness and delicacy in domestic life, which French women almost despise, are the graceful pillars of modesty; but, far from despising them, if the pure flame of patriotism have reached their bosoms, they should labour to improve the morals of their fellow-citizens, by teaching men, not only to respect modesty in women, but to acquire it themselves, as the only way to merit their esteem.
danishChanges.after: Omgangsformer og moral er så nært beslægtede, at de ofte er blevet forvekslet. Men selv om omgangsformerne kun burde være moralens naturlige afspejling, bliver moralen et tomt ord, når forskellige årsager frembringer kunstige og fordærvede omgangsformer, som man lærer meget tidligt. Den personlige tilbageholdenhed og den dybe respekt for renlighed og hensynsfuldhed i hjemmet, som franske kvinder næsten foragter, er blufærdighedens smukke støtter. Men langt fra at foragte dem bør kvinderne, hvis fædrelandskærlighedens rene flamme har nået deres hjerter, arbejde for at forbedre deres medborgeres moral. De bør lære mændene ikke blot at respektere blufærdighed hos kvinder, men selv at tilegne sig den som den eneste måde at gøre sig fortjent til kvindernes agtelse på.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Contending for the rights of women, my main argument is built on this simple principle, that if she be not prepared by education to become the companion of man, she will stop the progress of knowledge, for truth must be common to all, or it will be inefficacious with respect to its influence on general practice. And how can woman be expected to co-operate, unless she know why she ought to be virtuous? Unless freedom strengthen her reason till she comprehend her duty, and see in what manner it is connected with her real good? If children are to be educated to understand the true principle of patriotism, their mother must be a patriot; and the love of mankind, from which an orderly train of virtues spring, can only be produced by considering the moral and civil interest of mankind; but the education and situation of woman, at present, shuts her out from such investigations.
danishChanges.after: I mit forsvar for kvinders rettigheder bygger mit hovedargument på dette enkle princip: Hvis kvinden ikke gennem uddannelse forberedes til at blive mandens ledsager, vil hun standse kundskabens fremskridt. Sandheden må nemlig være fælles for alle, hvis den skal få virkning i det almindelige liv. Og hvordan kan man forvente, at kvinden bidrager, hvis hun ikke ved, hvorfor hun bør være dydig? Hvis friheden ikke styrker hendes fornuft, så hun forstår sin pligt og ser, hvordan den hænger sammen med hendes sande bedste? Skal børn opdrages til at forstå fædrelandskærlighedens sande princip, må deres mor selv elske sit fædreland. Og den kærlighed til menneskeheden, hvoraf en sammenhængende række dyder udspringer, kan kun skabes ved at overveje menneskehedens moralske og samfundsmæssige interesser; men kvindens nuværende uddannelse og stilling udelukker hende fra sådanne undersøgelser.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In this work I have produced many arguments, which to me were conclusive, to prove, that the prevailing notion respecting a sexual character was subversive of morality, and I have contended, that to render the human body and mind more perfect, chastity must more universally prevail, and that chastity will never be respected in the male world till the person of a woman is not, as it were, idolized when little virtue or sense embellish it with the grand traces of mental beauty, or the interesting simplicity of affection.
danishChanges.after: I dette værk har jeg fremlagt mange argumenter, som jeg selv fandt afgørende, for at vise, at den gængse forestilling om en særlig kønskarakter underminerer moralen. Jeg har også hævdet, at kyskhed må blive mere almindelig, hvis menneskets krop og sind skal udvikles mod større fuldkommenhed. Og mænd vil aldrig respektere kyskheden, før kvindens krop holder op med nærmest at blive tilbedt, selv når kun lidt dyd eller forstand smykker den med sjælens skønne træk eller hengivenhedens tiltalende enkelhed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Consider, Sir, dispassionately, these observations, for a glimpse of this truth seemed to open before you when you observed, "that to see one half of the human race excluded by the other from all participation of government, was a political phenomenon that, according to abstract principles, it was impossible to explain." If so, on what does your constitution rest? If the abstract rights of man will bear discussion and explanation, those of woman, by a parity of reasoning, will not shrink from the same test: though a different opinion prevails in this country, built on the very arguments which you use to justify the oppression of woman, prescription.
danishChanges.after: Overvej disse bemærkninger lidenskabsløst, min herre. Et glimt af denne sandhed syntes nemlig at vise sig for Dem, da De bemærkede, »at det var et politisk fænomen, som ikke kunne forklares ud fra abstrakte principper, når den ene halvdel af menneskeheden udelukkede den anden fra enhver deltagelse i regeringen«. Hvis det forholder sig sådan, hvad hviler Deres forfatning så på? Hvis mandens abstrakte rettigheder tåler drøftelse og forklaring, vil kvindens efter samme ræsonnement ikke vige tilbage for den samme prøve. Her i landet hersker ganske vist en anden opfattelse, bygget på netop det argument, De bruger til at retfærdiggøre kvindens undertrykkelse: hævd.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Consider, I address you as a legislator, whether, when men contend for their freedom, and to be allowed to judge for themselves, respecting their own happiness, it be not inconsistent and unjust to subjugate women, even though you firmly believe that you are acting in the manner best calculated to promote their happiness? Who made man the exclusive judge, if woman partake with him the gift of reason?
danishChanges.after: Overvej — jeg henvender mig til Dem som lovgiver — om det ikke er selvmodsigende og uretfærdigt, at mænd kæmper for deres frihed og for retten til selv at vurdere, hvad der gør dem lykkelige, men samtidig underlægger sig kvinder, selv når de oprigtigt tror, at det bedst fremmer kvindernes lykke. Hvem gjorde manden til den eneste dommer, hvis kvinden deler fornuftens gave med ham?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In this style, argue tyrants of every denomination from the weak king to the weak father of a family; they are all eager to crush reason; yet always assert that they usurp its throne only to be useful. Do you not act a similar part, when you FORCE all women, by denying them civil and political rights, to remain immured in their families groping in the dark? For surely, sir, you will not assert, that a duty can be binding which is not founded on reason? If, indeed, this be their destination, arguments may be drawn from reason; and thus augustly supported, the more understanding women acquire, the more they will be attached to their duty, comprehending it, for unless they comprehend it, unless their morals be fixed on the same immutable principles as those of man, no authority can make them discharge it in a virtuous manner. They may be convenient slaves, but slavery will have its constant effect, degrading the master and the abject dependent.
danishChanges.after: Sådan argumenterer tyranner af enhver slags, fra den svage konge til den svage familiefar. De vil alle knuse fornuften, men hævder altid, at de kun tilraner sig dens trone for at gøre gavn. Handler De ikke på samme måde, når De ved at nægte kvinder borgerlige og politiske rettigheder TVINGER dem alle til at blive indespærret i deres familier og famle i mørket? De vil vel ikke hævde, min herre, at en pligt kan være bindende, hvis den ikke er grundlagt på fornuften? Hvis dette virkelig er kvindernes bestemmelse, må der kunne findes fornuftige argumenter for den. Med denne ophøjede støtte vil de, jo mere forståelse de får, knytte sig desto stærkere til pligten, fordi de begriber den. For hvis de ikke begriber den, og hvis deres moral ikke hviler på de samme uforanderlige principper som mandens, kan ingen myndighed få dem til at opfylde den på en dydig måde. De kan være bekvemme slaver, men slaveriet vil have sin sædvanlige virkning: at nedværdige både herren og den kuede afhængige.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, if women are to be excluded, without having a voice, from a participation of the natural rights of mankind, prove first, to ward off the charge of injustice and inconsistency, that they want reason, else this flaw in your NEW CONSTITUTION, the first constitution founded on reason, will ever show that man must, in some shape, act like a tyrant, and tyranny, in whatever part of society it rears its brazen front, will ever undermine morality.
danishChanges.after: Men skal kvinder udelukkes fra at få del i menneskehedens naturlige rettigheder uden selv at have en stemme, må De først bevise, at de mangler fornuft, hvis De vil undgå anklagen om uretfærdighed og selvmodsigelse. Ellers vil denne fejl i Deres NYE FORFATNING, den første forfatning grundlagt på fornuft, altid vise, at manden må optræde som tyran i en eller anden skikkelse. Og tyranniet vil altid underminere moralen, uanset hvor i samfundet det løfter sin skamløse pande.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I have repeatedly asserted, and produced what appeared to me irrefragable arguments drawn from matters of fact, to prove my assertion, that women cannot, by force, be confined to domestic concerns; for they will however ignorant, intermeddle with more weighty affairs, neglecting private duties only to disturb, by cunning tricks, the orderly plans of reason which rise above their comprehension.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har gentagne gange hævdet, og underbygget min påstand med argumenter hentet fra kendsgerninger, som jeg fandt uigendrivelige, at kvinder ikke med magt kan begrænses til hjemmets anliggender. For uanset hvor uvidende de er, vil de blande sig i vigtigere spørgsmål og forsømme deres private pligter for med snedige kneb at forstyrre fornuftens velordnede planer, som ligger over deres fatteevne.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, whilst they are only made to acquire personal accomplishments, men will seek for pleasure in variety, and faithless husbands will make faithless wives; such ignorant beings, indeed, will be very excusable when, not taught to respect public good, nor allowed any civil right, they attempt to do themselves justice by retaliation.
danishChanges.after: Desuden vil mænd søge fornøjelse i afveksling, så længe kvinder kun lærer selskabelige færdigheder og ydre fortrin, og utro ægtemænd vil skabe utro hustruer. Sådanne uvidende mennesker vil faktisk være ganske undskyldelige, når de forsøger at skaffe sig ret ved gengældelse, eftersom de hverken har lært at respektere det fælles bedste eller fået nogen borgerlige rettigheder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The box of mischief thus opened in society, what is to preserve private virtue, the only security of public freedom and universal happiness?
danishChanges.after: Når først denne æske af ulykker er åbnet i samfundet, hvad skal så bevare den personlige dyd, den eneste sikkerhed for offentlig frihed og alles lykke?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Let there be then no coercion ESTABLISHED in society, and the common law of gravity prevailing, the sexes will fall into their proper places. And, now that more equitable laws are forming your citizens, marriage may become more sacred; your young men may choose wives from motives of affection, and your maidens allow love to root out vanity.
danishChanges.after: Lad derfor ingen tvang være FASTLAGT i samfundets ordning. Når den almindelige tyngdelov får lov at virke, vil kønnene finde deres rette plads. Og nu, hvor mere retfærdige love former Deres medborgere, kan ægteskabet blive mere helligt; de unge mænd kan vælge hustruer af kærlighed, og de unge kvinder lade kærligheden rykke forfængeligheden op med rode.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The father of a family will not then weaken his constitution and debase his sentiments, by visiting the harlot, nor forget, in obeying the call of appetite, the purpose for which it was implanted; and the mother will not neglect her children to practise the arts of coquetry, when sense and modesty secure her the friendship of her husband.
danishChanges.after: Så vil familiefaderen ikke svække sit helbred og nedværdige sine følelser ved at besøge den prostituerede eller glemme begærets formål, når han følger dets kald. Og moderen vil ikke forsømme sine børn for at øve sig i koketteriets kunster, når forstand og blufærdighed sikrer hende mandens venskab.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, till men become attentive to the duty of a father, it is vain to expect women to spend that time in their nursery which they, "wise in their generation," choose to spend at their glass; for this exertion of cunning is only an instinct of nature to enable them to obtain indirectly a little of that power of which they are unjustly denied a share; for, if women are not permitted to enjoy legitimate rights, they will render both men and themselves vicious, to obtain illicit privileges.
danishChanges.after: Men før mænd tager en fars pligt alvorligt, er det forgæves at vente, at kvinder tilbringer den tid på børneværelset, som de, »kloge på deres egen tids forhold«, vælger at bruge foran spejlet. Denne snedighed er nemlig blot et naturligt instinkt, der gør dem i stand til indirekte at få lidt af den magt, som de uretfærdigt nægtes del i. Hvis kvinder ikke får lov til at nyde deres retmæssige rettigheder, vil de fordærve både mændene og sig selv for at skaffe sig uretmæssige privilegier.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I wish, sir, to set some investigations of this kind afloat in France; and should they lead to a confirmation of my principles, when your constitution is revised, the rights of woman may be respected, if it be fully proved that reason calls for this respect, and loudly demands JUSTICE for one half of the human race.
danishChanges.after: Jeg ønsker, min herre, at sætte undersøgelser af denne art i gang i Frankrig. Skulle de bekræfte mine principper, kan kvindens rettigheder blive respekteret, når Deres forfatning revideres, hvis det fuldt ud bevises, at fornuften kræver denne respekt og højlydt forlanger RETFÆRDIGHED for halvdelen af menneskeheden.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.after: Deres med højagtelse,

danishChanges.before: After considering the historic page, and viewing the living world with anxious solicitude, the most melancholy emotions of sorrowful indignation have depressed my spirits, and I have sighed when obliged to confess, that either nature has made a great difference between man and man, or that the civilization, which has hitherto taken place in the world, has been very partial. I have turned over various books written on the subject of education, and patiently observed the conduct of parents and the management of schools; but what has been the result? a profound conviction, that the neglected education of my fellow creatures is the grand source of the misery I deplore; and that women in particular, are rendered weak and wretched by a variety of concurring causes, originating from one hasty conclusion. The conduct and manners of women, in fact, evidently prove, that their minds are not in a healthy state; for, like the flowers that are planted in too rich a soil, strength and usefulness are sacrificed to beauty; and the flaunting leaves, after having pleased a fastidious eye, fade, disregarded on the stalk, long before the season when they ought to have arrived at maturity. One cause of this barren blooming I attribute to a false system of education, gathered from the books written on this subject by men, who, considering females rather as women than human creatures, have been more anxious to make them alluring mistresses than rational wives; and the understanding of the sex has been so bubbled by this specious homage, that the civilized women of the present century, with a few exceptions, are only anxious to inspire love, when they ought to cherish a nobler ambition, and by their abilities and virtues exact respect.
danishChanges.after: Efter at have studeret historien og betragtet den levende verden med ængstelig omsorg er mit sind blevet tynget af den dybeste, sorgfulde harme. Jeg har sukket over at måtte erkende, at enten har naturen gjort en stor forskel på mennesker, eller også er den civilisation, verden hidtil har opnået, kun kommet nogle til gode. Jeg har gennemgået forskellige bøger om opdragelse og uddannelse og tålmodigt iagttaget forældres adfærd og skolers ledelse. Men hvad er resultatet blevet? En dyb overbevisning om, at den forsømte uddannelse af mine medmennesker er hovedkilden til den elendighed, jeg beklager, og at især kvinder gøres svage og ulykkelige af flere samvirkende årsager, som alle udspringer af én forhastet slutning. Kvinders adfærd og omgangsformer viser tydeligt, at deres sind ikke er i en sund tilstand. Som blomster plantet i alt for næringsrig jord ofres deres styrke og nytte for skønheden; og efter at have behaget et kræsent øje visner de prangende blade ubemærket på stilken, længe før de burde have nået deres fulde udvikling. En af årsagerne til denne frugtesløse blomstring finder jeg i et forkert opdragelsessystem, hentet fra bøger om emnet skrevet af mænd. De har betragtet kvinder mere som kvindelige væsener end som mennesker og har været mere optaget af at gøre dem til tillokkende elskerinder end til fornuftige hustruer. Og kønnets forstand er blevet så bedraget af denne besnærende hyldest, at dette århundredes civiliserede kvinder, med få undtagelser, kun ønsker at vække kærlighed, skønt de burde nære en ædlere ambition og gennem deres evner og dyder gøre krav på respekt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In a treatise, therefore, on female rights and manners, the works which have been particularly written for their improvement must not be overlooked; especially when it is asserted, in direct terms, that the minds of women are enfeebled by false refinement; that the books of instruction, written by men of genius, have had the same tendency as more frivolous productions; and that, in the true style of Mahometanism, they are only considered as females, and not as a part of the human species, when improvable reason is allowed to be the dignified distinction, which raises men above the brute creation, and puts a natural sceptre in a feeble hand.
danishChanges.after: I en afhandling om kvinders rettigheder og levevis må man derfor ikke overse de værker, som særlig er skrevet for at udvikle dem. Det gælder især, når man ligefrem hævder, at kvinders sind svækkes af en falsk forfinelse; at opdragende bøger skrevet af geniale mænd har virket i samme retning som mere overfladiske skrifter; og at kvinder helt i muhamedanismens ånd kun betragtes som kvindelige væsener, ikke som en del af menneskeheden. Og dog anerkendes den fornuft, der kan udvikles, som det ophøjede særkende, der hæver mennesket over dyrene og lægger et naturligt scepter i en svag hånd.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Yet, because I am a woman, I would not lead my readers to suppose, that I mean violently to agitate the contested question respecting the equality and inferiority of the sex; but as the subject lies in my way, and I cannot pass it over without subjecting the main tendency of my reasoning to misconstruction, I shall stop a moment to deliver, in a few words, my opinion. In the government of the physical world, it is observable that the female, in general, is inferior to the male. The male pursues, the female yields--this is the law of nature; and it does not appear to be suspended or abrogated in favour of woman. This physical superiority cannot be denied--and it is a noble prerogative! But not content with this natural pre-eminence, men endeavour to sink us still lower, merely to render us alluring objects for a moment; and women, intoxicated by the adoration which men, under the influence of their senses, pay them, do not seek to obtain a durable interest in their hearts, or to become the friends of the fellow creatures who find amusement in their society.
danishChanges.after: Jeg vil dog ikke have mine læsere til at tro, blot fordi jeg er kvinde, at jeg agter voldsomt at puste til striden om kønnets lighed eller underlegenhed. Men da emnet ligger på min vej, og jeg ikke kan gå uden om det uden at udsætte hovedretningen i min argumentation for misforståelser, vil jeg standse et øjeblik og kort give min mening til kende. I den fysiske verdens orden kan man iagttage, at hunnen i almindelighed er hannen underlegen. Hannen forfølger, hunnen giver efter — det er naturens lov, og den synes ikke at være sat ud af kraft eller ophævet til fordel for kvinden. Denne fysiske overlegenhed kan ikke benægtes, og det er et ædelt fortrin! Men mænd nøjes ikke med denne naturlige forrang; de forsøger at sænke os endnu længere ned, blot for at gøre os til tillokkende genstande for et øjeblik. Og kvinder, berusede af den tilbedelse, mænd under sansernes indflydelse viser dem, søger ikke at vinde en varig plads i deres hjerter eller at blive venner med de medmennesker, som morer sig i deres selskab.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I am aware of an obvious inference: from every quarter have I heard exclamations against masculine women; but where are they to be found? If, by this appellation, men mean to inveigh against their ardour in hunting, shooting, and gaming, I shall most cordially join in the cry; but if it be, against the imitation of manly virtues, or, more properly speaking, the attainment of those talents and virtues, the exercise of which ennobles the human character, and which raise females in the scale of animal being, when they are comprehensively termed mankind--all those who view them with a philosophical eye must, I should think, wish with me, that they may every day grow more and more masculine.
danishChanges.after: Jeg er klar over en nærliggende slutning: Fra alle sider har jeg hørt udbrud mod mandhaftige kvinder. Men hvor findes de? Hvis mænd med denne betegnelse vil angribe kvinders iver efter jagt, skydning og hasardspil, vil jeg af hele mit hjerte stemme i. Men hvis de angriber efterligningen af mandlige dyder — eller rettere tilegnelsen af de evner og dyder, hvis udøvelse forædler den menneskelige karakter og hæver kvinder i de levende væseners rangorden, når de sammenfattes under betegnelsen menneskeheden — så må enhver, der ser filosofisk på dem, efter min mening ønske med mig, at de dag for dag bliver mere og mere mandhaftige.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This discussion naturally divides the subject. I shall first consider women in the grand light of human creatures, who, in common with men, are placed on this earth to unfold their faculties; and afterwards I shall more particularly point out their peculiar designation.
danishChanges.after: Denne drøftelse giver en naturlig opdeling af emnet. Først vil jeg betragte kvinder i det store perspektiv som mennesker, der ligesom mænd er sat på jorden for at udfolde deres evner. Derefter vil jeg nærmere pege på deres særlige bestemmelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I wish also to steer clear of an error, which many respectable writers have fallen into; for the instruction which has hitherto been addressed to women, has rather been applicable to LADIES, if the little indirect advice, that is scattered through Sandford and Merton, be excepted; but, addressing my sex in a firmer tone, I pay particular attention to those in the middle class, because they appear to be in the most natural state. Perhaps the seeds of false refinement, immorality, and vanity have ever been shed by the great. Weak, artificial beings raised above the common wants and affections of their race, in a premature unnatural manner, undermine the very foundation of virtue, and spread corruption through the whole mass of society! As a class of mankind they have the strongest claim to pity! the education of the rich tends to render them vain and helpless, and the unfolding mind is not strengthened by the practice of those duties which dignify the human character. They only live to amuse themselves, and by the same law which in nature invariably produces certain effects, they soon only afford barren amusement.
danishChanges.after: Jeg ønsker også at undgå en fejl, som mange agtværdige forfattere er faldet i. Den undervisning, man hidtil har rettet mod kvinder, har snarere været beregnet på DAMER, bortset fra de få indirekte råd, der er spredt gennem Sandford og Merton. Men når jeg taler til mit køn i en fastere tone, retter jeg særlig opmærksomheden mod middelklassens kvinder, fordi de synes at befinde sig i den mest naturlige tilstand. Måske er frøene til falsk forfinelse, umoral og forfængelighed altid blevet sået af de fornemme. Svage, kunstige væsener, der på en for tidlig og unaturlig måde er hævet over deres medmenneskers almindelige behov og følelser, underminerer selve dydens grundlag og spreder fordærv gennem hele samfundet! Som gruppe blandt mennesker har de størst krav på medlidenhed. De riges opdragelse gør dem forfængelige og hjælpeløse, og sindet under udvikling styrkes ikke ved at øve de pligter, der giver mennesket værdighed. De lever kun for at more sig, og efter den samme lov, som i naturen uvægerligt frembringer bestemte virkninger, bliver de snart selv kun til tom underholdning.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But as I purpose taking a separate view of the different ranks of society, and of the moral character of women, in each, this hint is, for the present, sufficient; and I have only alluded to the subject, because it appears to me to be the very essence of an introduction to give a cursory account of the contents of the work it introduces.
danishChanges.after: Men da jeg vil behandle samfundets forskellige lag og kvindernes moralske karakter i hvert af dem særskilt, er denne antydning tilstrækkelig her. Jeg har kun berørt emnet, fordi det forekommer mig at være selve indledningens opgave kort at gøre rede for indholdet i det værk, den indleder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: My own sex, I hope, will excuse me, if I treat them like rational creatures, instead of flattering their FASCINATING graces, and viewing them as if they were in a state of perpetual childhood, unable to stand alone. I earnestly wish to point out in what true dignity and human happiness consists--I wish to persuade women to endeavour to acquire strength, both of mind and body, and to convince them, that the soft phrases, susceptibility of heart, delicacy of sentiment, and refinement of taste, are almost synonymous with epithets of weakness, and that those beings who are only the objects of pity and that kind of love, which has been termed its sister, will soon become objects of contempt.
danishChanges.after: Jeg håber, at mit eget køn vil undskylde mig, hvis jeg behandler kvinder som fornuftsvæsener i stedet for at smigre deres FORTRYLLENDE ynde og betragte dem, som om de levede i en evig barndom, ude af stand til at stå på egne ben. Jeg ønsker inderligt at vise, hvad sand værdighed og menneskelig lykke består i. Jeg vil overtale kvinder til at søge styrke i både sind og krop og overbevise dem om, at blide talemåder, et letpåvirkeligt hjerte, sarte følelser og forfinet smag næsten er andre ord for svaghed, og at de mennesker, som kun er genstand for medlidenhed og den slags kærlighed, man har kaldt dens søster, snart vil blive genstand for foragt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Dismissing then those pretty feminine phrases, which the men condescendingly use to soften our slavish dependence, and despising that weak elegancy of mind, exquisite sensibility, and sweet docility of manners, supposed to be the sexual characteristics of the weaker vessel, I wish to show that elegance is inferior to virtue, that the first object of laudable ambition is to obtain a character as a human being, regardless of the distinction of sex; and that secondary views should be brought to this simple touchstone.
danishChanges.after: Jeg vil derfor afvise de pæne, kvindelige talemåder, som mænd nedladende bruger til at mildne vores slaviske afhængighed, og foragte den svage elegance i sindet, den udsøgte følsomhed og den søde føjelighed, som antages at være det svagere køns særkende. Jeg vil vise, at elegance står under dyd, at en prisværdig ambitions første mål er at udvikle en karakter som menneske, uanset køn, og at alle sekundære hensyn må prøves mod denne enkle målestok.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This is a rough sketch of my plan; and should I express my conviction with the energetic emotions that I feel whenever I think of the subject, the dictates of experience and reflection will be felt by some of my readers. Animated by this important object, I shall disdain to cull my phrases or polish my style--I aim at being useful, and sincerity will render me unaffected; for wishing rather to persuade by the force of my arguments, than dazzle by the elegance of my language, I shall not waste my time in rounding periods, nor in fabricating the turgid bombast of artificial feelings, which, coming from the head, never reach the heart. I shall be employed about things, not words! and, anxious to render my sex more respectable members of society, I shall try to avoid that flowery diction which has slided from essays into novels, and from novels into familiar letters and conversation.
danishChanges.after: Dette er en grov skitse af min plan. Hvis jeg udtrykker min overbevisning med den stærke følelse, jeg oplever, hver gang jeg tænker over emnet, vil nogle af mine læsere mærke erfaringens og eftertankens stemme. Drevet af dette vigtige mål vil jeg ikke bruge kræfter på at udvælge smukke vendinger eller polere min stil. Jeg vil være nyttig, og oprigtigheden vil gøre mig ligefrem. Jeg ønsker hellere at overbevise med mine argumenters styrke end at blænde med sprogets elegance og vil derfor ikke spilde tid på at afrunde sætninger eller fremstille kunstige følelsers oppustede svulstighed, som kommer fra hovedet og aldrig når hjertet. Jeg vil beskæftige mig med sagen, ikke med ord! Og fordi jeg ønsker at gøre mit køn til mere agtværdige samfundsmedlemmer, vil jeg forsøge at undgå det blomstrende sprog, som er gledet fra essays ind i romaner og fra romaner ind i private breve og samtaler.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These pretty nothings, these caricatures of the real beauty of sensibility, dropping glibly from the tongue, vitiate the taste, and create a kind of sickly delicacy that turns away from simple unadorned truth; and a deluge of false sentiments and over-stretched feelings, stifling the natural emotions of the heart, render the domestic pleasures insipid, that ought to sweeten the exercise of those severe duties, which educate a rational and immortal being for a nobler field of action.
danishChanges.after: Disse smukke tomheder, disse karikaturer af følsomhedens virkelige skønhed, som så let glider over tungen, fordærver smagen og skaber en sygelig sarthed, der vender sig bort fra den enkle, usminkede sandhed. Og en strøm af falske følelser og overdreven følsomhed kvæler hjertets naturlige bevægelser og gør hjemmets glæder smagløse. Netop de glæder burde ellers forsøde udøvelsen af de strenge pligter, som forbereder et fornuftigt og udødeligt væsen til et ædlere virkefelt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The education of women has, of late, been more attended to than formerly; yet they are still reckoned a frivolous sex, and ridiculed or pitied by the writers who endeavour by satire or instruction to improve them. It is acknowledged that they spend many of the first years of their lives in acquiring a smattering of accomplishments: meanwhile, strength of body and mind are sacrificed to libertine notions of beauty, to the desire of establishing themselves, the only way women can rise in the world--by marriage. And this desire making mere animals of them, when they marry, they act as such children may be expected to act: they dress; they paint, and nickname God's creatures. Surely these weak beings are only fit for the seraglio! Can they govern a family, or take care of the poor babes whom they bring into the world?
danishChanges.after: På det seneste har kvinders uddannelse fået mere opmærksomhed end før, men de regnes stadig for et overfladisk køn og bliver latterliggjort eller beklaget af de forfattere, der søger at forbedre dem gennem satire eller vejledning. Det erkendes, at de bruger mange af deres første leveår på overfladisk at tilegne sig forskellige selskabelige færdigheder. Imens ofres kroppens og sindets styrke for vellystige forestillinger om skønhed og for ønsket om at skabe sig en stilling på den eneste måde, kvinder kan komme frem i verden: gennem ægteskabet. Og når dette ønske har gjort dem til rene dyr, opfører de sig efter brylluppet, som man kan vente af sådanne børn: De klæder sig ud, sminker sig og giver Guds skabninger øgenavne. Disse svage væsener egner sig vel kun til haremet! Kan de lede en familie eller tage sig af de stakkels spædbørn, de sætter i verden?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: If then it can be fairly deduced from the present conduct of the sex, from the prevalent fondness for pleasure, which takes place of ambition and those nobler passions that open and enlarge the soul; that the instruction which women have received has only tended, with the constitution of civil society, to render them insignificant objects of desire; mere propagators of fools! if it can be proved, that in aiming to accomplish them, without cultivating their understandings, they are taken out of their sphere of duties, and made ridiculous and useless when the short lived bloom of beauty is over*, I presume that RATIONAL men will excuse me for endeavouring to persuade them to become more masculine and respectable.
danishChanges.after: Hvis man altså med rimelighed kan slutte af kønnets nuværende adfærd og den udbredte lyst til fornøjelse, som træder i stedet for ambition og de ædlere lidenskaber, der åbner og udvider sjælen, at kvinders undervisning sammen med samfundets indretning kun har gjort dem til ubetydelige genstande for begær, til rene avlere af tåber; hvis det kan bevises, at bestræbelsen på at give dem ydre færdigheder uden at udvikle deres forstand fjerner dem fra deres pligters område og gør dem latterlige og unyttige, når skønhedens korte blomstring er forbi*, så går jeg ud fra, at FORNUFTIGE mænd vil undskylde mig, når jeg forsøger at overtale kvinder til at blive mere mandhaftige og agtværdige.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: (*Footnote. A lively writer, I cannot recollect his name, asks what business women turned of forty have to do in the world.)
danishChanges.after: (*Note. En livlig forfatter, hvis navn jeg ikke kan huske, spørger, hvad kvinder over fyrre overhovedet har at gøre i verden.)
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Indeed the word masculine is only a bugbear: there is little reason to fear that women will acquire too much courage or fortitude; for their apparent inferiority with respect to bodily strength, must render them, in some degree, dependent on men in the various relations of life; but why should it be increased by prejudices that give a sex to virtue, and confound simple truths with sensual reveries?
danishChanges.after: Ordet mandhaftig er i virkeligheden kun et skræmmebillede. Der er ikke meget grund til at frygte, at kvinder får for meget mod eller standhaftighed, for deres tilsyneladende underlegenhed i fysisk styrke må gøre dem til en vis grad afhængige af mænd i livets forskellige forhold. Men hvorfor skal denne afhængighed forstærkes af fordomme, som giver dyden et køn og sammenblander enkle sandheder med sanselige drømmerier?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women are, in fact, so much degraded by mistaken notions of female excellence, that I do not mean to add a paradox when I assert, that this artificial weakness produces a propensity to tyrannize, and gives birth to cunning, the natural opponent of strength, which leads them to play off those contemptible infantile airs that undermine esteem even whilst they excite desire. Do not foster these prejudices, and they will naturally fall into their subordinate, yet respectable station in life.
danishChanges.after: Kvinder er faktisk så nedværdigede af fejlagtige forestillinger om kvindelig fortræffelighed, at jeg ikke fremsætter et paradoks, når jeg hævder, at denne kunstige svaghed frembringer en trang til at tyrannisere og avler list, styrkens naturlige modstander. Den får dem til at anvende de foragtelige, barnlige manerer, som underminerer agtelsen, selv mens de vækker begær. Hold op med at nære disse fordomme, så vil kvinder naturligt finde deres underordnede, men agtværdige plads i livet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It seems scarcely necessary to say, that I now speak of the sex in general. Many individuals have more sense than their male relatives; and, as nothing preponderates where there is a constant struggle for an equilibrium, without it has naturally more gravity, some women govern their husbands without degrading themselves, because intellect will always govern.
danishChanges.after: Det er næppe nødvendigt at sige, at jeg her taler om kønnet som helhed. Mange enkelte kvinder har mere forstand end deres mandlige slægtninge. Og ligesom intet kan få overvægt i en vedvarende kamp om ligevægt, medmindre det naturligt vejer mere, styrer nogle kvinder deres mænd uden at nedværdige sig selv, fordi forstanden altid vil styre.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In the present state of society, it appears necessary to go back to first principles in search of the most simple truths, and to dispute with some prevailing prejudice every inch of ground. To clear my way, I must be allowed to ask some plain questions, and the answers will probably appear as unequivocal as the axioms on which reasoning is built; though, when entangled with various motives of action, they are formally contradicted, either by the words or conduct of men.
danishChanges.after: I samfundets nuværende tilstand synes det nødvendigt at vende tilbage til de grundlæggende principper for at finde de enkleste sandheder og kæmpe med en eller anden herskende fordom om hver tomme jord. For at rydde vejen må jeg have lov til at stille nogle ligefremme spørgsmål. Svarene vil sandsynligvis virke lige så entydige som de aksiomer, vores ræsonnementer bygger på, selv om mennesker direkte modsiger dem i ord eller handling, når de blandes sammen med forskellige bevæggrunde.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In what does man's pre-eminence over the brute creation consist? The answer is as clear as that a half is less than the whole; in Reason.
danishChanges.after: Hvad består menneskets forrang frem for dyrene i? Svaret er lige så klart, som at en halvdel er mindre end det hele: i fornuften.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: What acquirement exalts one being above another? Virtue; we spontaneously reply.
danishChanges.after: Hvilken egenskab, man kan tilegne sig, hæver det ene væsen over det andet? Dyd, svarer vi spontant.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: For what purpose were the passions implanted? That man by struggling with them might attain a degree of knowledge denied to the brutes: whispers Experience.
danishChanges.after: Hvorfor blev lidenskaberne nedlagt i os? For at mennesket gennem kampen med dem kunne nå en grad af erkendelse, som dyrene er nægtet, hvisker erfaringen.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Consequently the perfection of our nature and capability of happiness, must be estimated by the degree of reason, virtue, and knowledge, that distinguish the individual, and direct the laws which bind society: and that from the exercise of reason, knowledge and virtue naturally flow, is equally undeniable, if mankind be viewed collectively.
danishChanges.after: Derfor må fuldkommenheden i vores natur og vores evne til lykke måles efter den grad af fornuft, dyd og viden, som kendetegner det enkelte menneske og styrer de love, der binder samfundet sammen. Og ser man på menneskeheden som helhed, er det lige så ubestrideligt, at viden og dyd naturligt følger af at bruge fornuften.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The rights and duties of man thus simplified, it seems almost impertinent to attempt to illustrate truths that appear so incontrovertible: yet such deeply rooted prejudices have clouded reason, and such spurious qualities have assumed the name of virtues, that it is necessary to pursue the course of reason as it has been perplexed and involved in error, by various adventitious circumstances, comparing the simple axiom with casual deviations.
danishChanges.after: Når menneskets rettigheder og pligter på den måde er ført tilbage til noget enkelt, virker det næsten påtrængende at forsøge at belyse sandheder, der synes så uigendrivelige. Men så dybt rodfæstede fordomme har formørket fornuften, og så falske egenskaber har tiltaget sig navnet dyder, at vi må følge fornuftens vej gennem den forvirring og de fejltagelser, forskellige tilfældige omstændigheder har viklet den ind i, og sammenligne det enkle aksiom med de afvigelser, der er opstået.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Men, in general, seem to employ their reason to justify prejudices, which they have imbibed, they cannot trace how, rather than to root them out. The mind must be strong that resolutely forms its own principles; for a kind of intellectual cowardice prevails which makes many men shrink from the task, or only do it by halves. Yet the imperfect conclusions thus drawn, are frequently very plausible, because they are built on partial experience, on just, though narrow, views.
danishChanges.after: Mennesker synes i almindelighed at bruge deres fornuft til at retfærdiggøre fordomme, som de har optaget uden at vide hvordan, snarere end til at rykke dem op med rode. Det kræver et stærkt sind beslutsomt at danne sine egne principper, for en slags intellektuel fejhed får mange til at vige tilbage fra opgaven eller kun løse den halvt. Alligevel virker de ufuldkomne slutninger, de sådan når frem til, ofte meget overbevisende, fordi de bygger på en begrænset erfaring og på synspunkter, som er rigtige, men snævre.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Going back to first principles, vice skulks, with all its native deformity, from close investigation; but a set of shallow reasoners are always exclaiming that these arguments prove too much, and that a measure rotten at the core may be expedient. Thus expediency is continually contrasted with simple principles, till truth is lost in a mist of words, virtue in forms, and knowledge rendered a sounding nothing, by the specious prejudices that assume its name.
danishChanges.after: Vender man tilbage til de grundlæggende principper, lister lasten med al sin medfødte hæslighed bort fra en nærmere undersøgelse. Men overfladiske tænkere udbryder altid, at disse argumenter beviser for meget, og at en foranstaltning, der er rådden i sin kerne, godt kan være hensigtsmæssig. Sådan stilles hensigtsmæssighed hele tiden op imod enkle principper, indtil sandheden forsvinder i en tåge af ord, dyden i ydre former, og viden bliver til en klingende tomhed gennem de besnærende fordomme, der tager dens navn.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: That the society is formed in the wisest manner, whose constitution is founded on the nature of man, strikes, in the abstract, every thinking being so forcibly, that it looks like presumption to endeavour to bring forward proofs; though proof must be brought, or the strong hold of prescription will never be forced by reason; yet to urge prescription as an argument to justify the depriving men (or women) of their natural rights, is one of the absurd sophisms which daily insult common sense.
danishChanges.after: At det samfund er klogest indrettet, hvis forfatning bygger på menneskets natur, forekommer i det abstrakte ethvert tænkende væsen så indlysende, at det virker anmassende at fremlægge beviser. Alligevel må der beviser til, ellers vil fornuften aldrig bryde hævdens fæstning. Men at bruge hævd som argument for at berøve mænd — eller kvinder — deres naturlige rettigheder er et af de absurde skinargumenter, der dagligt fornærmer den sunde fornuft.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The civilization of the bulk of the people of Europe, is very partial; nay, it may be made a question, whether they have acquired any virtues in exchange for innocence, equivalent to the misery produced by the vices that have been plastered over unsightly ignorance, and the freedom which has been bartered for splendid slavery. The desire of dazzling by riches, the most certain pre-eminence that man can obtain, the pleasure of commanding flattering sycophants, and many other complicated low calculations of doting self-love, have all contributed to overwhelm the mass of mankind, and make liberty a convenient handle for mock patriotism. For whilst rank and titles are held of the utmost importance, before which Genius "must hide its diminished head," it is, with a few exceptions, very unfortunate for a nation when a man of abilities, without rank or property, pushes himself forward to notice. Alas! what unheard of misery have thousands suffered to purchase a cardinal's hat for an intriguing obscure adventurer, who longed to be ranked with princes, or lord it over them by seizing the triple crown!
danishChanges.after: Civilisationen blandt Europas brede befolkning er meget ufuldkommen. Man kan endda spørge, om folk til gengæld for deres uskyld har vundet dyder, der opvejer den elendighed, som er skabt af laster smurt hen over en uskøn uvidenhed, og af frihed byttet bort for pragtfuldt slaveri. Ønsket om at blænde med rigdom, den sikreste forrang et menneske kan opnå, glæden ved at kommandere med smigrende spytslikkere og selvkærlighedens mange andre indviklede, lave beregninger har alle bidraget til at kue menneskehedens flertal og gøre friheden til et bekvemt redskab for falsk fædrelandskærlighed. For så længe rang og titler tillægges den største betydning, så talentet må »skjule sit formindskede hoved« for dem, er det med få undtagelser meget ulykkeligt for et land, når en begavet mand uden rang eller ejendom kæmper sig frem til opmærksomhed. Ak, hvilke uhørte lidelser har tusinder ikke gennemgået for at skaffe en kardinalhat til en intrigant, ukendt eventyrer, som længtes efter at blive regnet blandt fyrster eller herske over dem ved at gribe den tredobbelte krone!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Such, indeed, has been the wretchedness that has flowed from hereditary honours, riches, and monarchy, that men of lively sensibility have almost uttered blasphemy in order to justify the dispensations of providence. Man has been held out as independent of his power who made him, or as a lawless planet darting from its orbit to steal the celestial fire of reason; and the vengeance of heaven, lurking in the subtile flame, sufficiently punished his temerity, by introducing evil into the world.
danishChanges.after: Så stor har den elendighed været, der udsprang af arvelige æresbevisninger, rigdom og monarki, at mennesker med levende følsomhed næsten har grebet til blasfemi for at retfærdiggøre forsynets ordninger. Mennesket er blevet fremstillet som uafhængigt af sin skabers magt eller som en lovløs planet, der farer ud af sin bane for at stjæle fornuftens himmelske ild; og himlens hævn, som lurede i den fine flamme, straffede rigeligt dets dristighed ved at indføre det onde i verden.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Impressed by this view of the misery and disorder which pervaded society, and fatigued with jostling against artificial fools, Rousseau became enamoured of solitude, and, being at the same time an optimist, he labours with uncommon eloquence to prove that man was naturally a solitary animal. Misled by his respect for the goodness of God, who certainly for what man of sense and feeling can doubt it! gave life only to communicate happiness, he considers evil as positive, and the work of man; not aware that he was exalting one attribute at the expense of another, equally necessary to divine perfection.
danishChanges.after: Påvirket af dette syn på den elendighed og uorden, der gennemtrængte samfundet, og træt af at støde mod kunstige tåber forelskede Rousseau sig i ensomheden. Og da han samtidig var optimist, anstrenger han sig med usædvanlig veltalenhed for at bevise, at mennesket fra naturens hånd var et ensomt dyr. Hans respekt for Guds godhed vildleder ham — Gud, som ganske vist, og hvilket menneske med forstand og følelse kan tvivle på det, kun gav liv for at skænke lykke. Rousseau betragter det onde som noget selvstændigt og som menneskets værk uden at indse, at han ophøjede én af Guds egenskaber på bekostning af en anden, som var lige så nødvendig for den guddommelige fuldkommenhed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Reared on a false hypothesis, his arguments in favour of a state of nature are plausible, but unsound. I say unsound; for to assert that a state of nature is preferable to civilization in all its possible perfection, is, in other words, to arraign supreme wisdom; and the paradoxical exclamation, that God has made all things right, and that evil has been introduced by the creature whom he formed, knowing what he formed, is as unphilosophical as impious.
danishChanges.after: Hans argumenter for naturtilstanden er bygget på en falsk antagelse og virker derfor overbevisende, men holder ikke. Jeg siger, at de ikke holder: At hævde, at naturtilstanden er at foretrække frem for civilisationen i hele dens mulige fuldkommenhed, er med andre ord at anklage den højeste visdom. Og det paradoksale udbrud, at Gud har skabt alt godt, mens det onde blev indført af den skabning, han formede med fuld viden om, hvad han formede, er lige så ufilosofisk, som det er ugudeligt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: When that wise Being, who created us and placed us here, saw the fair idea, he willed, by allowing it to be so, that the passions should unfold our reason, because he could see that present evil would produce future good. Could the helpless creature whom he called from nothing, break loose from his providence, and boldly learn to know good by practising evil without his permission? No. How could that energetic advocate for immortality argue so inconsistently? Had mankind remained for ever in the brutal state of nature, which even his magic pen cannot paint as a state in which a single virtue took root, it would have been clear, though not to the sensitive unreflecting wanderer, that man was born to run the circle of life and death, and adorn God's garden for some purpose which could not easily be reconciled with his attributes.
danishChanges.after: Da det vise væsen, som skabte os og satte os her, så den smukke idé for sig, ville han — ved at tillade det — lade lidenskaberne udvikle vores fornuft, fordi han kunne se, at nutidens onde ville frembringe fremtidens gode. Kunne den hjælpeløse skabning, han kaldte frem af intet, rive sig løs fra hans forsyn og dristigt lære det gode at kende ved at øve det onde uden hans tilladelse? Nej. Hvordan kunne denne ivrige forsvarer for udødeligheden argumentere så selvmodsigende? Var menneskeheden for altid forblevet i den dyriske naturtilstand, som selv hans magiske pen ikke kan fremstille som et sted, hvor en eneste dyd slog rod, ville det have været klart — dog ikke for den følsomme, tankeløse vandrer — at mennesket var født til at gennemløbe livets og dødens kredsløb og smykke Guds have med et formål, som vanskeligt kunne forenes med Guds egenskaber.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But if, to crown the whole, there were to be rational creatures produced, allowed to rise in excellency by the exercise of powers implanted for that purpose; if benignity itself thought fit to call into existence a creature above the brutes, who could think and improve himself, why should that inestimable gift, for a gift it was, if a man was so created as to have a capacity to rise above the state in which sensation produced brutal ease, be called, in direct terms, a curse? A curse it might be reckoned, if all our existence was bounded by our continuance in this world; for why should the gracious fountain of life give us passions, and the power of reflecting, only to embitter our days, and inspire us with mistaken notions of dignity? Why should he lead us from love of ourselves to the sublime emotions which the discovery of his wisdom and goodness excites, if these feelings were not set in motion to improve our nature, of which they make a part, and render us capable of enjoying a more godlike portion of happiness? Firmly persuaded that no evil exists in the world that God did not design to take place, I build my belief on the perfection of God.
danishChanges.after: Men hvis der som kronen på værket skulle frembringes fornuftsvæsener, som fik lov at hæve sig mod større fortræffelighed ved at øve de evner, der var lagt i dem til dette formål; hvis godheden selv fandt det rigtigt at skabe et væsen over dyrene, som kunne tænke og forbedre sig, hvorfor skulle denne uvurderlige gave så ligefrem kaldes en forbandelse? En gave var den jo, hvis mennesket blev skabt med evnen til at hæve sig over den tilstand, hvor sanseoplevelser gav dyrisk velbehag. Den kunne regnes for en forbandelse, hvis hele vores eksistens var begrænset til opholdet i denne verden. For hvorfor skulle livets nådige kilde give os lidenskaber og evnen til eftertanke, blot for at forsure vores dage og indgive os falske forestillinger om værdighed? Hvorfor skulle han føre os fra selvkærlighed til de ophøjede følelser, opdagelsen af hans visdom og godhed vækker, hvis disse følelser ikke blev sat i bevægelse for at forbedre vores natur, som de selv er en del af, og gøre os i stand til at nyde en mere guddommelig lykke? Jeg er fast overbevist om, at der ikke findes noget ondt i verden, som Gud ikke har bestemt skulle ske, og jeg bygger min tro på Guds fuldkommenhed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Rousseau exerts himself to prove, that all WAS right originally: a crowd of authors that all IS now right: and I, that all WILL BE right.
danishChanges.after: Rousseau anstrenger sig for at bevise, at alt VAR godt fra begyndelsen; en mængde forfattere, at alt ER godt nu; og jeg, at alt VIL BLIVE godt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, true to his first position, next to a state of nature, Rousseau celebrates barbarism, and, apostrophizing the shade of Fabricius, he forgets that, in conquering the world, the Romans never dreamed of establishing their own liberty on a firm basis, or of extending the reign of virtue. Eager to support his system, he stigmatizes, as vicious, every effort of genius; and uttering the apotheosis of savage virtues, he exalts those to demigods, who were scarcely human--the brutal Spartans, who in defiance of justice and gratitude, sacrificed, in cold blood, the slaves that had shown themselves men to rescue their oppressors.
danishChanges.after: Men tro mod sit udgangspunkt priser Rousseau barbariet næsthøjest efter naturtilstanden. Når han påkalder Fabricius’ skygge, glemmer han, at romerne, mens de erobrede verden, aldrig drømte om at give deres egen frihed et fast grundlag eller udvide dydens herredømme. I sin iver efter at støtte sit system stempler han enhver udfoldelse af talent som lastefuld; og mens han guddommeliggør de vilde dyder, ophøjer han mennesker, som knap var menneskelige, til halvguder: de brutale spartanere, der i strid med retfærdighed og taknemmelighed koldblodigt ofrede de slaver, som havde vist sig som mænd ved at redde deres undertrykkere.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Disgusted with artificial manners and virtues, the citizen of Geneva, instead of properly sifting the subject, threw away the wheat with the chaff, without waiting to inquire whether the evils, which his ardent soul turned from indignantly, were the consequence of civilization, or the vestiges of barbarism. He saw vice trampling on virtue, and the semblance of goodness taking place of the reality; he saw talents bent by power to sinister purposes, and never thought of tracing the gigantic mischief up to arbitrary power, up to the hereditary distinctions that clash with the mental superiority that naturally raises a man above his fellows. He did not perceive, that the regal power, in a few generations, introduces idiotism into the noble stem, and holds out baits to render thousands idle and vicious.
danishChanges.after: I sin afsky for kunstige omgangsformer og dyder kastede borgeren fra Genève hveden bort sammen med avnerne i stedet for at sigte emnet ordentligt. Han standsede ikke for at undersøge, om de onder, hans brændende sjæl vendte sig fra med harme, var følger af civilisationen eller rester af barbariet. Han så lasten trampe på dyden og skinnet af godhed erstatte dens virkelighed; han så magten bøje talenter mod skumle formål, men tænkte aldrig på at føre den vældige skade tilbage til vilkårlig magt og til arvelige rangforskelle, som strider mod den åndelige overlegenhed, der naturligt hæver et menneske over dets medmennesker. Han indså ikke, at kongemagten på få generationer bringer tåbelighed ind i den ædle slægt og lokker tusinder til lediggang og laster.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Nothing can set the regal character in a more contemptible point of view, than the various crimes that have elevated men to the supreme dignity. Vile intrigues, unnatural crimes, and every vice that degrades our nature, have been the steps to this distinguished eminence; yet millions of men have supinely allowed the nerveless limbs of the posterity of such rapacious prowlers, to rest quietly on their ensanguined thrones.
danishChanges.after: Intet kan stille kongeværdigheden i et mere foragteligt lys end de forskellige forbrydelser, der har hævet mennesker til den øverste rang. Usle intriger, unaturlige forbrydelser og enhver last, der nedværdiger vores natur, har været trin op til denne særlige ophøjelse. Og dog har millioner af mennesker sløvt tilladt, at efterkommerne af sådanne rovgriske røvere lod deres slappe lemmer hvile fredeligt på blodplettede troner.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: What but a pestilential vapour can hover over society, when its chief director is only instructed in the invention of crimes, or the stupid routine of childish ceremonies? Will men never be wise? will they never cease to expect corn from tares, and figs from thistles?
danishChanges.after: Hvad andet end en pestbefængt damp kan hænge over samfundet, når dets øverste leder kun oplæres i at udtænke forbrydelser eller i barnlige ceremoniers tåbelige rutine? Bliver mennesker aldrig kloge? Holder de aldrig op med at vente korn fra ukrudt og figner fra tidsler?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is impossible for any man, when the most favourable circumstances concur, to acquire sufficient knowledge and strength of mind to discharge the duties of a king, entrusted with uncontrolled power; how then must they be violated when his very elevation is an insuperable bar to the attainment of either wisdom or virtue; when all the feelings of a man are stifled by flattery, and reflection shut out by pleasure! Surely it is madness to make the fate of thousands depend on the caprice of a weak fellow creature, whose very station sinks him NECESSARILY below the meanest of his subjects! But one power should not be thrown down to exalt another--for all power intoxicates weak man; and its abuse proves, that the more equality there is established among men, the more virtue and happiness will reign in society. But this, and any similar maxim deduced from simple reason, raises an outcry--the church or the state is in danger, if faith in the wisdom of antiquity is not implicit; and they who, roused by the sight of human calamity, dare to attack human authority, are reviled as despisers of God, and enemies of man. These are bitter calumnies, yet they reached one of the best of men, (Dr. Price.) whose ashes still preach peace, and whose memory demands a respectful pause, when subjects are discussed that lay so near his heart.
danishChanges.after: Selv under de gunstigste omstændigheder er det umuligt for noget menneske at opnå tilstrækkelig viden og åndelig styrke til at opfylde en konges pligter, når han er betroet uindskrænket magt. Hvor voldsomt må disse pligter da ikke forsømmes, når selve hans ophøjede stilling er en uoverstigelig hindring for både visdom og dyd, når alle menneskelige følelser kvæles af smiger, og fornøjelsen holder eftertanken ude! Det er vel vanvid at lade tusinders skæbne afhænge af lunerne hos et svagt medmenneske, hvis stilling i sig selv NØDVENDIGVIS sænker ham under den ringeste af hans undersåtter! Men én magt bør ikke styrtes for at ophøje en anden, for al magt beruser det svage menneske. Misbruget af den viser, at jo større lighed der skabes mellem mennesker, desto mere dyd og lykke vil herske i samfundet. Men denne og enhver lignende grundsætning, der følger af den enkle fornuft, vækker et ramaskrig: Kirken eller staten er i fare, hvis troen på fortidens visdom ikke er ubetinget. Og de, som vækkes af synet af menneskelig elendighed og vover at angribe menneskelig autoritet, udskældes som gudsforagtere og menneskefjender. Det er bitre bagvaskelser, og alligevel ramte de et af de bedste mennesker, dr. Price, hvis aske stadig prædiker fred, og hvis minde kræver en respektfuld pause, når vi drøfter emner, der lå hans hjerte så nær.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: After attacking the sacred majesty of kings, I shall scarcely excite surprise, by adding my firm persuasion, that every profession, in which great subordination of rank constitutes its power, is highly injurious to morality.
danishChanges.after: Efter at have angrebet kongernes hellige majestæt vækker jeg næppe overraskelse ved at tilføje min faste overbevisning om, at enhver stand, hvis magt bygger på en streng rangorden og underordning, er stærkt skadelig for moralen.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A standing army, for instance, is incompatible with freedom; because subordination and rigour are the very sinews of military discipline; and despotism is necessary to give vigour to enterprises that one will directs. A spirit inspired by romantic notions of honour, a kind of morality founded on the fashion of the age, can only be felt by a few officers, whilst the main body must be moved by command, like the waves of the sea; for the strong wind of authority pushes the crowd of subalterns forward, they scarcely know or care why, with headlong fury.
danishChanges.after: En stående hær er for eksempel uforenelig med frihed, fordi underordning og strenghed er selve den militære disciplins styrke, og fordi despoti er nødvendigt for at give kraft til foretagender, som styres af én vilje. Kun få officerer kan være båret af romantiske forestillinger om ære, en slags moral grundlagt på tidens skik. Hovedstyrken må derimod sættes i bevægelse ved kommando som havets bølger, for autoritetens stærke vind driver mængden af underordnede frem med hovedkulds raseri, mens de knap ved eller bekymrer sig om hvorfor.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, nothing can be so prejudicial to the morals of the inhabitants of country towns, as the occasional residence of a set of idle superficial young men, whose only occupation is gallantry, and whose polished manners render vice more dangerous, by concealing its deformity under gay ornamental drapery. An air of fashion, which is but a badge of slavery, and proves that the soul has not a strong individual character, awes simple country people into an imitation of the vices, when they cannot catch the slippery graces of politeness. Every corps is a chain of despots, who, submitting and tyrannizing without exercising their reason, become dead weights of vice and folly on the community. A man of rank or fortune, sure of rising by interest, has nothing to do but to pursue some extravagant freak; whilst the needy GENTLEMAN, who is to rise, as the phrase turns, by his merit, becomes a servile parasite or vile pander.
danishChanges.after: Desuden kan intet være mere skadeligt for moralen i provinsbyerne end det lejlighedsvise ophold af en flok ledige, overfladiske unge mænd, hvis eneste beskæftigelse er kurmageri, og hvis polerede omgangsformer gør lasten farligere ved at skjule dens hæslighed under munter pynt. Et mondænt ydre, som blot er et tegn på slaveri og viser, at sjælen mangler en stærk selvstændig karakter, får jævne folk på landet til ærefrygtigt at efterligne lasterne, når de ikke kan tilegne sig høflighedens undvigende ynde. Ethvert korps er en kæde af despoter, som underkaster sig og tyranniserer uden at bruge deres fornuft og dermed bliver tunge byrder af last og dårskab for samfundet. En mand med rang eller formue, som ved, at han vil avancere gennem forbindelser, behøver kun at følge et eller andet udskejende indfald, mens den fattige GENTLEMAN, der som det hedder skal avancere ved egen fortjeneste, bliver en underdanig snylter eller en ussel håndlanger for andres laster.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Sailors, the naval gentlemen, come under the same description, only their vices assume a different and a grosser cast. They are more positively indolent, when not discharging the ceremonials of their station; whilst the insignificant fluttering of soldiers may be termed active idleness. More confined to the society of men, the former acquire a fondness for humour and mischievous tricks; whilst the latter, mixing frequently with well-bred women, catch a sentimental cant. But mind is equally out of the question, whether they indulge the horse-laugh or polite simper.
danishChanges.after: Søfolkene, flådens gentlemen, passer på samme beskrivelse, blot får deres laster en anden og grovere form. De er mere udpræget dovne, når de ikke udfører deres stillings ceremonier, mens soldaternes ubetydelige flakken omkring kan kaldes aktiv lediggang. Da søfolkene er mere henvist til mænds selskab, udvikler de smag for vittigheder og skarnsstreger, mens soldaterne, som ofte omgås velopdragne kvinder, tilegner sig et sentimentalt klichésprog. Men forstanden er lige fraværende, hvad enten de hengiver sig til rå latter eller høflige småsmil.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.
