danishChanges.before: May I be allowed to extend the comparison to a profession where more mind is certainly to be found; for the clergy have superior opportunities of improvement, though subordination almost equally cramps their faculties? The blind submission imposed at college to forms of belief, serves as a noviciate to the curate who most obsequiously respects the opinion of his rector or patron, if he means to rise in his profession. Perhaps there cannot be a more forcible contrast than between the servile, dependent gait of a poor curate, and the courtly mien of a bishop. And the respect and contempt they inspire render the discharge of their separate functions equally useless.
danishChanges.after: Må jeg udvide sammenligningen til en stand, hvor der ganske vist findes mere ånd? Præsterne har bedre muligheder for at udvikle sig, selv om underordningen næsten lige så meget hæmmer deres evner. Den blinde underkastelse under trosformularer, som påtvinges dem under studierne, er en læretid for den hjælpepræst, der yderst underdanigt respekterer sin sognepræsts eller beskytters mening, hvis han vil avancere i sit fag. Måske findes der ingen skarpere kontrast end mellem en fattig hjælpepræsts krybende, afhængige fremtræden og en biskops hofmandsmanerer. Og den respekt og foragt, de hver især vækker, gør udførelsen af deres forskellige opgaver lige unyttig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is of great importance to observe, that the character of every man is, in some degree, formed by his profession. A man of sense may only have a cast of countenance that wears off as you trace his individuality, whilst the weak, common man, has scarcely ever any character, but what belongs to the body; at least, all his opinions have been so steeped in the vat consecrated by authority, that the faint spirit which the grape of his own vine yields cannot be distinguished.
danishChanges.after: Det er meget vigtigt at bemærke, at ethvert menneskes karakter til en vis grad formes af dets erhverv. Hos et forstandigt menneske kan det blot sætte et præg, som svinder, når man lærer dets individualitet at kende, mens det svage, almindelige menneske næsten aldrig har anden karakter end den, standen giver det. I det mindste er alle dets meninger blevet så gennemvædet i det kar, autoriteten har indviet, at den svage ånd, druen fra dets egen vinstok giver, ikke kan skelnes.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Samfundet bør derfor, efterhånden som det bliver mere oplyst, være meget påpasseligt med ikke at oprette stænder af mænd, som nødvendigvis må blive tåbelige eller lastefulde af selve deres professions forfatning.
danishChanges.after: Efterhånden som samfundet bliver mere oplyst, bør det derfor være meget omhyggeligt med ikke at oprette grupper af mennesker, som selve deres stands indretning nødvendigvis gør tåbelige eller lastefulde.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In the infancy of society, when men were just emerging out of barbarism, chiefs and priests, touching the most powerful springs of savage conduct--hope and fear--must have had unbounded sway. An aristocracy, of course, is naturally the first form of government. But clashing interests soon losing their equipoise, a monarchy and hierarchy break out of the confusion of ambitious struggles, and the foundation of both is secured by feudal tenures. This appears to be the origin of monarchial and priestly power, and the dawn of civilization. But such combustible materials cannot long be pent up; and getting vent in foreign wars and intestine insurrections, the people acquire some power in the tumult, which obliges their rulers to gloss over their oppression with a show of right. Thus, as wars, agriculture, commerce, and literature, expands the mind, despots are compelled, to make covert corruption hold fast the power which was formerly snatched by open force.* And this baneful lurking gangrene is most quickly spread by luxury and superstition, the sure dregs of ambition. The indolent puppet of a court first becomes a luxurious monster, or fastidious sensualist, and then makes the contagion which his unnatural state spreads, the instrument of tyranny.
danishChanges.after: I samfundets barndom, da menneskene netop var ved at træde ud af barbariet, må høvdinge og præster have haft ubegrænset magt ved at spille på de stærkeste drivkræfter i de vildes adfærd: håb og frygt. Et aristokrati er derfor naturligt den første styreform. Men de stridende interesser mister snart deres ligevægt, og af de ambitiøse kampes forvirring opstår et monarki og et præstevælde, hvis grundlag sikres gennem lensbesiddelser. Dette synes at være oprindelsen til konge- og præstemagten og civilisationens begyndelse. Men så brændbart et stof kan ikke holdes indespærret længe. Når det får udløb i krige mod fremmede og oprør hjemme, vinder folket en vis magt i uroen, og det tvinger herskerne til at dække undertrykkelsen med et skin af ret. Efterhånden som krig, landbrug, handel og litteratur udvider sindet, tvinges despoterne derfor til gennem skjult fordærv at fastholde den magt, de tidligere greb med åben vold.* Og denne skadelige, skjulte koldbrand spredes hurtigst af luksus og overtro, ambitionens sikre bundfald. Hoffets dovne marionet bliver først et overdådigt uhyre eller en kræsen nydelsessøger og gør derpå den smitte, som dens unaturlige tilstand spreder, til et redskab for tyranniet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: (*Footnote. Men of abilities scatter seeds that grow up, and have a great influence on the forming opinion; and when once the public opinion preponderates, through the exertion of reason, the overthrow of arbitrary power is not very distant.)
danishChanges.after: (*Note. Begavede mennesker spreder frø, som vokser op og får stor indflydelse på meningsdannelsen. Og når den offentlige mening først får overtaget gennem fornuftens arbejde, er den vilkårlige magts fald ikke langt borte.)
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is the pestiferous purple which renders the progress of civilization a curse, and warps the understanding, till men of sensibility doubt whether the expansion of intellect produces a greater portion of happiness or misery. But the nature of the poison points out the antidote; and had Rousseau mounted one step higher in his investigation; or could his eye have pierced through the foggy atmosphere, which he almost disdained to breathe, his active mind would have darted forward to contemplate the perfection of man in the establishment of true civilization, instead of taking his ferocious flight back to the night of sensual ignorance.
danishChanges.after: Det er den pestbefængte kongelige purpur, der gør civilisationens fremskridt til en forbandelse og forvrider forstanden, indtil følsomme mennesker tvivler på, om fornuftens udvikling skaber mest lykke eller elendighed. Men giftens natur viser, hvad modgiften er. Havde Rousseau løftet sin undersøgelse ét trin højere, eller havde hans blik kunnet trænge gennem den tågede atmosfære, han næsten foragtede at indånde, ville hans virksomme sind have skudt frem mod tanken om menneskets fuldkommengørelse gennem en sand civilisation i stedet for vildt at flygte tilbage til den sanselige uvidenheds nat.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To account for, and excuse the tyranny of man, many ingenious arguments have been brought forward to prove, that the two sexes, in the acquirement of virtue, ought to aim at attaining a very different character: or, to speak explicitly, women are not allowed to have sufficient strength of mind to acquire what really deserves the name of virtue. Yet it should seem, allowing them to have souls, that there is but one way appointed by providence to lead MANKIND to either virtue or happiness.
danishChanges.after: For at forklare og undskylde mandens tyranni har man fremsat mange sindrige argumenter, som skal bevise, at de to køn bør stræbe efter vidt forskellige karakterer, når de tilegner sig dyd. Eller mere ligefremt: Man vil ikke tilkende kvinder tilstrækkelig åndelig styrke til at tilegne sig det, der virkelig fortjener navnet dyd. Men hvis man indrømmer, at de har sjæle, synes forsynet kun at have anvist én vej, som fører MENNESKEHEDEN til enten dyd eller lykke.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: If then women are not a swarm of ephemeron triflers, why should they be kept in ignorance under the specious name of innocence? Men complain, and with reason, of the follies and caprices of our sex, when they do not keenly satirize our headstrong passions and groveling vices. Behold, I should answer, the natural effect of ignorance! The mind will ever be unstable that has only prejudices to rest on, and the current will run with destructive fury when there are no barriers to break its force. Women are told from their infancy, and taught by the example of their mothers, that a little knowledge of human weakness, justly termed cunning, softness of temper, OUTWARD obedience, and a scrupulous attention to a puerile kind of propriety, will obtain for them the protection of man; and should they be beautiful, every thing else is needless, for at least twenty years of their lives.
danishChanges.after: Hvis kvinder da ikke er en sværm af døgnfluer, der kun beskæftiger sig med tomheder, hvorfor skal de så holdes i uvidenhed under det besnærende navn uskyld? Mænd klager med rette over vores køns dårskaber og luner, når de ikke ligefrem spidder vores ustyrlige lidenskaber og krybende laster med skarp satire. Se dér, ville jeg svare, uvidenhedens naturlige virkning! Et sind, der kun har fordomme at støtte sig til, vil altid være ustadigt, og strømmen vil løbe med ødelæggende kraft, når ingen dæmninger bryder den. Fra den tidligste barndom får kvinder at vide, og lærer gennem deres mødres eksempel, at lidt kendskab til menneskelig svaghed — med rette kaldet list — et mildt sind, YDRE lydighed og pinlig overholdelse af en barnlig form for anstændighed vil skaffe dem mandens beskyttelse. Og hvis de er smukke, behøver de intet andet i mindst tyve år af deres liv.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Thus Milton describes our first frail mother; though when he tells us that women are formed for softness and sweet attractive grace, I cannot comprehend his meaning, unless, in the true Mahometan strain, he meant to deprive us of souls, and insinuate that we were beings only designed by sweet attractive grace, and docile blind obedience, to gratify the senses of man when he can no longer soar on the wing of contemplation.
danishChanges.after: Sådan beskriver Milton vores første skrøbelige mor. Men når han siger, at kvinder er skabt til mildhed og sød, tillokkende ynde, kan jeg ikke forstå ham, medmindre han i ægte muhamedansk ånd ville berøve os sjæle og antyde, at vi kun er skabt til gennem sød, tillokkende ynde og føjelig, blind lydighed at tilfredsstille mandens sanser, når han ikke længere kan svæve på eftertankens vinger.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: How grossly do they insult us, who thus advise us only to render ourselves gentle, domestic brutes! For instance, the winning softness, so warmly, and frequently recommended, that governs by obeying. What childish expressions, and how insignificant is the being--can it be an immortal one? who will condescend to govern by such sinister methods! "Certainly," says Lord Bacon, "man is of kin to the beasts by his body: and if he be not of kin to God by his spirit, he is a base and ignoble creature!" Men, indeed, appear to me to act in a very unphilosophical manner, when they try to secure the good conduct of women by attempting to keep them always in a state of childhood. Rousseau was more consistent when he wished to stop the progress of reason in both sexes; for if men eat of the tree of knowledge, women will come in for a taste: but, from the imperfect cultivation which their understandings now receive, they only attain a knowledge of evil.
danishChanges.after: Hvor groft fornærmer de os ikke, som på den måde råder os til blot at gøre os til blide husdyr! Tænk for eksempel på den vindende mildhed, der så varmt og ofte anbefales, og som hersker ved at adlyde. Hvilke barnlige udtryk, og hvor ubetydeligt er ikke det væsen — kan det være udødeligt? — som nedlader sig til at herske med sådanne skumle midler! »Mennesket er ganske vist,« siger lord Bacon, »gennem sin krop beslægtet med dyrene; og hvis det ikke gennem sin ånd er beslægtet med Gud, er det et lavt og uædelt væsen!« Mænd forekommer mig virkelig at handle meget ufilosofisk, når de vil sikre kvinders gode opførsel ved at holde dem i evig barndom. Rousseau var mere konsekvent, da han ville standse fornuftens udvikling hos begge køn. For hvis mænd spiser af kundskabens træ, vil kvinder også få en smagsprøve; men med den ufuldkomne udvikling, deres forstand nu får, opnår de kun kendskab til det onde.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Children, I grant, should be innocent; but when the epithet is applied to men, or women, it is but a civil term for weakness. For if it be allowed that women were destined by Providence to acquire human virtues, and by the exercise of their understandings, that stability of character which is the firmest ground to rest our future hopes upon, they must be permitted to turn to the fountain of light, and not forced to shape their course by the twinkling of a mere satellite. Milton, I grant, was of a very different opinion; for he only bends to the indefeasible right of beauty, though it would be difficult to render two passages, which I now mean to contrast, consistent: but into similar inconsistencies are great men often led by their senses:--
danishChanges.after: Jeg indrømmer gerne, at børn bør være uskyldige; men når ordet bruges om mænd eller kvinder, er det blot en høflig betegnelse for svaghed. Hvis man anerkender, at forsynet har bestemt kvinder til at tilegne sig menneskelige dyder og gennem brugen af deres forstand opnå den karakterfasthed, som er det sikreste grundlag for vores fremtidige håb, må man lade dem vende sig mod selve lysets kilde i stedet for at tvinge dem til at styre efter en månes svage glimt. Milton var ganske vist af en helt anden mening, for han bøjer sig kun for skønhedens ukrænkelige ret. Men det bliver svært at forene de to passager, jeg nu vil stille over for hinanden. Til lignende selvmodsigelser bliver store mænd ofte ført af deres sanser:
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "To whom thus Eve with perfect beauty adorned: My author and disposer, what thou bidst Unargued I obey; so God ordains; God is thy law, thou mine; to know no more Is woman's happiest knowledge and her praise."
danishChanges.after:
»Til ham sagde Eva, smykket med fuldkommen skønhed:
Min skaber og hersker, hvad du befaler,
adlyder jeg uden indvending; sådan vil Gud.
Gud er din lov, du er min; ikke at vide mere
er kvindens lykkeligste viden og hendes hæder.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These are exactly the arguments that I have used to children; but I have added, "Your reason is now gaining strength, and, till it arrives at some degree of maturity, you must look up to me for advice: then you ought to THINK, and only rely on God."
danishChanges.after: Det er præcis de argumenter, jeg har brugt over for børn, men jeg har tilføjet: »Jeres fornuft er ved at få styrke, og indtil den når en vis modenhed, må I søge råd hos mig. Derefter bør I TÆNKE og kun stole på Gud.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Yet, in the following lines, Milton seems to coincide with me, when he makes Adam thus expostulate with his Maker:--
danishChanges.after: Alligevel synes Milton i de følgende linjer at være enig med mig, når han lader Adam indvende over for sin skaber:
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "Hast thou not made me here thy substitute, And these inferior far beneath me set? Among unequals what society Can sort, what harmony or delight? Which must be mutual, in proportion due Given and received; but in disparity The one intense, the other still remiss Cannot well suit with either, but soon prove Tedious alike: of fellowship I speak Such as I seek fit to participate All rational delight."
danishChanges.after:
»Har du ikke sat mig her som din stedfortræder
og disse ringere væsener langt under mig?
Hvilket samvær kan der være mellem ulige,
hvilken harmoni eller glæde?
Den må jo være gensidig, givet og modtaget
i rette forhold; men i uligheden,
hvor den ene er ivrig og den anden altid lunken,
kan ingen af dem trives, og snart bliver det
en byrde for begge. Jeg taler om fællesskab,
som det, jeg søger, egnet til at dele
al fornuftig glæde.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In treating, therefore, of the manners of women, let us, disregarding sensual arguments, trace what we should endeavour to make them in order to co-operate, if the expression be not too bold, with the Supreme Being.
danishChanges.after: Lad os derfor, når vi behandler kvinders levevis, se bort fra sanselige argumenter og undersøge, hvad vi bør søge at gøre dem til for — hvis udtrykket ikke er for dristigt — at samarbejde med det højeste væsen.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: By individual education, I mean--for the sense of the word is not precisely defined--such an attention to a child as will slowly sharpen the senses, form the temper, regulate the passions, as they begin to ferment, and set the understanding to work before the body arrives at maturity; so that the man may only have to proceed, not to begin, the important task of learning to think and reason.
danishChanges.after: Med individuel opdragelse mener jeg — for ordets betydning er ikke præcist fastlagt — en omsorg for barnet, som langsomt skærper sanserne, former sindelaget, styrer lidenskaberne, når de begynder at røre sig, og sætter forstanden i arbejde, før kroppen er udvokset. Så behøver det voksne menneske kun at fortsætte, ikke at begynde på, den vigtige opgave at lære at tænke og ræsonnere.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To prevent any misconstruction, I must add, that I do not believe that a private education can work the wonders which some sanguine writers have attributed to it. Men and women must be educated, in a great degree, by the opinions and manners of the society they live in. In every age there has been a stream of popular opinion that has carried all before it, and given a family character, as it were, to the century. It may then fairly be inferred, that, till society be differently constituted, much cannot be expected from education. It is, however, sufficient for my present purpose to assert, that, whatever effect circumstances have on the abilities, every being may become virtuous by the exercise of its own reason; for if but one being was created with vicious inclinations--that is, positively bad-- what can save us from atheism? or if we worship a God, is not that God a devil?
danishChanges.after: For at undgå misforståelser må jeg tilføje, at jeg ikke tror, en privat opdragelse kan udrette de mirakler, nogle optimistiske forfattere har tilskrevet den. Mænd og kvinder formes nødvendigvis i høj grad af meningerne og omgangsformerne i det samfund, de lever i. I enhver tidsalder har der været en strøm af gængse opfattelser, som har revet alt med sig og så at sige givet århundredet et familiepræg. Derfor kan man med rimelighed slutte, at der ikke kan ventes meget af opdragelsen, før samfundet er anderledes indrettet. Til mit nuværende formål er det dog nok at hævde, at uanset hvordan omstændighederne påvirker evnerne, kan ethvert væsen blive dydigt ved at bruge sin egen fornuft. For hvis blot ét væsen var skabt med lastefulde tilbøjeligheder, altså som ligefrem ondt, hvad skulle da redde os fra ateismen? Eller hvis vi tilbeder en Gud, er den Gud så ikke en djævel?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Consequently, the most perfect education, in my opinion, is such an exercise of the understanding as is best calculated to strengthen the body and form the heart; or, in other words, to enable the individual to attain such habits of virtue as will render it independent. In fact, it is a farce to call any being virtuous whose virtues do not result from the exercise of its own reason. This was Rousseau's opinion respecting men: I extend it to women, and confidently assert that they have been drawn out of their sphere by false refinement, and not by an endeavour to acquire masculine qualities. Still the regal homage which they receive is so intoxicating, that, till the manners of the times are changed, and formed on more reasonable principles, it may be impossible to convince them that the illegitimate power, which they obtain by degrading themselves, is a curse, and that they must return to nature and equality, if they wish to secure the placid satisfaction that unsophisticated affections impart. But for this epoch we must wait--wait, perhaps, till kings and nobles, enlightened by reason, and, preferring the real dignity of man to childish state, throw off their gaudy hereditary trappings; and if then women do not resign the arbitrary power of beauty, they will prove that they have LESS mind than man. I may be accused of arrogance; still I must declare, what I firmly believe, that all the writers who have written on the subject of female education and manners, from Rousseau to Dr. Gregory, have contributed to render women more artificial, weaker characters, than they would otherwise have been; and, consequently, more useless members of society. I might have expressed this conviction in a lower key; but I am afraid it would have been the whine of affectation, and not the faithful expression of my feelings, of the clear result, which experience and reflection have led me to draw. When I come to that division of the subject, I shall advert to the passages that I more particularly disapprove of, in the works of the authors I have just alluded to; but it is first necessary to observe, that my objection extends to the whole purport of those books, which tend, in my opinion, to degrade one half of the human species, and render women pleasing at the expense of every solid virtue.
danishChanges.after: Den mest fuldkomne opdragelse er derfor efter min mening den træning af forstanden, som bedst styrker kroppen og former hjertet, eller med andre ord sætter det enkelte menneske i stand til at tilegne sig dydige vaner, der gør det uafhængigt. Det er faktisk en farce at kalde et væsen dydigt, hvis dets dyder ikke udspringer af brugen af dets egen fornuft. Det mente Rousseau om mænd; jeg udvider det til kvinder og hævder med sikkerhed, at det er falsk forfinelse, ikke forsøget på at tilegne sig mandlige egenskaber, der har trukket dem bort fra deres rette område. Men den kongelige hyldest, de modtager, er så berusende, at det måske er umuligt at overbevise dem, før tidens omgangsformer ændres og bygges på mere fornuftige principper. De må indse, at den uretmæssige magt, de opnår ved at nedværdige sig selv, er en forbandelse, og at de må vende tilbage til natur og lighed, hvis de vil sikre sig den rolige tilfredshed, ufordærvede følelser giver. Men på denne tid må vi vente — måske vente, indtil konger og adelige, oplyst af fornuften og med forkærlighed for menneskets sande værdighed frem for barnlig pragt, kaster deres skrigende arvelige pynt af sig. Hvis kvinder så ikke opgiver skønhedens vilkårlige magt, vil de bevise, at de har MINDRE forstand end mænd. Man kan beskylde mig for hovmod; alligevel må jeg erklære min faste overbevisning om, at alle, som har skrevet om kvinders opdragelse og levevis, fra Rousseau til dr. Gregory, har bidraget til at gøre kvinder til mere kunstige og svagere karakterer, end de ellers ville have været, og dermed til mere unyttige samfundsmedlemmer. Jeg kunne have udtrykt denne overbevisning mere afdæmpet, men jeg er bange for, at det ville have været påtaget klynkeri, ikke et troværdigt udtryk for mine følelser og den klare slutning, erfaring og eftertanke har ført mig til. Når jeg kommer til denne del af emnet, vil jeg pege på de passager i de nævnte forfatteres værker, som jeg særlig tager afstand fra. Men først må jeg bemærke, at min indvending gælder hele hensigten med disse bøger. Efter min mening nedværdiger de halvdelen af menneskeheden og gør kvinder behagelige på bekostning af enhver solid dyd.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Though to reason on Rousseau's ground, if man did attain a degree of perfection of mind when his body arrived at maturity, it might be proper in order to make a man and his wife ONE, that she should rely entirely on his understanding; and the graceful ivy, clasping the oak that supported it, would form a whole in which strength and beauty would be equally conspicuous. But, alas! husbands, as well as their helpmates, are often only overgrown children; nay, thanks to early debauchery, scarcely men in their outward form, and if the blind lead the blind, one need not come from heaven to tell us the consequence.
danishChanges.after: Ræsonnerer man dog ud fra Rousseaus forudsætninger, kunne det være passende, at hustruen helt støttede sig til mandens forstand, hvis han virkelig nåede en vis åndelig fuldkommenhed, når hans krop blev voksen, så mand og kone kunne blive ÉT. Den yndefulde vedbend, som slynger sig om den støttende eg, ville da danne en helhed, hvor styrke og skønhed trådte lige tydeligt frem. Men ak, ægtemænd er ligesom deres livsledsagere ofte blot forvoksede børn; takket være tidlige udskejelser er de endda knap mænd i deres ydre skikkelse. Og hvis blinde leder blinde, behøver ingen komme ned fra himlen for at fortælle os, hvad følgerne bliver.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Many are the causes that, in the present corrupt state of society, contribute to enslave women by cramping their understandings and sharpening their senses. One, perhaps, that silently does more mischief than all the rest, is their disregard of order.
danishChanges.after: I samfundets nuværende fordærvede tilstand er der mange årsager til, at kvinder gøres til slaver ved at få deres forstand hæmmet og deres sanser skærpet. En af dem, som måske i stilhed gør større skade end alle de andre, er deres manglende sans for orden.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To do every thing in an orderly manner, is a most important precept, which women, who, generally speaking, receive only a disorderly kind of education, seldom attend to with that degree of exactness that men, who from their infancy are broken into method, observe. This negligent kind of guesswork, for what other epithet can be used to point out the random exertions of a sort of instinctive common sense, never brought to the test of reason? prevents their generalizing matters of fact, so they do to-day, what they did yesterday, merely because they did it yesterday.
danishChanges.after: At gøre alt på en ordnet måde er en meget vigtig regel. Men kvinder, som i almindelighed kun får en usammenhængende opdragelse, følger den sjældent med samme nøjagtighed som mænd, der fra barndommen vænnes til systematik. Dette sjuskede gætteri — for hvad andet skal man kalde de tilfældige forsøg med en slags instinktiv sund fornuft, som aldrig prøves ved hjælp af egentlig fornuft? — forhindrer dem i at udlede generelle sammenhænge af kendsgerninger. Derfor gør de i dag, hvad de gjorde i går, blot fordi de gjorde det i går.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This contempt of the understanding in early life has more baneful consequences than is commonly supposed; for the little knowledge which women of strong minds attain, is, from various circumstances, of a more desultory kind than the knowledge of men, and it is acquired more by sheer observations on real life, than from comparing what has been individually observed with the results of experience generalized by speculation. Led by their dependent situation and domestic employments more into society, what they learn is rather by snatches; and as learning is with them, in general, only a secondary thing, they do not pursue any one branch with that persevering ardour necessary to give vigour to the faculties, and clearness to the judgment. In the present state of society, a little learning is required to support the character of a gentleman; and boys are obliged to submit to a few years of discipline. But in the education of women the cultivation of the understanding is always subordinate to the acquirement of some corporeal accomplishment; even while enervated by confinement and false notions of modesty, the body is prevented from attaining that grace and beauty which relaxed half-formed limbs never exhibit. Besides, in youth their faculties are not brought forward by emulation; and having no serious scientific study, if they have natural sagacity it is turned too soon on life and manners. They dwell on effects, and modifications, without tracing them back to causes; and complicated rules to adjust behaviour are a weak substitute for simple principles.
danishChanges.after: Denne tilsidesættelse af forstanden tidligt i livet har mere skadelige følger, end man almindeligvis tror. Den smule viden, som kvinder med stærke sind opnår, bliver af forskellige grunde mere spredt end mænds viden og tilegnes mere gennem rene iagttagelser af det virkelige liv end ved at sammenholde egne iagttagelser med de generelle resultater, eftertanken drager af erfaringen. Deres afhængige stilling og huslige gøremål fører dem mere ud i selskabeligt samvær, og de lærer derfor i brudstykker. Og da læring i almindelighed kun er en biting for dem, forfølger de ikke et enkelt fag med den vedholdende iver, som skal til for at styrke evnerne og gøre dømmekraften klar. I samfundets nuværende tilstand kræves der en smule lærdom for at kunne gælde som gentleman, og drenge må underkaste sig nogle års disciplin. Men i kvinders opdragelse står udviklingen af forstanden altid under tilegnelsen af en eller anden kropslig færdighed. Samtidig svækkes kroppen af indespærring og falske forestillinger om blufærdighed og hindres i at opnå den ynde og skønhed, som slappe, halvt udviklede lemmer aldrig viser. Desuden udvikles deres evner ikke gennem kappestrid i ungdommen. Og da de ikke beskæftiger sig alvorligt med noget videnskabeligt fag, rettes deres naturlige skarpsindighed, hvis de har den, for tidligt mod livet og omgangsformerne. De dvæler ved virkninger og variationer uden at føre dem tilbage til årsagerne, og indviklede regler for opførsel er en svag erstatning for enkle principper.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: As a proof that education gives this appearance of weakness to females, we may instance the example of military men, who are, like them, sent into the world before their minds have been stored with knowledge or fortified by principles. The consequences are similar; soldiers acquire a little superficial knowledge, snatched from the muddy current of conversation, and, from continually mixing with society, they gain, what is termed a knowledge of the world; and this acquaintance with manners and customs has frequently been confounded with a knowledge of the human heart. But can the crude fruit of casual observation, never brought to the test of judgment, formed by comparing speculation and experience, deserve such a distinction? Soldiers, as well as women, practice the minor virtues with punctilious politeness. Where is then the sexual difference, when the education has been the same; all the difference that I can discern, arises from the superior advantage of liberty which enables the former to see more of life.
danishChanges.after: Som bevis på, at det er opdragelsen, der giver kvinder dette præg af svaghed, kan vi pege på militærfolk. Ligesom kvinder sendes de ud i verden, før deres sind er fyldt med kundskaber eller styrket af principper. Følgerne ligner hinanden: Soldater tilegner sig lidt overfladisk viden, opsnappet fra samtalens grumsede strøm, og gennem stadig selskabelig omgang opnår de det, man kalder verdenskendskab. Dette kendskab til skikke og omgangsformer er ofte blevet forvekslet med kendskab til menneskehjertet. Men fortjener den umodne frugt af tilfældige iagttagelser, som aldrig prøves af en dømmekraft udviklet gennem sammenligning af tanke og erfaring, sådan en betegnelse? Soldater udøver ligesom kvinder de mindre dyder med omhyggelig høflighed. Hvor er kønsforskellen så, når opdragelsen har været den samme? Den eneste forskel, jeg kan se, udspringer af soldaternes større frihed, som giver dem mulighed for at se mere af livet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is wandering from my present subject, perhaps, to make a political remark; but as it was produced naturally by the train of my reflections, I shall not pass it silently over.
danishChanges.after: Det er måske en afstikker fra mit nuværende emne at komme med en politisk bemærkning, men da den opstod naturligt af mine overvejelser, vil jeg ikke gå tavst hen over den.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Standing armies can never consist of resolute, robust men; they may be well disciplined machines, but they will seldom contain men under the influence of strong passions or with very vigorous faculties. And as for any depth of understanding, I will venture to affirm, that it is as rarely to be found in the army as amongst women; and the cause, I maintain, is the same. It may be further observed, that officers are also particularly attentive to their persons, fond of dancing, crowded rooms, adventures, and ridicule. Like the FAIR sex, the business of their lives is gallantry. They were taught to please, and they only live to please. Yet they do not lose their rank in the distinction of sexes, for they are still reckoned superior to women, though in what their superiority consists, beyond what I have just mentioned, it is difficult to discover.
danishChanges.after: Stående hære kan aldrig bestå af beslutsomme, robuste mænd. De kan være veldisciplinerede maskiner, men de vil sjældent rumme mænd med stærke lidenskaber eller meget kraftfulde evner. Og hvad dyb forståelse angår, tør jeg hævde, at den findes lige så sjældent i hæren som blandt kvinder, og årsagen er efter min mening den samme. Man kan desuden bemærke, at officerer er særlig optaget af deres udseende og holder af dans, fyldte selskabslokaler, eventyr og spot. Ligesom det SMUKKE køn gør de kurmageri til deres livs beskæftigelse. De blev oplært til at behage, og de lever kun for at behage. Alligevel mister de ikke deres rang i kønnenes hierarki, for de regnes stadig for kvinder overlegne, skønt det er svært at se, hvori overlegenheden består ud over det, jeg netop har nævnt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The great misfortune is this, that they both acquire manners before morals, and a knowledge of life before they have from reflection, any acquaintance with the grand ideal outline of human nature. The consequence is natural; satisfied with common nature, they become a prey to prejudices, and taking all their opinions on credit, they blindly submit to authority. So that if they have any sense, it is a kind of instinctive glance, that catches proportions, and decides with respect to manners; but fails when arguments are to be pursued below the surface, or opinions analyzed.
danishChanges.after: Den store ulykke er, at begge grupper lærer omgangsformer før moral og får kendskab til livet, før eftertanken har givet dem nogen forståelse af menneskenaturens store ideale grundtræk. Følgen er naturlig: De stiller sig tilfredse med mennesket, som det almindeligvis er, bliver bytte for fordomme og underkaster sig blindt autoriteten, fordi de overtager alle deres meninger uden selv at prøve dem. Hvis de har forstand, viser den sig derfor som et instinktivt blik, der opfatter forhold og træffer afgørelser om omgangsformer, men svigter, når argumenter skal følges under overfladen, eller meninger analyseres.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: May not the same remark be applied to women? Nay, the argument may be carried still further, for they are both thrown out of a useful station by the unnatural distinctions established in civilized life. Riches and hereditary honours have made cyphers of women to give consequence to the numerical figure; and idleness has produced a mixture of gallantry and despotism in society, which leads the very men who are the slaves of their mistresses, to tyrannize over their sisters, wives, and daughters. This is only keeping them in rank and file, it is true. Strengthen the female mind by enlarging it, and there will be an end to blind obedience; but, as blind obedience is ever sought for by power, tyrants and sensualists are in the right when they endeavour to keep women in the dark, because the former only want slaves, and the latter a play-thing. The sensualist, indeed, has been the most dangerous of tyrants, and women have been duped by their lovers, as princes by their ministers, whilst dreaming that they reigned over them.
danishChanges.after: Kan den samme bemærkning ikke gælde kvinder? Ja, argumentet kan føres endnu videre, for begge grupper bliver trængt bort fra en nyttig plads af de unaturlige skel, som er indført i det civiliserede liv. Rigdom og arvelige æresbevisninger har gjort kvinder til nuller, der skal give tallet foran større værdi. Og lediggang har skabt en blanding af galanteri og despoti i samfundet, som får netop de mænd, der er deres elskerinders slaver, til at tyrannisere deres søstre, hustruer og døtre. Det er ganske vist blot at holde dem på geled. Styrk kvindens sind ved at udvide det, og den blinde lydighed vil ophøre. Men fordi magten altid søger blind lydighed, handler tyranner og nydelsessøgere i overensstemmelse med deres interesser, når de holder kvinder i mørke: De første ønsker kun slaver, de sidste et stykke legetøj. Nydelsessøgeren har faktisk været den farligste tyran, og kvinder er blevet bedraget af deres elskere, ligesom fyrster af deres ministre, mens de drømte, at de herskede over dem.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I now principally allude to Rousseau, for his character of Sophia is, undoubtedly, a captivating one, though it appears to me grossly unnatural; however, it is not the superstructure, but the foundation of her character, the principles on which her education was built, that I mean to attack; nay, warmly as I admire the genius of that able writer, whose opinions I shall often have occasion to cite, indignation always takes place of admiration, and the rigid frown of insulted virtue effaces the smile of complacency, which his eloquent periods are wont to raise, when I read his voluptuous reveries. Is this the man, who, in his ardour for virtue, would banish all the soft arts of peace, and almost carry us back to Spartan discipline? Is this the man who delights to paint the useful struggles of passion, the triumphs of good dispositions, and the heroic flights which carry the glowing soul out of itself? How are these mighty sentiments lowered when he describes the prettyfoot and enticing airs of his little favourite! But, for the present, I waive the subject, and, instead of severely reprehending the transient effusions of overweening sensibility, I shall only observe, that whoever has cast a benevolent eye on society, must often have been gratified by the sight of humble mutual love, not dignified by sentiment, nor strengthened by a union in intellectual pursuits. The domestic trifles of the day have afforded matter for cheerful converse, and innocent caresses have softened toils which did not require great exercise of mind, or stretch of thought: yet, has not the sight of this moderate felicity excited more tenderness than respect? An emotion similar to what we feel when children are playing, or animals sporting, whilst the contemplation of the noble struggles of suffering merit has raised admiration, and carried our thoughts to that world where sensation will give place to reason.
danishChanges.after: Jeg tænker nu især på Rousseau, for hans skildring af Sophie er uden tvivl fængslende, selv om den forekommer mig groft unaturlig. Men det er ikke overbygningen, jeg vil angribe; det er grundlaget for hendes karakter, de principper, hendes opdragelse bygger på. Hvor varmt jeg end beundrer denne dygtige forfatters geni — hans meninger får jeg ofte anledning til at citere — afløses beundringen altid af harme, når jeg læser hans vellystige drømmerier. Den krænkede dyds strenge panderynken udsletter det tilfredse smil, hans veltalende sætninger ellers fremkalder. Er det denne mand, som i sin iver for dyden vil fordrive alle fredens blide kunster og næsten føre os tilbage til spartansk disciplin? Er det ham, som elsker at skildre lidenskabens nyttige kampe, gode anlægs sejre og de heroiske flugter, der løfter den glødende sjæl ud over sig selv? Hvor synker disse mægtige følelser ikke, når han beskriver sin lille yndlings kønne fod og tillokkende manerer! Men foreløbig lægger jeg emnet til side. I stedet for strengt at revse en overdreven følsomheds flygtige udgydelser vil jeg blot bemærke, at enhver, som har betragtet samfundet med et velvilligt blik, ofte må have glædet sig ved synet af beskeden, gensidig kærlighed, som hverken ophøjes af ædle følelser eller styrkes af fælles intellektuelle interesser. Dagens små huslige begivenheder har givet stof til munter samtale, og uskyldige kærtegn har mildnet et slid, som ikke krævede store åndelige anstrengelser eller vidtrækkende tanker. Men har synet af denne beskedne lykke ikke vakt mere ømhed end respekt? En følelse, der ligner den, vi får ved at se børn lege eller dyr boltre sig, mens synet af fortjenstfulde menneskers ædle kamp under lidelse har vakt beundring og ført vores tanker til den verden, hvor sansningen skal vige for fornuften.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women are, therefore, to be considered either as moral beings, or so weak that they must be entirely subjected to the superior faculties of men.
danishChanges.after: Kvinder må derfor betragtes enten som moralske væsener eller som så svage, at de helt må underordnes mænds overlegne evner.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Let us examine this question. Rousseau declares, that a woman should never, for a moment feel herself independent, that she should be governed by fear to exercise her NATURAL cunning, and made a coquetish slave in order to render her a more alluring object of desire, a SWEETER companion to man, whenever he chooses to relax himself. He carries the arguments, which he pretends to draw from the indications of nature, still further, and insinuates that truth and fortitude the corner stones of all human virtue, shall be cultivated with certain restrictions, because with respect to the female character, obedience is the grand lesson which ought to be impressed with unrelenting rigour.
danishChanges.after: Lad os undersøge spørgsmålet. Rousseau erklærer, at en kvinde aldrig et øjeblik bør føle sig uafhængig, at hun bør styres af frygt til at bruge sin NATURLIGE list og gøres til en koket slave, så hun bliver en mere tillokkende genstand for begær og en SØDERE ledsager for manden, når han ønsker at slappe af. Han fører de argumenter, som han hævder at udlede af naturens tegn, endnu videre og antyder, at sandfærdighed og standhaftighed, hjørnestenene i al menneskelig dyd, skal udvikles med visse begrænsninger. For når det gælder kvindens karakter, er lydighed den store lektie, der bør indprentes med ubøjelig strenghed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: What nonsense! When will a great man arise with sufficient strength of mind to puff away the fumes which pride and sensuality have thus spread over the subject! If women are by nature inferior to men, their virtues must be the same in quality, if not in degree, or virtue is a relative idea; consequently, their conduct should be founded on the same principles, and have the same aim.
danishChanges.after: Hvilket vrøvl! Hvornår vil der komme et stort menneske med åndelig styrke nok til at blæse de dampe bort, som stolthed og sanselighed har spredt over emnet? Hvis kvinder af natur er mænd underlegne, må deres dyder stadig være af samme art, om ikke af samme grad; ellers er dyd et relativt begreb. Deres adfærd bør derfor bygge på de samme principper og have det samme mål.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Connected with man as daughters, wives, and mothers, their moral character may be estimated by their manner of fulfilling those simple duties; but the end, the grand end of their exertions should be to unfold their own faculties, and acquire the dignity of conscious virtue. They may try to render their road pleasant; but ought never to forget, in common with man, that life yields not the felicity which can satisfy an immortal soul. I do not mean to insinuate, that either sex should be so lost, in abstract reflections or distant views, as to forget the affections and duties that lie before them, and are, in truth, the means appointed to produce the fruit of life; on the contrary, I would warmly recommend them, even while I assert, that they afford most satisfaction when they are considered in their true subordinate light.
danishChanges.after: Som døtre, hustruer og mødre er kvinder knyttet til mænd, og deres moralske karakter kan vurderes ud fra måden, de opfylder disse enkle pligter på. Men målet, det store mål for deres bestræbelser, bør være at udfolde deres egne evner og opnå den værdighed, som bevidst dyd giver. De må gerne forsøge at gøre deres vej behagelig, men ligesom mænd bør de aldrig glemme, at livet ikke giver den lykke, som kan tilfredsstille en udødelig sjæl. Jeg vil ikke antyde, at noget af kønnene bør fortabe sig så meget i abstrakte overvejelser eller fjerne udsigter, at de glemmer de nære følelser og pligter, som i sandhed er de midler, der skal frembringe livets frugt. Tværtimod vil jeg varmt anbefale dem, selv mens jeg fastholder, at de giver størst tilfredsstillelse, når de ses i deres rette, underordnede lys.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Probably the prevailing opinion, that woman was created for man, may have taken its rise from Moses's poetical story; yet, as very few it is presumed, who have bestowed any serious thought on the subject, ever supposed that Eve was, literally speaking, one of Adam's ribs, the deduction must be allowed to fall to the ground; or, only be so far admitted as it proves that man, from the remotest antiquity, found it convenient to exert his strength to subjugate his companion, and his invention to show that she ought to have her neck bent under the yoke; because she as well as the brute creation, was created to do his pleasure.
danishChanges.after: Den udbredte opfattelse af, at kvinden blev skabt for mandens skyld, stammer måske fra Moses’ digteriske fortælling. Men da næppe ret mange, som har tænkt alvorligt over emnet, nogensinde har troet, at Eva bogstaveligt var et af Adams ribben, må denne slutning falde bort. Eller den kan kun accepteres som bevis på, at manden fra den fjerneste oldtid fandt det bekvemt at bruge sin styrke til at underkue sin ledsager og sin opfindsomhed til at vise, at hun burde bøje nakken under åget, fordi hun ligesom dyrene var skabt til at føje ham.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Let it not be concluded, that I wish to invert the order of things; I have already granted, that, from the constitution of their bodies, men seem to be designed by Providence to attain a greater degree of virtue. I speak collectively of the whole sex; but I see not the shadow of a reason to conclude that their virtues should differ in respect to their nature. In fact, how can they, if virtue has only one eternal standard? I must, therefore, if I reason consequentially, as strenuously maintain, that they have the same simple direction, as that there is a God.
danishChanges.after: Man må ikke slutte, at jeg vil vende tingenes orden på hovedet. Jeg har allerede indrømmet, at mænd på grund af deres kropslige indretning synes bestemt af forsynet til at opnå en højere grad af dyd. Jeg taler om kønnet som helhed, men jeg ser ikke skyggen af en grund til at slutte, at deres dyder skulle være forskellige af art. Hvordan skulle de være det, hvis dyden kun har én evig målestok? Vil jeg ræsonnere konsekvent, må jeg derfor lige så bestemt fastholde, at begge køns dyder har samme enkle retning, som at der findes en Gud.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It follows then, that cunning should not be opposed to wisdom, little cares to great exertions, nor insipid softness, varnished over with the name of gentleness, to that fortitude which grand views alone can inspire.
danishChanges.after: Heraf følger, at list ikke bør sættes op imod visdom, små bekymringer imod store anstrengelser eller indholdsløs blødhed, ferniseret med navnet mildhed, imod den standhaftighed, som kun store perspektiver kan indgyde.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I shall be told, that woman would then lose many of her peculiar graces, and the opinion of a well known poet might be quoted to refute my unqualified assertions. For Pope has said, in the name of the whole male sex,
danishChanges.after: Man vil sige til mig, at kvinden så ville miste mange af sine særlige ynder, og måske citere en kendt digter for at tilbagevise mine ubetingede påstande. For Pope har sagt på hele det mandlige køns vegne:
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "Yet ne'er so sure our passions to create, As when she touch'd the brink of all we hate."
danishChanges.after:
»Aldrig vækker hun sikrere vores lidenskab,
end når hun strejfer grænsen til alt det, vi hader.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In what light this sally places men and women, I shall leave to the judicious to determine; meanwhile I shall content myself with observing, that I cannot discover why, unless they are mortal, females should always be degraded by being made subservient to love or lust.
danishChanges.after: Hvilket lys denne vittighed stiller mænd og kvinder i, vil jeg overlade til den dømmekraftige læser at afgøre. Foreløbig vil jeg nøjes med at bemærke, at jeg ikke kan se, hvorfor kvinder, medmindre de kun er dødelige væsener, altid skal nedværdiges ved at underordnes kærlighed eller begær.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To speak disrespectfully of love is, I know, high treason against sentiment and fine feelings; but I wish to speak the simple language of truth, and rather to address the head than the heart. To endeavour to reason love out of the world, would be to out Quixote Cervantes, and equally offend against common sense; but an endeavour to restrain this tumultuous passion, and to prove that it should not be allowed to dethrone superior powers, or to usurp the sceptre which the understanding should ever coolly wield, appears less wild.
danishChanges.after: At tale respektløst om kærligheden er, ved jeg, højforræderi mod følsomheden og de fine følelser. Men jeg ønsker at tale sandhedens enkle sprog og henvende mig mere til hovedet end til hjertet. At forsøge at ræsonnere kærligheden ud af verden ville være at overgå Cervantes i donquixoteri og lige så meget stride mod den sunde fornuft. Mindre vildt forekommer det dog at søge at tøjle denne stormfulde lidenskab og vise, at den ikke bør have lov til at styrte højere evner fra tronen eller tilrane sig det scepter, som forstanden altid bør føre roligt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Youth is the season for love in both sexes; but in those days of thoughtless enjoyment, provision should be made for the more important years of life, when reflection takes place of sensation. But Rousseau, and most of the male writers who have followed his steps, have warmly inculcated that the whole tendency of female education ought to be directed to one point to render them pleasing.
danishChanges.after: Ungdommen er kærlighedens tid for begge køn. Men i disse dage med tankeløs nydelse bør man forberede sig på livets vigtigere år, hvor eftertanken træder i sanseoplevelsens sted. Rousseau og de fleste mandlige forfattere, som har fulgt i hans spor, har imidlertid ivrigt indprentet, at hele kvindens opdragelse bør rettes mod ét mål: at gøre hende behagelig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Let me reason with the supporters of this opinion, who have any knowledge of human nature, do they imagine that marriage can eradicate the habitude of life? The woman who has only been taught to please, will soon find that her charms are oblique sun-beams, and that they cannot have much effect on her husband's heart when they are seen every day, when the summer is past and gone. Will she then have sufficient native energy to look into herself for comfort, and cultivate her dormant faculties? or, is it not more rational to expect, that she will try to please other men; and, in the emotions raised by the expectation of new conquests, endeavour to forget the mortification her love or pride has received? When the husband ceases to be a lover--and the time will inevitably come, her desire of pleasing will then grow languid, or become a spring of bitterness; and love, perhaps, the most evanescent of all passions, gives place to jealousy or vanity.
danishChanges.after: Lad mig ræsonnere med de tilhængere af denne opfattelse, som kender noget til menneskets natur. Forestiller de sig, at ægteskabet kan udrydde et helt livs vaner? Den kvinde, som kun har lært at behage, vil snart opdage, at hendes charme er som skrå solstråler og ikke kan virke stærkt på mandens hjerte, når han ser den hver dag, når sommeren er forbi. Vil hun så have tilstrækkelig medfødt kraft til at søge trøst i sig selv og udvikle sine slumrende evner? Eller er det ikke mere rimeligt at vente, at hun prøver at behage andre mænd og i forventningen om nye erobringer søger at glemme den krænkelse, hendes kærlighed eller stolthed har lidt? Når ægtemanden holder op med at være elsker — og den tid kommer uundgåeligt — vil hendes ønske om at behage enten sygne hen eller blive en kilde til bitterhed. Og kærligheden, måske den flygtigste af alle lidenskaber, giver plads for jalousi eller forfængelighed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I now speak of women who are restrained by principle or prejudice; such women though they would shrink from an intrigue with real abhorrence, yet, nevertheless, wish to be convinced by the homage of gallantry, that they are cruelly neglected by their husbands; or, days and weeks are spent in dreaming of the happiness enjoyed by congenial souls, till the health is undermined and the spirits broken by discontent. How then can the great art of pleasing be such a necessary study? it is only useful to a mistress; the chaste wife, and serious mother, should only consider her power to please as the polish of her virtues, and the affection of her husband as one of the comforts that render her task less difficult, and her life happier. But, whether she be loved or neglected, her first wish should be to make herself respectable, and not rely for all her happiness on a being subject to like infirmities with herself.
danishChanges.after: Jeg taler nu om kvinder, som holdes tilbage af principper eller fordomme. Selv om de ville vige tilbage fra en affære med oprigtig afsky, ønsker de alligevel gennem kurmageriets hyldest at blive bekræftet i, at deres ægtemænd grusomt forsømmer dem. Eller de tilbringer dage og uger med at drømme om den lykke, beslægtede sjæle nyder, indtil utilfredsheden undergraver helbredet og knækker livsmodet. Hvordan kan den store kunst at behage så være et så nødvendigt studium? Den er kun nyttig for en elskerinde. Den kyske hustru og alvorlige mor bør blot betragte sin evne til at behage som glansen på sine dyder og mandens hengivenhed som en af de glæder, der letter hendes opgave og gør hendes liv lykkeligere. Men hvad enten hun bliver elsket eller forsømt, bør hendes første ønske være at gøre sig fortjent til agtelse og ikke bygge hele sin lykke på et væsen, som er underlagt de samme svagheder som hun selv.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The amiable Dr. Gregory fell into a similar error. I respect his heart; but entirely disapprove of his celebrated Legacy to his Daughters.
danishChanges.after: Den elskværdige dr. Gregory begik en lignende fejl. Jeg respekterer hans gode hjerte, men tager fuldstændig afstand fra hans berømte Arv til mine døtre.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: He advises them to cultivate a fondness for dress, because a fondness for dress, he asserts, is natural to them. I am unable to comprehend what either he or Rousseau mean, when they frequently use this indefinite term. If they told us, that in a pre-existent state the soul was fond of dress, and brought this inclination with it into a new body, I should listen to them with a half smile, as I often do when I hear a rant about innate elegance. But if he only meant to say that the exercise of the faculties will produce this fondness, I deny it. It is not natural; but arises, like false ambition in men, from a love of power.
danishChanges.after: Han råder dem til at dyrke glæden ved pynt, fordi den efter hans påstand er naturlig for dem. Jeg kan ikke forstå, hvad hverken han eller Rousseau mener, når de så ofte bruger dette ubestemte ord. Hvis de fortalte os, at sjælen i en tidligere tilværelse havde holdt af pynt og bragt denne tilbøjelighed med sig ind i en ny krop, ville jeg lytte med et halvt smil, som jeg ofte gør, når jeg hører svulstig tale om medfødt elegance. Men hvis han blot mener, at brugen af evnerne frembringer denne forkærlighed, benægter jeg det. Den er ikke naturlig, men udspringer ligesom mænds falske ambition af kærlighed til magt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Dr. Gregory goes much further; he actually recommends dissimulation, and advises an innocent girl to give the lie to her feelings, and not dance with spirit, when gaiety of heart would make her feet eloquent, without making her gestures immodest. In the name of truth and common sense, why should not one woman acknowledge that she can take more exercise than another? or, in other words, that she has a sound constitution; and why to damp innocent vivacity, is she darkly to be told, that men will draw conclusions which she little thinks of? Let the libertine draw what inference he pleases; but, I hope, that no sensible mother will restrain the natural frankness of youth, by instilling such indecent cautions. Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh; and a wiser than Solomon hath said, that the heart should be made clean, and not trivial ceremonies observed, which it is not very difficult to fulfill with scrupulous exactness when vice reigns in the heart.
danishChanges.after: Dr. Gregory går langt videre. Han anbefaler ligefrem forstillelse og råder en uskyldig pige til at lyve om sine følelser og lade være med at danse livligt, når hjertets glæde ellers ville gøre fødderne veltalende uden at gøre bevægelserne uanstændige. I sandhedens og den sunde fornufts navn: Hvorfor skulle en kvinde ikke indrømme, at hun kan tåle mere fysisk udfoldelse end en anden, eller med andre ord at hun har et godt helbred? Og hvorfor skal hendes uskyldige livlighed dæmpes med dunkle antydninger om, at mænd vil drage slutninger, hun ikke selv forestiller sig? Lad den udsvævende mand slutte, hvad han vil. Jeg håber blot, at ingen fornuftig mor vil hæmme ungdommens naturlige åbenhed ved at indprente sådanne uanstændige forsigtighedsregler. Hvad hjertet er fuldt af, løber munden over med; og en, der var visere end Salomon, har sagt, at hjertet skal gøres rent, ikke at man skal overholde ubetydelige ceremonier, som det ikke er svært at udføre med pinlig nøjagtighed, selv når lasten hersker i hjertet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women ought to endeavour to purify their hearts; but can they do so when their uncultivated understandings make them entirely dependent on their senses for employment and amusement, when no noble pursuit sets them above the little vanities of the day, or enables them to curb the wild emotions that agitate a reed over which every passing breeze has power? To gain the affections of a virtuous man, is affectation necessary?
danishChanges.after: Kvinder bør søge at rense deres hjerter. Men kan de det, når deres uudviklede forstand gør dem helt afhængige af sanserne for beskæftigelse og underholdning, når ingen ædel stræben løfter dem over dagens små forfængeligheder eller gør dem i stand til at tøjle de vilde følelser, der ryster et siv, som enhver forbipasserende brise har magt over? Er forstillelse nødvendig for at vinde en dydig mands hengivenhed?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Nature has given woman a weaker frame than man; but, to ensure her husband's affections, must a wife, who, by the exercise of her mind and body, whilst she was discharging the duties of a daughter, wife, and mother, has allowed her constitution to retain its natural strength, and her nerves a healthy tone, is she, I say, to condescend, to use art, and feign a sickly delicacy, in order to secure her husband's affection? Weakness may excite tenderness, and gratify the arrogant pride of man; but the lordly caresses of a protector will not gratify a noble mind that pants for and deserves to be respected. Fondness is a poor substitute for friendship!
danishChanges.after: Naturen har givet kvinden en svagere krop end manden. Men skal en hustru, som gennem brug af både sind og krop, samtidig med at hun opfyldte sine pligter som datter, hustru og mor, har bevaret sin naturlige styrke og sunde nerver, virkelig nedlade sig til kneb og foregive en sygelig sarthed for at sikre sig mandens kærlighed? Svaghed kan vække ømhed og tilfredsstille mandens hovmodige stolthed, men en beskytters overlegne kærtegn vil ikke tilfredsstille et ædelt sind, som længes efter og fortjener respekt. Kæleri er en ringe erstatning for venskab!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In a seraglio, I grant, that all these arts are necessary; the epicure must have his palate tickled, or he will sink into apathy; but have women so little ambition as to be satisfied with such a condition? Can they supinely dream life away in the lap of pleasure, or in the languor of weariness, rather than assert their claim to pursue reasonable pleasures, and render themselves conspicuous, by practising the virtues which dignify mankind? Surely she has not an immortal soul who can loiter life away, merely employed to adorn her person, that she may amuse the languid hours, and soften the cares of a fellow-creature who is willing to be enlivened by her smiles and tricks, when the serious business of life is over.
danishChanges.after: I et harem er alle disse kunster nødvendige, indrømmer jeg. Nydelsesmenneskets gane må kildres, ellers synker han hen i sløvhed. Men har kvinder så lidt ambition, at de vil stille sig tilfredse med den tilstand? Kan de passivt drømme livet bort i nydelsens skød eller i træthedens mathed frem for at hævde deres ret til fornuftige glæder og gøre sig bemærkede ved at øve de dyder, der giver menneskeheden værdighed? Hun kan vel ikke have en udødelig sjæl, hvis hun kan drive livet bort og kun beskæftige sig med at pynte sig, så hun kan underholde et medmenneskes træge timer og mildne hans bekymringer, når han efter livets alvorlige arbejde lader sig oplive af hendes smil og kunster.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, the woman who strengthens her body and exercises her mind will, by managing her family and practising various virtues, become the friend, and not the humble dependent of her husband; and if she deserves his regard by possessing such substantial qualities, she will not find it necessary to conceal her affection, nor to pretend to an unnatural coldness of constitution to excite her husband's passions. In fact, if we revert to history, we shall find that the women who have distinguished themselves have neither been the most beautiful nor the most gentle of their sex.
danishChanges.after: Desuden vil den kvinde, som styrker sin krop og bruger sit sind, gennem ledelsen af familien og udøvelsen af forskellige dyder blive sin mands ven, ikke hans ydmygt afhængige. Og hvis hun fortjener hans agtelse gennem sådanne solide egenskaber, vil hun ikke behøve at skjule sin hengivenhed eller foregive en unaturlig følelseskulde for at vække hans lidenskab. Ser vi tilbage på historien, finder vi faktisk, at de kvinder, der har udmærket sig, hverken har været deres køns smukkeste eller mildeste.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Nature, or to speak with strict propriety God, has made all things right; but man has sought him out many inventions to mar the work. I now allude to that part of Dr. Gregory's treatise, where he advises a wife never to let her husband know the extent of her sensibility or affection. Voluptuous precaution; and as ineffectual as absurd. Love, from its very nature, must be transitory. To seek for a secret that would render it constant, would be as wild a search as for the philosopher's stone, or the grand panacea; and the discovery would be equally useless, or rather pernicious to mankind. The most holy band of society is friendship. It has been well said, by a shrewd satirist, "that rare as true love is, true friendship is still rarer."
danishChanges.after: Naturen, eller helt præcist Gud, har skabt alt godt, men mennesket har udtænkt mange påfund, som ødelægger værket. Jeg tænker nu på den del af dr. Gregorys afhandling, hvor han råder en hustru til aldrig at lade sin mand vide, hvor dyb hendes følsomhed eller hengivenhed er. En vellystig forsigtighedsregel, lige så virkningsløs som absurd. Kærlighedens lidenskab må i kraft af sin natur være forbigående. At lede efter en hemmelighed, der kunne gøre den varig, ville være lige så vild en jagt som efter de vises sten eller et middel mod alle sygdomme; og opdagelsen ville være lige så unyttig, eller snarere skadelig, for menneskeheden. Samfundets helligste bånd er venskabet. En skarpsindig satiriker har med rette sagt, »at hvor sjælden sand kærlighed end er, er sandt venskab endnu sjældnere«.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This is an obvious truth, and the cause not lying deep, will not elude a slight glance of inquiry.
danishChanges.after: Det er en indlysende sandhed, og da årsagen ikke ligger dybt, vil selv en kort undersøgelse kunne afdække den.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Love, the common passion, in which chance and sensation take place of choice and reason, is in some degree, felt by the mass of mankind; for it is not necessary to speak, at present, of the emotions that rise above or sink below love. This passion, naturally increased by suspense and difficulties, draws the mind out of its accustomed state, and exalts the affections; but the security of marriage, allowing the fever of love to subside, a healthy temperature is thought insipid, only by those who have not sufficient intellect to substitute the calm tenderness of friendship, the confidence of respect, instead of blind admiration, and the sensual emotions of fondness.
danishChanges.after: Kærlighed, den almindelige lidenskab, hvor tilfældighed og sansning træder i valgets og fornuftens sted, mærkes i nogen grad af de fleste mennesker. Her behøver vi ikke tale om de følelser, der hæver sig over eller synker under kærligheden. Denne lidenskab, som naturligt vokser gennem uvished og vanskeligheder, løfter sindet ud af dets vante tilstand og højner følelserne. Men når ægteskabets tryghed lader forelskelsens feber falde, virker den sunde temperatur kun kedelig på dem, der ikke har ånd nok til at sætte venskabets rolige ømhed og respektens tillid i stedet for blind beundring og kæleriets sanselige følelser.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This is, must be, the course of nature--friendship or indifference inevitably succeeds love. And this constitution seems perfectly to harmonize with the system of government which prevails in the moral world. Passions are spurs to action, and open the mind; but they sink into mere appetites, become a personal momentary gratification, when the object is gained, and the satisfied mind rests in enjoyment. The man who had some virtue whilst he was struggling for a crown, often becomes a voluptuous tyrant when it graces his brow; and, when the lover is not lost in the husband, the dotard a prey to childish caprices, and fond jealousies, neglects the serious duties of life, and the caresses which should excite confidence in his children are lavished on the overgrown child, his wife.
danishChanges.after: Sådan er og må naturens gang være: Venskab eller ligegyldighed følger uundgåeligt efter forelskelsen. Denne indretning synes at stemme fuldstændig med den orden, som hersker i den moralske verden. Lidenskaber ansporer til handling og åbner sindet, men de synker til rene drifter og bliver en personlig, kortvarig tilfredsstillelse, når målet er nået, og det tilfredse sind hviler i nydelsen. Den mand, som havde en vis dyd, mens han kæmpede for en krone, bliver ofte en nydelsessyg tyran, når den pryder hans pande. Og når elskeren ikke går op i ægtemanden, forsømmer den blinde tilbeder livets alvorlige pligter, prisgivet barnlige luner og øm jalousi, mens de kærtegn, der skulle skabe tillid hos hans børn, ødsles på det forvoksede barn, hans hustru.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In order to fulfil the duties of life, and to be able to pursue with vigour the various employments which form the moral character, a master and mistress of a family ought not to continue to love each other with passion. I mean to say, that they ought not to indulge those emotions which disturb the order of society, and engross the thoughts that should be otherwise employed. The mind that has never been engrossed by one object wants vigour--if it can long be so, it is weak.
danishChanges.after: For at opfylde livets pligter og med kraft kunne udføre de forskellige opgaver, som former den moralske karakter, bør en families mand og kvinde ikke blive ved med at elske hinanden lidenskabeligt. Jeg mener, at de ikke bør hengive sig til følelser, som forstyrrer samfundets orden og opsluger tanker, der burde bruges anderledes. Det sind, som aldrig har været helt optaget af én ting, mangler kraft; kan det blive ved med at være det længe, er det svagt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A mistaken education, a narrow, uncultivated mind, and many sexual prejudices, tend to make women more constant than men; but, for the present, I shall not touch on this branch of the subject. I will go still further, and advance, without dreaming of a paradox, that an unhappy marriage is often very advantageous to a family, and that the neglected wife is, in general, the best mother. And this would almost always be the consequence, if the female mind was more enlarged; for, it seems to be the common dispensation of Providence, that what we gain in present enjoyment should be deducted from the treasure of life, experience; and that when we are gathering the flowers of the day and revelling in pleasure, the solid fruit of toil and wisdom should not be caught at the same time. The way lies before us, we must turn to the right or left; and he who will pass life away in bounding from one pleasure to another, must not complain if he neither acquires wisdom nor respectability of character.
danishChanges.after: En fejlagtig opdragelse, et snævert, uudviklet sind og mange kønsfordomme gør kvinder mere vedholdende i kærlighed end mænd, men foreløbig vil jeg ikke berøre denne del af emnet. Jeg vil gå endnu videre og uden at ville opstille et paradoks hævde, at et ulykkeligt ægteskab ofte er meget gavnligt for familien, og at den forsømte hustru i almindelighed er den bedste mor. Sådan ville det næsten altid gå, hvis kvindens sind var mere udviklet. For forsynets almindelige ordning synes at være, at det, vi vinder i øjeblikkelig nydelse, må trækkes fra livets skat, erfaringen; og når vi plukker dagens blomster og svælger i fornøjelse, kan vi ikke samtidig høste slidets og visdommens faste frugt. Vejen ligger foran os; vi må dreje til højre eller venstre. Den, som vil tilbringe livet med at springe fra den ene fornøjelse til den anden, må ikke klage, hvis han hverken opnår visdom eller en agtværdig karakter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Supposing for a moment, that the soul is not immortal, and that man was only created for the present scene; I think we should have reason to complain that love, infantine fondness, ever grew insipid and palled upon the sense. Let us eat, drink, and love, for to-morrow we die, would be in fact the language of reason, the morality of life; and who but a fool would part with a reality for a fleeting shadow? But, if awed by observing the improvable powers of the mind, we disdain to confine our wishes or thoughts to such a comparatively mean field of action; that only appears grand and important as it is connected with a boundless prospect and sublime hopes; what necessity is there for falsehood in conduct, and why must the sacred majesty of truth be violated to detain a deceitful good that saps the very foundation of virtue?
