Why must the female mind be tainted by coquetish arts to gratify the sensualist, and prevent love from subsiding into friendship or compassionate tenderness, when there are not qualities on which friendship can be built? Let the honest heart show itself, and REASON teach passion to submit to necessity; or, let the dignified pursuit of virtue and knowledge raise the mind above those emotions which rather imbitter than sweeten the cup of life, when they are not restrained within due bounds.
danishChanges.after: Antager vi et øjeblik, at sjælen ikke er udødelig, og at mennesket kun blev skabt til denne tilværelse, mener jeg, at vi havde grund til at beklage, at kærligheden, den barnlige ømhed, nogensinde blev kedelig og mistede sin tiltrækning for sanserne. »Lad os spise, drikke og elske, for i morgen dør vi« ville da virkelig være fornuftens sprog og livets moral. Og hvem andre end en tåbe ville opgive noget virkeligt for en flygtig skygge? Men hvis sindets evne til at udvikle sig fylder os med ærefrygt, og vi derfor ikke vil begrænse vores ønsker og tanker til et så forholdsvis ringe virkefelt — som kun virker stort og vigtigt i kraft af forbindelsen til grænseløse udsigter og ophøjede håb — hvorfor er falskhed i vores adfærd så nødvendig? Hvorfor skal sandhedens hellige majestæt krænkes for at fastholde et bedragerisk gode, som undergraver selve dydens grundlag? Hvorfor skal kvindens sind besmittes af koketteriets kunster for at tilfredsstille nydelsessøgeren og hindre kærligheden i at falde til ro som venskab eller som medfølende ømhed, hvis der ikke findes egenskaber at bygge et venskab på? Lad det ærlige hjerte vise sig, og lad FORNUFTEN lære lidenskaben at bøje sig for nødvendigheden. Eller lad den værdige stræben efter dyd og kundskab løfte sindet over de følelser, som snarere gør livets bæger bittert end sødt, når de ikke holdes inden for rimelige grænser.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I do not mean to allude to the romantic passion, which is the concomitant of genius. Who can clip its wings? But that grand passion not proportioned to the puny enjoyments of life, is only true to the sentiment, and feeds on itself. The passions which have been celebrated for their durability have always been unfortunate. They have acquired strength by absence and constitutional melancholy. The fancy has hovered round a form of beauty dimly seen--but familiarity might have turned admiration into disgust; or, at least, into indifference, and allowed the imagination leisure to start fresh game. With perfect propriety, according to this view of things, does Rousseau make the mistress of his soul, Eloisa, love St. Preux, when life was fading before her; but this is no proof of the immortality of the passion.
danishChanges.after: Jeg tænker ikke på den romantiske lidenskab, som ledsager geniet. Hvem kan stække dens vinger? Men denne store lidenskab, som ikke står i forhold til livets små glæder, er kun tro mod selve følelsen og næres af sig selv. De lidenskaber, man har berømmet for deres varighed, har altid været ulykkelige. De er vokset gennem fravær og en medfødt melankoli. Fantasien har svævet om en skønhedsskikkelse, kun dunkelt set; men fortrolighed kunne have forvandlet beundring til væmmelse eller i det mindste ligegyldighed og givet fantasien tid til at jage nyt vildt. Ud fra dette syn på sagen lader Rousseau med fuld ret sin sjæls elskerinde, Héloïse, elske Saint-Preux, mens livet svinder for hende. Men det beviser ikke lidenskabens udødelighed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Of the same complexion is Dr. Gregory's advice respecting delicacy of sentiment, which he advises a woman not to acquire, if she has determined to marry. This determination, however, perfectly consistent with his former advice, he calls INDELICATE, and earnestly persuades his daughters to conceal it, though it may govern their conduct: as if it were indelicate to have the common appetites of human nature.
danishChanges.after: Af samme slags er dr. Gregorys råd om følelsernes finhed, som han fraråder en kvinde at udvikle, hvis hun har besluttet at gifte sig. Denne beslutning, som ellers stemmer fuldstændig med hans tidligere råd, kalder han dog UANSTÆNDIG og opfordrer indtrængende sine døtre til at skjule, selv om den gerne må styre deres adfærd — som om det var uanstændigt at have menneskenaturens almindelige drifter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Noble morality! and consistent with the cautious prudence of a little soul that cannot extend its views beyond the present minute division of existence. If all the faculties of woman's mind are only to be cultivated as they respect her dependence on man; if, when she obtains a husband she has arrived at her goal, and meanly proud, is satisfied with such a paltry crown, let her grovel contentedly, scarcely raised by her employments above the animal kingdom; but, if she is struggling for the prize of her high calling, let her cultivate her understanding without stopping to consider what character the husband may have whom she is destined to marry. Let her only determine, without being too anxious about present happiness, to acquire the qualities that ennoble a rational being, and a rough, inelegant husband may shock her taste without destroying her peace of mind. She will not model her soul to suit the frailties of her companion, but to bear with them: his character may be a trial, but not an impediment to virtue.
danishChanges.after: Ædel moral! Og helt i tråd med en lille sjæls forsigtige klogskab, som ikke kan se ud over dette lille udsnit af tilværelsen. Hvis alle kvindens åndsevner kun skal udvikles med henblik på hendes afhængighed af manden; hvis hun har nået sit mål, når hun har fået en ægtemand, og småligt stolt stiller sig tilfreds med så ussel en krone, så lad hende krybe tilfreds omkring, af sine beskæftigelser knap hævet over dyreriget. Men hvis hun kæmper for sit høje kalds pris, så lad hende udvikle sin forstand uden at standse op og overveje, hvilken karakter den mand har, som hun er bestemt til at gifte sig med. Lad hende blot beslutte at tilegne sig de egenskaber, der forædler et fornuftsvæsen, uden overdreven bekymring for den øjeblikkelige lykke. Så kan en rå og ufølsom mand krænke hendes smag uden at ødelægge hendes indre ro. Hun vil ikke forme sin sjæl efter sin ledsagers svagheder, men til at bære over med dem. Hans karakter kan være en prøvelse, men ikke en hindring for dyden.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: If Dr. Gregory confined his remark to romantic expectations of constant love and congenial feelings, he should have recollected, that experience will banish what advice can never make us cease to wish for, when the imagination is kept alive at the expence of reason.
danishChanges.after: Hvis dr. Gregory kun mente romantiske forventninger om vedvarende forelskelse og beslægtede følelser, burde han have husket, at erfaringen vil fordrive det, som råd aldrig kan få os til at holde op med at ønske, når fantasien næres på fornuftens bekostning.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I own it frequently happens, that women who have fostered a romantic unnatural delicacy of feeling, waste their lives in IMAGINING how happy they should have been with a husband who could love them with a fervid increasing affection every day, and all day. But they might as well pine married as single, and would not be a jot more unhappy with a bad husband than longing for a good one. That a proper education; or, to speak with more precision, a well stored mind, would enable a woman to support a single life with dignity, I grant; but that she should avoid cultivating her taste, lest her husband should occasionally shock it, is quitting a substance for a shadow. To say the truth, I do not know of what use is an improved taste, if the individual be not rendered more independent of the casualties of life; if new sources of enjoyment, only dependent on the solitary operations of the mind, are not opened. People of taste, married or single, without distinction, will ever be disgusted by various things that touch not less observing minds. On this conclusion the argument must not be allowed to hinge; but in the whole sum of enjoyment is taste to be denominated a blessing?
danishChanges.after: Jeg indrømmer, at kvinder, som har næret en romantisk, unaturlig følelsessarthed, ofte spilder livet på at FORESTILLE SIG, hvor lykkelige de ville have været med en mand, som kunne elske dem med en brændende, stadig voksende hengivenhed hver dag og hele dagen. Men de kan lige så godt længes som gifte som ugifte og ville ikke være en smule mere ulykkelige med en dårlig mand end ved at længes efter en god. Jeg indrømmer, at en ordentlig uddannelse, eller mere præcist et sind rigt på indhold, ville gøre en kvinde i stand til at leve ugift med værdighed. Men at hun skulle undlade at udvikle sin smag af frygt for, at hendes mand lejlighedsvis kunne støde den, er at opgive noget virkeligt for en skygge. Sandt at sige ved jeg ikke, hvad en udviklet smag skal gøre gavn for, hvis den ikke gør mennesket mere uafhængigt af livets tilfældigheder og åbner nye kilder til glæde, som kun afhænger af sindets eget arbejde. Mennesker med smag, gifte som ugifte, vil altid stødes af forskellige ting, som ikke berører mindre opmærksomme sind. Argumentet må ikke afgøres af den konstatering. Spørgsmålet er, om smagen samlet set er en velsignelse for livets glæde.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The question is, whether it procures most pain or pleasure? The answer will decide the propriety of Dr. Gregory's advice, and show how absurd and tyrannic it is thus to lay down a system of slavery; or to attempt to educate moral beings by any other rules than those deduced from pure reason, which apply to the whole species.
danishChanges.after: Spørgsmålet er, om den giver mest smerte eller nydelse. Svaret afgør, om dr. Gregorys råd er rigtigt, og viser, hvor absurd og tyrannisk det er at opstille et sådant slaverisystem eller forsøge at opdrage moralske væsener efter andre regler end dem, der udledes af den rene fornuft og gælder hele menneskeheden.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Gentleness of manners, forbearance, and long suffering, are such amiable godlike qualities, that in sublime poetic strains the Deity has been invested with them; and, perhaps, no representation of his goodness so strongly fastens on the human affections as those that represent him abundant in mercy and willing to pardon. Gentleness, considered in this point of view, bears on its front all the characteristics of grandeur, combined with the winning graces of condescension; but what a different aspect it assumes when it is the submissive demeanour of dependence, the support of weakness that loves, because it wants protection; and is forbearing, because it must silently endure injuries; smiling under the lash at which it dare not snarl. Abject as this picture appears, it is the portrait of an accomplished woman, according to the received opinion of female excellence, separated by specious reasoners from human excellence. Or, they (Vide Rousseau, and Swedenborg) kindly restore the rib, and make one moral being of a man and woman; not forgetting to give her all the "submissive charms."
danishChanges.after: Mildhed i optræden, overbærenhed og langmodighed er så elskværdige, guddommelige egenskaber, at man i ophøjet digtning har tillagt Gud dem. Måske er der ingen fremstilling af hans godhed, som griber menneskets følelser stærkere, end den, der viser ham rig på barmhjertighed og villig til at tilgive. Set sådan bærer mildheden alle storhedens kendetegn, forenet med den vindende ynde hos den, der venligt bøjer sig ned mod andre. Men hvor anderledes ser den ud, når den er afhængighedens underdanige optræden, støtten for en svaghed, som elsker, fordi den behøver beskyttelse, og er overbærende, fordi den tavst må udholde krænkelser, smilende under pisken, som den ikke vover at knurre ad. Hvor ynkeligt billedet end er, er det portrættet af en velopdragen kvinde efter den gængse opfattelse af kvindelig fortræffelighed, som besnærende tænkere skiller fra menneskelig fortræffelighed. Eller også sætter de venligt ribbenet tilbage — se Rousseau og Swedenborg — og gør mand og kvinde til ét moralsk væsen, uden at glemme at give hende al den »underdanige ynde«.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: How women are to exist in that state where there is to be neither marrying nor giving in marriage, we are not told. For though moralists have agreed, that the tenor of life seems to prove that MAN is prepared by various circumstances for a future state, they constantly concur in advising WOMAN only to provide for the present. Gentleness, docility, and a spaniel-like affection are, on this ground, consistently recommended as the cardinal virtues of the sex; and, disregarding the arbitrary economy of nature, one writer has declared that it is masculine for a woman to be melancholy. She was created to be the toy of man, his rattle, and it must jingle in his ears, whenever, dismissing reason, he chooses to be amused.
danishChanges.after: Hvordan kvinder skal eksistere i den tilstand, hvor man hverken gifter sig eller bliver gift bort, får vi ikke at vide. For selv om moralisterne er enige om, at livets forløb synes at vise, at MANDEN gennem forskellige omstændigheder forberedes til en fremtidig tilværelse, er de til stadighed enige om at råde KVINDEN til kun at sørge for nutiden. På det grundlag anbefales mildhed, føjelighed og en spaniels hundeagtige hengivenhed konsekvent som kønnets hoveddyder. Og uden hensyn til naturens egenrådige indretning har en forfatter erklæret, at det er mandhaftigt af en kvinde at være tungsindig. Hun blev skabt som mandens legetøj, hans rangle, og den skal rasle i hans ører, hver gang han lægger fornuften fra sig og ønsker underholdning.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To recommend gentleness, indeed, on a broad basis is strictly philosophical. A frail being should labour to be gentle. But when forbearance confounds right and wrong, it ceases to be a virtue; and, however convenient it may be found in a companion, that companion will ever be considered as an inferior, and only inspire a vapid tenderness, which easily degenerates into contempt. Still, if advice could really make a being gentle, whose natural disposition admitted not of such a fine polish, something toward the advancement of order would be attained; but if, as might quickly be demonstrated, only affectation be produced by this indiscriminate counsel, which throws a stumbling block in the way of gradual improvement, and true melioration of temper, the sex is not much benefited by sacrificing solid virtues to the attainment of superficial graces, though for a few years they may procure the individual's regal sway.
danishChanges.after: At anbefale mildhed på et bredt grundlag er ganske vist fuldt filosofisk. Et skrøbeligt væsen bør arbejde på at blive mildt. Men når overbærenhed udvisker forskellen mellem ret og uret, holder den op med at være en dyd. Hvor bekvem den end er hos en ledsager, vil denne ledsager altid blive betragtet som underlegen og kun vække en indholdsløs ømhed, der let bliver til foragt. Hvis råd virkelig kunne gøre et væsen mildt, selv om dets naturlige sindelag ikke tillod så fin en polering, ville man dog have vundet noget for ordenens fremme. Men hvis disse råd, som gives uden skelnen, kun frembringer forstillelse — hvad der hurtigt kunne bevises — og dermed står i vejen for gradvis udvikling og virkelig forbedring af sindelaget, har kønnet ikke megen gavn af at ofre solide dyder for overfladisk ynde, selv om den i nogle år kan skaffe den enkelte kvinde kongelig magt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: As a philosopher, I read with indignation the plausible epithets which men use to soften their insults; and, as a moralist, I ask what is meant by such heterogeneous associations, as fair defects, amiable weaknesses, etc.? If there is but one criterion of morals, but one archetype for man, women appear to be suspended by destiny, according to the vulgar tale of Mahomet's coffin; they have neither the unerring instinct of brutes, nor are allowed to fix the eye of reason on a perfect model. They were made to be loved, and must not aim at respect, lest they should be hunted out of society as masculine.
danishChanges.after: Som filosof læser jeg med harme de besnærende betegnelser, mænd bruger til at mildne deres fornærmelser; og som moralist spørger jeg, hvad der menes med så uforenelige sammenstillinger som smukke fejl, elskværdige svagheder og så videre. Hvis der kun findes én moralsk målestok og ét forbillede for mennesket, synes skæbnen at have hængt kvinderne frit i luften, ligesom i den folkelige fortælling om Muhammeds kiste. De har hverken dyrenes usvigelige instinkt eller lov til at rette fornuftens blik mod et fuldkomment forbillede. De blev skabt til at blive elsket og må ikke stræbe efter respekt, for så bliver de jaget ud af samfundet som mandhaftige.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But to view the subject in another point of view. Do passive indolent women make the best wives? Confining our discussion to the present moment of existence, let us see how such weak creatures perform their part? Do the women who, by the attainment of a few superficial accomplishments, have strengthened the prevailing prejudice, merely contribute to the happiness of their husbands? Do they display their charms merely to amuse them? And have women, who have early imbibed notions of passive obedience, sufficient character to manage a family or educate children? So far from it, that, after surveying the history of woman, I cannot help agreeing with the severest satirist, considering the sex as the weakest as well as the most oppressed half of the species. What does history disclose but marks of inferiority, and how few women have emancipated themselves from the galling yoke of sovereign man? So few, that the exceptions remind me of an ingenious conjecture respecting Newton: that he was probably a being of a superior order, accidentally caged in a human body. In the same style I have been led to imagine that the few extraordinary women who have rushed in eccentrical directions out of the orbit prescribed to their sex, were MALE spirits, confined by mistake in a female frame. But if it be not philosophical to think of sex when the soul is mentioned, the inferiority must depend on the organs; or the heavenly fire, which is to ferment the clay, is not given in equal portions.
danishChanges.after: Men lad os se sagen fra en anden side. Er passive, dovne kvinder de bedste hustruer? Begrænser vi os til denne nuværende tilværelse, hvordan udfører sådanne svage væsener så deres opgave? Bidrager de kvinder, som ved at tilegne sig nogle få overfladiske færdigheder har styrket den herskende fordom, kun til deres mænds lykke? Viser de kun deres ynde for at underholde dem? Og har kvinder, der tidligt har optaget forestillinger om passiv lydighed, karakter nok til at lede en familie eller opdrage børn? Langtfra. Efter at have gennemgået kvindens historie kan jeg ikke lade være med at give den skarpeste satiriker ret, når han betragter kønnet som både menneskehedens svageste og mest undertrykte halvdel. Hvad viser historien andet end tegn på underlegenhed, og hvor få kvinder har ikke frigjort sig fra den herskende mands smertelige åg? Så få, at undtagelserne minder mig om en sindrig formodning om Newton: at han sandsynligvis var et væsen af højere orden, som ved et tilfælde var blevet fanget i en menneskekrop. På lignende vis er jeg blevet fristet til at forestille mig, at de få usædvanlige kvinder, som i afvigende retninger har sprængt den bane, deres køn fik foreskrevet, var MANDLIGE ånder, der ved en fejl var lukket inde i kvindekroppe. Men hvis det er ufilosofisk at tænke på køn, når man taler om sjælen, må underlegenheden bero på organerne; ellers gives den himmelske ild, der skal sætte leret i bevægelse, ikke i lige store portioner.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But avoiding, as I have hitherto done, any direct comparison of the two sexes collectively, or frankly acknowledging the inferiority of woman, according to the present appearance of things, I shall only insist, that men have increased that inferiority till women are almost sunk below the standard of rational creatures. Let their faculties have room to unfold, and their virtues to gain strength, and then determine where the whole sex must stand in the intellectual scale. Yet, let it be remembered, that for a small number of distinguished women I do not ask a place.
danishChanges.after: Men jeg vil som hidtil undgå en direkte sammenligning af de to køn som helheder, eller åbent indrømme kvindens underlegenhed, sådan som forholdene nu ser ud. Jeg vil kun fastholde, at mænd har forøget denne underlegenhed, indtil kvinder næsten er sunket under fornuftsvæsenernes niveau. Giv deres evner plads til at udfolde sig og deres dyder mulighed for at vokse i styrke, og afgør så, hvor hele kønnet skal stå på forstandens rangstige. Husk dog, at jeg ikke beder om en plads til et lille antal fremragende kvinder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is difficult for us purblind mortals to say to what height human discoveries and improvements may arrive, when the gloom of despotism subsides, which makes us stumble at every step; but, when morality shall be settled on a more solid basis, then, without being gifted with a prophetic spirit, I will venture to predict, that woman will be either the friend or slave of man. We shall not, as at present, doubt whether she is a moral agent, or the link which unites man with brutes. But, should it then appear, that like the brutes they were principally created for the use of man, he will let them patiently bite the bridle, and not mock them with empty praise; or, should their rationality be proved, he will not impede their improvement merely to gratify his sensual appetites. He will not with all the graces of rhetoric, advise them to submit implicitly their understandings to the guidance of man. He will not, when he treats of the education of women, assert, that they ought never to have the free use of reason, nor would he recommend cunning and dissimulation to beings who are acquiring, in like manner as himself, the virtues of humanity.
danishChanges.after: For os nærsynede dødelige er det svært at sige, hvor højt menneskets opdagelser og forbedringer kan nå, når despotiets mørke, som får os til at snuble ved hvert skridt, letter. Men når moralen hviler på et fastere grundlag, tør jeg uden nogen profetisk gave forudsige, at kvinden enten vil være mandens ven eller hans slave. Vi vil ikke som nu være i tvivl om, hvorvidt hun er et moralsk handlende væsen eller bindeleddet mellem mennesket og dyrene. Viser det sig da, at kvinder ligesom dyrene hovedsagelig blev skabt til mandens brug, vil han lade dem tålmodigt bide i bidslet og ikke håne dem med tom ros. Eller hvis deres fornuft bevises, vil han ikke hindre deres udvikling blot for at tilfredsstille sine sanselige drifter. Han vil ikke med al retorikkens ynde råde dem til ubetinget at underordne deres forstand under mandens ledelse. Når han behandler kvinders opdragelse, vil han ikke hævde, at de aldrig bør have fri brug af fornuften, og han vil heller ikke anbefale list og forstillelse til væsener, som ligesom han selv er ved at tilegne sig menneskehedens dyder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Surely there can be but one rule of right, if morality has an eternal foundation, and whoever sacrifices virtue, strictly so called, to present convenience, or whose DUTY it is to act in such a manner, lives only for the passing day, and cannot be an accountable creature.
danishChanges.after: Hvis moralen har et evigt grundlag, kan der vel kun være én regel for, hvad der er ret. Den, som ofrer dyd i egentlig forstand for øjeblikkelig bekvemmelighed, eller hvis PLIGT det er at handle sådan, lever kun for den flygtige dag og kan ikke være et væsen, der holdes ansvarligt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The poet then should have dropped his sneer when he says,
danishChanges.after: Digteren burde derfor have opgivet sin hån, når han siger:
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "If weak women go astray, The stars are more in fault than they."
danishChanges.after:
»Hvis svage kvinder farer vild,
har stjernerne større skyld end de.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: For that they are bound by the adamantine chain of destiny is most certain, if it be proved that they are never to exercise their own reason, never to be independent, never to rise above opinion, or to feel the dignity of a rational will that only bows to God, and often forgets that the universe contains any being but itself, and the model of perfection to which its ardent gaze is turned, to adore attributes that, softened into virtues, may be imitated in kind, though the degree overwhelms the enraptured mind.
danishChanges.after: For de er ganske sikkert bundet af skæbnens ubrydelige kæde, hvis det bevises, at de aldrig må bruge deres egen fornuft, aldrig være uafhængige, aldrig hæve sig over andres meninger eller føle værdigheden i en fornuftig vilje, som kun bøjer sig for Gud. En vilje, som ofte glemmer, at universet rummer andre væsener end den selv og det fuldkomne forbillede, dens brændende blik vender sig mod, for at tilbede egenskaber, der i mildere form som dyder kan efterlignes i art, selv om deres grad overvælder det henførte sind.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: If, I say, for I would not impress by declamation when reason offers her sober light, if they are really capable of acting like rational creatures, let them not be treated like slaves; or, like the brutes who are dependent on the reason of man, when they associate with him; but cultivate their minds, give them the salutary, sublime curb of principle, and let them attain conscious dignity by feeling themselves only dependent on God. Teach them, in common with man, to submit to necessity, instead of giving, to render them more pleasing, a sex to morals.
danishChanges.after: Hvis, siger jeg — for jeg vil ikke gøre indtryk med svulstige ord, når fornuften tilbyder sit nøgterne lys — hvis kvinder virkelig kan handle som fornuftsvæsener, så lad være med at behandle dem som slaver eller som dyr, der er afhængige af menneskets fornuft, når de lever sammen med det. Udvikl i stedet deres sind, giv dem princippernes gavnlige, ophøjede tøjle, og lad dem opnå bevidst værdighed ved kun at føle sig afhængige af Gud. Lær dem ligesom mænd at bøje sig for nødvendigheden i stedet for at give moralen et køn for at gøre dem mere behagelige.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Further, should experience prove that they cannot attain the same degree of strength of mind, perseverance and fortitude, let their virtues be the same in kind, though they may vainly struggle for the same degree; and the superiority of man will be equally clear, if not clearer; and truth, as it is a simple principle, which admits of no modification, would be common to both. Nay, the order of society, as it is at present regulated, would not be inverted, for woman would then only have the rank that reason assigned her, and arts could not be practised to bring the balance even, much less to turn it.
danishChanges.after: Og skulle erfaringen vise, at de ikke kan opnå samme åndelige styrke, udholdenhed og standhaftighed, så lad deres dyder være af samme art, selv om de forgæves stræber efter samme grad. Mandens overlegenhed vil da være lige så tydelig, om ikke tydeligere, og sandheden vil være fælles for begge, fordi den er et enkelt princip, som ikke tillader tilpasninger. Selv samfundsordenen, som den nu er indrettet, ville ikke blive vendt på hovedet, for kvinden ville da kun have den rang, fornuften tildelte hende, og man kunne ikke bruge kneb til at skabe ligevægt, endnu mindre til at forskyde den.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These may be termed Utopian dreams. Thanks to that Being who impressed them on my soul, and gave me sufficient strength of mind to dare to exert my own reason, till becoming dependent only on him for the support of my virtue, I view with indignation, the mistaken notions that enslave my sex.
danishChanges.after: Man kan kalde dette utopiske drømme. Tak til det væsen, som prægede dem i min sjæl og gav mig åndelig styrke nok til at vove at bruge min egen fornuft, indtil jeg kun blev afhængig af ham som støtte for min dyd og med harme kunne betragte de fejlagtige forestillinger, der gør mit køn til slaver.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I love man as my fellow; but his sceptre real or usurped, extends not to me, unless the reason of an individual demands my homage; and even then the submission is to reason, and not to man. In fact, the conduct of an accountable being must be regulated by the operations of its own reason; or on what foundation rests the throne of God?
danishChanges.after: Jeg elsker manden som mit medmenneske, men hans scepter, retmæssigt eller tilranet, rækker ikke over mig, medmindre det enkelte menneskes fornuft kræver min anerkendelse. Og selv da underkaster jeg mig fornuften, ikke manden. Et ansvarligt væsens adfærd må faktisk styres af dets egen fornufts arbejde; hvilket grundlag hviler Guds trone ellers på?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It appears to me necessary to dwell on these obvious truths, because females have been insulted, as it were; and while they have been stripped of the virtues that should clothe humanity, they have been decked with artificial graces, that enable them to exercise a short lived tyranny. Love, in their bosoms, taking place of every nobler passion, their sole ambition is to be fair, to raise emotion instead of inspiring respect; and this ignoble desire, like the servility in absolute monarchies, destroys all strength of character. Liberty is the mother of virtue, and if women are, by their very constitution, slaves, and not allowed to breathe the sharp invigorating air of freedom, they must ever languish like exotics, and be reckoned beautiful flaws in nature; let it also be remembered, that they are the only flaw.
danishChanges.after: Jeg finder det nødvendigt at dvæle ved disse indlysende sandheder, fordi kvinder så at sige er blevet krænket. Mens man har frataget dem de dyder, som burde klæde menneskeheden, har man pyntet dem med kunstig ynde, der gør det muligt at udøve et kortvarigt tyranni. Når kærligheden i deres hjerter fortrænger enhver ædlere lidenskab, bliver deres eneste ambition at være smukke, vække følelser frem for respekt. Og dette uædle ønske ødelægger, ligesom underdanigheden i enevældige monarkier, al karakterstyrke. Friheden er dydens mor. Hvis kvinder i kraft af selve deres indretning er slaver og ikke får lov til at indånde frihedens skarpe, styrkende luft, må de altid sygne hen som eksotiske planter og regnes for smukke fejl i naturen. Husk også, at de i så fald er den eneste fejl.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: As to the argument respecting the subjection in which the sex has ever been held, it retorts on man. The many have always been enthralled by the few; and, monsters who have scarcely shown any discernment of human excellence, have tyrannized over thousands of their fellow creatures. Why have men of superior endowments submitted to such degradation? For, is it not universally acknowledged that kings, viewed collectively, have ever been inferior, in abilities and virtue, to the same number of men taken from the common mass of mankind--yet, have they not, and are they not still treated with a degree of reverence, that is an insult to reason? China is not the only country where a living man has been made a God. MEN have submitted to superior strength, to enjoy with impunity the pleasure of the moment--WOMEN have only done the same, and therefore till it is proved that the courtier, who servilely resigns the birthright of a man, is not a moral agent, it cannot be demonstrated that woman is essentially inferior to man, because she has always been subjugated.
danishChanges.after: Hvad angår argumentet om, at kønnet altid har været holdt undertrykt, vender det sig mod manden selv. De mange har altid været trælbundet af de få, og uhyrer, som knap har vist nogen forståelse for menneskelig fortræffelighed, har tyranniseret tusinder af deres medmennesker. Hvorfor har mænd med overlegne evner underkastet sig sådan en nedværdigelse? Er det ikke almindeligt anerkendt, at konger som gruppe altid har været ringere i evner og dyd end et tilsvarende antal mænd udtaget af den øvrige menneskehed? Og er de alligevel ikke blevet og bliver de ikke stadig behandlet med en ærbødighed, som fornærmer fornuften? Kina er ikke det eneste land, hvor et levende menneske er blevet gjort til en Gud. MÆND har underkastet sig overlegen styrke for ustraffet at kunne nyde øjeblikkets glæder; KVINDER har blot gjort det samme. Derfor kan man ikke bevise, at kvinden i sit væsen er manden underlegen, fordi hun altid har været underkuet, før man har bevist, at hofmanden, som underdanigt opgiver sin medfødte menneskeret, ikke er et moralsk handlende væsen.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Brutal force has hitherto governed the world, and that the science of politics is in its infancy, is evident from philosophers scrupling to give the knowledge most useful to man that determinate distinction.
danishChanges.after: Rå magt har hidtil styret verden. Og at den politiske videnskab endnu er i sin barndom, ses af, at filosoffer tøver med at give den viden, der er nyttigst for mennesket, netop denne præcise betegnelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I shall not pursue this argument any further than to establish an obvious inference, that as sound politics diffuse liberty, mankind, including woman, will become more wise and virtuous.
danishChanges.after: Jeg vil ikke føre argumentet længere end til denne indlysende slutning: Efterhånden som en sund politik udbreder frihed, vil menneskeheden, kvinder indbefattet, blive klogere og mere dydig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Bodily strength from being the distinction of heroes is now sunk into such unmerited contempt, that men as well as women, seem to think it unnecessary: the latter, as it takes from their feminine graces, and from that lovely weakness, the source of their undue power; and the former, because it appears inimical with the character of a gentleman.
danishChanges.after: Fra at være heltenes særkende er fysisk styrke nu sunket i en så ufortjent foragt, at både mænd og kvinder synes at anse den for overflødig: kvinder, fordi den tager noget fra deres kvindelige ynde og den yndige svaghed, som er kilden til deres uretmæssige magt; mænd, fordi den synes uforenelig med en gentlemans væsen.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: That they have both by departing from one extreme run into another, may easily be proved; but it first may be proper to observe, that a vulgar error has obtained a degree of credit, which has given force to a false conclusion, in which an effect has been mistaken for a cause.
danishChanges.after: Det er let at vise, at begge køn er flygtet fra den ene yderlighed ind i den anden. Men først bør vi bemærke, at en almindelig fejltagelse har vundet så stor tiltro, at den har styrket en falsk slutning, hvor man forveksler virkning og årsag.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: People of genius have, very frequently, impaired their constitutions by study, or careless inattention to their health, and the violence of their passions bearing a proportion to the vigour of their intellects, the sword's destroying the scabbard has become almost proverbial, and superficial observers have inferred from thence, that men of genius have commonly weak, or to use a more fashionable phrase, delicate constitutions. Yet the contrary, I believe, will appear to be the fact; for, on diligent inquiry, I find that strength of mind has, in most cases, been accompanied by superior strength of body, natural soundness of constitution, not that robust tone of nerves and vigour of muscles, which arise from bodily labour, when the mind is quiescent, or only directs the hands.
danishChanges.after: Geniale mennesker har meget ofte svækket deres helbred gennem studier eller skødesløs forsømmelse af det. Og eftersom deres lidenskabers voldsomhed står i forhold til deres intellektuelle kraft, er det næsten blevet et ordsprog, at sværdet ødelægger skeden. Overfladiske iagttagere har deraf sluttet, at geniale mænd som regel har et svagt eller, med et mere moderne udtryk, sart helbred. Jeg tror dog, at det modsatte vil vise sig at være tilfældet. Ved grundig undersøgelse finder jeg, at åndelig styrke oftest har været ledsaget af usædvanlig kropslig styrke og et naturligt sundt helbred, ikke den robusthed i nerverne og kraft i musklerne, som fysisk arbejde skaber, når sindet hviler eller blot leder hænderne.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Dr. Priestley has remarked, in the preface to his biographical chart, that the majority of great men have lived beyond forty-five. And, considering the thoughtless manner in which they lavished their strength, when investigating a favourite science, they have wasted the lamp of life, forgetful of the midnight hour; or, when, lost in poetic dreams, fancy has peopled the scene, and the soul has been disturbed, till it shook the constitution, by the passions that meditation had raised; whose objects, the baseless fabric of a vision, faded before the exhausted eye, they must have had iron frames. Shakespeare never grasped the airy dagger with a nerveless hand, nor did Milton tremble when he led Satan far from the confines of his dreary prison. These were not the ravings of imbecility, the sickly effusions of distempered brains; but the exuberance of fancy, that "in a fine phrenzy" wandering, was not continually reminded of its material shackles.
danishChanges.after: Dr. Priestley bemærker i forordet til sin biografiske oversigt, at de fleste store mænd blev mere end femogfyrre år. Og når man tænker på, hvor tankeløst de ødslede med deres kræfter, må de have haft kroppe af jern. Optaget af deres yndlingsvidenskab brændte de livets lampe ned og glemte, at det var midnat. Eller de fortabte sig i digteriske drømme, mens fantasien befolkede scenen, og de lidenskaber, eftertanken havde vakt, bragte sjælen i en uro, som rystede kroppen; lidenskabernes genstande, et syns grundløse bygningsværk, blegnede så for det udmattede øje. Shakespeare greb aldrig luftdolken med en slap hånd, og Milton skælvede ikke, da han førte Satan langt bort fra sit dystre fængsels grænser. Det var ikke svaghedens vildelser eller syge hjerners usunde udgydelser, men fantasiens frodighed, som vandrede »i et skønt vanvid« uden hele tiden at blive mindet om sine materielle lænker.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I am aware, that this argument would carry me further than it may be supposed I wish to go; but I follow truth, and still adhering to my first position, I will allow that bodily strength seems to give man a natural superiority over woman; and this is the only solid basis on which the superiority of the sex can be built. But I still insist, that not only the virtue, but the KNOWLEDGE of the two sexes should be the same in nature, if not in degree, and that women, considered not only as moral, but rational creatures, ought to endeavour to acquire human virtues (or perfections) by the SAME means as men, instead of being educated like a fanciful kind of HALF being, one of Rousseau's wild chimeras.
danishChanges.after: Jeg er klar over, at dette argument fører mig længere, end man måske tror, jeg ønsker. Men jeg følger sandheden, og tro mod mit første standpunkt indrømmer jeg, at fysisk styrke synes at give manden en naturlig overlegenhed over kvinden. Det er det eneste solide grundlag, kønnets overlegenhed kan bygges på. Jeg fastholder dog stadig, at ikke kun de to køns dyd, men også deres VIDEN bør være af samme art, om ikke af samme grad. Kvinder bør betragtes som både moralske og fornuftige væsener og søge at tilegne sig menneskelige dyder eller fuldkommenheder med de SAMME midler som mænd, i stedet for at blive opdraget som en fantasifuld slags HALVT væsen, en af Rousseaus vilde kimærer.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, if strength of body be, with some show of reason, the boast of men, why are women so infatuated as to be proud of a defect? Rousseau has furnished them with a plausible excuse, which could only have occurred to a man, whose imagination had been allowed to run wild, and refine on the impressions made by exquisite senses, that they might, forsooth have a pretext for yielding to a natural appetite without violating a romantic species of modesty, which gratifies the pride and libertinism of man.
danishChanges.after: Men hvis mænd med en vis ret kan være stolte af deres kropsstyrke, hvorfor er kvinder så forblindede, at de er stolte af en mangel? Rousseau har givet dem en besnærende undskyldning, som kun kunne falde en mand ind, hvis fantasi havde fået lov at løbe løbsk og forfine indtrykkene fra udsøgte sanser: at de sandelig kunne få et påskud til at give efter for en naturlig drift uden at krænke en romantisk form for blufærdighed, som tilfredsstiller mandens stolthed og udsvævende tilbøjeligheder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women deluded by these sentiments, sometimes boast of their weakness, cunningly obtaining power by playing on the WEAKNESS of men; and they may well glory in their illicit sway, for, like Turkish bashaws, they have more real power than their masters: but virtue is sacrificed to temporary gratifications, and the respectability of life to the triumph of an hour.
danishChanges.after: Bedraget af disse forestillinger praler kvinder somme tider af deres svaghed og skaffer sig snedigt magt ved at spille på mændenes SVAGHED. Og de kan nok prale af deres uretmæssige herredømme, for ligesom tyrkiske pashaer har de mere virkelig magt end deres herrer. Men dyden ofres for kortvarige tilfredsstillelser, og et agtværdigt liv for en enkelt times triumf.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women, as well as despots, have now, perhaps, more power than they would have, if the world, divided and subdivided into kingdoms and families, was governed by laws deduced from the exercise of reason; but in obtaining it, to carry on the comparison, their character is degraded, and licentiousness spread through the whole aggregate of society. The many become pedestal to the few. I, therefore will venture to assert, that till women are more rationally educated, the progress of human virtue and improvement in knowledge must receive continual checks. And if it be granted, that woman was not created merely to gratify the appetite of man, nor to be the upper servant, who provides his meals and takes care of his linen, it must follow, that the first care of those mothers or fathers, who really attend to the education of females, should be, if not to strengthen the body, at least, not to destroy the constitution by mistaken notions of beauty and female excellence; nor should girls ever be allowed to imbibe the pernicious notion that a defect can, by any chemical process of reasoning become an excellence. In this respect, I am happy to find, that the author of one of the most instructive books, that our country has produced for children, coincides with me in opinion; I shall quote his pertinent remarks to give the force of his respectable authority to reason.*
danishChanges.after: Kvinder har måske nu, ligesom despoter, større magt, end de ville have, hvis verden, opdelt og underopdelt i riger og familier, blev styret af love udledt af fornuften. Men for at fortsætte sammenligningen: Ved at skaffe sig denne magt nedværdiges deres karakter, og tøjlesløshed spredes gennem hele samfundet. De mange bliver sokkel for de få. Derfor tør jeg hævde, at fremskridtet i menneskelig dyd og kundskab bestandig vil blive hæmmet, indtil kvinder får en mere fornuftig uddannelse. Og hvis man indrømmer, at kvinden ikke blot blev skabt til at tilfredsstille mandens begær eller være den øverste tjenestepige, som laver hans mad og passer hans linned, følger det, at de mødre og fædre, der virkelig tager pigers opdragelse alvorligt, først og fremmest må sørge for, om ikke at styrke kroppen, så i det mindste ikke at ødelægge helbredet gennem fejlagtige forestillinger om skønhed og kvindelig fortræffelighed. Piger bør heller aldrig få lov til at optage den skadelige forestilling, at en mangel gennem en slags tankens kemiske proces kan blive til et fortrin. Her glæder det mig at finde enighed hos forfatteren til en af de mest lærerige børnebøger, vores land har frembragt. Jeg vil citere hans relevante bemærkninger for at give fornuften støtte fra hans agtværdige autoritet.*
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: (*Footnote. A respectable old man gives the following sensible account of the method he pursued when educating his daughter. "I endeavoured to give both to her mind and body a degree of vigour, which is seldom found in the female sex. As soon as she was sufficiently advanced in strength to be capable of the lighter labours of husbandry and gardening, I employed her as my constant companion. Selene, for that was her name, soon acquired a dexterity in all these rustic employments which I considered with equal pleasure and admiration. If women are in general feeble both in body and mind, it arises less from nature than from education. We encourage a vicious indolence and inactivity, which we falsely call delicacy; instead of hardening their minds by the severer principles of reason and philosophy, we breed them to useless arts, which terminate in vanity and sensuality. In most of the countries which I had visited, they are taught nothing of an higher nature than a few modulations of the voice, or useless postures of the body; their time is consumed in sloth or trifles, and trifles become the only pursuits capable of interesting them. We seem to forget, that it is upon the qualities of the female sex, that our own domestic comforts and the education of our children must depend. And what are the comforts or the education which a race of beings corrupted from their infancy, and unacquainted with all the duties of life, are fitted to bestow? To touch a musical instrument with useless skill, to exhibit their natural or affected graces, to the eyes of indolent and debauched young men, who dissipate their husbands' patrimony in riotous and unnecessary expenses: these are the only arts cultivated by women in most of the polished nations I had seen. And the consequences are uniformly such as may be expected to proceed from such polluted sources, private misery, and public servitude.
danishChanges.after: (*Note. En agtværdig gammel mand giver denne fornuftige beskrivelse af, hvordan han opdragede sin datter: »Jeg søgte at give både hendes sind og hendes krop en styrke, som sjældent findes hos kvinder. Så snart hun var stærk nok til lettere arbejde i landbrug og have, gjorde jeg hende til min faste ledsager. Selene, for det hed hun, blev snart så dygtig til alle disse landlige sysler, at jeg betragtede det med lige stor glæde og beundring. Hvis kvinder i almindelighed er svage i både krop og sind, skyldes det mindre naturen end opdragelsen. Vi opmuntrer en skadelig dovenskab og passivitet, som vi fejlagtigt kalder sarthed. I stedet for at styrke deres sind med fornuftens og filosofiens strengere principper oplærer vi dem i unyttige kunster, som ender i forfængelighed og sanselighed. I de fleste lande, jeg havde besøgt, lærte de intet højere end nogle stemmevariationer eller unyttige kropsstillinger. Deres tid går med dovenskab eller bagateller, og bagateller bliver det eneste, der kan interessere dem. Vi synes at glemme, at vores eget hjemlige velbefindende og vores børns opdragelse afhænger af kvindekønnets egenskaber. Og hvilken trivsel eller opdragelse kan væsener, som er fordærvede fra barndommen og ukendte med alle livets pligter, give? At spille på et instrument med unyttig færdighed og vise deres naturlige eller påtagede ynde for dovne, udsvævende unge mænd, som ødsler deres ægtemænds arv bort på vilde og unødvendige udgifter: Det er de eneste kunster, kvinder dyrker i de fleste af de forfinede nationer, jeg har set. Og følgerne er overalt, hvad man kan vente af så forurenede kilder: privat elendighed og offentlig trældom.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "But, Selene's education was regulated by different views, and conducted upon severer principles; if that can be called severity which opens the mind to a sense of moral and religious duties, and most effectually arms it against the inevitable evils of life."--Mr. Day's "Sandford and Merton," Volume 3.)
danishChanges.after: »Men Selenes opdragelse blev styret af andre hensyn og gennemført efter strengere principper, hvis man da kan kalde det strengt at åbne sindet for moralske og religiøse pligter og mest virkningsfuldt ruste det mod livets uundgåelige onder.« — Hr. Days Sandford og Merton, bind 3.)
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But should it be proved that woman is naturally weaker than man, from whence does it follow that it is natural for her to labour to become still weaker than nature intended her to be? Arguments of this cast are an insult to common sense, and savour of passion. The DIVINE RIGHT of husbands, like the divine right of kings, may, it is to be hoped, in this enlightened age, be contested without danger, and though conviction may not silence many boisterous disputants, yet, when any prevailing prejudice is attacked, the wise will consider, and leave the narrow-minded to rail with thoughtless vehemence at innovation.
danishChanges.after: Men hvis det bevises, at kvinden af natur er svagere end manden, hvordan følger det så, at det er naturligt for hende at arbejde på at blive endnu svagere, end naturen bestemte? Argumenter af den slags fornærmer den sunde fornuft og lugter af lidenskab. Man må håbe, at ægtemænds GUDDOMMELIGE RET, ligesom kongers guddommelige ret, kan anfægtes uden fare i denne oplyste tidsalder. Og selv om overbevisende argumenter ikke vil bringe mange højtråbende debattører til tavshed, vil de kloge tænke efter, når en herskende fordom angribes, og overlade det til de snæversynede at rase tankeløst mod fornyelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The mother, who wishes to give true dignity of character to her daughter, must, regardless of the sneers of ignorance, proceed on a plan diametrically opposite to that which Rousseau has recommended with all the deluding charms of eloquence and philosophical sophistry: for his eloquence renders absurdities plausible, and his dogmatic conclusions puzzle, without convincing those who have not ability to refute them.
danishChanges.after: En mor, som ønsker at give sin datter sand karakterværdighed, må uden hensyn til uvidenhedens hån følge en plan, der er stik modsat den, Rousseau har anbefalet med alle veltalenhedens og de filosofiske skinargumenters bedrageriske fortrin. For hans veltalenhed får absurditeter til at lyde troværdige, og hans skråsikre slutninger forvirrer uden at overbevise dem, der ikke har evner til at tilbagevise dem.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Throughout the whole animal kingdom every young creature requires almost continual exercise, and the infancy of children, conformable to this intimation, should be passed in harmless gambols, that exercise the feet and hands, without requiring very minute direction from the head, or the constant attention of a nurse. In fact, the care necessary for self-preservation is the first natural exercise of the understanding, as little inventions to amuse the present moment unfold the imagination. But these wise designs of nature are counteracted by mistaken fondness or blind zeal. The child is not left a moment to its own direction, particularly a girl, and thus rendered dependent--dependence is called natural.
danishChanges.after: I hele dyreriget har unge væsener brug for næsten uafbrudt bevægelse. I overensstemmelse med dette tegn bør små børn tilbringe tiden med harmløs leg, som bruger fødder og hænder uden at kræve detaljeret styring fra hovedet eller en barnepiges konstante opmærksomhed. Den omsorg, der er nødvendig for at passe på sig selv, er faktisk forstandens første naturlige øvelse, ligesom små påfund, der underholder i øjeblikket, udvikler fantasien. Men naturens kloge hensigter modarbejdes af misforstået kærlighed eller blind iver. Barnet får ikke et øjeblik lov til selv at bestemme, især ikke pigen, og gøres dermed afhængigt — hvorefter afhængigheden kaldes naturlig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To preserve personal beauty, woman's glory! the limbs and faculties are cramped with worse than Chinese bands, and the sedentary life which they are condemned to live, whilst boys frolic in the open air, weakens the muscles and relaxes the nerves. As for Rousseau's remarks, which have since been echoed by several writers, that they have naturally, that is from their birth, independent of education, a fondness for dolls, dressing, and talking, they are so puerile as not to merit a serious refutation. That a girl, condemned to sit for hours together listening to the idle chat of weak nurses or to attend at her mother's toilet, will endeavour to join the conversation, is, indeed very natural; and that she will imitate her mother or aunts, and amuse herself by adorning her lifeless doll, as they do in dressing her, poor innocent babe! is undoubtedly a most natural consequence. For men of the greatest abilities have seldom had sufficient strength to rise above the surrounding atmosphere; and, if the page of genius has always been blurred by the prejudices of the age, some allowance should be made for a sex, who, like kings, always see things through a false medium.
danishChanges.after: For at bevare den personlige skønhed, kvindens hæder, indsnævres lemmer og evner af bånd, som er værre end de kinesiske. Det stillesiddende liv, piger dømmes til, mens drengene leger ude i det fri, svækker musklerne og gør nerverne slappe. Rousseaus bemærkninger, som flere forfattere siden har gentaget, om at piger naturligt, altså fra fødslen og uafhængigt af opdragelsen, holder af dukker, pynt og snak, er så barnlige, at de ikke fortjener en alvorlig gendrivelse. At en pige, som dømmes til i timevis at lytte til svage barnepigers tomme snak eller overvære sin mors påklædning, vil forsøge at deltage i samtalen, er ganske naturligt. Og at hun efterligner sin mor eller sine tanter og morer sig med at pynte sin livløse dukke, som de pynter hende, det stakkels uskyldige barn, er uden tvivl en helt naturlig følge. For selv mænd med de største evner har sjældent haft styrke nok til at hæve sig over deres omgivelser. Og når selv geniets skrifter altid er blevet plettet af tidens fordomme, må man vise en vis overbærenhed med et køn, der ligesom konger altid ser tingene gennem et forvrængende filter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In this manner may the fondness for dress, conspicuous in women, be easily accounted for, without supposing it the result of a desire to please the sex on which they are dependent. The absurdity, in short, of supposing that a girl is naturally a coquette, and that a desire connected with the impulse of nature to propagate the species, should appear even before an improper education has, by heating the imagination, called it forth prematurely, is so unphilosophical, that such a sagacious observer as Rousseau would not have adopted it, if he had not been accustomed to make reason give way to his desire of singularity, and truth to a favourite paradox.
danishChanges.after: Sådan kan man let forklare den tydelige forkærlighed for pynt hos kvinder uden at antage, at den skyldes ønsket om at behage det køn, de er afhængige af. Kort sagt er det absurd og ufilosofisk at antage, at en pige naturligt er koket, og at et ønske forbundet med naturens drift til at videreføre arten skulle vise sig, allerede før en forkert opdragelse har ophedet fantasien og vakt det for tidligt. En så skarpsindig iagttager som Rousseau ville ikke have antaget det, hvis han ikke havde været vant til at lade fornuften vige for ønsket om at være særpræget og sandheden for et yndlingsparadoks.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Yet thus to give a sex to mind was not very consistent with the principles of a man who argued so warmly, and so well, for the immortality of the soul. But what a weak barrier is truth when it stands in the way of an hypothesis! Rousseau respected--almost adored virtue--and yet allowed himself to love with sensual fondness. His imagination constantly prepared inflammable fuel for his inflammable senses; but, in order to reconcile his respect for self-denial, fortitude and those heroic virtues, which a mind like his could not coolly admire, he labours to invert the law of nature, and broaches a doctrine pregnant with mischief, and derogatory to the character of supreme wisdom.
danishChanges.after: Men at give sindet et køn på den måde stemte dårligt med principperne hos en mand, som så varmt og så godt argumenterede for sjælens udødelighed. Hvor er sandheden dog en svag barriere, når den står i vejen for en hypotese! Rousseau respekterede, næsten tilbad dyden, og alligevel tillod han sig at elske med sanselig ømhed. Hans fantasi lagde bestandig brændbart stof til hans letantændelige sanser. Men for at forene dette med sin respekt for selvfornægtelse, standhaftighed og de heroiske dyder, som et sind som hans ikke kunne beundre køligt, forsøger han at vende naturens lov på hovedet og fremsætter en lære, der er fuld af farlige følger og uværdig for den højeste visdom.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: His ridiculous stories, which tend to prove that girls are NATURALLY attentive to their persons, without laying any stress on daily example, are below contempt. And that a little miss should have such a correct taste as to neglect the pleasing amusement of making O's, merely because she perceived that it was an ungraceful attitude, should be selected with the anecdotes of the learned pig.*
danishChanges.after: Hans latterlige historier, som skal bevise, at piger NATURLIGT er optaget af deres udseende, uden at tillægge hverdagens eksempler betydning, fortjener ikke engang foragt. Og historien om den lille frøken, som havde så sikker en smag, at hun opgav den fornøjelige leg med at skrive O’er, blot fordi hun opdagede, at hendes stilling var uskøn, burde samles med anekdoterne om den lærde gris.*
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: (*Footnote. "I once knew a young person who learned to write before she learned to read, and began to write with her needle before she could use a pen. At first indeed, she took it into her head to make no other letter than the O: this letter she was constantly making of all sizes, and always the wrong way. Unluckily one day, as she was intent on this employment, she happened to see herself in the looking glass; when, taking a dislike to the constrained attitude in which she sat while writing, she threw away her pen, like another Pallas, and determined against making the O any more. Her brother was also equally averse to writing: it was the confinement, however, and not the constrained attitude, that most disgusted him." Rousseau's "Emilius.")
danishChanges.after: (*Note. »Jeg kendte engang en ung pige, som lærte at skrive, før hun lærte at læse, og begyndte at skrive med nålen, før hun kunne bruge en pen. Først fik hun den idé kun at lave bogstavet O. Det lavede hun bestandig i alle størrelser og altid den forkerte vej. Uheldigvis fik hun en dag, mens hun var optaget af dette, øje på sig selv i spejlet. Da hun ikke brød sig om den anspændte stilling, hun sad i, mens hun skrev, kastede hun pennen fra sig som en anden Pallas og besluttede aldrig mere at lave O’er. Hendes bror havde lige så stor modvilje mod at skrive, men det var tvangen til at sidde stille, ikke den anspændte stilling, han især ikke kunne lide.« Rousseaus Émile.)
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I have, probably, had an opportunity of observing more girls in their infancy than J. J. Rousseau. I can recollect my own feelings, and I have looked steadily around me; yet, so far from coinciding with him in opinion respecting the first dawn of the female character, I will venture to affirm, that a girl, whose spirits have not been damped by inactivity, or innocence tainted by false shame, will always be a romp, and the doll will never excite attention unless confinement allows her no alternative. Girls and boys, in short, would play harmless together, if the distinction of sex was not inculcated long before nature makes any difference. I will, go further, and affirm, as an indisputable fact, that most of the women, in the circle of my observation, who have acted like rational creatures, or shown any vigour of intellect, have accidentally been allowed to run wild, as some of the elegant formers of the fair sex would insinuate.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har sandsynligvis haft lejlighed til at iagttage flere små piger end J. J. Rousseau. Jeg kan huske mine egne følelser og har set opmærksomt omkring mig. Alligevel er jeg så langt fra enig med ham om kvindekarakterens første fremkomst, at jeg tør hævde, at en pige, hvis livsmod ikke er blevet dæmpet af passivitet eller hendes uskyld besmittet af falsk skam, altid vil være vild med at tumle sig. Dukken vil kun fange hendes opmærksomhed, hvis indespærringen ikke giver hende andre muligheder. Kort sagt ville piger og drenge lege harmløst sammen, hvis kønsforskellen ikke blev indprentet, længe før naturen gør nogen forskel. Jeg vil gå videre og som en ubestridelig kendsgerning hævde, at de fleste kvinder, jeg har kendt, som har handlet som fornuftsvæsener eller vist åndelig kraft, tilfældigvis har fået lov at løbe vildt omkring, som nogle af det smukke køns elegante opdragere ville antyde.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The baneful consequences which flow from inattention to health during infancy, and youth, extend further than is supposed, dependence of body naturally produces dependence of mind; and how can she be a good wife or mother, the greater part of whose time is employed to guard against or endure sickness; nor can it be expected, that a woman will resolutely endeavour to strengthen her constitution and abstain from enervating indulgences, if artificial notions of beauty, and false descriptions of sensibility, have been early entangled with her motives of action. Most men are sometimes obliged to bear with bodily inconveniences, and to endure, occasionally, the inclemency of the elements; but genteel women are, literally speaking, slaves to their bodies, and glory in their subjection.
danishChanges.after: De skadelige følger af at forsømme helbredet i barndom og ungdom rækker længere, end man tror. Kroppens afhængighed skaber naturligt sindets afhængighed. Og hvordan kan hun være en god hustru eller mor, når det meste af hendes tid går med at undgå eller udholde sygdom? Man kan heller ikke vente, at en kvinde beslutsomt vil styrke sit helbred og afstå fra svækkende nydelser, hvis kunstige skønhedsidealer og falske beskrivelser af følsomhed tidligt er blevet viklet ind i hendes bevæggrunde. De fleste mænd er somme tider nødt til at udholde fysisk ubehag og lejlighedsvis vejrets barskhed, men fine damer er bogstaveligt talt slaver af deres kroppe og er stolte af deres underkastelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I once knew a weak woman of fashion, who was more than commonly proud of her delicacy and sensibility. She thought a distinguishing taste and puny appetite the height of all human perfection, and acted accordingly. I have seen this weak sophisticated being neglect all the duties of life, yet recline with self-complacency on a sofa, and boast of her want of appetite as a proof of delicacy that extended to, or, perhaps, arose from, her exquisite sensibility: for it is difficult to render intelligible such ridiculous jargon. Yet, at the moment, I have seen her insult a worthy old gentlewoman, whom unexpected misfortunes had made dependent on her ostentatious bounty, and who, in better days, had claims on her gratitude. Is it possible that a human creature should have become such a weak and depraved being, if, like the Sybarites, dissolved in luxury, every thing like virtue had not been worn away, or never impressed by precept, a poor substitute it is true, for cultivation of mind, though it serves as a fence against vice?
danishChanges.after: Jeg kendte engang en svag, mondæn kvinde, som var usædvanligt stolt af sin sarthed og følsomhed. Hun anså en kræsen smag og en ringe appetit for højdepunktet af al menneskelig fuldkommenhed og handlede derefter. Jeg har set dette svage, kunstige væsen forsømme alle livets pligter og alligevel læne sig selvtilfreds på en sofa og prale af sin manglende appetit som bevis på en sarthed, der også omfattede, eller måske udsprang af, hendes udsøgte følsomhed. For det er svært at gøre sådan en latterlig jargon forståelig. Og samtidig har jeg set hende fornærme en agtværdig ældre kvinde, som uventede ulykker havde gjort afhængig af hendes pralende gavmildhed, og som i bedre dage havde gjort sig fortjent til hendes taknemmelighed. Kunne et menneske være blevet så svagt og fordærvet, hvis ikke alt, hvad der lignede dyd, som hos de luksusopløste sybaritter var blevet slidt bort eller aldrig indprentet gennem formaninger? Formaninger er ganske vist en ringe erstatning for sindets udvikling, men de tjener dog som et værn mod lasten.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Such a woman is not a more irrational monster than some of the Roman emperors, who were depraved by lawless power. Yet, since kings have been more under the restraint of law, and the curb, however weak, of honour, the records of history are not filled with such unnatural instances of folly and cruelty, nor does the despotism that kills virtue and genius in the bud, hover over Europe with that destructive blast which desolates Turkey, and renders the men, as well as the soil unfruitful.
danishChanges.after: En sådan kvinde er ikke et mere ufornuftigt uhyre end nogle af de romerske kejsere, som blev fordærvet af en magt uden lovens grænser. Men siden kongerne i højere grad er blevet holdt i tømme af loven og af æren, hvor svagt dette bånd end er, er historiens optegnelser ikke længere fyldt med så unaturlige eksempler på dårskab og grusomhed. Og det despoti, der kvæler dyd og begavelse i fødslen, hænger ikke over Europa med den ødelæggende vind, som lægger Tyrkiet øde og gør både menneskene og jorden ufrugtbare.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women are every where in this deplorable state; for, in order to preserve their innocence, as ignorance is courteously termed, truth is hidden from them, and they are made to assume an artificial character before their faculties have acquired any strength. Taught from their infancy, that beauty is woman's sceptre, the mind shapes itself to the body, and, roaming round its gilt cage, only seeks to adorn its prison. Men have various employments and pursuits which engage their attention, and give a character to the opening mind; but women, confined to one, and having their thoughts constantly directed to the most insignificant part of themselves, seldom extend their views beyond the triumph of the hour. But was their understanding once emancipated from the slavery to which the pride and sensuality of man and their short sighted desire, like that of dominion in tyrants, of present sway, has subjected them, we should probably read of their weaknesses with surprise. I must be allowed to pursue the argument a little farther.
danishChanges.after: Kvinder befinder sig overalt i denne sørgelige tilstand. For at bevare deres uskyld, som man høfligt kalder deres uvidenhed, skjuler man sandheden for dem og får dem til at påtage sig en kunstig karakter, før deres evner har nået at udvikle nogen styrke. Fra den tidligste barndom lærer de, at skønheden er kvindens scepter; derfor former sindet sig efter kroppen og bevæger sig rundt i sit forgyldte bur med det eneste ønske at pynte sit fængsel. Mænd har forskellige beskæftigelser og interesser, som optager deres opmærksomhed og giver det spirende sind karakter. Men kvinder begrænses til én beskæftigelse, og deres tanker rettes bestandig mod den mest ubetydelige del af dem selv; derfor rækker deres udsyn sjældent ud over øjeblikkets triumf. Hvis deres forstand først blev befriet fra det slaveri, som mænds stolthed og sanselighed og deres eget kortsynede ønske om magt i nuet — et ønske som tyrannernes hersketrang — har underlagt dem, ville vi sandsynligvis læse om deres svagheder med forundring. Jeg må have lov til at føre argumentet lidt videre.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Perhaps, if the existence of an evil being was allowed, who, in the allegorical language of scripture, went about seeking whom he should devour, he could not more effectually degrade the human character than by giving a man absolute power.
danishChanges.after: Hvis man antog, at der fandtes et ondt væsen, som med Skriftens billedlige ord gik omkring og søgte nogen at sluge, kunne det måske ikke fornedre menneskets karakter mere effektivt end ved at give et menneske absolut magt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This argument branches into various ramifications. Birth, riches, and every intrinsic advantage that exalt a man above his fellows, without any mental exertion, sink him in reality below them. In proportion to his weakness, he is played upon by designing men, till the bloated monster has lost all traces of humanity. And that tribes of men, like flocks of sheep, should quietly follow such a leader, is a solecism that only a desire of present enjoyment and narrowness of understanding can solve. Educated in slavish dependence, and enervated by luxury and sloth, where shall we find men who will stand forth to assert the rights of man; or claim the privilege of moral beings, who should have but one road to excellence? Slavery to monarchs and ministers, which the world will be long in freeing itself from, and whose deadly grasp stops the progress of the human mind, is not yet abolished.
danishChanges.after: Dette argument forgrener sig i mange retninger. Herkomst, rigdom og enhver medfølgende fordel, der hæver et menneske over dets medmennesker uden nogen åndelig anstrengelse, sænker det i virkeligheden under dem. Jo svagere det er, desto mere bliver det manipuleret af beregnende mennesker, indtil det oppustede uhyre har mistet ethvert spor af menneskelighed. At hele menneskeskarer stille følger en sådan leder som fåreflokke, er en selvmodsigelse, der kun kan forklares ved ønsket om nydelse i nuet og en snæver forstand. Hvor skal vi blandt mennesker, der er opdraget til slavisk afhængighed og svækket af luksus og dovenskab, finde nogen, som vil træde frem og hævde menneskerettighederne eller gøre krav på moralske væseners ret til at have én og samme vej til menneskelig fuldkommenhed? Slaveriet under monarker og ministre er endnu ikke afskaffet. Verden vil være længe om at befri sig fra det, og dets dødbringende greb standser menneskeåndens fremskridt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Let not men then in the pride of power, use the same arguments that tyrannic kings and venal ministers have used, and fallaciously assert, that woman ought to be subjected because she has always been so. But, when man, governed by reasonable laws, enjoys his natural freedom, let him despise woman, if she do not share it with him; and, till that glorious period arrives, in descanting on the folly of the sex, let him not overlook his own.
danishChanges.after: Lad derfor ikke mænd i magtens overmod bruge de samme argumenter, som tyranniske konger og bestikkelige ministre har brugt, og fejlagtigt hævde, at kvinden bør være underkastet, fordi hun altid har været det. Men når manden, styret af fornuftige love, nyder sin naturlige frihed, må han gerne foragte kvinden, hvis hun ikke deler den med ham. Indtil denne herlige tid kommer, bør han ikke overse sin egen dårskab, når han breder sig om kvindekønnets.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women, it is true, obtaining power by unjust means, by practising or fostering vice, evidently lose the rank which reason would assign them, and they become either abject slaves or capricious tyrants. They lose all simplicity, all dignity of mind, in acquiring power, and act as men are observed to act when they have been exalted by the same means.
danishChanges.after: Det er sandt, at kvinder, der skaffer sig magt med uretmæssige midler ved selv at udøve eller fremme laster, tydeligvis mister den plads, fornuften ville tildele dem, og bliver enten krybende slaver eller lunefulde tyranner. Når de vinder magt, mister de al naturlighed og al åndelig værdighed og handler, som man ser mænd handle, når de har hævet sig ved de samme midler.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is time to effect a revolution in female manners, time to restore to them their lost dignity, and make them, as a part of the human species, labour by reforming themselves to reform the world. It is time to separate unchangeable morals from local manners. If men be demi-gods, why let us serve them!
