And if the dignity of the female soul be as disputable as that of animals, if their reason does not afford sufficient light to direct their conduct whilst unerring instinct is denied, they are surely of all creatures the most miserable and, bent beneath the iron hand of destiny, must submit to be a FAIR DEFECT in creation. But to justify the ways of providence respecting them, by pointing out some irrefragable reason for thus making such a large portion of mankind accountable and not accountable, would puzzle the subtlest casuist.
danishChanges.after: Det er på tide at skabe en revolution i kvinders levevis, at give dem deres tabte værdighed tilbage og få dem til som en del af menneskeheden at arbejde på at reformere verden ved at reformere sig selv. Det er på tide at skille den uforanderlige moral fra lokale skikke. Hvis mænd er halvguder, så lad os da tjene dem! Og hvis kvindesjælens værdighed er lige så tvivlsom som dyrenes, hvis kvinders fornuft ikke giver tilstrækkeligt lys til at styre deres adfærd, mens de heller ikke har fået et ufejlbarligt instinkt, så er de vel de ulykkeligste af alle skabninger og må, bøjet under skæbnens jernhånd, finde sig i at være en SMUK FEJL i skaberværket. Men selv den mest spidsfindige kasuist ville komme til kort, hvis han skulle retfærdiggøre Forsynets behandling af dem ved at påvise en uigendrivelig grund til således at gøre en så stor del af menneskeheden både ansvarlig og ikke ansvarlig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The only solid foundation for morality appears to be the character of the Supreme Being; the harmony of which arises from a balance of attributes; and, to speak with reverence, one attribute seems to imply the NECESSITY of another. He must be just, because he is wise, he must be good, because he is omnipotent. For, to exalt one attribute at the expense of another equally noble and necessary, bears the stamp of the warped reason of man, the homage of passion. Man, accustomed to bow down to power in his savage state, can seldom divest himself of this barbarous prejudice even when civilization determines how much superior mental is to bodily strength; and his reason is clouded by these crude opinions, even when he thinks of the Deity. His omnipotence is made to swallow up, or preside over his other attributes, and those mortals are supposed to limit his power irreverently, who think that it must be regulated by his wisdom.
danishChanges.after: Det eneste sikre grundlag for moralen synes at være det højeste væsens karakter, hvis harmoni udspringer af en balance mellem dets egenskaber. Og sagt med ærbødighed synes den ene egenskab at gøre den anden NØDVENDIG. Han må være retfærdig, fordi han er vis; han må være god, fordi han er almægtig. At ophøje én egenskab på bekostning af en anden, der er lige så ædel og nødvendig, bærer nemlig præg af menneskets fordrejede fornuft og er en hyldest dikteret af lidenskab. Mennesket er fra sin vilde tilstand vant til at bøje sig for magten og kan sjældent frigøre sig fra denne barbariske fordom, selv når civilisationen viser, hvor langt åndelig styrke overgår fysisk styrke. Disse primitive forestillinger formørker dets fornuft, selv når det tænker på Gud. Man lader hans almagt opsluge eller herske over hans øvrige egenskaber og mener, at de dødelige, som tænker, at hans magt må styres af hans visdom, uærbødigt sætter grænser for den.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Jeg afviser den slags ydmyghed, der efter at have udforsket naturen standser ved skaberen. Den Høje og Ophøjede, som bor i evigheden, besidder uden tvivl mange egenskaber, vi ikke kan danne os nogen forestilling om; men fornuften siger mig, at de ikke kan stride mod dem, jeg tilbeder, og jeg er nødt til at lytte til dens stemme.
danishChanges.after: Jeg tager afstand fra den slags ydmyghed, som undersøger naturen, men standser ved dens skaber. Den høje og ophøjede, som bor i evigheden, besidder utvivlsomt mange egenskaber, vi ikke kan danne os nogen forestilling om. Men fornuften siger mig, at de ikke kan stride mod dem, jeg tilbeder, og jeg er nødt til at lytte til dens stemme.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It seems natural for man to search for excellence, and either to trace it in the object that he worships, or blindly to invest it with perfection as a garment. But what good effect can the latter mode of worship have on the moral conduct of a rational being? He bends to power; he adores a dark cloud, which may open a bright prospect to him, or burst in angry, lawless fury on his devoted head, he knows not why. And, supposing that the Deity acts from the vague impulse of an undirected will, man must also follow his own, or act according to rules, deduced from principles which he disclaims as irreverent. Into this dilemma have both enthusiasts and cooler thinkers fallen, when they laboured to free men from the wholesome restraints which a just conception of the character of God imposes.
danishChanges.after: Det synes naturligt for mennesket at søge det fuldkomne og enten finde spor af det i det, det tilbeder, eller blindt klæde dette i fuldkommenhed som i en dragt. Men hvilken gavnlig virkning kan den sidste form for tilbedelse have på et fornuftigt væsens moralske adfærd? Det bøjer sig for magten; det tilbeder en mørk sky, som enten kan åbne en lys udsigt for det eller bryde løs over dets prisgivne hoved i vred og lovløs rasen, uden at det ved hvorfor. Og hvis Gud antages at handle ud fra den uklare indskydelse fra en vilje uden retning, må mennesket også følge sin egen vilje eller handle efter regler udledt af principper, som det afviser som uærbødige. I dette dilemma er både sværmere og mere kølige tænkere havnet, når de har arbejdet på at befri mennesker fra de gavnlige begrænsninger, som en ret forståelse af Guds karakter pålægger dem.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is not impious thus to scan the attributes of the Almighty: in fact, who can avoid it that exercises his faculties? for to love God as the fountain of wisdom, goodness, and power, appears to be the only worship useful to a being who wishes to acquire either virtue or knowledge. A blind unsettled affection may, like human passions, occupy the mind and warm the heart, whilst, to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with our God, is forgotten. I shall pursue this subject still further, when I consider religion in a light opposite to that recommended by Dr. Gregory, who treats it as a matter of sentiment or taste.
danishChanges.after: Det er ikke ugudeligt på denne måde at granske den Almægtiges egenskaber. Hvem, der bruger sine evner, kan i virkeligheden undgå det? At elske Gud som kilden til visdom, godhed og magt synes nemlig at være den eneste tilbedelse, der gavner et væsen, som ønsker at opnå enten dyd eller viden. En blind og ustadig kærlighed kan ligesom menneskelige lidenskaber optage sindet og varme hjertet, mens man glemmer at øve ret, elske barmhjertighed og vandre ydmygt med sin Gud. Jeg vil gå videre med dette emne, når jeg betragter religionen i et andet lys end det, dr. Gregory anbefaler, når han behandler den som et spørgsmål om følelse eller smag.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To return from this apparent digression. It were to be wished, that women would cherish an affection for their husbands, founded on the same principle that devotion ought to rest upon. No other firm base is there under heaven, for let them beware of the fallacious light of sentiment; too often used as a softer phrase for sensuality. It follows then, I think, that from their infancy women should either be shut up like eastern princes, or educated in such a manner as to be able to think and act for themselves.
danishChanges.after: For at vende tilbage fra denne tilsyneladende afstikker: Det ville være ønskeligt, at kvinder nærede en kærlighed til deres mænd, som byggede på det samme princip, som gudsfrygt bør hvile på. Der findes intet andet fast grundlag under himlen. De bør tage sig i agt for følelsens vildledende lys; alt for ofte bruges ordet som en pænere betegnelse for sanselighed. Heraf følger efter min mening, at kvinder enten fra barndommen bør holdes indespærret som østerlandske fyrster eller opdrages, så de kan tænke og handle på egen hånd.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Hvorfor vakler mænd mellem to opfattelser og forventer umuligheder? Hvorfor forventer de dyd af en slave eller af et væsen, som det borgerlige samfunds forfatning har gjort svagt, om ikke lastefuldt?
danishChanges.after: Hvorfor vakler mænd mellem to standpunkter og forventer det umulige? Hvorfor forventer de dyd af en slave eller af et væsen, som samfundets indretning har gjort svagt, om ikke ligefrem lastefuldt?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Still I know that it will require a considerable length of time to eradicate the firmly rooted prejudices which sensualists have planted; it will also require some time to convince women that they act contrary to their real interest on an enlarged scale, when they cherish or affect weakness under the name of delicacy, and to convince the world that the poisoned source of female vices and follies, if it be necessary, in compliance with custom, to use synonymous terms in a lax sense, has been the sensual homage paid to beauty: to beauty of features; for it has been shrewdly observed by a German writer, that a pretty woman, as an object of desire, is generally allowed to be so by men of all descriptions; whilst a fine woman, who inspires more sublime emotions by displaying intellectual beauty, may be overlooked or observed with indifference, by those men who find their happiness in the gratification of their appetites. I foresee an obvious retort; whilst man remains such an imperfect being as he appears hitherto to have been, he will, more or less, be the slave of his appetites; and those women obtaining most power who gratify a predominant one, the sex is degraded by a physical, if not by a moral necessity.
danishChanges.after: Jeg ved dog, at det vil kræve lang tid at udrydde de fast indgroede fordomme, som sansenydelsens dyrkere har plantet. Det vil også tage tid at overbevise kvinder om, at de set i et større perspektiv handler imod deres virkelige interesser, når de dyrker eller foregiver svaghed under navn af finhed. Og det vil tage tid at overbevise verden om, at den forgiftede kilde til kvinders laster og dårskaber — hvis det af hensyn til sprogbrugen er nødvendigt at bruge synonyme ord i en løs betydning — har været den sanselige hyldest til skønheden, altså ansigtstrækkenes skønhed. En tysk forfatter har nemlig skarpsindigt bemærket, at mænd af enhver slags som regel er enige om, at en køn kvinde er begærlig, mens en fremragende kvinde, der vækker mere ophøjede følelser ved at vise åndelig skønhed, kan blive overset eller betragtet med ligegyldighed af de mænd, som finder deres lykke i at tilfredsstille deres drifter. Jeg forudser en nærliggende indvending: Så længe manden forbliver et så ufuldkomment væsen, som han hidtil synes at have været, vil han i større eller mindre grad være slave af sine drifter. Og når de kvinder, som tilfredsstiller en af hans stærkeste drifter, opnår størst magt, bliver kønnet fornedret af en fysisk, om ikke en moralsk, nødvendighed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This objection has, I grant, some force; but while such a sublime precept exists, as, "be pure as your heavenly father is pure;" it would seem that the virtues of man are not limited by the Being who alone could limit them; and that he may press forward without considering whether he steps out of his sphere by indulging such a noble ambition. To the wild billows it has been said, "thus far shalt thou go, and no further; and here shall thy proud waves be stayed." Vainly then do they beat and foam, restrained by the power that confines the struggling planets within their orbits, matter yields to the great governing Spirit. But an immortal soul, not restrained by mechanical laws, and struggling to free itself from the shackles of matter, contributes to, instead of disturbing, the order of creation, when, co-operating with the Father of spirits, it tries to govern itself by the invariable rule that, in a degree, before which our imagination faints, the universe is regulated.
danishChanges.after: Jeg indrømmer, at denne indvending har en vis vægt. Men så længe et så ophøjet bud som »vær rene, ligesom jeres himmelske fader er ren« består, synes menneskets dyder ikke at være begrænset af det væsen, som alene kunne begrænse dem. Mennesket kan derfor stræbe fremad uden at spørge, om det overskrider sit område ved at nære en så ædel ambition. Til de vilde bølger er der blevet sagt: »Hertil må du komme og ikke længere; her skal dine stolte bølger standse.« Forgæves slår de da og skummer, holdt tilbage af den magt, som fastholder de stridende planeter i deres baner; stoffet bøjer sig for den store styrende ånd. Men en udødelig sjæl, der ikke er bundet af mekaniske love og kæmper for at befri sig fra stoffets lænker, bidrager til skabelsens orden i stedet for at forstyrre den, når den i samarbejde med åndernes fader prøver at styre sig selv efter den uforanderlige regel, som styrer universet i en grad, vores forestillingsevne kommer til kort over for.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, if women are educated for dependence, that is, to act according to the will of another fallible being, and submit, right or wrong, to power, where are we to stop? Are they to be considered as viceregents, allowed to reign over a small domain, and answerable for their conduct to a higher tribunal, liable to error?
danishChanges.after: Hvis kvinder desuden opdrages til afhængighed, altså til at handle efter et andet fejlbarligt væsens vilje og underkaste sig magten, hvad enten den har ret eller uret, hvor skal vi så sætte grænsen? Skal de betragtes som stedfortrædende regenter, der får lov til at herske over et lille område og skal stå til ansvar for deres adfærd over for en højere domstol, som selv kan tage fejl?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It will not be difficult to prove, that such delegates will act like men subjected by fear, and make their children and servants endure their tyrannical oppression. As they submit without reason, they will, having no fixed rules to square their conduct by, be kind or cruel, just as the whim of the moment directs; and we ought not to wonder if sometimes, galled by their heavy yoke, they take a malignant pleasure in resting it on weaker shoulders.
danishChanges.after: Det vil ikke være svært at bevise, at sådanne stedfortrædere vil handle som mænd, der holdes i underkastelse af frygt, og lade deres børn og tjenestefolk udholde deres tyranniske undertrykkelse. Da de underkaster sig uden fornuftens medvirken og ikke har faste regler at rette deres adfærd efter, vil de være venlige eller grusomme, alt efter øjeblikkets indfald. Og vi bør ikke undre os, hvis de, plaget af deres tunge åg, undertiden finder en ondskabsfuld glæde i at lade det hvile på svagere skuldre.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, supposing a woman, trained up to obedience, be married to a sensible man, who directs her judgment, without making her feel the servility of her subjection, to act with as much propriety by this reflected light as can be expected when reason is taken at second hand, yet she cannot ensure the life of her protector; he may die and leave her with a large family.
danishChanges.after: Men lad os antage, at en kvinde, der er oplært til lydighed, bliver gift med en forstandig mand, som leder hendes dømmekraft uden at lade hende mærke det slaviske i hendes underkastelse. Ved dette lånte lys handler hun så passende, som man kan forvente, når fornuften kommer på anden hånd. Alligevel kan hun ikke sikre sin beskytters liv; han kan dø og efterlade hende med en stor børneflok.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A double duty devolves on her; to educate them in the character of both father and mother; to form their principles and secure their property. But, alas! she has never thought, much less acted for herself. She has only learned to please men, to depend gracefully on them; yet, encumbered with children, how is she to obtain another protector; a husband to supply the place of reason? A rational man, for we are not treading on romantic ground, though he may think her a pleasing docile creature, will not choose to marry a FAMILY for love, when the world contains many more pretty creatures. What is then to become of her? She either falls an easy prey to some mean fortune hunter, who defrauds her children of their paternal inheritance, and renders her miserable; or becomes the victim of discontent and blind indulgence. Unable to educate her sons, or impress them with respect; for it is not a play on words to assert, that people are never respected, though filling an important station, who are not respectable; she pines under the anguish of unavailing impotent regret. The serpent's tooth enters into her very soul, and the vices of licentious youth bring her with sorrow, if not with poverty also, to the grave.
danishChanges.after: Hun får da en dobbelt pligt: at opdrage børnene som både far og mor, forme deres principper og sikre deres formue. Men ak! Hun har aldrig tænkt, langt mindre handlet, på egen hånd. Hun har kun lært at behage mænd og være afhængig af dem med ynde. Men hvordan skal hun, tynget af børn, skaffe sig en ny beskytter, en ægtemand til at træde i fornuftens sted? En fornuftig mand — for vi befinder os ikke i en romantisk fortælling — vil måske finde hende behagelig og føjelig, men han vil ikke vælge at gifte sig med en hel FAMILIE af kærlighed, når verden rummer så mange andre kønne skabninger. Hvad skal der så blive af hende? Enten bliver hun et let bytte for en ussel lykkejæger, som bedrager hendes børn for deres fædrene arv og gør hende ulykkelig, eller også bliver hun offer for utilfredshed og blind eftergivenhed. Hun kan hverken opdrage sine sønner eller indgyde dem respekt — for det er ikke blot et ordspil at hævde, at mennesker aldrig bliver respekteret, selv om de indtager en vigtig stilling, hvis de ikke er værd at respektere. Hun visner hen i smerten over en nytteløs, magtesløs fortrydelse. Slangens tand trænger ind i selve hendes sjæl, og den tøjlesløse ungdoms laster bringer hende i graven med sorg, om ikke også med fattigdom.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Dette er ikke et overdrevet billede; tværtimod er det et yderst sandsynligt tilfælde, og noget lignende må være faldet ethvert opmærksomt øje for.
danishChanges.after: Dette billede er ikke overdrevet. Tværtimod er det et ganske muligt tilfælde, og enhver opmærksom iagttager må have set noget lignende.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I have, however, taken it for granted, that she was well disposed, though experience shows, that the blind may as easily be led into a ditch as along the beaten road. But supposing, no very improbable conjecture, that a being only taught to please must still find her happiness in pleasing; what an example of folly, not to say vice, will she be to her innocent daughters! The mother will be lost in the coquette, and, instead of making friends of her daughters, view them with eyes askance, for they are rivals--rivals more cruel than any other, because they invite a comparison, and drive her from the throne of beauty, who has never thought of a seat on the bench of reason.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har dog taget for givet, at hun var velmenende, selv om erfaringen viser, at en blind lige så let kan føres i grøften som ad den banede vej. Men lad os antage — og det er ingen særlig usandsynlig antagelse — at et væsen, der kun er blevet lært at behage, fortsat må finde sin lykke i at behage. Hvilket eksempel på dårskab, for ikke at sige last, vil hun da være for sine uskyldige døtre! Moderen forsvinder i koketten, og i stedet for at gøre sine døtre til venner vil hun se skævt til dem, for de er rivaler. De er mere grusomme rivaler end nogen andre, fordi de indbyder til sammenligning og fordriver hende fra skønhedens trone, mens hun aldrig har tænkt på at tage sæde på fornuftens dommerbænk.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It does not require a lively pencil, or the discriminating outline of a caricature, to sketch the domestic miseries and petty vices which such a mistress of a family diffuses. Still she only acts as a woman ought to act, brought up according to Rousseau's system. She can never be reproached for being masculine, or turning out of her sphere; nay, she may observe another of his grand rules, and, cautiously preserving her reputation free from spot, be reckoned a good kind of woman. Yet in what respect can she be termed good? She abstains, it is true, without any great struggle, from committing gross crimes; but how does she fulfil her duties? Duties!--in truth she has enough to think of to adorn her body and nurse a weak constitution.
danishChanges.after: Det kræver hverken en livlig pensel eller karikaturens skarpe konturer at skildre den elendighed og de smålige laster, som en sådan husmoder spreder i hjemmet. Alligevel handler hun blot, som en kvinde bør handle, når hun er opdraget efter Rousseaus system. Man kan aldrig bebrejde hende, at hun er mandhaftig eller går uden for sit område. Ja, hun kan overholde endnu en af hans store regler og, ved omhyggeligt at holde sit ry uplettet, blive regnet for en god og ordentlig kvinde. Men i hvilken henseende kan hun kaldes god? Ganske vist afholder hun sig uden større kamp fra at begå grove forbrydelser, men hvordan opfylder hun sine pligter? Pligter! Hun har sandelig nok at tænke på med at pynte sin krop og pleje sit svagelige helbred.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: With respect to religion, she never presumed to judge for herself; but conformed, as a dependent creature should, to the ceremonies of the church which she was brought up in, piously believing, that wiser heads than her own have settled that business: and not to doubt is her point of perfection. She therefore pays her tythe of mint and cummin, and thanks her God that she is not as other women are. These are the blessed effects of a good education! these the virtues of man's helpmate. I must relieve myself by drawing a different picture.
danishChanges.after: Hvad religionen angår, har hun aldrig dristet sig til at dømme selv. Som et afhængigt væsen bør, har hun rettet sig efter ritualerne i den kirke, hun er opdraget i, i den fromme tro, at klogere hoveder end hendes har ordnet den sag; ikke at tvivle er hendes fuldkommenhed. Derfor giver hun tiende af mynte og kommen og takker sin Gud for, at hun ikke er som andre kvinder. Dette er de velsignede følger af en god opdragelse! Dette er dyderne hos mandens medhjælper. Jeg må skaffe mig luft ved at tegne et andet billede.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Let fancy now present a woman with a tolerable understanding, for I do not wish to leave the line of mediocrity, whose constitution, strengthened by exercise, has allowed her body to acquire its full vigour; her mind, at the same time, gradually expanding itself to comprehend the moral duties of life, and in what human virtue and dignity consist. Formed thus by the relative duties of her station, she marries from affection, without losing sight of prudence, and looking beyond matrimonial felicity, she secures her husband's respect before it is necessary to exert mean arts to please him, and feed a dying flame, which nature doomed to expire when the object became familiar, when friendship and forbearance take place of a more ardent affection. This is the natural death of love, and domestic peace is not destroyed by struggles to prevent its extinction. I also suppose the husband to be virtuous; or she is still more in want of independent principles.
danishChanges.after: Lad os nu forestille os en kvinde med en ganske almindelig forstand, for jeg ønsker ikke at gå ud over det middelmådige, og med et helbred, som motion har styrket, så hendes krop har kunnet udvikle sin fulde kraft. Samtidig har hendes sind gradvis udvidet sig, så hun forstår livets moralske pligter og det, menneskelig dyd og værdighed består i. Formet på denne måde af de pligter, hendes stilling indebærer over for andre, gifter hun sig af kærlighed uden at tabe omtanken af syne. Hun ser ud over ægteskabets lykke og sikrer sig sin mands respekt, før det bliver nødvendigt at bruge uværdige kneb for at behage ham og nære en døende flamme, som naturen har bestemt skal slukkes, når den elskede er blevet velkendt, og venskab og overbærenhed afløser en mere brændende følelse. Dette er forelskelsens naturlige død, og hjemmets fred bliver ikke ødelagt af kampe for at forhindre, at den slukkes. Jeg antager også, at ægtemanden er dydig; ellers har hun endnu mere brug for selvstændige principper.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Fate, however, breaks this tie. She is left a widow, perhaps, without a sufficient provision: but she is not desolate! The pang of nature is felt; but after time has softened sorrow into melancholy resignation, her heart turns to her children with redoubled fondness, and anxious to provide for them, affection gives a sacred heroic cast to her maternal duties. She thinks that not only the eye sees her virtuous efforts, from whom all her comfort now must flow, and whose approbation is life; but her imagination, a little abstracted and exalted by grief, dwells on the fond hope, that the eyes which her trembling hand closed, may still see how she subdues every wayward passion to fulfil the double duty of being the father as well as the mother of her children. Raised to heroism by misfortunes, she represses the first faint dawning of a natural inclination, before it ripens into love, and in the bloom of life forgets her sex--forgets the pleasure of an awakening passion, which might again have been inspired and returned. She no longer thinks of pleasing, and conscious dignity prevents her from priding herself on account of the praise which her conduct demands. Her children have her love, and her brightest hopes are beyond the grave, where her imagination often strays.
danishChanges.after: Men skæbnen bryder dette bånd. Hun bliver enke, måske uden tilstrækkelige midler til sit underhold; men hun er ikke uden håb! Hun føler det naturlige smertestik. Men når tiden har mildnet sorgen til en vemodig accept, vender hendes hjerte sig mod børnene med fordoblet ømhed. I sin omsorg for at forsørge dem giver kærligheden hendes moderpligter et helligt, heroisk præg. Hun tænker, at hendes dydige anstrengelser ikke alene ses af ham, som al hendes trøst nu må komme fra, og hvis anerkendelse er selve livet. Hendes fantasi, som sorgen har gjort lidt fjern fra verden og løftet over den, dvæler også ved det kærlige håb, at de øjne, hendes skælvende hånd lukkede, stadig kan se, hvordan hun behersker enhver ustyrlig lidenskab for at opfylde den dobbelte pligt at være både far og mor for sine børn. Ulykken løfter hende til heltemod. Hun undertrykker den første svage spire til en naturlig tilbøjelighed, før den modnes til kærlighed, og glemmer i livets blomstring sit køn — glemmer glæden ved en vågnende lidenskab, som igen kunne være blevet vakt og gengældt. Hun tænker ikke længere på at behage, og bevidstheden om sin værdighed hindrer hende i at hovmode sig over den ros, hendes adfærd fortjener. Hendes børn har hendes kærlighed, og hendes lyseste håb ligger hinsides graven, hvor hendes fantasi ofte vandrer.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I think I see her surrounded by her children, reaping the reward of her care. The intelligent eye meets her's, whilst health and innocence smile on their chubby cheeks, and as they grow up the cares of life are lessened by their grateful attention. She lives to see the virtues which she endeavoured to plant on principles, fixed into habits, to see her children attain a strength of character sufficient to enable them to endure adversity without forgetting their mother's example.
danishChanges.after: Jeg synes at se hende omgivet af sine børn, mens hun høster lønnen for sin omsorg. Deres intelligente øjne møder hendes, mens sundhed og uskyld smiler på deres runde kinder. Efterhånden som de vokser op, letter deres taknemmelige omsorg livets byrder for hende. Hun lever længe nok til at se de dyder, som hun søgte at plante på et grundlag af principper, slå rod som vaner og til at se sine børn opnå en karakterstyrke, der gør dem i stand til at udholde modgang uden at glemme deres mors eksempel.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The task of life thus fulfilled, she calmly waits for the sleep of death, and rising from the grave may say, behold, thou gavest me a talent, and here are five talents.
danishChanges.after: Med livets opgave fuldført venter hun roligt på dødens søvn, og når hun rejser sig fra graven, kan hun sige: Se, du gav mig én talent, og her er fem talenter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I wish to sum up what I have said in a few words, for I here throw down my gauntlet, and deny the existence of sexual virtues, not excepting modesty. For man and woman, truth, if I understand the meaning of the word, must be the same; yet the fanciful female character, so prettily drawn by poets and novelists, demanding the sacrifice of truth and sincerity, virtue becomes a relative idea, having no other foundation than utility, and of that utility men pretend arbitrarily to judge, shaping it to their own convenience.
danishChanges.after: Jeg vil sammenfatte det sagte i få ord, for her kaster jeg handsken og benægter, at der findes kønsbestemte dyder, heller ikke blufærdigheden. For mand og kvinde må sandheden være den samme, hvis jeg forstår ordets betydning. Men når den fantasiskabte kvindekarakter, som digtere og romanforfattere tegner så smukt, kræver, at sandhed og oprigtighed ofres, bliver dyden en relativ forestilling uden andet grundlag end nytten. Og denne nytte gør mænd krav på vilkårligt at bedømme og forme efter deres eget forgodtbefindende.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women, I allow, may have different duties to fulfil; but they are HUMAN duties, and the principles that should regulate the discharge of them, I sturdily maintain, must be the same.
danishChanges.after: Jeg indrømmer, at kvinder kan have andre pligter at opfylde. Men det er MENNESKELIGE pligter, og jeg fastholder bestemt, at de principper, som bør styre opfyldelsen af dem, må være de samme.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To become respectable, the exercise of their understanding is necessary, there is no other foundation for independence of character; I mean explicitly to say, that they must only bow to the authority of reason, instead of being the MODEST slaves of opinion.
danishChanges.after: For at blive værd at respektere må de bruge deres forstand; der findes intet andet grundlag for en selvstændig karakter. Jeg vil udtrykkeligt sige, at de kun må bøje sig for fornuftens myndighed i stedet for at være den offentlige menings BLUFÆRDIGE slaver.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In the superior ranks of life how seldom do we meet with a man of superior abilities, or even common acquirements? The reason appears to me clear; the state they are born in was an unnatural one. The human character has ever been formed by the employments the individual, or class pursues; and if the faculties are not sharpened by necessity, they must remain obtuse. The argument may fairly be extended to women; for seldom occupied by serious business, the pursuit of pleasure gives that insignificancy to their character which renders the society of the GREAT so insipid. The same want of firmness, produced by a similar cause, forces them both to fly from themselves to noisy pleasures, and artificial passions, till vanity takes place of every social affection, and the characteristics of humanity can scarcely be discerned. Such are the blessings of civil governments, as they are at present organized, that wealth and female softness equally tend to debase mankind, and are produced by the same cause; but allowing women to be rational creatures they should be incited to acquire virtues which they may call their own, for how can a rational being be ennobled by any thing that is not obtained by its OWN exertions?
danishChanges.after: Hvor sjældent møder vi ikke i samfundets øverste lag en mand med fremragende evner eller blot almindelige kundskaber? Grunden synes mig klar: Den tilstand, de fødes ind i, er unaturlig. Menneskets karakter er altid blevet formet af den beskæftigelse, individet eller klassen følger; og hvis evnerne ikke skærpes af nødvendigheden, må de forblive sløve. Argumentet kan med rette udstrækkes til kvinder. Da de sjældent beskæftiger sig med alvorlige anliggender, giver jagten på fornøjelser deres karakter den samme ubetydelighed, som gør samværet med de FORNEMME så indholdsløst. Den samme mangel på fasthed, frembragt af en lignende årsag, tvinger begge grupper til at flygte fra sig selv ind i støjende fornøjelser og kunstige lidenskaber, indtil forfængeligheden afløser enhver følelse for andre, og menneskelighedens kendetegn knap kan skelnes. Sådan er velsignelserne ved samfundets styreformer, som de nu er indrettet: Rigdom og kvindelig blødagtighed bidrager i lige grad til at fornedre menneskeheden og frembringes af den samme årsag. Men anerkender man kvinder som fornuftige væsener, bør man tilskynde dem til at tilegne sig dyder, de kan kalde deres egne. For hvordan kan et fornuftigt væsen blive forædlet af noget, det ikke har opnået ved sin EGEN anstrengelse?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: That woman is naturally weak, or degraded by a concurrence of circumstances is, I think, clear. But this position I shall simply contrast with a conclusion, which I have frequently heard fall from sensible men in favour of an aristocracy: that the mass of mankind cannot be any thing, or the obsequious slaves, who patiently allow themselves to be penned up, would feel their own consequence, and spurn their chains. Men, they further observe, submit every where to oppression, when they have only to lift up their heads to throw off the yoke; yet, instead of asserting their birthright, they quietly lick the dust, and say, let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we die. Women, I argue from analogy, are degraded by the same propensity to enjoy the present moment; and, at last, despise the freedom which they have not sufficient virtue to struggle to attain. But I must be more explicit.
danishChanges.after: At kvinden enten er svag af natur eller er blevet fornedret af et samspil mellem omstændigheder, er efter min mening klart. Men jeg vil blot stille denne påstand over for en slutning, som jeg ofte har hørt forstandige mænd drage til forsvar for aristokratiet: at den store masse af mennesker ikke kan være noget værd; ellers ville de føjelige slaver, som tålmodigt lader sig lukke inde, føle deres egen betydning og kaste lænkerne fra sig. Mennesker, bemærker de videre, underkaster sig overalt undertrykkelse, selv om de blot behøver at løfte hovedet for at ryste åget af sig. Men i stedet for at hævde deres medfødte ret slikker de stille støvet og siger: Lad os spise og drikke, for i morgen skal vi dø. Jeg slutter ved sammenligning, at kvinder fornedres af den samme tilbøjelighed til at nyde øjeblikket og til sidst foragter den frihed, de ikke har dyd nok til at kæmpe for. Men jeg må udtrykke mig tydeligere.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: With respect to the culture of the heart, it is unanimously allowed that sex is out of the question; but the line of subordination in the mental powers is never to be passed over. Only "absolute in loveliness," the portion of rationality granted to woman is, indeed, very scanty; for, denying her genius and judgment, it is scarcely possible to divine what remains to characterize intellect.
danishChanges.after: Når det gælder hjertets dannelse, er alle enige om, at kønnet ikke spiller nogen rolle. Men grænsen, som underordner kvindens åndsevner, må aldrig overskrides. Hun er kun »fuldkommen i yndighed«, og den del af fornuften, man indrømmer kvinden, er sandelig meget lille. For når man nægter hende både begavelse og dømmekraft, er det næppe muligt at gætte, hvad der er tilbage, som kan kendetegne et intellekt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The stamina of immortality, if I may be allowed the phrase, is the perfectibility of human reason; for, was man created perfect, or did a flood of knowledge break in upon him, when he arrived at maturity, that precluded error, I should doubt whether his existence would be continued after the dissolution of the body. But in the present state of things, every difficulty in morals, that escapes from human discussion, and equally baffles the investigation of profound thinking, and the lightning glance of genius, is an argument on which I build my belief of the immortality of the soul. Reason is, consequentially, the simple power of improvement; or, more properly speaking, of discerning truth. Every individual is in this respect a world in itself. More or less may be conspicuous in one being than other; but the nature of reason must be the same in all, if it be an emanation of divinity, the tie that connects the creature with the Creator; for, can that soul be stamped with the heavenly image, that is not perfected by the exercise of its own reason? Yet outwardly ornamented with elaborate care, and so adorned to delight man, "that with honour he may love," (Vide Milton) the soul of woman is not allowed to have this distinction, and man, ever placed between her and reason, she is always represented as only created to see through a gross medium, and to take things on trust. But, dismissing these fanciful theories, and considering woman as a whole, let it be what it will, instead of a part of man, the inquiry is, whether she has reason or not. If she has, which, for a moment, I will take for granted, she was not created merely to be the solace of man, and the sexual should not destroy the human character.
danishChanges.after: Grundlaget for udødeligheden, hvis jeg må bruge det udtryk, er den menneskelige fornufts mulighed for at blive fuldkommengjort. For hvis mennesket var skabt fuldkomment, eller hvis en strøm af viden skyllede ind over det, når det blev voksent, og udelukkede enhver fejltagelse, ville jeg tvivle på, at dets tilværelse fortsatte efter kroppens opløsning. Men som forholdene er, er ethvert moralsk problem, som menneskers drøftelser ikke kan løse, og som både trodser den dybe tænknings undersøgelser og geniets lynsnare blik, et argument, jeg bygger min tro på sjælens udødelighed på. Fornuften er følgelig ganske enkelt evnen til at udvikle sig eller, mere præcist, til at skelne sandheden. Hvert individ er i den henseende en verden i sig selv. Denne evne kan træde mere eller mindre tydeligt frem hos det ene væsen end hos det andet, men fornuftens natur må være den samme hos alle, hvis den er en udstråling fra det guddommelige, det bånd, der forbinder skabningen med skaberen. For kan en sjæl bære det himmelske billede, hvis den ikke fuldkommengøres ved at bruge sin egen fornuft? Men kvindens sjæl får ikke lov til at have dette særkende, skønt hun udvendigt pyntes med udsøgt omhu og smykkes for at glæde manden, »så han med ære kan elske« (se Milton). Manden stilles altid mellem hende og fornuften, og hun fremstilles bestandig, som om hun kun var skabt til at se gennem et groft filter og tage tingene for gode varer. Men lad os lægge disse fantasifulde teorier til side og betragte kvinden som et helt væsen, hvad det så end måtte være, i stedet for som en del af manden. Spørgsmålet er da, om hun har fornuft eller ej. Hvis hun har — og det vil jeg et øjeblik tage for givet — blev hun ikke skabt blot for at være mandens trøst, og hendes køn må ikke ødelægge hendes menneskelige karakter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Into this error men have, probably, been led by viewing education in a false light; not considering it as the first step to form a being advancing gradually toward perfection; (This word is not strictly just, but I cannot find a better.) but only as a preparation for life. On this sensual error, for I must call it so, has the false system of female manners been reared, which robs the whole sex of its dignity, and classes the brown and fair with the smiling flowers that only adorn the land. This has ever been the language of men, and the fear of departing from a supposed sexual character, has made even women of superior sense adopt the same sentiments. Thus understanding, strictly speaking, has been denied to woman; and instinct, sublimated into wit and cunning, for the purposes of life, has been substituted in its stead.
danishChanges.after: Mænd er sandsynligvis blevet ført til denne fejl ved at se opdragelsen i et forkert lys: De betragter den ikke som det første skridt i dannelsen af et væsen, der gradvis nærmer sig fuldkommenheden (dette ord er ikke helt præcist, men jeg kan ikke finde et bedre), men blot som en forberedelse til livet. På denne sanselige vildfarelse — for det må jeg kalde den — har man opbygget det falske system for kvinders levevis, som berøver hele kønnet dets værdighed og sætter mørke og lyse kvinder i klasse med de smilende blomster, der blot pynter landskabet. Sådan har mænd altid talt, og frygten for at afvige fra en formodet kvindelig karakter har fået selv kvinder med fremragende forstand til at antage de samme synspunkter. Dermed har man strengt taget nægtet kvinden forstand og i stedet givet hende instinkt, forfinet til vid og list til brug i livet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The power of generalizing ideas, of drawing comprehensive conclusions from individual observations, is the only acquirement for an immortal being, that really deserves the name of knowledge. Merely to observe, without endeavouring to account for any thing, may, (in a very incomplete manner) serve as the common sense of life; but where is the store laid up that is to clothe the soul when it leaves the body?
danishChanges.after: Evnen til at generalisere, til at drage omfattende slutninger ud fra enkelte iagttagelser, er det eneste, et udødeligt væsen kan tilegne sig, som virkelig fortjener navnet viden. Blot at iagttage uden at forsøge at forklare noget kan — på en meget ufuldstændig måde — gøre det ud for sund fornuft i dagliglivet. Men hvor er det forråd, der er samlet til at klæde sjælen, når den forlader kroppen?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This power has not only been denied to women; but writers have insisted that it is inconsistent, with a few exceptions, with their sexual character. Let men prove this, and I shall grant that woman only exists for man. I must, however, previously remark, that the power of generalizing ideas, to any great extent, is not very common amongst men or women. But this exercise is the true cultivation of the understanding; and every thing conspires to render the cultivation of the understanding more difficult in the female than the male world.
danishChanges.after: Denne evne er ikke blot blevet nægtet kvinder. Forfattere har ligefrem hævdet, at den med få undtagelser er uforenelig med deres køns karakter. Lad mændene bevise dette, og jeg vil indrømme, at kvinden kun eksisterer for mandens skyld. Først må jeg dog bemærke, at evnen til at generalisere i større omfang ikke er særlig udbredt hos hverken mænd eller kvinder. Men det er gennem denne øvelse, forstanden virkelig udvikles, og alt forener sig om at gøre udviklingen af forstanden vanskeligere i kvindernes verden end i mændenes.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Denne påstand fører mig naturligt over til hovedemnet for dette kapitel, og jeg vil nu forsøge at pege på nogle af de årsager, der nedværdiger kønnet og forhindrer kvinder i at almengøre deres iagttagelser.
danishChanges.after: Denne påstand fører mig naturligt til dette kapitels hovedemne, og jeg vil nu forsøge at påpege nogle af de årsager, der fornedrer kønnet og hindrer kvinder i at drage almene slutninger af deres iagttagelser.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I shall not go back to the remote annals of antiquity to trace the history of woman; it is sufficient to allow, that she has always been either a slave or a despot, and to remark, that each of these situations equally retards the progress of reason. The grand source of female folly and vice has ever appeared to me to arise from narrowness of mind; and the very constitution of civil governments has put almost insuperable obstacles in the way to prevent the cultivation of the female understanding: yet virtue can be built on no other foundation! The same obstacles are thrown in the way of the rich, and the same consequences ensue.
danishChanges.after: Jeg vil ikke gå tilbage til oldtidens fjerne annaler for at følge kvindens historie. Det er nok at indrømme, at hun altid har været enten slave eller despot, og at bemærke, at begge stillinger i lige høj grad hæmmer fornuftens udvikling. Den vigtigste kilde til kvindelig dårskab og last har efter min opfattelse altid været et snævert sind. Og selve samfundets styreformer har lagt næsten uoverstigelige hindringer i vejen for udviklingen af kvinders forstand. Alligevel kan dyd ikke bygges på noget andet grundlag! De samme hindringer lægges i vejen for de rige, og følgerne er de samme.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Necessity has been proverbially termed the mother of invention; the aphorism may be extended to virtue. It is an acquirement, and an acquirement to which pleasure must be sacrificed, and who sacrifices pleasure when it is within the grasp, whose mind has not been opened and strengthened by adversity, or the pursuit of knowledge goaded on by necessity? Happy is it when people have the cares of life to struggle with; for these struggles prevent their becoming a prey to enervating vices, merely from idleness! But, if from their birth men and women are placed in a torrid zone, with the meridian sun of pleasure darting directly upon them, how can they sufficiently brace their minds to discharge the duties of life, or even to relish the affections that carry them out of themselves?
danishChanges.after: Man siger i et ordsprog, at nød er opfindelsens moder; det samme kan siges om dyden. Den må tilegnes, og for at tilegne sig den må man ofre nydelse. Men hvem ofrer en nydelse, der er inden for rækkevidde, hvis sindet ikke er blevet åbnet og styrket af modgang eller af en søgen efter viden, som nødvendigheden har drevet frem? Det er heldigt, når mennesker har livets bekymringer at kæmpe med, for disse kampe hindrer dem i af ren lediggang at blive bytte for svækkende laster. Men hvis mænd og kvinder fra fødslen anbringes i en brændende varm zone, hvor nydelsens middagssol sender sine stråler lodret ned på dem, hvordan skal de så kunne styrke deres sind nok til at opfylde livets pligter eller blot værdsætte de følelser, som fører dem ud over dem selv?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Pleasure is the business of a woman's life, according to the present modification of society, and while it continues to be so, little can be expected from such weak beings. Inheriting, in a lineal descent from the first fair defect in nature, the sovereignty of beauty, they have, to maintain their power, resigned their natural rights, which the exercise of reason, might have procured them, and chosen rather to be short-lived queens than labour to attain the sober pleasures that arise from equality. Exalted by their inferiority (this sounds like a contradiction) they constantly demand homage as women, though experience should teach them that the men who pride themselves upon paying this arbitrary insolent respect to the sex, with the most scrupulous exactness, are most inclined to tyrannize over, and despise the very weakness they cherish. Often do they repeat Mr. Hume's sentiments; when comparing the French and Athenian character, he alludes to women. "But what is more singular in this whimsical nation, say I to the Athenians, is, that a frolic of yours during the Saturnalia, when the slaves are served by their masters, is seriously continued by them through the whole year, and through the whole course of their lives; accompanied too with some circumstances, which still further augment the absurdity and ridicule. Your sport only elevates for a few days, those whom fortune has thrown down, and whom she too, in sport, may really elevate forever above you. But this nation gravely exalts those, whom nature has subjected to them, and whose inferiority and infirmities are absolutely incurable. The women, though without virtue, are their masters and sovereigns."
danishChanges.after: Efter samfundets nuværende indretning er fornøjelsen kvindens livsopgave, og så længe det fortsætter, kan der ikke forventes meget af så svage væsener. I lige linje fra naturens første smukke fejl har de arvet skønhedens herredømme. For at bevare deres magt har de opgivet de naturlige rettigheder, som brugen af fornuften kunne have skaffet dem, og foretrukket at være dronninger for en kort tid frem for at arbejde for de sindige glæder, der udspringer af lighed. Ophøjet ved deres underlegenhed — det lyder som en selvmodsigelse — kræver de bestandig hyldest som kvinder. Erfaringen burde dog lære dem, at de mænd, som roser sig af med den største omhu at vise kønnet denne vilkårlige og uforskammede respekt, er mest tilbøjelige til at tyrannisere og foragte netop den svaghed, de dyrker. Ofte gentager de hr. Humes synspunkter, når han sammenligner franskmændenes og athenernes karakter og omtaler kvinder: »Men hvad der er endnu mere besynderligt hos dette lunefulde folk, siger jeg til athenerne, er, at det, som hos jer er en spøg under saturnalierne, når slaverne bliver betjent af deres herrer, hos dem fortsættes i ramme alvor gennem hele året og hele livet. Dertil kommer omstændigheder, som yderligere forstærker det absurde og latterlige. Jeres leg ophøjer kun i få dage dem, som lykken har styrtet ned, og som den, ligeledes i spøg, virkelig kan hæve over jer for bestandig. Men dette folk ophøjer alvorligt dem, som naturen har underordnet dem, og hvis underlegenhed og svagheder er fuldstændig uhelbredelige. Kvinderne er, skønt uden dyd, deres herrer og herskere.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Ah! why do women, I write with affectionate solicitude, condescend to receive a degree of attention and respect from strangers, different from that reciprocation of civility which the dictates of humanity, and the politeness of civilization authorise between man and man? And why do they not discover, when "in the noon of beauty's power," that they are treated like queens only to be deluded by hollow respect, till they are led to resign, or not assume, their natural prerogatives? Confined then in cages, like the feathered race, they have nothing to do but to plume themselves, and stalk with mock-majesty from perch to perch. It is true, they are provided with food and raiment, for which they neither toil nor spin; but health, liberty, and virtue are given in exchange. But, where, amongst mankind has been found sufficient strength of mind to enable a being to resign these adventitious prerogatives; one who rising with the calm dignity of reason above opinion, dared to be proud of the privileges inherent in man? and it is vain to expect it whilst hereditary power chokes the affections, and nips reason in the bud.
danishChanges.after: Åh, hvorfor nedlader kvinder sig — jeg skriver med kærlig bekymring — til at modtage en anden slags opmærksomhed og respekt fra fremmede end den gensidige høflighed, som menneskelighedens bud og civilisationens omgangsformer tilsiger mellem mennesker? Og hvorfor opdager de ikke, mens de står »på skønhedsmagtens middagshøjde«, at de kun behandles som dronninger for at blive vildledt af tom respekt, indtil de lader sig overtale til at opgive eller undlade at gøre krav på deres naturlige rettigheder? Når de så er spærret inde i bure som fuglene, har de ikke andet at gøre end at pudse fjerene og spankulere fra pind til pind med påtaget majestæt. Ganske vist får de føde og klæder, som de hverken arbejder eller spinder for, men de betaler med sundhed, frihed og dyd. Men hvor blandt menneskene har man fundet tilstrækkelig åndelig styrke til, at et væsen kan give afkald på disse tilfældige fortrin — et menneske, der med fornuftens rolige værdighed hævede sig over andres mening og vovede at være stolt af de rettigheder, som tilkommer mennesket? Og det er forgæves at vente det, så længe arvelig magt kvæler følelserne for andre og standser fornuftens vækst i opløbet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The passions of men have thus placed women on thrones; and, till mankind become more reasonable, it is to be feared that women will avail themselves of the power which they attain with the least exertion, and which is the most indisputable. They will smile, yes, they will smile, though told that--
danishChanges.after: Mænds lidenskaber har således sat kvinder på troner. Og indtil menneskeheden bliver mere fornuftig, må man frygte, at kvinder vil udnytte den magt, som de opnår med mindst anstrengelse, og som er mest ubestridelig. De vil smile, ja, de vil smile, selv om man siger til dem, at —
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "In beauty's empire is no mean, And woman either slave or queen, Is quickly scorn'd when not ador'd."
danishChanges.after:
»I skønhedens rige findes ingen mellemvej,
og kvinden, enten slave eller dronning,
bliver hurtigt foragtet, når hun ikke tilbedes.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Men tilbedelsen kommer først, og foragten forudses ikke.
danishChanges.after: Men tilbedelsen kommer først, og foragten forudser man ikke.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Lewis the XIVth, in particular, spread factitious manners, and caught in a specious way, the whole nation in his toils; for establishing an artful chain of despotism, he made it the interest of the people at large, individually to respect his station, and support his power. And women, whom he flattered by a puerile attention to the whole sex, obtained in his reign that prince-like distinction so fatal to reason and virtue.
danishChanges.after: Især Ludvig XIV udbredte kunstlede omgangsformer og fangede på en tilforladelig måde hele nationen i sit net. Ved at skabe en snedigt udtænkt kæde af despoti gjorde han det til hvert enkelt menneskes interesse at respektere hans stilling og støtte hans magt. Og kvinderne, som han smigrede ved at vise hele kønnet en barnlig opmærksomhed, opnåede under hans regeringstid den fyrstelige særstilling, der er så ødelæggende for fornuft og dyd.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A king is always a king, and a woman always a woman: (And a wit, always a wit, might be added; for the vain fooleries of wits and beauties to obtain attention, and make conquests, are much upon a par.) his authority and her sex, ever stand between them and rational converse. With a lover, I grant she should be so, and her sensibility will naturally lead her to endeavour to excite emotion, not to gratify her vanity but her heart. This I do not allow to be coquetry, it is the artless impulse of nature, I only exclaim against the sexual desire of conquest, when the heart is out of the question.
danishChanges.after: En konge er altid en konge, og en kvinde altid en kvinde. (Og et vittigt hoved altid et vittigt hoved, kunne man tilføje; for vittige hoveders og skønheders forfængelige tåbeligheder for at få opmærksomhed og gøre erobringer står omtrent lige.) Hans myndighed og hendes køn står bestandig mellem dem og en fornuftig samtale. Over for en elsker indrømmer jeg, at hun bør være kvinde, og hendes følsomhed vil naturligt få hende til at forsøge at vække følelser, ikke for at tilfredsstille sin forfængelighed, men sit hjerte. Dette vil jeg ikke kalde koketteri; det er naturens umiddelbare tilskyndelse. Jeg protesterer kun mod kønnets trang til at erobre, når hjertet ikke har noget med det at gøre.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This desire is not confined to women; "I have endeavoured," says Lord Chesterfield, "to gain the hearts of twenty women, whose persons I would not have given a fig for." The libertine who in a gust of passion, takes advantage of unsuspecting tenderness, is a saint when compared with this cold-hearted rascal; for I like to use significant words. Yet only taught to please, women are always on the watch to please, and with true heroic ardour endeavour to gain hearts merely to resign, or spurn them, when the victory is decided, and conspicuous.
danishChanges.after: Denne trang er ikke begrænset til kvinder. »Jeg har bestræbt mig på,« siger lord Chesterfield, »at vinde tyve kvinders hjerter, skønt jeg ikke ville have givet en døjt for deres personer.« Den libertiner, som i et anfald af lidenskab udnytter en intetanende ømhed, er en helgen sammenlignet med denne koldhjertede slyngel; for jeg foretrækker ord, der siger noget. Men når kvinder kun har lært at behage, er de bestandig på udkig efter at behage og stræber med sandt heroisk ildhu efter at vinde hjerter blot for at slippe dem eller støde dem fra sig, når sejren er sikker og synlig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Jeg må stige ned til emnets små enkeltheder.
danishChanges.after: Jeg må gå ned i emnets enkeltheder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I lament that women are systematically degraded by receiving the trivial attentions, which men think it manly to pay to the sex, when, in fact, they are insultingly supporting their own superiority. It is not condescension to bow to an inferior. So ludicrous, in fact, do these ceremonies appear to me, that I scarcely am able to govern my muscles, when I see a man start with eager, and serious solicitude to lift a handkerchief, or shut a door, when the LADY could have done it herself, had she only moved a pace or two.
danishChanges.after: Jeg beklager, at kvinder systematisk fornedres ved at modtage de ubetydelige opmærksomheder, som mænd mener, det er mandigt at vise kønnet, mens de i virkeligheden på en fornærmende måde befæster deres egen overlegenhed. Man viser ikke nedladenhed ved at bukke for en underordnet. Disse ceremonier forekommer mig faktisk så latterlige, at jeg knap kan holde masken, når jeg ser en mand fare op med ivrig og alvorlig omsorg for at samle et lommetørklæde op eller lukke en dør, som DAMEN selv kunne have klaret, hvis hun blot havde flyttet sig et skridt eller to.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A wild wish has just flown from my heart to my head, and I will not stifle it though it may excite a horse laugh. I do earnestly wish to see the distinction of sex confounded in society, unless where love animates the behaviour. For this distinction is, I am firmly persuaded, the foundation of the weakness of character ascribed to woman; is the cause why the understanding is neglected, whilst accomplishments are acquired with sedulous care: and the same cause accounts for their preferring the graceful before the heroic virtues.
danishChanges.after: Et vildt ønske er netop fløjet fra mit hjerte til mit hoved, og jeg vil ikke kvæle det, selv om det måske vil vække en brølende latter. Jeg ønsker oprigtigt, at skellet mellem kønnene i selskabslivet må udviskes, undtagen hvor kærligheden præger adfærden. For jeg er fast overbevist om, at dette skel er grundlaget for den karaktersvaghed, man tillægger kvinden. Det er årsagen til, at forstanden forsømmes, mens selskabelige færdigheder tilegnes med utrættelig omhu; og samme årsag forklarer, at kvinder foretrækker de yndefulde frem for de heroiske dyder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Mankind, including every description, wish to be loved and respected for SOMETHING; and the common herd will always take the nearest road to the completion of their wishes. The respect paid to wealth and beauty is the most certain and unequivocal; and of course, will always attract the vulgar eye of common minds. Abilities and virtues are absolutely necessary to raise men from the middle rank of life into notice; and the natural consequence is notorious, the middle rank contains most virtue and abilities. Men have thus, in one station, at least, an opportunity of exerting themselves with dignity, and of rising by the exertions which really improve a rational creature; but the whole female sex are, till their character is formed, in the same condition as the rich: for they are born, I now speak of a state of civilization, with certain sexual privileges, and whilst they are gratuitously granted them, few will ever think of works of supererogation, to obtain the esteem of a small number of superior people.
danishChanges.after: Mennesker af enhver slags ønsker at blive elsket og respekteret for NOGET, og den store flok vil altid vælge den korteste vej til at få sine ønsker opfyldt. Respekten for rigdom og skønhed er den sikreste og mest utvetydige og vil derfor altid tiltrække almindelige sinds vulgære blik. Evner og dyder er helt nødvendige, hvis mænd fra samfundets mellemste lag skal gøre sig bemærket. Den naturlige følge er velkendt: Det er i dette lag, man finder mest dyd og flest evner. Mænd har således i det mindste i én samfundsgruppe mulighed for at udfolde sig med værdighed og hæve sig gennem anstrengelser, som virkelig udvikler et fornuftigt væsen. Men hele kvindekønnet befinder sig, indtil karakteren er dannet, i samme situation som de rige. For kvinder fødes — jeg taler nu om et civiliseret samfund — med visse kønsbestemte privilegier. Og så længe de får dem foræret, vil kun få tænke på at yde mere end det nødvendige for at vinde agtelse hos et lille antal fremragende mennesker.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: When do we hear of women, who starting out of obscurity, boldly claim respect on account of their great abilities or daring virtues? Where are they to be found? "To be observed, to be attended to, to be taken notice of with sympathy, complacency, and approbation, are all the advantages which they seek." True! my male readers will probably exclaim; but let them, before they draw any conclusion, recollect, that this was not written originally as descriptive of women, but of the rich. In Dr. Smith's Theory of Moral Sentiments, I have found a general character of people of rank and fortune, that in my opinion, might with the greatest propriety be applied to the female sex. I refer the sagacious reader to the whole comparison; but must be allowed to quote a passage to enforce an argument that I mean to insist on, as the one most conclusive against a sexual character. For if, excepting warriors, no great men of any denomination, have ever appeared amongst the nobility, may it not be fairly inferred, that their local situation swallowed up the man, and produced a character similar to that of women, who are LOCALIZED, if I may be allowed the word, by the rank they are placed in, by COURTESY? Women, commonly called Ladies, are not to be contradicted in company, are not allowed to exert any manual strength; and from them the negative virtues only are expected, when any virtues are expected, patience, docility, good-humour, and flexibility; virtues incompatible with any vigorous exertion of intellect. Besides by living more with each other, and to being seldom absolutely alone, they are more under the influence of sentiments than passions. Solitude and reflection are necessary to give to wishes the force of passions, and enable the imagination to enlarge the object and make it the most desirable. The same may be said of the rich; they do not sufficiently deal in general ideas, collected by impassionate thinking, or calm investigation, to acquire that strength of character, on which great resolves are built. But hear what an acute observer says of the great.
danishChanges.after: Hvornår hører vi om kvinder, der træder frem fra ubemærketheden og modigt kræver respekt for deres store evner eller dristige dyder? Hvor findes de? »At blive set, få opmærksomhed og blive bemærket med medfølelse, velvilje og anerkendelse er alle de fordele, de søger.« Sandt! vil mine mandlige læsere sandsynligvis udbryde. Men før de drager nogen slutning, bør de huske, at dette oprindelig ikke blev skrevet om kvinder, men om de rige. I dr. Smiths Teori om de moralske følelser har jeg fundet en generel beskrivelse af mennesker med rang og formue, som efter min mening med største ret kunne anvendes på kvindekønnet. Jeg henviser den skarpsindige læser til hele sammenligningen, men må have lov til at citere et afsnit for at styrke et argument, jeg vil fastholde som det mest afgørende imod en kønsbestemt karakter. For hvis der bortset fra krigere aldrig er fremstået store mænd af nogen art blandt adelen, kan man da ikke med rimelighed slutte, at deres særlige stilling opslugte mennesket og frembragte en karakter, der lignede kvindernes? Kvinder er jo, hvis jeg må bruge ordet, BUNDET TIL DERES PLADS af den rang, HØFLIGHEDEN tildeler dem. Kvinder, almindeligvis kaldet damer, må ikke modsiges i selskab og får ikke lov til at bruge fysisk styrke. Af dem forventes kun de passive dyder, når der overhovedet forventes dyder: tålmodighed, føjelighed, godt humør og tilpasningsevne — dyder, der er uforenelige med enhver kraftig udfoldelse af intellektet. Desuden lever de mere sammen med hinanden og er sjældent helt alene, og derfor påvirkes de mere af stemninger end af lidenskaber. Ensomhed og eftertanke er nødvendige for at give ønsker lidenskabens styrke og lade fantasien forstørre det ønskede og gøre det mere tillokkende end alt andet. Det samme kan siges om de rige: De beskæftiger sig ikke nok med almene ideer, samlet gennem lidenskabelig tænkning eller rolig undersøgelse, til at opnå den karakterstyrke, som store beslutninger bygger på. Men hør, hvad en skarp iagttager siger om de fornemme.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "Do the great seem insensible of the easy price at which they may acquire the public admiration? or do they seem to imagine, that to them, as to other men, it must be the purchase either of sweat or of blood? By what important accomplishments is the young nobleman instructed to support the dignity of his rank, and to render himself worthy of that superiority over his fellow citizens, to which the virtue of his ancestors had raised them? Is it by knowledge, by industry, by patience, by self-denial, or by virtue of any kind? As all his words, as all his motions are attended to, he learns an habitual regard for every circumstance of ordinary behaviour, and studies to perform all those small duties with the most exact propriety. As he is conscious how much he is observed, and how much mankind are disposed to favour all his inclinations, he acts, upon the most indifferent occasions, with that freedom and elevation which the thought of this naturally inspires. His air, his manner, his deportment all mark that elegant and graceful sense of his own superiority, which those who are born to an inferior station can hardly ever arrive at. These are the arts by which he proposes to make mankind more easily submit to his authority, and to govern their inclinations according to his own pleasure: and in this he is seldom disappointed. These arts, supported by rank and pre-eminence, are, upon ordinary occasions, sufficient to govern the world. Lewis XIV. during the greater part of his reign, was regarded, not only in France, but over all Europe, as the most perfect model of a great prince. But what were the talents and virtues, by which he acquired this great reputation? Was it by the scrupulous and inflexible justice of all his undertakings, by the immense dangers and difficulties with which they were attended, or by the unwearied and unrelenting application with which he pursued them? Was it by his extensive knowledge, by his exquisite judgment, or by his heroic valour? It was by none of these qualities. But he was, first of all, the most powerful prince in Europe, and consequently held the highest rank among kings; and then, says his historian, 'he surpassed all his courtiers in the gracefulness of his shape, and the majestic beauty of his features. The sound of his voice noble and affecting, gained those hearts which his presence intimidated. He had a step and a deportment, which could suit only him and his rank, and which would have been ridiculous in any other person. The embarrassment which he occasioned to those who spoke to him, flattered that secret satisfaction with which he felt his own superiority.' These frivolous accomplishments, supported by his rank, and, no doubt, too, by a degree of other talents and virtues, which seems, however, not to have been much above mediocrity, established this prince in the esteem of his own age, and have drawn even from posterity, a good deal of respect for his memory. Compared with these, in his own times, and in his own presence, no other virtue, it seems, appeared to have any merit. Knowledge, industry, valour, and beneficence, trembling, were abashed, and lost all dignity before them."
danishChanges.after: »Synes de fornemme at være uvidende om, hvor billigt de kan købe offentlighedens beundring? Eller synes de at forestille sig, at den for dem som for andre mennesker må købes med enten sved eller blod? Hvilke vigtige færdigheder lærer den unge adelsmand at bruge for at opretholde sin stands værdighed og gøre sig værdig til den overlegenhed over sine medborgere, som hans forfædres dyd hævede dem til? Er det viden, flid, tålmodighed, selvfornægtelse eller nogen form for dyd? Fordi man lægger mærke til alle hans ord og bevægelser, lærer han vanemæssigt at være opmærksom på enhver omstændighed ved almindelig adfærd og bestræber sig på at udføre alle disse små pligter med den største korrekthed. Fordi han er bevidst om, hvor meget han bliver iagttaget, og hvor tilbøjelige mennesker er til at føje alle hans ønsker, handler han selv ved de mest ligegyldige lejligheder med den frihed og ophøjethed, som tanken om dette naturligt indgiver ham. Hans udtryk, hans væsen og hans holdning viser alle denne elegante og yndefulde bevidsthed om egen overlegenhed, som de, der er født i en lavere stilling, næsten aldrig kan opnå. Med disse kunster vil han få menneskene til lettere at underkaste sig hans myndighed og styre deres tilbøjeligheder efter sit eget forgodtbefindende; og heri bliver han sjældent skuffet. Støttet af rang og forrang er disse kunster under almindelige omstændigheder tilstrækkelige til at styre verden. Ludvig XIV blev gennem størstedelen af sin regeringstid betragtet som det mest fuldkomne forbillede på en stor fyrste, ikke blot i Frankrig, men i hele Europa. Men hvilke evner og dyder skaffede ham dette store ry? Var det den samvittighedsfulde og urokkelige retfærdighed i alle hans foretagender, de vældige farer og vanskeligheder, der ledsagede dem, eller den utrættelige og ubøjelige vedholdenhed, hvormed han gennemførte dem? Var det hans omfattende viden, udsøgte dømmekraft eller heroiske tapperhed? Det var ingen af disse egenskaber. Men først og fremmest var han Europas mægtigste fyrste og havde derfor den højeste rang blandt konger. Og dernæst, siger hans historieskriver, ‘overgik han alle sine hoffolk i sin skikkelses ynde og sine ansigtstræks majestætiske skønhed. Hans stemmes ædle og bevægende klang vandt de hjerter, som hans tilstedeværelse indgød frygt. Han havde en gang og en holdning, som kun kunne passe til ham og hans rang, og som ville have været latterlig hos enhver anden. Den forlegenhed, han fremkaldte hos dem, der talte til ham, smigrede den hemmelige tilfredshed, hvormed han følte sin egen overlegenhed.’ Disse overfladiske fortrin, støttet af hans rang og uden tvivl også af andre evner og dyder i et vist omfang — som dog ikke synes at have ligget meget over det middelmådige — sikrede denne fyrste hans samtids agtelse og har også fået eftertiden til at vise hans minde en god del respekt. Sammenlignet med disse fortrin syntes ingen anden dyd i hans egen tid og i hans nærvær at have nogen fortjeneste. Viden, flid, tapperhed og godgørenhed skælvede, blev forlegne og mistede al værdighed over for dem.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Woman, also, thus "in herself complete," by possessing all these FRIVOLOUS accomplishments, so changes the nature of things,
danishChanges.after: Når kvinden på samme måde er »fuldendt i sig selv« ved at besidde alle disse OVERFLADISKE fortrin, forandrer hun tingenes natur så meget,

danishChanges.before: --"That what she wills to do or say Seems wisest, virtuousest, discreetest, best; All higher knowledge in HER PRESENCE falls Degraded. Wisdom in discourse with her Loses discountenanc'd, and like folly shows; Authority and reason on her wait."--
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Og alt dette bygger på hendes ynde!
danishChanges.after: Og alt dette bygger på hendes yndighed!
