danishChanges.before: In the middle rank of life, to continue the comparison, men, in their youth, are prepared for professions, and marriage is not considered as the grand feature in their lives; whilst women, on the contrary, have no other scheme to sharpen their faculties. It is not business, extensive plans, or any of the excursive flights of ambition, that engross their attention; no, their thoughts are not employed in rearing such noble structures. To rise in the world, and have the liberty of running from pleasure to pleasure, they must marry advantageously, and to this object their time is sacrificed, and their persons often legally prostituted. A man, when he enters any profession, has his eye steadily fixed on some future advantage (and the mind gains great strength by having all its efforts directed to one point) and, full of his business, pleasure is considered as mere relaxation; whilst women seek for pleasure as the main purpose of existence. In fact, from the education which they receive from society, the love of pleasure may be said to govern them all; but does this prove that there is a sex in souls? It would be just as rational to declare, that the courtiers in France, when a destructive system of despotism had formed their character, were not men, because liberty, virtue, and humanity, were sacrificed to pleasure and vanity. Fatal passions, which have ever domineered over the WHOLE race!
danishChanges.after: For at fortsætte sammenligningen: I samfundets mellemste lag bliver mænd i ungdommen forberedt på et erhverv, og ægteskabet betragtes ikke som deres livs hovedsag. Kvinder har derimod ingen anden plan, der kan skærpe deres evner. Det er ikke arbejde, omfattende projekter eller ambitionens vidtrækkende flugt, som optager deres opmærksomhed; nej, deres tanker beskæftiger sig ikke med at rejse så ædle bygningsværker. For at komme frem i verden og få frihed til at løbe fra fornøjelse til fornøjelse må de gifte sig fordelagtigt. Til dette formål ofrer de deres tid og prostituerer ofte deres personer inden for lovens rammer. Når en mand går ind i et erhverv, holder han blikket fast rettet mod en fremtidig fordel — og sindet vinder stor styrke ved, at alle dets anstrengelser rettes mod ét mål. Optaget af sit arbejde betragter han fornøjelsen som ren afslapning, mens kvinder søger fornøjelsen som tilværelsens hovedformål. På grund af den opdragelse, samfundet giver dem, kan man faktisk sige, at kærligheden til fornøjelsen styrer dem alle. Men beviser dette, at sjæle har køn? Det ville være lige så fornuftigt at erklære, at de franske hoffolk, efter at et ødelæggende despotisk system havde formet deres karakter, ikke var mænd, fordi frihed, dyd og menneskelighed blev ofret for fornøjelse og forfængelighed. Skæbnesvangre lidenskaber, som altid har hersket over HELE menneskeslægten!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The same love of pleasure, fostered by the whole tendency of their education, gives a trifling turn to the conduct of women in most circumstances: for instance, they are ever anxious about secondary things; and on the watch for adventures, instead of being occupied by duties.
danishChanges.after: Den samme kærlighed til fornøjelsen, næret af hele deres opdragelses retning, giver kvinders adfærd et overfladisk præg i de fleste situationer. De bekymrer sig for eksempel bestandig om underordnede ting og holder udkig efter oplevelser i stedet for at være optaget af deres pligter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A man, when he undertakes a journey, has, in general the end in view; a woman thinks more of the incidental occurrences, the strange things that may possibly occur on the road; the impression that she may make on her fellow travellers; and, above all, she is anxiously intent on the care of the finery that she carries with her, which is more than ever a part of herself, when going to figure on a new scene; when, to use an apt French turn of expression, she is going to produce a sensation. Can dignity of mind exist with such trivial cares?
danishChanges.after: Når en mand begiver sig ud på en rejse, har han som regel målet for øje. En kvinde tænker mere på de tilfældige hændelser, de mærkelige ting, der måske kan ske undervejs, og det indtryk, hun kan gøre på sine medrejsende. Frem for alt er hun ængsteligt optaget af at passe på den pynt, hun har med sig, og som mere end nogensinde er en del af hende selv, når hun skal vise sig på en ny scene — når hun, for at bruge et rammende fransk udtryk, skal vække sensation. Kan åndelig værdighed forenes med så ubetydelige bekymringer?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In short, women, in general, as well as the rich of both sexes, have acquired all the follies and vices of civilization, and missed the useful fruit. It is not necessary for me always to premise, that I speak of the condition of the whole sex, leaving exceptions out of the question. Their senses are inflamed, and their understandings neglected; consequently they become the prey of their senses, delicately termed sensibility, and are blown about by every momentary gust of feeling. They are, therefore, in a much worse condition than they would be in, were they in a state nearer to nature. Ever restless and anxious, their over exercised sensibility not only renders them uncomfortable themselves, but troublesome, to use a soft phrase, to others. All their thoughts turn on things calculated to excite emotion; and, feeling, when they should reason, their conduct is unstable, and their opinions are wavering, not the wavering produced by deliberation or progressive views, but by contradictory emotions. By fits and starts they are warm in many pursuits; yet this warmth, never concentrated into perseverance, soon exhausts itself; exhaled by its own heat, or meeting with some other fleeting passion, to which reason has never given any specific gravity, neutrality ensues. Miserable, indeed, must be that being whose cultivation of mind has only tended to inflame its passions! A distinction should be made between inflaming and strengthening them. The passions thus pampered, whilst the judgment is left unformed, what can be expected to ensue? Undoubtedly, a mixture of madness and folly!
danishChanges.after: Kort sagt har kvinder i almindelighed, ligesom de rige af begge køn, tilegnet sig alle civilisationens dårskaber og laster og er gået glip af dens nyttige frugter. Det er ikke nødvendigt, at jeg hver gang indleder med at sige, at jeg taler om hele kønnets vilkår og ser bort fra undtagelserne. Deres sanser bliver ophidset, og deres forstand forsømt. Derfor bliver de bytte for deres sanser, som man fint kalder følsomhed, og blæses omkring af hver øjeblikkelig følelsesstorm. De er således langt dårligere stillet, end hvis de levede nærmere naturen. Deres overanstrengte følsomhed gør dem bestandig rastløse og ængstelige, så de ikke blot selv er utilpasse, men også bliver besværlige — for at bruge et mildt ord — for andre. Alle deres tanker kredser om ting, der kan vække følelser; og fordi de føler, når de burde tænke, er deres adfærd ustadig og deres meninger vaklende. Denne vaklen skyldes ikke overvejelse eller en voksende indsigt, men modstridende følelser. I ryk og anfald brænder de for mange foretagender, men denne varme samles aldrig til udholdenhed og udtømmer snart sig selv. Den fordamper i sin egen hede eller møder en anden flygtig lidenskab, som fornuften aldrig har givet nogen vægt, og resultatet bliver ligegyldighed. Det væsen må sandelig være ulykkeligt, hvis åndelige dannelse kun har tjent til at ophidse dets lidenskaber! Man bør skelne mellem at ophidse dem og at styrke dem. Når lidenskaberne forkæles på denne måde, mens dømmekraften forbliver uudviklet, hvad kan man da vente som følge? Uden tvivl en blanding af vanvid og dårskab!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This observation should not be confined to the FAIR sex; however, at present, I only mean to apply it to them.
danishChanges.after: Denne bemærkning bør ikke begrænses til det SMUKKE køn; men her vil jeg kun anvende den på kvinder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Novels, music, poetry and gallantry, all tend to make women the creatures of sensation, and their character is thus formed during the time they are acquiring accomplishments, the only improvement they are excited, by their station in society, to acquire. This overstretched sensibility naturally relaxes the other powers of the mind, and prevents intellect from attaining that sovereignty which it ought to attain, to render a rational creature useful to others, and content with its own station; for the exercise of the understanding, as life advances, is the only method pointed out by nature to calm the passions.
danishChanges.after: Romaner, musik, poesi og galanteri bidrager alle til at gøre kvinder til væsener, der styres af sanseindtryk. Sådan formes deres karakter i den tid, hvor de tilegner sig selskabelige færdigheder, den eneste udvikling, deres plads i samfundet tilskynder dem til. Denne overspændte følsomhed svækker naturligt sindets øvrige kræfter og hindrer intellektet i at opnå det herredømme, det burde have for at gøre et fornuftigt væsen nyttigt for andre og tilfreds med sin egen stilling. For at bruge forstanden, efterhånden som livet skrider frem, er den eneste vej, naturen anviser til at berolige lidenskaberne.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Satiety has a very different effect, and I have often been forcibly struck by an emphatical description of damnation, when the spirit is represented as continually hovering with abortive eagerness round the defiled body, unable to enjoy any thing without the organs of sense. Yet, to their senses, are women made slaves, because it is by their sensibility that they obtain present power.
danishChanges.after: Overmæthed har en ganske anden virkning. Jeg er ofte blevet stærkt ramt af en kraftfuld skildring af fortabelsen, hvor ånden fremstilles som bestandig svævende omkring det besmittede legeme i en frugtesløs længsel, ude af stand til at nyde noget uden sanseorganerne. Alligevel gør man kvinder til slaver af deres sanser, fordi det er gennem deres følsomhed, de opnår magt i nuet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: And will moralists pretend to assert, that this is the condition in which one half of the human race should be encouraged to remain with listless inactivity and stupid acquiescence? Kind instructors! what were we created for? To remain, it may be said, innocent; they mean in a state of childhood. We might as well never have been born, unless it were necessary that we should be created to enable man to acquire the noble privilege of reason, the power of discerning good from evil, whilst we lie down in the dust from whence we were taken, never to rise again.
danishChanges.after: Og vil moralister virkelig hævde, at dette er den tilstand, halvdelen af menneskeslægten bør opmuntres til at blive i med sløv passivitet og tankeløs føjelighed? I venlige læremestre! Hvad blev vi skabt til? Til at forblive uskyldige, vil man måske sige; de mener i en tilstand af barndom. Vi kunne lige så godt aldrig være blevet født, medmindre det var nødvendigt at skabe os for at sætte manden i stand til at opnå fornuftens ædle forret, evnen til at skelne godt fra ondt, mens vi lægger os i det støv, vi blev taget af, og aldrig rejser os igen.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It would be an endless task to trace the variety of meannesses, cares, and sorrows, into which women are plunged by the prevailing opinion, that they were created rather to feel than reason, and that all the power they obtain, must be obtained by their charms and weakness;
danishChanges.after: Det ville være en endeløs opgave at følge alle de former for uværdighed, bekymring og sorg, som kvinder styrtes ud i af den herskende opfattelse, at de blev skabt til at føle snarere end til at tænke, og at al den magt, de opnår, må vindes gennem deres ynde og svaghed;
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "Fine by defect, and amiably weak!"
danishChanges.after: »Smuk ved sin mangel og elskeligt svag!«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: And, made by this amiable weakness entirely dependent, excepting what they gain by illicit sway, on man, not only for protection, but advice, is it surprising that, neglecting the duties that reason alone points out, and shrinking from trials calculated to strengthen their minds, they only exert themselves to give their defects a graceful covering, which may serve to heighten their charms in the eye of the voluptuary, though it sink them below the scale of moral excellence?
danishChanges.after: Når denne elskelige svaghed gør dem helt afhængige af manden, bortset fra hvad de vinder gennem uretmæssig magt, ikke blot for beskyttelse, men også for råd, er det da overraskende, at de forsømmer de pligter, som kun fornuften viser dem, og viger tilbage for prøvelser, der kunne styrke deres sind? De anstrenger sig kun for at give deres mangler et yndefuldt dække, som kan gøre dem mere tillokkende i den sanselige nyders øjne, selv om det sænker dem under den moralske fortræffeligheds målestok.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Fragile in every sense of the word, they are obliged to look up to man for every comfort. In the most trifling dangers they cling to their support, with parasitical tenacity, piteously demanding succour; and their NATURAL protector extends his arm, or lifts up his voice, to guard the lovely trembler--from what? Perhaps the frown of an old cow, or the jump of a mouse; a rat, would be a serious danger. In the name of reason, and even common sense, what can save such beings from contempt; even though they be soft and fair?
danishChanges.after: Skøre i enhver betydning af ordet må de søge enhver trøst hos manden. Ved de ubetydeligste farer klamrer de sig til deres støtte med snylterens vedholdenhed og beder ynkeligt om hjælp. Og deres NATURLIGE beskytter rækker armen ud eller hæver stemmen for at værne den yndige, skælvende skabning — mod hvad? Måske en gammel kos sure blik eller en mus, der springer; en rotte ville være en alvorlig fare. I fornuftens og selv den sunde fornufts navn: Hvad kan redde sådanne væsener fra foragt, selv om de er blide og smukke?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These fears, when not affected, may be very pretty; but they shew a degree of imbecility, that degrades a rational creature in a way women are not aware of--for love and esteem are very distinct things.
danishChanges.after: Disse forskrækkelser kan være meget yndige, når de ikke er påtagede. Men de viser en svaghed, som fornedrer et fornuftigt væsen på en måde, kvinder ikke er klar over; for kærlighed og agtelse er to meget forskellige ting.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I am fully persuaded, that we should hear of none of these infantine airs, if girls were allowed to take sufficient exercise and not confined in close rooms till their muscles are relaxed and their powers of digestion destroyed. To carry the remark still further, if fear in girls, instead of being cherished, perhaps, created, were treated in the same manner as cowardice in boys, we should quickly see women with more dignified aspects. It is true, they could not then with equal propriety be termed the sweet flowers that smile in the walk of man; but they would be more respectable members of society, and discharge the important duties of life by the light of their own reason. "Educate women like men," says Rousseau, "and the more they resemble our sex the less power will they have over us." This is the very point I aim at. I do not wish them to have power over men; but over themselves.
danishChanges.after: Jeg er helt overbevist om, at vi ikke ville høre om nogen af disse barnagtige manerer, hvis piger fik tilstrækkelig motion og ikke blev holdt inde i indelukkede rum, indtil deres muskler var slappe og deres fordøjelse ødelagt. For at føre bemærkningen videre: Hvis frygt hos piger, i stedet for at blive næret og måske ligefrem skabt, blev behandlet ligesom fejhed hos drenge, ville vi hurtigt se kvinder med en mere værdig fremtræden. Ganske vist kunne man så ikke med samme ret kalde dem de søde blomster, der smiler langs mandens vej. Men de ville være mere agtværdige samfundsmedlemmer og opfylde livets vigtige pligter i lyset af deres egen fornuft. »Opdrag kvinder som mænd,« siger Rousseau, »og jo mere de ligner vores køn, desto mindre magt vil de have over os.« Det er netop det, jeg sigter mod. Jeg ønsker ikke, at de skal have magt over mænd, men over sig selv.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In the same strain have I heard men argue against instructing the poor; for many are the forms that aristocracy assumes. "Teach them to read and write," say they, "and you take them out of the station assigned them by nature." An eloquent Frenchman, has answered them; I will borrow his sentiments. But they know not, when they make man a brute, that they may expect every instant to see him transformed into a ferocious beast. Without knowledge there can be no morality!
danishChanges.after: I samme tone har jeg hørt mænd argumentere imod at undervise de fattige; for aristokratiet antager mange former. »Lær dem at læse og skrive,« siger de, »og I fører dem ud af den stilling, naturen har tildelt dem.« En veltalende franskmand har svaret dem; jeg vil låne hans tanker. Men de ved ikke, at når de gør mennesket til et dyr, kan de hvert øjeblik vente at se det forvandlet til et glubsk vilddyr. Uden viden kan der ikke være nogen moral!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Ignorance is a frail base for virtue! Yet, that it is the condition for which woman was organized, has been insisted upon by the writers who have most vehemently argued in favour of the superiority of man; a superiority not in degree, but essence; though, to soften the argument, they have laboured to prove, with chivalrous generosity, that the sexes ought not to be compared; man was made to reason, woman to feel: and that together, flesh and spirit, they make the most perfect whole, by blending happily reason and sensibility into one character.
danishChanges.after: Uvidenhed er et skrøbeligt grundlag for dyd! Alligevel har de forfattere, som mest lidenskabeligt har argumenteret for mandens overlegenhed, hævdet, at det er den tilstand, kvinden er skabt til. Denne overlegenhed gælder ikke blot graden, men selve væsenet. For at mildne argumentet har de dog med ridderlig gavmildhed bestræbt sig på at bevise, at kønnene ikke bør sammenlignes: Manden blev skabt til at tænke, kvinden til at føle, og tilsammen, kød og ånd, udgør de det mest fuldkomne hele ved lykkeligt at forene fornuft og følsomhed i én karakter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: And what is sensibility? "Quickness of sensation; quickness of perception; delicacy." Thus is it defined by Dr. Johnson; and the definition gives me no other idea than of the most exquisitely polished instinct. I discern not a trace of the image of God in either sensation or matter. Refined seventy times seven, they are still material; intellect dwells not there; nor will fire ever make lead gold!
danishChanges.after: Og hvad er følsomhed? »Hurtighed i sansning; hurtighed i opfattelse; finhed.« Sådan definerer dr. Johnson den, og definitionen giver mig ingen anden forestilling end det mest udsøgt forfinede instinkt. Jeg kan ikke se noget spor af Guds billede i hverken sansning eller stof. Selv forfinet halvfjerds gange syv er de stadig materielle; intellektet bor ikke dér, og ild vil aldrig gøre bly til guld!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I come round to my old argument; if woman be allowed to have an immortal soul, she must have as the employment of life, an understanding to improve. And when, to render the present state more complete, though every thing proves it to be but a fraction of a mighty sum, she is incited by present gratification to forget her grand destination. Nature is counteracted, or she was born only to procreate and rot. Or, granting brutes, of every description, a soul, though not a reasonable one, the exercise of instinct and sensibility may be the step, which they are to take, in this life, towards the attainment of reason in the next; so that through all eternity they will lag behind man, who, why we cannot tell, had the power given him of attaining reason in his first mode of existence.
danishChanges.after: Jeg vender tilbage til mit gamle argument: Hvis man anerkender, at kvinden har en udødelig sjæl, må hendes livsopgave være at udvikle sin forstand. Og når hun for at gøre den nuværende tilværelse mere fuldstændig — skønt alt viser, at den kun er en brøkdel af en vældig helhed — tilskyndes af øjeblikkets tilfredsstillelse til at glemme sin store bestemmelse, modarbejder man naturen; ellers blev hun kun født til at avle børn og rådne bort. Eller hvis vi indrømmer dyr af enhver slags en sjæl, om end ikke en fornuftig, kan brugen af instinkt og følsomhed være det skridt, de i dette liv skal tage for at opnå fornuft i det næste. Så vil de gennem hele evigheden halte efter manden, der af grunde, vi ikke kender, fik evnen til at opnå fornuft allerede i sin første tilværelsesform.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: When I treat of the peculiar duties of women, as I should treat of the peculiar duties of a citizen or father, it will be found that I do not mean to insinuate, that they should be taken out of their families, speaking of the majority. "He that hath wife and children," says Lord Bacon, "hath given hostages to fortune; for they are impediments to great enterprises, either of virtue or mischief. Certainly the best works, and of greatest merit for the public, have proceeded from the unmarried or childless men." I say the same of women. But, the welfare of society is not built on extraordinary exertions; and were it more reasonably organized, there would be still less need of great abilities, or heroic virtues. In the regulation of a family, in the education of children, understanding, in an unsophisticated sense, is particularly required: strength both of body and mind; yet the men who, by their writings, have most earnestly laboured to domesticate women, have endeavoured by arguments dictated by a gross appetite, that satiety had rendered fastidious, to weaken their bodies and cramp their minds. But, if even by these sinister methods they really PERSUADED women, by working on their feelings, to stay at home, and fulfil the duties of a mother and mistress of a family, I should cautiously oppose opinions that led women to right conduct, by prevailing on them to make the discharge of a duty the business of life, though reason were insulted. Yet, and I appeal to experience, if by neglecting the understanding they are as much, nay, more attached from these domestic duties, than they could be by the most serious intellectual pursuit, though it may be observed, that the mass of mankind will never vigorously pursue an intellectual object, I may be allowed to infer, that reason is absolutely necessary to enable a woman to perform any duty properly, and I must again repeat, that sensibility is not reason.
danishChanges.after: Når jeg behandler kvinders særlige pligter, sådan som jeg ville behandle en borgers eller en fars særlige pligter, vil det vise sig, at jeg ikke mener at antyde, at de skal tages ud af deres familier — jeg taler om flertallet. »Den, der har hustru og børn,« siger lord Bacon, »har givet skæbnen gidsler; for de er hindringer for store foretagender, hvad enten disse tjener det gode eller det onde. De bedste værker og dem, der har været til størst gavn for offentligheden, er ganske vist kommet fra ugifte eller barnløse mænd.« Jeg siger det samme om kvinder. Men samfundets velfærd bygger ikke på usædvanlige anstrengelser, og var det mere fornuftigt indrettet, ville der være endnu mindre behov for store evner eller heroiske dyder. At lede en familie og opdrage børn kræver især forstand i ordets enkle betydning: styrke i både krop og sind. Alligevel har de mænd, der i deres skrifter mest ihærdigt har arbejdet for at binde kvinder til hjemmet, forsøgt at svække deres kroppe og indsnævre deres sind med argumenter dikteret af et groft begær, som overmæthed har gjort kræsent. Men hvis de selv med disse skumle metoder virkelig OVERTALTE kvinder ved at påvirke deres følelser til at blive hjemme og opfylde en mors og husmoders pligter, ville jeg kun med forsigtighed modsætte mig anskuelser, der førte kvinder til rigtig adfærd ved at få dem til at gøre opfyldelsen af en pligt til livets opgave, selv om fornuften blev krænket. Men hvis forsømmelsen af forstanden — og her påberåber jeg mig erfaringen — fjerner dem lige så meget, ja mere fra disse huslige pligter, end selv den alvorligste intellektuelle beskæftigelse kunne gøre, må jeg have lov til at slutte, at fornuften er absolut nødvendig, hvis en kvinde skal opfylde nogen pligt ordentligt. Man kan ganske vist bemærke, at menneskehedens flertal aldrig energisk vil forfølge et intellektuelt mål. Men jeg må endnu en gang gentage, at følsomhed ikke er fornuft.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The comparison with the rich still occurs to me; for, when men neglect the duties of humanity, women will do the same; a common stream hurries them both along with thoughtless celerity. Riches and honours prevent a man from enlarging his understanding, and enervate all his powers, by reversing the order of nature, which has ever made true pleasure the reward of labour. Pleasure--enervating pleasure is, likewise, within woman's reach without earning it. But, till hereditary possessions are spread abroad, how can we expect men to be proud of virtue? And, till they are, women will govern them by the most direct means, neglecting their dull domestic duties, to catch the pleasure that is on the wing of time.
danishChanges.after: Sammenligningen med de rige bliver ved med at melde sig for mig. For når mænd forsømmer menneskelighedens pligter, vil kvinder gøre det samme; en fælles strøm river dem begge tankeløst med sig. Rigdom og æresbevisninger hindrer en mand i at udvide sin forstand og svækker alle hans kræfter ved at vende naturens orden om, som altid har gjort sand nydelse til lønnen for arbejde. Nydelse — svækkende nydelse — er ligeledes inden for kvindens rækkevidde, uden at hun har fortjent den. Men hvordan kan vi vente, at mænd skal være stolte af dyden, før arvede besiddelser bliver fordelt mere bredt? Og indtil da vil kvinder styre dem med de mest direkte midler og forsømme deres kedelige pligter i hjemmet for at gribe den fornøjelse, som flyver bort på tidens vinger.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "The power of women," says some author, "is her sensibility;" and men not aware of the consequence, do all they can to make this power swallow up every other. Those who constantly employ their sensibility will have most: for example; poets, painters, and composers. Yet, when the sensibility is thus increased at the expense of reason, and even the imagination, why do philosophical men complain of their fickleness? The sexual attention of man particularly acts on female sensibility, and this sympathy has been exercised from their youth up. A husband cannot long pay those attentions with the passion necessary to excite lively emotions, and the heart, accustomed to lively emotions, turns to a new lover, or pines in secret, the prey of virtue or prudence. I mean when the heart has really been rendered susceptible, and the taste formed; for I am apt to conclude, from what I have seen in fashionable life, that vanity is oftener fostered than sensibility by the mode of education, and the intercourse between the sexes, which I have reprobated; and that coquetry more frequently proceeds from vanity than from that inconstancy, which overstrained sensibility naturally produces.
danishChanges.after: »Kvindens magt,« siger en forfatter, »er hendes følsomhed.« Og mænd gør, uden at være klar over følgerne, alt, hvad de kan, for at lade denne magt opsluge enhver anden. De, der bestandig bruger deres følsomhed, vil have mest af den, for eksempel digtere, malere og komponister. Men når følsomheden således vokser på bekostning af fornuften og selv fantasien, hvorfor klager filosofiske mænd så over deres ustadighed? Mandens kønslige opmærksomhed påvirker især kvindens følsomhed, og denne følelsesmæssige gensidighed er blevet øvet fra ungdommen. En ægtemand kan ikke længe vise denne opmærksomhed med den lidenskab, som er nødvendig for at vække stærke følelser. Og hjertet, der er vant til stærke følelser, vender sig mod en ny elsker eller sygner i hemmelighed hen som offer for dyd eller forsigtighed. Jeg mener de tilfælde, hvor hjertet virkelig er blevet modtageligt og smagen udviklet. For ud fra det, jeg har set i det mondæne liv, er jeg tilbøjelig til at slutte, at den opdragelse og omgang mellem kønnene, som jeg har fordømt, oftere nærer forfængelighed end følsomhed, og at koketteri oftere udspringer af forfængelighed end af den ustadighed, en overspændt følsomhed naturligt frembringer.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Another argument that has had a great weight with me, must, I think, have some force with every considerate benevolent heart. Girls, who have been thus weakly educated, are often cruelly left by their parents without any provision; and, of course, are dependent on, not only the reason, but the bounty of their brothers. These brothers are, to view the fairest side of the question, good sort of men, and give as a favour, what children of the same parents had an equal right to. In this equivocal humiliating situation, a docile female may remain some time, with a tolerable degree of comfort. But, when the brother marries, a probable circumstance, from being considered as the mistress of the family, she is viewed with averted looks as an intruder, an unnecessary burden on the benevolence of the master of the house, and his new partner.
danishChanges.after: Et andet argument, som har vejet tungt for mig, må efter min mening have en vis vægt for ethvert eftertænksomt og velvilligt hjerte. Piger, der har fået en så svækkende opdragelse, bliver ofte grusomt efterladt af deres forældre uden midler til deres underhold og er derfor afhængige ikke blot af deres brødres fornuft, men også af deres gavmildhed. Set fra den gunstigste side er disse brødre gode og ordentlige mænd, som giver som en gunst, hvad børn af de samme forældre havde lige ret til. I denne tvetydige og ydmygende stilling kan en føjelig kvinde i nogen tid leve nogenlunde behageligt. Men når broderen gifter sig, hvad der sandsynligvis vil ske, går hun fra at blive betragtet som husets frue til at blive mødt med bortvendte blikke som en indtrænger, en unødvendig byrde for husets herres og hans nye livsledsagers godgørenhed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Who can recount the misery, which many unfortunate beings, whose minds and bodies are equally weak, suffer in such situations--unable to work and ashamed to beg? The wife, a cold-hearted, narrow-minded woman, and this is not an unfair supposition; for the present mode of education does not tend to enlarge the heart any more than the understanding, is jealous of the little kindness which her husband shows to his relations; and her sensibility not rising to humanity, she is displeased at seeing the property of HER children lavished on an helpless sister.
danishChanges.after: Hvem kan opregne den elendighed, som mange ulykkelige væsener, hvis sind og krop er lige svage, lider i sådanne situationer — ude af stand til at arbejde og skamfulde ved at tigge? Hustruen, en koldhjertet og snæversynet kvinde — og det er ingen urimelig antagelse, for den nuværende opdragelse udvider ikke hjertet mere end forstanden — er jaloux på den smule venlighed, hendes mand viser sine slægtninge. Og da hendes følsomhed ikke hæver sig til menneskelighed, er hun utilfreds med at se SINE børns ejendom ødslet bort på en hjælpeløs søster.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These are matters of fact, which have come under my eye again and again. The consequence is obvious, the wife has recourse to cunning to undermine the habitual affection, which she is afraid openly to oppose; and neither tears nor caresses are spared till the spy is worked out of her home, and thrown on the world, unprepared for its difficulties; or sent, as a great effort of generosity, or from some regard to propriety, with a small stipend, and an uncultivated mind into joyless solitude.
danishChanges.after: Dette er faktiske forhold, som jeg har set igen og igen. Følgen er indlysende: Hustruen griber til list for at undergrave den indgroede hengivenhed, hun ikke tør bekæmpe åbent. Hun sparer hverken tårer eller kærtegn, før spionen er manøvreret ud af sit hjem og kastet ud i verden, uforberedt på dens vanskeligheder. Eller også bliver søsteren, som et stort udslag af gavmildhed eller af et vist hensyn til anstændigheden, sendt med en lille understøttelse og et udannet sind ud i en glædesløs ensomhed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These two women may be much upon a par, with respect to reason and humanity; and changing situations, might have acted just the same selfish part; but had they been differently educated, the case would also have been very different. The wife would not have had that sensibility, of which self is the centre, and reason might have taught her not to expect, and not even to be flattered by the affection of her husband, if it led him to violate prior duties. She would wish not to love him, merely because he loved her, but on account of his virtues; and the sister might have been able to struggle for herself, instead of eating the bitter bread of dependence.
danishChanges.after: Disse to kvinder står måske omtrent lige, hvad fornuft og menneskelighed angår, og hvis de byttede plads, kunne de have spillet nøjagtig den samme selviske rolle. Men havde de fået en anden opdragelse, ville sagen også have været helt anderledes. Hustruen ville ikke have haft den følsomhed, som har selvet som sit centrum, og fornuften kunne have lært hende ikke at forvente eller blot føle sig smigret af sin mands kærlighed, hvis den fik ham til at tilsidesætte tidligere pligter. Hun ville ønske at elske ham, ikke blot fordi han elskede hende, men på grund af hans dyder. Og søsteren kunne have været i stand til at kæmpe for sig selv i stedet for at spise afhængighedens bitre brød.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I am, indeed, persuaded that the heart, as well as the understanding, is opened by cultivation; and by, which may not appear so clear, strengthening the organs; I am not now talking of momentary flashes of sensibility, but of affections. And, perhaps, in the education of both sexes, the most difficult task is so to adjust instruction as not to narrow the understanding, whilst the heart is warmed by the generous juices of spring, just raised by the electric fermentation of the season; nor to dry up the feelings by employing the mind in investigations remote from life.
danishChanges.after: Jeg er faktisk overbevist om, at hjertet ligesom forstanden åbnes gennem dannelse og — hvad der måske virker mindre indlysende — ved at styrke kroppens organer. Jeg taler ikke her om øjeblikkelige glimt af følsomhed, men om varige følelser. Og måske er den vanskeligste opgave i opdragelsen af begge køn at tilrettelægge undervisningen, så forstanden ikke indsnævres, mens hjertet varmes af forårets livgivende safter, som netop er steget op i årstidens elektriske gæring; og samtidig undgå at udtørre følelserne ved at lade sindet beskæftige sig med undersøgelser, der ligger fjernt fra livet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: With respect to women, when they receive a careful education, they are either made fine ladies, brimful of sensibility, and teeming with capricious fancies; or mere notable women. The latter are often friendly, honest creatures, and have a shrewd kind of good sense joined with worldly prudence, that often render them more useful members of society than the fine sentimental lady, though they possess neither greatness of mind nor taste. The intellectual world is shut against them; take them out of their family or neighbourhood, and they stand still; the mind finding no employment, for literature affords a fund of amusement, which they have never sought to relish, but frequently to despise. The sentiments and taste of more cultivated minds appear ridiculous, even in those whom chance and family connexions have led them to love; but in mere acquaintance they think it all affectation.
danishChanges.after: Når kvinder får en omhyggelig opdragelse, bliver de enten gjort til fine damer, fulde af følsomhed og lunefulde indfald, eller til rene husholdningsmennesker. De sidste er ofte venlige og hæderlige og har en skarp praktisk sans, som sammen med verdslig omtanke tit gør dem til nyttigere samfundsmedlemmer end den fine, følsomme dame, selv om de hverken har åndelig storhed eller smag. Den intellektuelle verden er lukket for dem. Tag dem ud af deres familie eller nabolag, og de går i stå; sindet finder ingen beskæftigelse, for litteraturens rige kilde til underholdning har de aldrig søgt at værdsætte, men ofte at foragte. Mere dannede sinds følelser og smag forekommer dem latterlige, selv hos dem, som tilfældet og familiebånd har fået dem til at elske. Hos folk, de blot kender, regner de det hele for skaberi.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A man of sense can only love such a woman on account of her sex, and respect her, because she is a trusty servant. He lets her, to preserve his own peace, scold the servants, and go to church in clothes made of the very best materials. A man of her own size of understanding would, probably, not agree so well with her; for he might wish to encroach on her prerogative, and manage some domestic concerns himself. Yet women, whose minds are not enlarged by cultivation, or the natural selfishness of sensibility expanded by reflection, are very unfit to manage a family; for by an undue stretch of power, they are always tyrannizing to support a superiority that only rests on the arbitrary distinction of fortune. The evil is sometimes more serious, and domestics are deprived of innocent indulgences, and made to work beyond their strength, in order to enable the notable woman to keep a better table, and outshine her neighbours in finery and parade. If she attend to her children, it is, in general, to dress them in a costly manner--and, whether, this attention arises from vanity or fondness, it is equally pernicious.
danishChanges.after: En forstandig mand kan kun elske sådan en kvinde på grund af hendes køn og respektere hende, fordi hun er en pålidelig tjener. For at bevare sin egen fred lader han hende skælde tjenestefolkene ud og gå i kirke i tøj af de allerbedste stoffer. En mand med en forstand på størrelse med hendes ville sandsynligvis ikke komme så godt ud af det med hende, for han kunne ønske at gribe ind i hendes beføjelser og selv styre nogle af hjemmets anliggender. Men kvinder, hvis sind ikke er blevet udvidet gennem dannelse, eller hvis følsomheds naturlige selvoptagethed ikke er blevet udvidet gennem eftertanke, er meget uegnede til at lede en familie. Ved at strække deres magt for langt tyranniserer de bestandig for at opretholde en overlegenhed, der kun hviler på den vilkårlige forskel i formue. Undertiden er ondet alvorligere: Tjenestefolk berøves uskyldige fornøjelser og sættes til at arbejde ud over deres kræfter, for at den dygtige husmoder kan servere bedre mad og overstråle naboerne med pynt og pragt. Hvis hun tager sig af sine børn, er det som regel for at klæde dem kostbart på; og hvad enten denne opmærksomhed udspringer af forfængelighed eller kærlighed, er den lige skadelig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, how many women of this description pass their days, or, at least their evenings, discontentedly. Their husbands acknowledge that they are good managers, and chaste wives; but leave home to seek for more agreeable, may I be allowed to use a significant French word, piquant society; and the patient drudge, who fulfils her task, like a blind horse in a mill, is defrauded of her just reward; for the wages due to her are the caresses of her husband; and women who have so few resources in themselves, do not very patiently bear this privation of a natural right.
danishChanges.after: Hvor mange kvinder af denne slags tilbringer desuden ikke deres dage, eller i det mindste deres aftener, i utilfredshed? Deres mænd anerkender, at de er gode husholdere og kyske hustruer, men forlader hjemmet for at søge mere behageligt og — hvis jeg må bruge et rammende fransk ord — pikant selskab. Og den tålmodige slider, som udfører sin opgave som en blind hest i en mølle, bliver snydt for sin retmæssige løn; for den løn, hun har til gode, er hendes mands kærtegn. Kvinder, som har så få ressourcer i sig selv, bærer ikke særlig tålmodigt dette tab af en naturlig ret.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A fine lady, on the contrary, has been taught to look down with contempt on the vulgar employments of life; though she has only been incited to acquire accomplishments that rise a degree above sense; for even corporeal accomplishments cannot be acquired with any degree of precision, unless the understanding has been strengthened by exercise. Without a foundation of principles taste is superficial; and grace must arise from something deeper than imitation. The imagination, however, is heated, and the feelings rendered fastidious, if not sophisticated; or, a counterpoise of judgment is not acquired, when the heart still remains artless, though it becomes too tender.
danishChanges.after: En fin dame er derimod blevet lært at se ned på livets almindelige beskæftigelser med foragt, selv om hun kun er blevet tilskyndet til at tilegne sig færdigheder, der hæver sig et trin over det rent sanselige. For selv kropslige færdigheder kan ikke opøves med nogen præcision, medmindre forstanden er blevet styrket gennem øvelse. Uden et grundlag af principper er smagen overfladisk, og ynde må udspringe af noget dybere end efterligning. Fantasien bliver imidlertid ophidset, og følelserne bliver kræsne, om ikke kunstlede; eller også udvikles dømmekraften ikke som modvægt, når hjertet stadig er umiddelbart, men bliver alt for ømtåleligt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These women are often amiable; and their hearts are really more sensible to general benevolence, more alive to the sentiments that civilize life, than the square elbowed family drudge; but, wanting a due proportion of reflection and self-government, they only inspire love; and are the mistresses of their husbands, whilst they have any hold on their affections; and the platonic friends of his male acquaintance. These are the fair defects in nature; the women who appear to be created not to enjoy the fellowship of man, but to save him from sinking into absolute brutality, by rubbing off the rough angles of his character; and by playful dalliance to give some dignity to the appetite that draws him to them. Gracious Creator of the whole human race! hast thou created such a being as woman, who can trace thy wisdom in thy works, and feel that thou alone art by thy nature, exalted above her--for no better purpose? Can she believe that she was only made to submit to man her equal; a being, who, like her, was sent into the world to acquire virtue? Can she consent to be occupied merely to please him; merely to adorn the earth, when her soul is capable of rising to thee? And can she rest supinely dependent on man for reason, when she ought to mount with him the arduous steeps of knowledge?
danishChanges.after: Disse kvinder er ofte elskværdige, og deres hjerter er virkelig mere modtagelige for almindelig velvilje og mere levende over for de følelser, der civiliserer livet, end den kantede, slidende husmoders. Men fordi de mangler tilstrækkelig eftertanke og selvbeherskelse, vækker de kun kærlighed. De er deres ægtemænds elskerinder, så længe de har noget greb om deres følelser, og de platoniske veninder for mændenes mandlige bekendte. Dette er naturens smukke fejl: kvinderne, som synes skabt, ikke til at dele fællesskabet med manden, men til at redde ham fra at synke ned i ren dyriskhed ved at slibe de ru kanter af hans karakter og gennem legende kærtegn give en vis værdighed til det begær, der drager ham til dem. Nådige skaber af hele menneskeslægten! Har du ikke skabt et væsen som kvinden til noget bedre — hende, der kan spore din visdom i dine værker og føle, at kun du ved din natur er hævet over hende? Kan hun tro, at hun blot blev skabt til at underkaste sig manden, sin ligemand, et væsen, der ligesom hun blev sendt ind i verden for at tilegne sig dyd? Kan hun gå med til kun at beskæftige sig med at behage ham, kun at pryde jorden, når hendes sjæl kan hæve sig til dig? Og kan hun forblive passivt afhængig af manden for at få fornuft, når hun sammen med ham burde bestige kundskabens stejle skrænter?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Yet, if love be the supreme good, let women be only educated to inspire it, and let every charm be polished to intoxicate the senses; but, if they are moral beings, let them have a chance to become intelligent; and let love to man be only a part of that glowing flame of universal love, which, after encircling humanity, mounts in grateful incense to God.
danishChanges.after: Men hvis kærligheden er det højeste gode, så lad kvinder alene blive opdraget til at vække den, og lad enhver ynde blive forfinet, så den beruser sanserne. Hvis de derimod er moralske væsener, så giv dem en mulighed for at blive indsigtsfulde, og lad kærligheden til manden kun være en del af den glødende flamme af universel kærlighed, som efter at have omsluttet menneskeheden stiger op som taknemmelig røgelse til Gud.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To fulfil domestic duties much resolution is necessary, and a serious kind of perseverance that requires a more firm support than emotions, however lively and true to nature. To give an example of order, the soul of virtue, some austerity of behaviour must be adopted, scarcely to be expected from a being who, from its infancy, has been made the weathercock of its own sensations. Whoever rationally means to be useful, must have a plan of conduct; and, in the discharge of the simplest duty, we are often obliged to act contrary to the present impulse of tenderness or compassion. Severity is frequently the most certain, as well as the most sublime proof of affection; and the want of this power over the feelings, and of that lofty, dignified affection, which makes a person prefer the future good of the beloved object to a present gratification, is the reason why so many fond mothers spoil their children, and has made it questionable, whether negligence or indulgence is most hurtful: but I am inclined to think, that the latter has done most harm.
danishChanges.after: At opfylde pligterne i hjemmet kræver stor beslutsomhed og en alvorlig udholdenhed, som må have en fastere støtte end følelser, hvor levende og naturlige de end er. For at være et eksempel på orden, dydens sjæl, må man udvise en vis strenghed i sin adfærd, som næppe kan forventes af et væsen, der fra barndommen er blevet gjort til en vejrhane for sine egne fornemmelser. Den, som fornuftigt vil være til nytte, må have en plan for sin adfærd. Og når vi opfylder selv den enkleste pligt, må vi ofte handle imod øjeblikkets tilskyndelse til ømhed eller medfølelse. Strenghed er ofte det sikreste og samtidig mest ophøjede bevis på kærlighed. Manglen på dette herredømme over følelserne og på den ophøjede, værdige kærlighed, som får et menneske til at foretrække den elskedes fremtidige bedste frem for øjeblikkelig tilfredsstillelse, er grunden til, at så mange kærlige mødre forkæler deres børn. Den har rejst tvivl om, hvorvidt forsømmelse eller eftergivenhed gør mest skade; men jeg hælder til, at det sidste har gjort størst skade.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Mankind seem to agree, that children should be left under the management of women during their childhood. Now, from all the observation that I have been able to make, women of sensibility are the most unfit for this task, because they will infallibly, carried away by their feelings, spoil a child's temper. The management of the temper, the first and most important branch of education, requires the sober steady eye of reason; a plan of conduct equally distant from tyranny and indulgence; yet these are the extremes that people of sensibility alternately fall into; always shooting beyond the mark. I have followed this train of reasoning much further, till I have concluded, that a person of genius is the most improper person to be employed in education, public or private. Minds of this rare species see things too much in masses, and seldom, if ever, have a good temper. That habitual cheerfulness, termed good humour, is, perhaps, as seldom united with great mental powers, as with strong feelings. And those people who follow, with interest and admiration, the flights of genius; or, with cooler approbation suck in the instruction, which has been elaborately prepared for them by the profound thinker, ought not to be disgusted, if they find the former choleric, and the latter morose; because liveliness of fancy, and a tenacious comprehension of mind, are scarcely compatible with that pliant urbanity which leads a man, at least to bend to the opinions and prejudices of others, instead of roughly confronting them.
danishChanges.after: Menneskene synes enige om, at børn i barndommen bør overlades til kvinders omsorg. Men ud fra alle de iagttagelser, jeg har kunnet gøre, er følsomme kvinder de mest uegnede til denne opgave, fordi de, revet med af deres følelser, uvægerligt vil ødelægge barnets sindelag. At forme sindelaget, opdragelsens første og vigtigste del, kræver fornuftens nøgterne, rolige blik og en plan for adfærden, som ligger lige langt fra tyranni og eftergivenhed. Men netop disse yderpunkter falder følsomme mennesker skiftevis i; de skyder altid over målet. Jeg har fulgt denne tankegang langt videre og er kommet til den slutning, at et geni er den mest uegnede person til at beskæftige sig med opdragelse, offentlig eller privat. Sind af denne sjældne art ser tingene for meget i store helheder og har sjældent, om nogensinde, et godt sindelag. Den vanemæssige munterhed, man kalder godt humør, er måske lige så sjældent forenet med store åndsevner som med stærke følelser. Og de, der med interesse og beundring følger geniets flugt eller med køligere anerkendelse suger den undervisning til sig, som den dybe tænker møjsommeligt har forberedt for dem, bør ikke føle afsky, hvis de finder den første hidsig og den anden gnaven. For en livlig fantasi og en vedholdende åndelig fatteevne er næppe forenelige med den smidige høflighed, som i det mindste får et menneske til at bøje sig for andres meninger og fordomme i stedet for at støde hårdt imod dem.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, treating of education or manners, minds of a superior class are not to be considered, they may be left to chance; it is the multitude, with moderate abilities, who call for instruction, and catch the colour of the atmosphere they breathe. This respectable concourse, I contend, men and women, should not have their sensations heightened in the hot-bed of luxurious indolence, at the expence of their understanding; for, unless there be a ballast of understanding, they will never become either virtuous or free: an aristocracy, founded on property, or sterling talents, will ever sweep before it, the alternately timid and ferocious slaves of feeling.
danishChanges.after: Men når vi taler om opdragelse eller omgangsformer, er det ikke de fremragende ånder, vi skal tage hensyn til; de kan overlades til tilfældet. Det er de mange med almindelige evner, der har brug for undervisning og tager farve af den atmosfære, de ånder i. Jeg hævder, at denne agtværdige skare, mænd og kvinder, ikke bør få deres sanseindtryk skærpet i den luksuriøse lediggangs drivhus på bekostning af forstanden. For uden forstandens ballast vil de aldrig blive hverken dydige eller frie. Et aristokrati, der bygger på ejendom eller ægte evner, vil altid feje følelsens skiftevis frygtsomme og rasende slaver foran sig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Numberless are the arguments, to take another view of the subject, brought forward with a show of reason; because supposed to be deduced from nature, that men have used morally and physically to degrade the sex. I must notice a few.
danishChanges.after: For at se emnet fra en anden side: Utallige er de argumenter, som mænd har brugt til at fornedre kønnet moralsk og fysisk, og som fremsættes med et skær af fornuft, fordi de antages at være udledt af naturen. Jeg må nævne nogle få.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The female understanding has often been spoken of with contempt, as arriving sooner at maturity than the male. I shall not answer this argument by alluding to the early proofs of reason, as well as genius, in Cowley, Milton, and Pope, (Many other names might be added.) but only appeal to experience to decide whether young men, who are early introduced into company (and examples now abound) do not acquire the same precocity. So notorious is this fact, that the bare mentioning of it must bring before people, who at all mix in the world, the idea of a number of swaggering apes of men whose understandings are narrowed by being brought into the society of men when they ought to have been spinning a top or twirling a hoop.
danishChanges.after: Man har ofte talt foragteligt om kvinders forstand, fordi den skulle modnes tidligere end mænds. Jeg vil ikke svare på dette argument ved at henvise til de tidlige tegn på både fornuft og geni hos Cowley, Milton og Pope (mange andre navne kunne tilføjes), men blot lade erfaringen afgøre, om unge mænd, der tidligt indføres i selskabslivet — og eksemplerne er nu talrige — ikke bliver lige så tidligt modne. Denne kendsgerning er så velkendt, at blot det at nævne den må få enhver, der overhovedet færdes i verden, til at tænke på en række pralende efterabere af voksne mænd, hvis forstand er blevet indsnævret, fordi de kom i voksnes selskab på et tidspunkt, hvor de burde have leget med snurretop eller tøndebånd.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It has also been asserted, by some naturalists, that men do not attain their full growth and strength till thirty; but that women arrive at maturity by twenty. I apprehend that they reason on false ground, led astray by the male prejudice, which deems beauty the perfection of woman--mere beauty of features and complexion, the vulgar acceptation of the world, whilst male beauty is allowed to have some connexion with the mind. Strength of body, and that character of countenance, which the French term a physionomie, women do not acquire before thirty, any more than men. The little artless tricks of children, it is true, are particularly pleasing and attractive; yet, when the pretty freshness of youth is worn off, these artless graces become studied airs, and disgust every person of taste. In the countenance of girls we only look for vivacity and bashful modesty; but, the springtide of life over, we look for soberer sense in the face, and for traces of passion, instead of the dimples of animal spirits; expecting to see individuality of character, the only fastener of the affections. We then wish to converse, not to fondle; to give scope to our imaginations, as well as to the sensations of our hearts.
danishChanges.after: Nogle naturforskere har også hævdet, at mænd ikke når deres fulde vækst og styrke før trediveårsalderen, mens kvinder er fuldt udviklede ved tyve. Jeg formoder, at de ræsonnerer ud fra et forkert grundlag, vildledt af den mandlige fordom, som anser skønhed for kvindens fuldkommenhed — blot skønhed i ansigtstræk og hudfarve, sådan som verden almindeligvis forstår ordet, mens mandlig skønhed får lov til at have en vis forbindelse med sindet. Kvinder opnår lige så lidt som mænd kroppens styrke og det særpræg i ansigtet, som franskmændene kalder en fysionomi, før de er tredive. Børns små, umiddelbare påfund er ganske vist særligt behagelige og tiltrækkende. Men når ungdommens kønne friskhed er slidt af, bliver disse naturlige ynder til indstuderede manerer, som vækker afsky hos enhver med smag. I pigers ansigter søger vi kun livlighed og genert blufærdighed. Men når livets forår er forbi, søger vi et mere sindigt vid i ansigtet og spor af lidenskab i stedet for livsglædens smilehuller. Vi forventer at se karakterens individuelle præg, det eneste, der kan fastholde kærligheden. Da ønsker vi at samtale, ikke at kæle, og at give vores fantasi såvel som hjertets følelser spillerum.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: At twenty the beauty of both sexes is equal; but the libertinism of man leads him to make the distinction, and superannuated coquettes are commonly of the same opinion; for when they can no longer inspire love, they pay for the vigour and vivacity of youth. The French who admit more of mind into their notions of beauty, give the preference to women of thirty. I mean to say, that they allow women to be in their most perfect state, when vivacity gives place to reason, and to that majestic seriousness of character, which marks maturity; or, the resting point. In youth, till twenty the body shoots out; till thirty the solids are attaining a degree of density; and the flexible muscles, growing daily more rigid, give character to the countenance; that is, they trace the operations of the mind with the iron pen of fate, and tell us not only what powers are within, but how they have been employed.
danishChanges.after: Ved tyveårsalderen er de to køns skønhed lige stor. Men mandens tøjlesløse seksualitet får ham til at skelne, og aldrende koketter er som regel af samme mening; for når de ikke længere kan vække kærlighed, betaler de for ungdommens kraft og livlighed. Franskmændene, som giver sindet større plads i deres forestillinger om skønhed, foretrækker kvinder på tredive. Jeg mener, at de anerkender kvinder som mest fuldkomne, når livligheden viger for fornuften og for den majestætiske alvor i karakteren, som kendetegner modenheden eller ligevægtspunktet. I ungdommen frem til tyveårsalderen skyder kroppen i vejret; frem til tredive får de faste væv en vis tæthed, og de smidige muskler, som dag for dag bliver stivere, giver ansigtet karakter. Det vil sige, at de med skæbnens jerngriffel indtegner sindets virksomhed og ikke blot fortæller os, hvilke kræfter der findes indeni, men også hvordan de er blevet brugt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is proper to observe, that animals who arrive slowly at maturity, are the longest lived, and of the noblest species. Men cannot, however, claim any natural superiority from the grandeur of longevity; for in this respect nature has not distinguished the male.
danishChanges.after: Det bør bemærkes, at de dyr, som modnes langsomt, lever længst og tilhører de ædleste arter. Mænd kan dog ikke gøre krav på nogen naturlig overlegenhed ud fra et langt livs storhed, for i denne henseende har naturen ikke begunstiget hankønnet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Polygamy is another physical degradation; and a plausible argument for a custom, that blasts every domestic virtue, is drawn from the well-attested fact, that in the countries where it is established, more females are born than males. This appears to be an indication of nature, and to nature apparently reasonable speculations must yield. A further conclusion obviously presents itself; if polygamy be necessary, woman must be inferior to man, and made for him.
danishChanges.after: Polygami er endnu en fysisk fornedrelse. Et tilsyneladende holdbart argument for denne skik, som ødelægger enhver dyd i hjemmet, hentes fra den veldokumenterede kendsgerning, at der i de lande, hvor den er udbredt, fødes flere piger end drenge. Dette synes at være et fingerpeg fra naturen, og for naturen må selv tilsyneladende fornuftige overvejelser vige. En yderligere slutning melder sig straks: Hvis polygami er nødvendig, må kvinden være underlegen i forhold til manden og skabt for hans skyld.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: With respect to the formation of the foetus in the womb, we are very ignorant; but it appears to me probable, that an accidental physical cause may account for this phenomenon, and prove it not to be a law of nature. I have met with some pertinent observations on the subject in Forster's Account of the Isles of the South Sea, that will explain my meaning. After observing that of the two sexes amongst animals, the most vigorous and hottest constitution always prevails, and produces its kind; he adds,--"If this be applied to the inhabitants of Africa, it is evident that the men there, accustomed to polygamy, are enervated by the use of so many women, and therefore less vigorous; the women on the contrary, are of a hotter constitution, not only on account of their more irritable nerves, more sensitive organization, and more lively fancy; but likewise because they are deprived in their matrimony of that share of physical love which in a monogamous condition, would all be theirs; and thus for the above reasons, the generality of children are born females."
danishChanges.after: Vi ved meget lidt om fosterets dannelse i livmoderen. Men det forekommer mig sandsynligt, at en tilfældig fysisk årsag kan forklare dette fænomen og vise, at det ikke er en naturlov. Jeg er stødt på nogle relevante bemærkninger om emnet i Forsters beretning om Sydhavsøerne, som vil forklare, hvad jeg mener. Efter at have bemærket, at det af dyrenes to køn, som har den kraftigste og varmeste kropslige beskaffenhed, altid får overtaget og frembringer sit eget køn, tilføjer han: »Anvender man dette på Afrikas indbyggere, er det tydeligt, at mændene dér, som er vant til polygami, svækkes af omgangen med så mange kvinder og derfor er mindre kraftige. Kvinderne har derimod en varmere kropslig beskaffenhed, ikke blot på grund af deres lettere pirrelige nerver, mere følsomme organisme og livligere fantasi, men også fordi de i deres ægteskab berøves den andel af den fysiske kærlighed, som i et monogamt forhold helt ville være deres. Af ovennævnte grunde fødes derfor størstedelen af børnene som piger.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: "In the greater part of Europe it has been proved by the most accurate lists of mortality, that the proportion of men to women is nearly equal, or, if any difference takes place, the males born are more numerous, in the proportion of 105 to 100."
danishChanges.after: »I størstedelen af Europa har de mest nøjagtige dødelighedsopgørelser vist, at forholdet mellem mænd og kvinder er næsten lige, eller at der, hvis nogen forskel forekommer, fødes flere drenge, i forholdet 105 til 100.«
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The necessity of polygamy, therefore, does not appear; yet when a man seduces a woman, it should I think, be termed a LEFT-HANDED marriage, and the man should be LEGALLY obliged to maintain the woman and her children, unless adultery, a natural divorcement, abrogated the law. And this law should remain in force as long as the weakness of women caused the word seduction to be used as an excuse for their frailty and want of principle; nay, while they depend on man for a subsistence, instead of earning it by the exercise of their own hands or heads. But these women should not in the full meaning of the relationship, be termed wives, or the very purpose of marriage would be subverted, and all those endearing charities that flow from personal fidelity, and give a sanctity to the tie, when neither love nor friendship unites the hearts, would melt into selfishness. The woman who is faithful to the father of her children demands respect, and should not be treated like a prostitute; though I readily grant, that if it be necessary for a man and woman to live together in order to bring up their offspring, nature never intended that a man should have more than one wife.
danishChanges.after: Der synes derfor ikke at være nogen nødvendighed for polygami. Men når en mand forfører en kvinde, bør det efter min mening kaldes et ÆGTESKAB TIL VENSTRE HÅND, og manden bør ved LOV være forpligtet til at forsørge kvinden og hendes børn, medmindre utroskab, en naturlig skilsmissegrund, ophæver forpligtelsen. Og denne lov bør gælde, så længe kvinders svaghed gør, at ordet forførelse bruges som undskyldning for deres skrøbelighed og mangel på principper — ja, så længe de er afhængige af manden for deres underhold i stedet for at tjene det ved at bruge deres egne hænder eller hoveder. Men disse kvinder bør ikke kaldes hustruer i forholdets fulde betydning. Ellers ville selve ægteskabets formål blive undergravet, og alle de kærlige hensyn, der udspringer af personlig troskab og helliger båndet, når hverken kærlighed eller venskab forener hjerterne, ville opløses i selviskhed. Den kvinde, som er tro mod sine børns far, har krav på respekt og bør ikke behandles som en prostitueret. Jeg indrømmer dog gerne, at hvis det er nødvendigt for en mand og en kvinde at leve sammen for at opdrage deres afkom, har naturen aldrig tilsigtet, at en mand skulle have mere end én hustru.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Still, highly as I respect marriage, as the foundation of almost every social virtue, I cannot avoid feeling the most lively compassion for those unfortunate females who are broken off from society, and by one error torn from all those affections and relationships that improve the heart and mind. It does not frequently even deserve the name of error; for many innocent girls become the dupes of a sincere affectionate heart, and still more are, as it may emphatically be termed, RUINED before they know the difference between virtue and vice: and thus prepared by their education for infamy, they become infamous. Asylums and Magdalens are not the proper remedies for these abuses. It is justice, not charity, that is wanting in the world!
danishChanges.after: Men hvor højt jeg end respekterer ægteskabet som grundlaget for næsten enhver social dyd, kan jeg ikke undgå at føle den stærkeste medfølelse med de ulykkelige kvinder, som udstødes af samfundet og på grund af ét fejltrin rives bort fra alle de kærlige bånd og forbindelser, der udvikler hjerte og sind. Ofte fortjener det ikke engang navnet fejltrin. For mange uskyldige piger bliver bedraget på grund af et oprigtigt og kærligt hjerte, og endnu flere bliver, som man med eftertryk kan sige, ØDELAGT, før de kender forskel på dyd og last. Deres opdragelse har således forberedt dem på vanære, og vanærede bliver de. Asyler og Magdalenehjem er ikke de rette midler mod disse misforhold. Det er retfærdighed, ikke velgørenhed, verden mangler!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A woman who has lost her honour, imagines that she cannot fall lower, and as for recovering her former station, it is impossible; no exertion can wash this stain away. Losing thus every spur, and having no other means of support, prostitution becomes her only refuge, and the character is quickly depraved by circumstances over which the poor wretch has little power, unless she possesses an uncommon portion of sense and loftiness of spirit. Necessity never makes prostitution the business of men's lives; though numberless are the women who are thus rendered systematically vicious. This, however, arises, in a great degree, from the state of idleness in which women are educated, who are always taught to look up to man for a maintenance, and to consider their persons as the proper return for his exertions to support them. Meretricious airs, and the whole science of wantonness, has then a more powerful stimulus than either appetite or vanity; and this remark gives force to the prevailing opinion, that with chastity all is lost that is respectable in woman. Her character depends on the observance of one virtue, though the only passion fostered in her heart--is love. Nay the honour of a woman is not made even to depend on her will.
danishChanges.after: En kvinde, som har mistet sin ære, forestiller sig, at hun ikke kan synke dybere. At genvinde sin tidligere stilling er umuligt; ingen anstrengelse kan vaske denne plet væk. Når hun således mister enhver tilskyndelse og ikke har andre midler til sit underhold, bliver prostitution hendes eneste tilflugt. Hendes karakter fordærves hurtigt af omstændigheder, som den stakkels kvinde kun har ringe magt over, medmindre hun besidder usædvanlig megen forstand og åndelig storhed. Nød gør aldrig prostitution til mænds livsgerning, mens utallige kvinder på denne måde systematisk gøres lastefulde. Dette skyldes dog i høj grad den tilstand af lediggang, kvinder opdrages til. De lærer altid at søge deres underhold hos manden og at betragte deres egen person som det rette vederlag for hans anstrengelser for at forsørge dem. Prostitueredes manerer og hele kunsten at vække lyst får da en stærkere drivkraft end enten begær eller forfængelighed. Og denne bemærkning styrker den herskende opfattelse, at med kyskheden går alt det tabt, som er værd at respektere hos en kvinde. Hendes karakter afhænger af, at hun overholder én dyd, skønt den eneste lidenskab, man nærer i hendes hjerte, er kærligheden. Ja, man lader ikke engang en kvindes ære afhænge af hendes egen vilje.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: When Richardson makes Clarissa tell Lovelace that he had robbed her of her honour, he must have had strange notions of honour and virtue. For, miserable beyond all names of misery is the condition of a being, who could be degraded without its own consent! This excess of strictness I have heard vindicated as a salutary error. I shall answer in the words of Leibnitz--"Errors are often useful; but it is commonly to remedy other errors."
danishChanges.after: Når Richardson lader Clarissa sige til Lovelace, at han har berøvet hende hendes ære, må han have haft mærkelige forestillinger om ære og dyd. For ulykkelig ud over alle ord for ulykke er den tilstand, et væsen befinder sig i, hvis det kan fornedres uden sit eget samtykke! Jeg har hørt denne overdrevne strenghed forsvaret som en gavnlig vildfarelse. Jeg vil svare med Leibniz’ ord: »Fejltagelser er ofte nyttige, men som regel til at afhjælpe andre fejltagelser.«
