But, the affection which is put on merely because it is the appropriated insignia of a certain character, when its duties are not fulfilled is one of the empty compliments which vice and folly are obliged to pay to virtue and the real nature of things.
danishChanges.after: Min slutning er derfor, at et samfund ikke er ordentligt indrettet, hvis det ikke tilskynder mænd og kvinder til at opfylde deres pligter ved at gøre det til den eneste vej til den anerkendelse, ethvert menneske ønsker fra andre. Respekten for rigdom og rent ydre tiltrækning er som en bidende nordøstenvind, der svider hengivenhedens og dydens spæde blomster. Naturen har klogt knyttet følelser til pligter for at forsøde arbejdet og give fornuftens anstrengelser den kraft, kun hjertet kan give. Men hengivenhed, man kun tager på sig, fordi den er en bestemt rolles rette kendetegn, uden at opfylde rollens pligter, er blot en af de tomme høfligheder, last og dårskab må vise dyden og tingenes virkelige natur.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To illustrate my opinion, I need only observe, that when a woman is admired for her beauty, and suffers herself to be so far intoxicated by the admiration she receives, as to neglect to discharge the indispensable duty of a mother, she sins against herself by neglecting to cultivate an affection that would equally tend to make her useful and happy. True happiness, I mean all the contentment, and virtuous satisfaction that can be snatched in this imperfect state, must arise from well regulated affections; and an affection includes a duty. Men are not aware of the misery they cause, and the vicious weakness they cherish, by only inciting women to render themselves pleasing; they do not consider, that they thus make natural and artificial duties clash, by sacrificing the comfort and respectability of a woman's life to voluptuous notions of beauty, when in nature they all harmonize.
danishChanges.after: For at forklare mig behøver jeg blot at bemærke, at en kvinde, som beundres for sin skønhed og beruses så stærkt af beundringen, at hun forsømmer moderens uundværlige pligt, synder mod sig selv. Hun forsømmer nemlig at udvikle en hengivenhed, som både ville gøre hende nyttig og lykkelig. Sand lykke — al den tilfredshed og dydige glæde, vi kan vinde i denne ufuldkomne tilstand — må komme af velordnede følelser, og enhver hengivenhed rummer en pligt. Mænd forstår ikke, hvilken elendighed de skaber, og hvilken lastefuld svaghed de nærer, når de kun opmuntrer kvinder til at gøre sig tiltrækkende. De ser ikke, at de bringer naturlige og kunstige pligter i konflikt ved at ofre kvinders tryghed og anseelse for sanselige skønhedsidealer, selv om alt dette i naturen harmonerer.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Cold would be the heart of a husband, were he not rendered unnatural by early debauchery, who did not feel more delight at seeing his child suckled by its mother, than the most artful wanton tricks could ever raise; yet this natural way of cementing the matrimonial tie, and twisting esteem with fonder recollections, wealth leads women to spurn. To preserve their beauty, and wear the flowery crown of the day, that gives them a kind of right to reign for a short time over the sex, they neglect to stamp impressions on their husbands' hearts, that would be remembered with more tenderness when the snow on the head began to chill the bosom, than even their virgin charms. The maternal solicitude of a reasonable affectionate woman is very interesting, and the chastened dignity with which a mother returns the caresses that she and her child receive from a father who has been fulfilling the serious duties of his station, is not only a respectable, but a beautiful sight. So singular, indeed, are my feelings, and I have endeavoured not to catch factitious ones, that after having been fatigued with the sight of insipid grandeur and the slavish ceremonies that with cumberous pomp supplied the place of domestic affections, I have turned to some other scene to relieve my eye, by resting it on the refreshing green every where scattered by nature. I have then viewed with pleasure a woman nursing her children, and discharging the duties of her station with, perhaps, merely a servant made to take off her hands the servile part of the household business. I have seen her prepare herself and children, with only the luxury of cleanliness, to receive her husband, who returning weary home in the evening, found smiling babes and a clean hearth. My heart has loitered in the midst of the group, and has even throbbed with sympathetic emotion, when the scraping of the well known foot has raised a pleasing tumult.
danishChanges.after: En mand måtte have et koldt hjerte, hvis tidlige udskejelser ikke allerede havde gjort ham unaturlig, hvis han ikke fandt større glæde ved at se sit barn blive ammet af sin mor end ved de mest udspekulerede forførelseskunster. Alligevel får rigdom kvinder til at afvise denne naturlige måde at styrke ægteskabet og flette respekt sammen med ømme minder på. For at bevare skønheden og bære dagens blomsterkrans, der giver dem en slags ret til kortvarigt at herske over mændene, forsømmer de at sætte spor i ægtemandens hjerte. Sådanne spor ville blive husket med større ømhed end selv deres jomfruelige ynde, når sneen på hovedet begyndte at kølne brystet. En fornuftig og kærlig kvindes moderlige omsorg er dybt rørende. Og når en mor med afdæmpet værdighed gengælder de kærtegn, hun og barnet får af en far, der har udført sine alvorlige pligter, er det både et respektindgydende og et smukt syn. Mine følelser er faktisk så særegne — og jeg har forsøgt at undgå kunstigt tillærte følelser — at jeg efter synet af tom pragt og slaveagtige ceremonier, som med tung pomp erstatter hjemmets hengivenhed, har søgt et andet billede at hvile øjnene på, den forfriskende grønhed, naturen spreder overalt. Så har jeg med glæde set en kvinde passe sine børn og opfylde sine pligter, måske blot med en tjenestepige til at tage det groveste husarbejde. Jeg har set hende gøre sig selv og børnene klar, uden anden luksus end renlighed, til at tage imod manden, der træt vendte hjem om aftenen og fandt smilende småbørn og et rent ildsted. Mit hjerte har dvælet midt i gruppen og banket af medfølelse, når lyden af de velkendte skridt skabte en glad uro.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Whilst my benevolence has been gratified by contemplating this artless picture, I have thought that a couple of this description, equally necessary and independent of each other, because each fulfilled the respective duties of their station, possessed all that life could give. Raised sufficiently above abject poverty not to be obliged to weigh the consequence of every farthing they spend, and having sufficient to prevent their attending to a frigid system of economy which narrows both heart and mind. I declare, so vulgar are my conceptions, that I know not what is wanted to render this the happiest as well as the most respectable situation in the world, but a taste for literature, to throw a little variety and interest into social converse, and some superfluous money to give to the needy, and to buy books. For it is not pleasant when the heart is opened by compassion, and the head active in arranging plans of usefulness, to have a prim urchin continually twitching back the elbow to prevent the hand from drawing out an almost empty purse, whispering at the same time some prudential maxim about the priority of justice.
danishChanges.after: Mens dette ligefremme billede har glædet min velvilje, har jeg tænkt, at et sådant par ejer alt, hvad livet kan give. De er lige nødvendige for hinanden og lige uafhængige, fordi begge opfylder deres pligter. De er tilstrækkeligt hævet over knugende fattigdom til ikke at skulle veje følgen af hver øre, de bruger, og har nok til at undgå et koldt sparsommelighedssystem, som indsnævrer både hjerte og sind. Mine forestillinger er så jævne, at jeg erklærer: Jeg ved ikke, hvad der ellers mangler for at gøre dette til verdens lykkeligste og mest respektable stilling, ud over smag for litteratur, som kan give samværet lidt variation og interesse, og lidt penge til overs til nødlidende og bøger. For det er ikke rart, når medfølelsen åbner hjertet, og hovedet ivrigt lægger nyttige planer, at en sippet lille plageånd hele tiden hiver en i albuen for at forhindre hånden i at trække en næsten tom pung frem, mens den hvisker en klog maksime om, at retfærdigheden kommer først.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Destructive, however, as riches and inherited honours are to the human character, women are more debased and cramped, if possible by them, than men, because men may still, in some degree, unfold their faculties by becoming soldiers and statesmen.
danishChanges.after: Men hvor ødelæggende rigdom og arvede hædersbevisninger end er for menneskets karakter, fornedrer og hæmmer de om muligt kvinder endnu mere end mænd. Mænd kan dog stadig til en vis grad udfolde deres evner som soldater og statsmænd.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: As soldiers, I grant, they can now only gather, for the most part, vainglorious laurels, whilst they adjust to a hair the European balance, taking especial care that no bleak northern nook or sound incline the beam. But the days of true heroism are over, when a citizen fought for his country like a Fabricius or a Washington, and then returned to his farm to let his virtuous fervour run in a more placid, but not a less salutary stream. No, our British heroes are oftener sent from the gaming table than from the plough; and their passions have been rather inflamed by hanging with dumb suspense on the turn of a die, than sublimated by panting after the adventurous march of virtue in the historic page.
danishChanges.after: Som soldater kan de ganske vist nu for det meste kun høste tomme laurbær, mens de afbalancerer Europas magter på et hår, omhyggeligt optaget af, at ingen barsk nordlig afkrog eller noget sund tipper vægten. Men den sande heltemods tid er forbi, da en borger som Fabricius eller Washington kæmpede for sit land og derefter vendte hjem til sin gård, hvor hans dydige ildhu kunne flyde i en roligere, men lige så gavnlig strøm. Nej, vores britiske helte sendes oftere fra spillebordet end fra ploven. Deres lidenskaber er snarere blevet opildnet af tavst at afvente et terningekast end forædlet af at længes efter dydens dristige fremmarch på historiens sider.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The statesman, it is true, might with more propriety quit the Faro Bank, or card-table, to guide the helm, for he has still but to shuffle and trick. The whole system of British politics, if system it may courteously be called, consisting in multiplying dependents and contriving taxes which grind the poor to pamper the rich; thus a war, or any wild goose chace is, as the vulgar use the phrase, a lucky turn-up of patronage for the minister, whose chief merit is the art of keeping himself in place.
danishChanges.after: Statsmanden kan ganske vist med større rimelighed forlade farobordet eller kortspillet for at tage roret, for han skal stadig blot blande kort og snyde. Hele det britiske politiske system, hvis man høfligt kan kalde det et system, består i at skabe flere afhængige tilhængere og udtænke skatter, som knuser de fattige for at forkæle de rige. En krig eller ethvert vildt jagtprojekt bliver derfor, som man siger, et heldigt kort i ministerens spil med embeder og tjenester. Hans største fortjeneste er kunsten at blive på sin post.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is not necessary then that he should have bowels for the poor, so he can secure for his family the odd trick. Or should some show of respect, for what is termed with ignorant ostentation an Englishman's birth-right, be expedient to bubble the gruff mastiff that he has to lead by the nose, he can make an empty show, very safely, by giving his single voice, and suffering his light squadron to file off to the other side. And when a question of humanity is agitated, he may dip a sop in the milk of human kindness, to silence Cerberus, and talk of the interest which his heart takes in an attempt to make the earth no longer cry for vengeance as it sucks in its children's blood, though his cold hand may at the very moment rivet their chains, by sanctioning the abominable traffick. A minister is no longer a minister than while he can carry a point, which he is determined to carry. Yet it is not necessary that a minister should feel like a man, when a bold push might shake his seat.
danishChanges.after: Han behøver altså ikke føle med de fattige, hvis han bare kan sikre sin familie det afgørende stik. Skal han vise lidt respekt for det, man med uvidende pral kalder en englænders fødselsret, for at narre den bidske mastiff, han må trække ved næsen, kan han ganske trygt gøre en tom gestus: selv stemme for, mens han lader sin lette eskadron slutte sig til modparten. Og når et menneskeligt spørgsmål debatteres, kan han dyppe en bid i menneskekærlighedens mælk for at få Kerberos til at tie og tale om, hvor dybt hans hjerte er engageret i forsøget på at få jorden til at holde op med at råbe på hævn, mens den opsuger sine børns blod. Samtidig kan hans kolde hånd nagle deres lænker fast ved at godkende den afskyelige handel. En minister er kun minister, så længe han kan gennemføre det, han har besluttet at gennemføre. Men han behøver ikke føle som et menneske, når et dristigt fremstød kan rokke ved hans plads.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, to have done with these episodical observations, let me return to the more specious slavery which chains the very soul of woman, keeping her for ever under the bondage of ignorance.
danishChanges.after: Men lad mig afslutte disse sidebemærkninger og vende tilbage til det mere tilslørede slaveri, som lænker selve kvindens sjæl og for altid holder hende i uvidenhedens trældom.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The preposterous distinctions of rank, which render civilization a curse, by dividing the world between voluptuous tyrants, and cunning envious dependents, corrupt, almost equally, every class of people, because respectability is not attached to the discharge of the relative duties of life, but to the station, and when the duties are not fulfilled, the affections cannot gain sufficient strength to fortify the virtue of which they are the natural reward. Still there are some loop-holes out of which a man may creep, and dare to think and act for himself; but for a woman it is an herculean task, because she has difficulties peculiar to her sex to overcome, which require almost super-human powers.
danishChanges.after: De absurde standsforskelle gør civilisationen til en forbandelse ved at dele verden mellem nydelsessyge tyranner og snu, misundelige afhængige. De fordærver næsten lige meget alle klasser, fordi anseelsen knyttes til stillingen, ikke til opfyldelsen af livets pligter mod andre. Når pligterne ikke opfyldes, kan følelserne ikke få styrke nok til at befæste den dyd, de er den naturlige belønning for. Mænd har dog stadig smuthuller, hvorigennem de kan krybe ud og vove at tænke og handle selv. For kvinder er det en herkulisk opgave, fordi de også må overvinde særlige kønsbestemte vanskeligheder, som kræver næsten overmenneskelige kræfter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A truly benevolent legislator always endeavours to make it the interest of each individual to be virtuous; and thus private virtue becoming the cement of public happiness, an orderly whole is consolidated by the tendency of all the parts towards a common centre. But, the private or public virtue of women is very problematical; for Rousseau, and a numerous list of male writers, insist that she should all her life, be subjected to a severe restraint, that of propriety. Why subject her to propriety--blind propriety, if she be capable of acting from a nobler spring, if she be an heir of immortality? Is sugar always to be produced by vital blood? Is one half of the human species, like the poor African slaves, to be subject to prejudices that brutalize them, when principles would be a surer guard only to sweeten the cup of man? Is not this indirectly to deny women reason? for a gift is a mockery, if it be unfit for use.
danishChanges.after: En virkelig menneskekærlig lovgiver forsøger altid at gøre det til den enkeltes interesse at være dydig. Når den private dyd sådan binder den fælles lykke sammen, skabes en ordnet helhed, fordi alle delene søger mod et fælles centrum. Men kvinders private og offentlige dyd bliver højst usikker, når Rousseau og en lang række mandlige forfattere kræver, at kvinden hele livet skal være underlagt den strenge tvang at opføre sig passende. Hvorfor underkaste hende blind sømmelighed, hvis hun kan handle af et ædlere motiv, hvis hun er arving til udødeligheden? Skal sukker altid fremstilles med menneskers livsblod? Skal halvdelen af menneskeheden, ligesom de stakkels afrikanske slaver, være underlagt fordomme, der gør dem rå, når principper ville være et sikrere værn — blot for at forsøde mandens bæger? Er det ikke indirekte at nægte kvinder fornuft? En gave er en hån, hvis den ikke kan bruges.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women are in common with men, rendered weak and luxurious by the relaxing pleasures which wealth procures; but added to this, they are made slaves to their persons, and must render them alluring, that man may lend them his reason to guide their tottering steps aright. Or should they be ambitious, they must govern their tyrants by sinister tricks, for without rights there cannot be any incumbent duties. The laws respecting woman, which I mean to discuss in a future part, make an absurd unit of a man and his wife; and then, by the easy transition of only considering him as responsible, she is reduced to a mere cypher.
danishChanges.after: Kvinder svækkes og vænnes ligesom mænd til luksus af de sløvende glæder, rigdommen skaffer. Men derudover gøres de til slaver af deres ydre. De må gøre det tillokkende, så manden låner dem sin fornuft til at lede deres vaklende skridt. Er de ærgerrige, må de styre deres tyranner med lumske kneb, for uden rettigheder kan der ikke være bindende pligter. Lovene om kvinder, som jeg vil drøfte i en senere del, gør på urimelig vis mand og hustru til én enhed. Ved derefter ganske let kun at gøre ham ansvarlig reducerer de hende til et nul.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The being who discharges the duties of its station, is independent; and, speaking of women at large, their first duty is to themselves as rational creatures, and the next, in point of importance, as citizens, is that, which includes so many, of a mother. The rank in life which dispenses with their fulfilling this duty, necessarily degrades them by making them mere dolls. Or, should they turn to something more important than merely fitting drapery upon a smooth block, their minds are only occupied by some soft platonic attachment; or, the actual management of an intrigue may keep their thoughts in motion; for when they neglect domestic duties, they have it not in their power to take the field and march and counter-march like soldiers, or wrangle in the senate to keep their faculties from rusting.
danishChanges.after: Den, der opfylder sin stillings pligter, er uafhængig. For kvinder som helhed gælder den første pligt dem selv som fornuftsvæsener. Den næstvigtigste som borgere er moderens, som rummer så mange andre. En stand, der fritager dem for denne pligt, fornedrer dem nødvendigvis ved at gøre dem til rene dukker. Vender de sig mod noget vigtigere end at tilpasse stof til en glat klods, optages sindet kun af en blid platonisk forelskelse. Eller en virkelig affære kan holde tankerne i gang. Når de forsømmer hjemmets pligter, kan de jo ikke drage i felten og marchere frem og tilbage som soldater eller skændes i senatet for at holde evnerne fri for rust.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I know, that as a proof of the inferiority of the sex, Rousseau has exultingly exclaimed, How can they leave the nursery for the camp! And the camp has by some moralists been termed the school of the most heroic virtues; though, I think, it would puzzle a keen casuist to prove the reasonableness of the greater number of wars, that have dubbed heroes. I do not mean to consider this question critically; because, having frequently viewed these freaks of ambition as the first natural mode of civilization, when the ground must be torn up, and the woods cleared by fire and sword, I do not choose to call them pests; but surely the present system of war, has little connection with virtue of any denomination, being rather the school of FINESSE and effeminacy, than of fortitude.
danishChanges.after: Jeg ved, at Rousseau triumferende har udbrudt som bevis på kvinders underlegenhed: Hvordan skulle de kunne forlade børneværelset for militærlejren? Nogle moralister har kaldt lejren de mest heroiske dyders skole. Men jeg tror, det ville sætte selv en skarp kasuist på prøve at begrunde de fleste af de krige, der har gjort mænd til helte. Jeg vil ikke undersøge spørgsmålet nærmere her. Jeg har ofte set disse udslag af ærgerrighed som civilisationens første naturlige form, hvor jorden må brydes og skovene ryddes med ild og sværd, og vil derfor ikke kalde dem landeplager. Men nutidens krigssystem har bestemt kun lidt at gøre med nogen form for dyd. Det er snarere en skole i FINTER og blødagtighed end i modstandskraft.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Yet, if defensive war, the only justifiable war, in the present advanced state of society, where virtue can show its face and ripen amidst the rigours which purify the air on the mountain's top, were alone to be adopted as just and glorious, the true heroism of antiquity might again animate female bosoms. But fair and softly, gentle reader, male or female, do not alarm thyself, for though I have contrasted the character of a modern soldier with that of a civilized woman, I am not going to advise them to turn their distaff into a musket, though I sincerely wish to see the bayonet converted into a pruning hook. I only recreated an imagination, fatigued by contemplating the vices and follies which all proceed from a feculent stream of wealth that has muddied the pure rills of natural affection, by supposing that society will some time or other be so constituted, that man must necessarily fulfil the duties of a citizen, or be despised, and that while he was employed in any of the departments of civil life, his wife, also an active citizen, should be equally intent to manage her family, educate her children, and assist her neighbours.
danishChanges.after: Men hvis man i samfundets nuværende udviklede tilstand kun anerkendte forsvarskrigen som retfærdig og ærefuld — den eneste krig, der kan forsvares, hvor dyden kan vise sig og modnes under den strenghed, som renser luften på bjergtoppen — kunne oldtidens sande heltemod igen besjæle kvinder. Men rolig nu, kære læser, mand eller kvinde! Bliv ikke forskrækket. Selv om jeg har sammenlignet den moderne soldat med den civiliserede kvinde, vil jeg ikke råde kvinderne til at bytte spinderokken ud med en musket, skønt jeg oprigtigt ønsker at se bajonetten omsmedet til en beskærekniv. Jeg gav blot fantasien lidt hvile efter synet af de laster og tåbeligheder, der alle strømmer fra rigdommens urene flod og gør den naturlige hengivenheds rene bække grumsede. Jeg forestillede mig, at samfundet en dag bliver indrettet sådan, at manden må opfylde sine borgerpligter eller blive foragtet. Mens han arbejder på et af det borgerlige livs områder, skal hans hustru, også en aktiv borger, med samme alvor lede hjemmet, opdrage børnene og hjælpe naboerne.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, to render her really virtuous and useful, she must not, if she discharge her civil duties, want, individually, the protection of civil laws; she must not be dependent on her husband's bounty for her subsistence during his life, or support after his death--for how can a being be generous who has nothing of its own? or, virtuous, who is not free? The wife, in the present state of things, who is faithful to her husband, and neither suckles nor educates her children, scarcely deserves the name of a wife, and has no right to that of a citizen. But take away natural rights, and there is of course an end of duties.
danishChanges.after: Men skal hun virkelig blive dydig og nyttig, må hun ikke mangle lovens beskyttelse som individ, når hun opfylder sine borgerpligter. Hendes underhold, både mens manden lever og efter hans død, må ikke afhænge af hans gavmildhed. Hvordan kan den, der intet ejer, være gavmild? Hvordan kan den, der ikke er fri, være dydig? Som forholdene er nu, fortjener den kvinde, der er sin mand tro, men hverken ammer eller opdrager sine børn, knap nok navnet hustru og har intet krav på navnet borger. Men tager man de naturlige rettigheder bort, ophører pligterne naturligvis også.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Women thus infallibly become only the wanton solace of men, when they are so weak in mind and body, that they cannot exert themselves, unless to pursue some frothy pleasure, or to invent some frivolous fashion. What can be a more melancholy sight to a thinking mind, than to look into the numerous carriages that drive helter-skelter about this metropolis in a morning, full of pale-faced creatures who are flying from themselves. I have often wished, with Dr. Johnson, to place some of them in a little shop, with half a dozen children looking up to their languid countenances for support. I am much mistaken, if some latent vigour would not soon give health and spirit to their eyes, and some lines drawn by the exercise of reason on the blank cheeks, which before were only undulated by dimples, might restore lost dignity to the character, or rather enable it to attain the true dignity of its nature. Virtue is not to be acquired even by speculation, much less by the negative supineness that wealth naturally generates.
danishChanges.after: Kvinder bliver uundgåeligt blot mændenes sanselige adspredelse, når de er så svage i krop og sind, at de kun kan anstrenge sig for at jage en luftig fornøjelse eller opfinde en overfladisk mode. Hvilket syn kunne være mere trist for et tænkende menneske end de mange vogne, som om morgenen farer planløst omkring i hovedstaden, fyldt med blege væsener, der flygter fra sig selv? Ligesom dr. Johnson har jeg ofte ønsket at sætte nogle af dem i en lille butik med et halvt dusin børn, der så op til deres matte ansigter for at få hjælp. Jeg tager meget fejl, hvis ikke en skjult kraft snart ville give deres øjne sundhed og liv. Nogle linjer, tegnet af fornuftens arbejde på de glatte kinder, der før kun blev kruset af smilehuller, kunne give karakteren dens tabte værdighed tilbage eller snarere lade den opnå sin naturs sande værdighed. Dyd vindes ikke engang ved overvejelse alene, og langt mindre ved den passive magelighed, rigdom naturligt skaber.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, when poverty is more disgraceful than even vice, is not morality cut to the quick? Still to avoid misconstruction, though I consider that women in the common walks of life are called to fulfil the duties of wives and mothers, by religion and reason, I cannot help lamenting that women of a superiour cast have not a road open by which they can pursue more extensive plans of usefulness and independence. I may excite laughter, by dropping an hint, which I mean to pursue, some future time, for I really think that women ought to have representatives, instead of being arbitrarily governed without having any direct share allowed them in the deliberations of government.
danishChanges.after: Og rammes moralen ikke i sit inderste, når fattigdom er mere skamfuld end selve lasten? For ikke at blive misforstået: Selv om jeg mener, at religion og fornuft kalder kvinder i livets almindelige stillinger til at opfylde hustruers og mødres pligter, beklager jeg, at kvinder med større evner ikke har en åben vej til mere vidtrækkende nyttigt arbejde og uafhængighed. Måske vækker jeg latter ved at nævne en tanke, jeg vil følge op senere: Jeg mener faktisk, at kvinder bør have repræsentanter i stedet for at blive styret vilkårligt uden nogen direkte del i regeringens overvejelser.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, as the whole system of representation is now, in this country, only a convenient handle for despotism, they need not complain, for they are as well represented as a numerous class of hard working mechanics, who pay for the support of royality when they can scarcely stop their children's mouths with bread. How are they represented, whose very sweat supports the splendid stud of an heir apparent, or varnishes the chariot of some female favourite who looks down on shame? Taxes on the very necessaries of life, enable an endless tribe of idle princes and princesses to pass with stupid pomp before a gaping crowd, who almost worship the very parade which costs them so dear. This is mere gothic grandeur, something like the barbarous, useless parade of having sentinels on horseback at Whitehall, which I could never view without a mixture of contempt and indignation.
danishChanges.after: Men da hele repræsentationssystemet her i landet nu blot er et bekvemt redskab for enevælde, behøver de ikke klage. De er lige så godt repræsenteret som den store gruppe hårdtarbejdende håndværkere, der betaler til kongehusets underhold, mens de knap kan mætte deres børn med brød. Hvordan er de repræsenteret, hvis sved betaler for en tronarvings pragtfulde hestehold eller lakerer vognen for en kvindelig favorit, som ser ned på skammen? Skatter på livets nødvendigheder lader en endeløs flok ledige prinser og prinsesser passere i tom pomp foran en måbende menneskemængde, der næsten tilbeder den pragt, den selv betaler så dyrt for. Det er ren middelalderlig storhed, som den barbariske og unyttige opvisning med beredne vagter ved Whitehall, jeg aldrig har kunnet se uden både foragt og harme.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: How strangely must the mind be sophisticated when this sort of state impresses it! But till these monuments of folly are levelled by virtue, similar follies will leaven the whole mass. For the same character, in some degree, will prevail in the aggregate of society: and the refinements of luxury, or the vicious repinings of envious poverty, will equally banish virtue from society, considered as the characteristic of that society, or only allow it to appear as one of the stripes of the harlequin coat, worn by the civilized man.
danishChanges.after: Hvor sært må sindet ikke være fordrejet, når det imponeres af sådan en pragt! Men indtil dyden river disse monumenter over dårskaben ned, vil lignende tåbeligheder gennemsyre hele samfundet. Den samme karakter vil nemlig til en vis grad herske i helheden. Luksussens raffinementer og den misundelige fattigdoms lastefulde bitterhed vil lige meget fordrive dyden som samfundets kendetegn eller kun lade den vise sig som en stribe på den harlekindragt, det civiliserede menneske bærer.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In the superiour ranks of life, every duty is done by deputies, as if duties could ever be waved, and the vain pleasures which consequent idleness forces the rich to pursue, appear so enticing to the next rank, that the numerous scramblers for wealth sacrifice every thing to tread on their heels. The most sacred trusts are then considered as sinecures, because they were procured by interest, and only sought to enable a man to keep GOOD COMPANY. Women, in particular, all want to be ladies. Which is simply to have nothing to do, but listlessly to go they scarcely care where, for they cannot tell what.
danishChanges.after: I de højere klasser udføres alle pligter af stedfortrædere, som om man nogensinde kunne frasige sig en pligt. De tomme fornøjelser, lediggangen tvinger de rige til at søge, virker så tillokkende på klassen nedenunder, at de mange, der kæmper om rigdom, ofrer alt for at følge dem i hælene. Selv de helligste tillidshverv regnes for stillinger uden arbejde, fordi de er skaffet gennem forbindelser og kun søgt for at kunne omgås DET GODE SELSKAB. Især kvinder vil alle være fine damer. Det vil blot sige ikke at have andet at gøre end sløvt at tage et sted hen, de knap interesserer sig for, for at gøre noget, de ikke kan sige hvad er.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But what have women to do in society? I may be asked, but to loiter with easy grace; surely you would not condemn them all to suckle fools, and chronicle small beer! No. Women might certainly study the art of healing, and be physicians as well as nurses. And midwifery, decency seems to allot to them, though I am afraid the word midwife, in our dictionaries, will soon give place to accoucheur, and one proof of the former delicacy of the sex be effaced from the language.
danishChanges.after: Hvad skal kvinder ellers gøre i samfundet, vil man spørge, end at drive omkring med ubesværet ynde? Du vil vel ikke dømme dem alle til at amme tåber og føre regnskab over småøl? Nej. Kvinder kunne bestemt studere lægekunsten og være læger såvel som sygeplejersker. Anstændigheden synes også at tildele dem fødselshjælpen, selv om jeg frygter, at ordet jordemoder snart vil vige for accoucheur i vores ordbøger, så endnu et tegn på kønnets tidligere finfølelse slettes af sproget.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: They might, also study politics, and settle their benevolence on the broadest basis; for the reading of history will scarcely be more useful than the perusal of romances, if read as mere biography; if the character of the times, the political improvements, arts, etc. be not observed. In short, if it be not considered as the history of man; and not of particular men, who filled a niche in the temple of fame, and dropped into the black rolling stream of time, that silently sweeps all before it, into the shapeless void called eternity. For shape can it be called, "that shape hath none?"
danishChanges.after: De kunne også studere politik og give deres velvilje det bredest mulige grundlag. Historielæsning er næppe nyttigere end romanlæsning, hvis historien kun læses som biografi, uden blik for tidens karakter, politiske forbedringer, kunst og færdigheder. Kort sagt: hvis den ikke læses som menneskets historie, men blot som historien om bestemte mænd, der fyldte en niche i berømmelsens tempel og sank ned i tidens sorte, rullende strøm. Den fejer lydløst alt foran sig ind i det formløse tomrum, vi kalder evigheden. For kan det kaldes en form, »som ingen form har«?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Business of various kinds, they might likewise pursue, if they were educated in a more orderly manner, which might save many from common and legal prostitution. Women would not then marry for a support, as men accept of places under government, and neglect the implied duties; nor would an attempt to earn their own subsistence, a most laudable one! sink them almost to the level of those poor abandoned creatures who live by prostitution. For are not milliners and mantuamakers reckoned the next class? The few employments open to women, so far from being liberal, are menial; and when a superior education enables them to take charge of the education of children as governesses, they are not treated like the tutors of sons, though even clerical tutors are not always treated in a manner calculated to render them respectable in the eyes of their pupils, to say nothing of the private comfort of the individual. But as women educated like gentlewomen, are never designed for the humiliating situation which necessity sometimes forces them to fill; these situations are considered in the light of a degradation; and they know little of the human heart, who need to be told, that nothing so painfully sharpens the sensibility as such a fall in life.
danishChanges.after: De kunne også drive forskellige slags virksomhed, hvis de fik en mere systematisk uddannelse. Det kunne redde mange fra både almindelig og lovlig prostitution. Så ville kvinder ikke gifte sig for at blive forsørget, som mænd tager imod statslige stillinger og forsømmer pligterne. Heller ikke ville et forsøg på at tjene til eget underhold — et yderst prisværdigt forsøg! — sænke dem næsten til samme niveau som de stakkels fortabte kvinder, der lever af prostitution. Regner man ikke hattemagere og dameskræddere for den nærmeste klasse? De få erhverv, der er åbne for kvinder, er langt fra frie og ansete; de er tjenende. Når en bedre uddannelse lader dem overtage børns undervisning som guvernanter, behandles de ikke som sønnernes huslærere. Selv gejstlige huslærere behandles dog ikke altid, så eleverne kan respektere dem, for slet ikke at tale om deres eget velbefindende. Kvinder, der er opdraget som damer, er aldrig tiltænkt den ydmygende stilling, nøden undertiden tvinger dem ind i. Derfor regnes disse stillinger for en fornedrelse. Man kender kun lidt til menneskehjertet, hvis man skal have at vide, at intet skærper følsomheden så smertefuldt som et sådant fald i livet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Some of these women might be restrained from marrying by a proper spirit or delicacy, and others may not have had it in their power to escape in this pitiful way from servitude; is not that government then very defective, and very unmindful of the happiness of one half of its members, that does not provide for honest, independent women, by encouraging them to fill respectable stations? But in order to render their private virtue a public benefit, they must have a civil existence in the state, married or single; else we shall continually see some worthy woman, whose sensibility has been rendered painfully acute by undeserved contempt, droop like "the lily broken down by a plough share."
danishChanges.after: Nogle af disse kvinder kan af rette stolthed eller finfølelse afholde sig fra at gifte sig. Andre har måske ikke haft mulighed for at slippe fra tjenesteforholdet på denne ynkelige måde. Er en regering da ikke dybt mangelfuld og ligeglad med halvdelen af borgernes lykke, hvis den ikke sørger for hæderlige, uafhængige kvinder ved at opmuntre dem til at indtage ansete stillinger? Men skal deres private dyd gavne samfundet, må de have en borgerlig tilværelse i staten, gifte som ugifte. Ellers vil vi bestandigt se en agtværdig kvinde, hvis følsomhed er gjort smertefuldt skarp af ufortjent foragt, bøje sig som »liljen, der er knækket af plovskæret«.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is a melancholy truth; yet such is the blessed effects of civilization! the most respectable women are the most oppressed; and, unless they have understandings far superiour to the common run of understandings, taking in both sexes, they must, from being treated like contemptible beings, become contemptible. How many women thus waste life away, the prey of discontent, who might have practised as physicians, regulated a farm, managed a shop, and stood erect, supported by their own industry, instead of hanging their heads surcharged with the dew of sensibility, that consumes the beauty to which it at first gave lustre; nay, I doubt whether pity and love are so near a-kin as poets feign, for I have seldom seen much compassion excited by the helplessness of females, unless they were fair; then, perhaps, pity was the soft handmaid of love, or the harbinger of lust.
danishChanges.after: Det er en sørgelig sandhed — og dog er det civilisationens velsignede virkning! — at de mest respektable kvinder er de mest undertrykte. Medmindre deres forstand ligger langt over gennemsnittet for begge køn, må behandlingen som foragtelige væsener gøre dem foragtelige. Hvor mange kvinder spilder ikke sådan livet som bytte for utilfredshed, selv om de kunne have virket som læger, drevet en gård eller ledet en butik og stået oprejst, båret af deres eget arbejde! I stedet hænger de med hovedet, tynget af følsomhedens dug, som fortærer den skønhed, den først gav glans. Jeg tvivler endda på, at medlidenhed og kærlighed er så nært beslægtede, som digterne hævder. Jeg har sjældent set kvinders hjælpeløshed vække megen medfølelse, medmindre de var smukke. Da var medlidenheden måske kærlighedens blide tjener eller begærets forløber.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: How much more respectable is the woman who earns her own bread by fulfilling any duty, than the most accomplished beauty! beauty did I say? so sensible am I of the beauty of moral loveliness, or the harmonious propriety that attunes the passions of a well-regulated mind, that I blush at making the comparison; yet I sigh to think how few women aim at attaining this respectability, by withdrawing from the giddy whirl of pleasure, or the indolent calm that stupifies the good sort of women it sucks in.
danishChanges.after: Hvor meget mere respektabel er ikke den kvinde, der tjener sit eget brød ved at opfylde en pligt, end den mest dannede skønhed! Sagde jeg skønhed? Jeg føler så stærkt den moralske skønhed og den harmoniske orden, der afstemmer et velordnet sinds lidenskaber, at jeg skammer mig over sammenligningen. Alligevel sukker jeg ved tanken om, hvor få kvinder der søger denne anseelse ved at trække sig ud af fornøjelsernes svimlende hvirvel eller den dovne ro, som sløver de ellers gode kvinder, den opsluger.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Proud of their weakness, however, they must always be protected, guarded from care, and all the rough toils that dignify the mind. If this be the fiat of fate, if they will make themselves insignificant and contemptible, sweetly to waste "life away," let them not expect to be valued when their beauty fades, for it is the fate of the fairest flowers to be admired and pulled to pieces by the careless hand that plucked them. In how many ways do I wish, from the purest benevolence, to impress this truth on my sex; yet I fear that they will not listen to a truth, that dear-bought experience has brought home to many an agitated bosom, nor willingly resign the privileges of rank and sex for the privileges of humanity, to which those have no claim who do not discharge its duties.
danishChanges.after: Men stolte af deres svaghed skal de altid beskyttes mod bekymringer og alt det hårde arbejde, der giver sindet værdighed. Er det skæbnens bud, og vil de gøre sig ubetydelige og foragtelige for sødt at lade »livet svinde«, må de ikke vente at blive værdsat, når skønheden falmer. Selv de smukkeste blomsters lod er at blive beundret og revet i stykker af den ligegyldige hånd, der plukkede dem. På hvor mange måder ønsker jeg ikke, af den reneste velvilje, at indprente denne sandhed i kvinder! Men jeg frygter, at de ikke vil høre en sandhed, som dyrt købt erfaring har lært så mange urolige hjerter, eller frivilligt bytte standens og kønnets privilegier for menneskelighedens. Dem har ingen krav på, som ikke opfylder dens pligter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Those writers are particularly useful, in my opinion, who make man feel for man, independent of the station he fills, or the drapery of factitious sentiments. I then would fain convince reasonable men of the importance of some of my remarks and prevail on them to weigh dispassionately the whole tenor of my observations. I appeal to their understandings; and, as a fellow-creature claim, in the name of my sex, some interest in their hearts. I entreat them to assist to emancipate their companion to make her a help meet for them!
danishChanges.after: De forfattere er efter min mening særlig nyttige, som får mennesket til at føle med mennesket, uanset dets stilling eller de kunstige følelsers draperi. Jeg vil derfor gerne overbevise fornuftige mænd om betydningen af nogle af mine bemærkninger og få dem til lidenskabsløst at overveje den samlede retning i mine iagttagelser. Jeg henvender mig til deres forstand og gør som medmenneske på mit køns vegne krav på en plads i deres hjerter. Jeg beder dem hjælpe med at frigøre deres ledsager, så hun kan blive en passende hjælper for dem!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Would men but generously snap our chains, and be content with rational fellowship, instead of slavish obedience, they would find us more observant daughters, more affectionate sisters, more faithful wives, more reasonable mothers--in a word, better citizens. We should then love them with true affection, because we should learn to respect ourselves; and the peace of mind of a worthy man would not be interrupted by the idle vanity of his wife, nor his babes sent to nestle in a strange bosom, having never found a home in their mother's.
danishChanges.after: Hvis mænd blot storsindet brød vores lænker og nøjedes med et fornuftigt fællesskab frem for slavisk lydighed, ville de få mere hensynsfulde døtre, mere kærlige søstre, mere trofaste hustruer og mere fornuftige mødre — kort sagt bedre borgere. Vi ville da elske dem med ægte hengivenhed, fordi vi lærte at respektere os selv. En god mands fred i sindet ville ikke blive forstyrret af hustruens tomme forfængelighed, og hans spædbørn ville ikke blive sendt til at putte sig ved et fremmed bryst, fordi de aldrig havde fundet et hjem ved deres mors.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Parental affection is, perhaps, the blindest modification of perverse self-love; for we have not, like the French two terms (L'amour propre, L'amour de soi meme) to distinguish the pursuit of a natural and reasonable desire, from the ignorant calculations of weakness. Parents often love their children in the most brutal manner, and sacrifice every relative duty to promote their advancement in the world. To promote, such is the perversity of unprincipled prejudices, the future welfare of the very beings whose present existence they imbitter by the most despotic stretch of power. Power, in fact, is ever true to its vital principle, for in every shape it would reign without controul or inquiry. Its throne is built across a dark abyss, which no eye must dare to explore, lest the baseless fabric should totter under investigation. Obedience, unconditional obedience, is the catch-word of tyrants of every description, and to render "assurance doubly sure," one kind of despotism supports another. Tyrants would have cause to tremble if reason were to become the rule of duty in any of the relations of life, for the light might spread till perfect day appeared. And when it did appear, how would men smile at the sight of the bugbears at which they started during the night of ignorance, or the twilight of timid inquiry.
danishChanges.after: Forældrekærlighed er måske den blindeste form for fordrejet selvkærlighed. På engelsk har vi jo ikke som franskmændene to ord — l’amour-propre og l’amour de soi-même — til at skelne mellem et naturligt og fornuftigt ønske og svaghedens uvidende beregninger. Forældre elsker ofte deres børn på den mest rå måde og ofrer enhver pligt mod andre for at fremme børnenes stilling i verden. Så fordrejede er de principløse fordomme, at forældrene vil sikre den fremtidige lykke for netop de væsener, hvis nuværende liv de forgifter gennem den mest despotiske magtudøvelse. Magten er altid tro mod sit grundprincip: I enhver form vil den herske uden kontrol eller undersøgelse. Dens trone er bygget over en mørk afgrund, som intet blik må vove at udforske, for så kunne det grundløse bygningsværk vakle. Lydighed, ubetinget lydighed, er alle tyranners slagord. Og for at gøre »sikkerheden dobbelt sikker« støtter den ene form for despoti den anden. Tyranner ville have grund til at ryste, hvis fornuften blev pligtens målestok i blot ét af livets forhold, for lyset kunne brede sig, indtil fuldt dagslys brød frem. Hvor ville mennesker da ikke smile over de skræmmebilleder, som fik dem til at fare sammen i uvidenhedens nat eller den frygtsomme undersøgelses tusmørke!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Parental affection, indeed, in many minds, is but a pretext to tyrannize where it can be done with impunity, for only good and wise men are content with the respect that will bear discussion. Convinced that they have a right to what they insist on, they do not fear reason, or dread the sifting of subjects that recur to natural justice: because they firmly believe, that the more enlightened the human mind becomes, the deeper root will just and simple principles take. They do not rest in expedients, or grant that what is metaphysically true can be practically false; but disdaining the shifts of the moment they calmly wait till time, sanctioning innovation, silences the hiss of selfishness or envy.
danishChanges.after: Hos mange er forældrekærligheden faktisk blot et påskud for at tyrannisere, hvor det kan ske ustraffet. Kun gode og kloge mennesker nøjes med en respekt, som tåler diskussion. Fordi de er overbevist om deres kravs retmæssighed, frygter de hverken fornuften eller en grundig undersøgelse af spørgsmål, der henviser til naturlig retfærdighed. De tror fast på, at jo mere oplyst menneskesindet bliver, desto dybere slår retfærdige og enkle principper rod. De nøjes ikke med nødløsninger og indrømmer ikke, at noget kan være sandt i teorien og falsk i praksis. De foragter øjeblikkets kneb og venter roligt på, at tiden bekræfter fornyelsen og bringer egoismens eller misundelsens hvæsen til tavshed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: If the power of reflecting on the past, and darting the keen eye of contemplation into futurity, be the grand privilege of man, it must be granted that some people enjoy this prerogative in a very limited degree. Every thing now appears to them wrong; and not able to distinguish the possible from the monstrous, they fear where no fear should find a place, running from the light of reason as if it were a firebrand; yet the limits of the possible have never been defined to stop the sturdy innovator's hand.
danishChanges.after: Er menneskets store privilegium evnen til at tænke over fortiden og rette eftertankens skarpe blik mod fremtiden, må man indrømme, at nogle kun nyder det i meget begrænset grad. For dem ser alt nyt forkert ud. De kan ikke skelne mellem det mulige og det uhyrlige og frygter, hvor der ingen grund er til frygt. De flygter fra fornuftens lys, som var det en brandfakkel. Men ingen har nogensinde fastlagt det muliges grænser, så den beslutsomme fornyers hånd måtte standse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Woman, however, a slave in every situation to prejudice seldom exerts enlightened maternal affection; for she either neglects her children, or spoils them by improper indulgence. Besides, the affection of some women for their children is, as I have before termed it, frequently very brutish; for it eradicates every spark of humanity. Justice, truth, every thing is sacrificed by these Rebekahs, and for the sake of their own children they violate the most sacred duties, forgetting the common relationship that binds the whole family on earth together. Yet, reason seems to say, that they who suffer one duty, or affection to swallow up the rest, have not sufficient heart or mind to fulfil that one conscientiously. It then loses the venerable aspect of a duty, and assumes the fantastic form of a whim.
danishChanges.after: Kvinden, som i enhver stilling er fordommenes slave, udøver sjældent en oplyst moderkærlighed. Enten forsømmer hun sine børn eller forkæler dem med urimelig eftergivenhed. Nogle kvinders kærlighed til deres børn er desuden, som jeg tidligere har sagt, rent dyrisk, for den udrydder enhver gnist af menneskelighed. Disse Rebekkaer ofrer retfærdighed, sandhed, alt. For deres egne børns skyld bryder de de helligste pligter og glemmer det fælles slægtskab, som binder hele jordens familie sammen. Men fornuften synes at sige, at den, der lader én pligt eller hengivenhed opsluge alle andre, ikke har hjerte eller ånd nok til samvittighedsfuldt at opfylde selv denne ene. Så mister den sit ærværdige præg af pligt og antager en lunefuld indskydelses fantastiske form.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: As the care of children in their infancy is one of the grand duties annexed to the female character by nature, this duty would afford many forcible arguments for strengthening the female understanding, if it were properly considered.
danishChanges.after: Omsorgen for små børn er en af de store pligter, naturen har knyttet til kvinden. Hvis den blev ordentligt overvejet, ville den give mange stærke argumenter for at udvikle kvinders forstand.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The formation of the mind must be begun very early, and the temper, in particular, requires the most judicious attention--an attention which women cannot pay who only love their children because they are their children, and seek no further for the foundation of their duty, than in the feelings of the moment. It is this want of reason in their affections which makes women so often run into extremes, and either be the most fond, or most careless and unnatural mothers.
danishChanges.after: Sindets dannelse må begynde meget tidligt, og især temperamentet kræver den mest velovervejede omsorg. Den kan kvinder ikke give, hvis de kun elsker børnene, fordi de er deres egne, og ikke søger pligtens grundlag andre steder end i øjeblikkets følelser. Netop manglen på fornuft i hengivenheden får så ofte kvinder til at gå til yderligheder og blive enten overdrevent kærlige eller forsømmelige og ukærlige mødre.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To be a good mother--a woman must have sense, and that independence of mind which few women possess who are taught to depend entirely on their husbands. Meek wives are, in general, foolish mothers; wanting their children to love them best, and take their part, in secret, against the father, who is held up as a scarecrow. If they are to be punished, though they have offended the mother, the father must inflict the punishment; he must be the judge in all disputes: but I shall more fully discuss this subject when I treat of private education, I now only mean to insist, that unless the understanding of woman be enlarged, and her character rendered more firm, by being allowed to govern her own conduct, she will never have sufficient sense or command of temper to manage her children properly. Her parental affection, indeed, scarcely deserves the name, when it does not lead her to suckle her children, because the discharge of this duty is equally calculated to inspire maternal and filial affection; and it is the indispensable duty of men and women to fulfil the duties which give birth to affections that are the surest preservatives against vice. Natural affection, as it is termed, I believe to be a very weak tie, affections must grow out of the habitual exercise of a mutual sympathy; and what sympathy does a mother exercise who sends her babe to a nurse, and only takes it from a nurse to send it to a school?
danishChanges.after: For at være en god mor må en kvinde have forstand og den selvstændighed i sindet, som kun få kvinder ejer, når de lærer at være helt afhængige af deres ægtemænd. Føjelige hustruer er som regel ufornuftige mødre. De ønsker, at børnene skal elske dem højest og i hemmelighed tage deres parti mod faren, som fremstilles som en skræmmefigur. Skal børnene straffes, må faren gøre det, selv når de har krænket moren. Han skal dømme i enhver strid. Jeg vil drøfte dette grundigere, når jeg behandler opdragelsen i hjemmet. Nu vil jeg blot fastholde, at kvinden aldrig får forstand eller selvbeherskelse nok til at opdrage sine børn ordentligt, medmindre hendes forstand udvides og karakteren styrkes ved, at hun får lov til at styre sin egen adfærd. Hendes forældrekærlighed fortjener faktisk knap navnet, hvis den ikke får hende til at amme sine børn. Denne pligt er lige egnet til at vække moderens og barnets hengivenhed. Både mænd og kvinder har den uomgængelige pligt at udføre de opgaver, som skaber de følelser, der sikrest beskytter mod last. Det, man kalder naturlig hengivenhed, tror jeg er et meget svagt bånd. Hengivenhed må vokse frem gennem den vanemæssige udøvelse af gensidig omsorg. Hvilken omsorg udøver en mor, som sender sit spædbarn til en amme og kun tager det fra ammen for at sende det i skole?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In the exercise of their natural feelings, providence has furnished women with a natural substitute for love, when the lover becomes only a friend and mutual confidence takes place of overstrained admiration--a child then gently twists the relaxing cord, and a mutual care produces a new mutual sympathy. But a child, though a pledge of affection, will not enliven it, if both father and mother are content to transfer the charge to hirelings; for they who do their duty by proxy should not murmur if they miss the reward of duty--parental affection produces filial duty.
danishChanges.after: Gennem kvinders naturlige følelser har forsynet givet dem en naturlig erstatning for forelskelsen, når elskeren blot bliver en ven, og gensidig tillid afløser den overdrevne beundring. Barnet strammer da blidt det slappe bånd, og fælles omsorg skaber en ny gensidig samhørighed. Men et barn, selv som tegn på hengivenhed, vil ikke give den nyt liv, hvis både far og mor gladeligt overlader omsorgen til betalt hjælp. De, der lader andre udføre deres pligt, bør ikke klage over at gå glip af dens belønning. Forældrenes kærlighed frembringer barnets pligtfølelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: There seems to be an indolent propensity in man to make prescription always take place of reason, and to place every duty on an arbitrary foundation. The rights of kings are deduced in a direct line from the King of kings; and that of parents from our first parent.
danishChanges.after: Mennesket synes af dovenskab tilbøjeligt til altid at lade hævd erstatte fornuft og give enhver pligt et vilkårligt grundlag. Kongers rettigheder udledes i lige linje fra kongernes konge og forældres fra vores første stamfar.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Why do we thus go back for principles that should always rest on the same base, and have the same weight to-day that they had a thousand years ago--and not a jot more? If parents discharge their duty they have a strong hold and sacred claim on the gratitude of their children; but few parents are willing to receive the respectful affection of their offspring on such terms. They demand blind obedience, because they do not merit a reasonable service: and to render these demands of weakness and ignorance more binding, a mysterious sanctity is spread round the most arbitrary principle; for what other name can be given to the blind duty of obeying vicious or weak beings, merely because they obeyed a powerful instinct? The simple definition of the reciprocal duty, which naturally subsists between parent and child, may be given in a few words: The parent who pays proper attention to helpless infancy has a right to require the same attention when the feebleness of age comes upon him. But to subjugate a rational being to the mere will of another, after he is of age to answer to society for his own conduct, is a most cruel and undue stretch of power; and perhaps as injurious to morality, as those religious systems which do not allow right and wrong to have any existence, but in the Divine will.
danishChanges.after: Hvorfor søger vi sådan bagud efter principper, som altid bør hvile på samme grund og have samme vægt i dag som for tusind år siden — ikke en smule mere? Opfylder forældre deres pligt, har de et stærkt og helligt krav på børnenes taknemmelighed. Men få forældre vil modtage deres børns respektfulde kærlighed på de vilkår. De kræver blind lydighed, fordi de ikke fortjener en fornuftigt begrundet tjeneste. For at gøre svaghedens og uvidenhedens krav mere bindende omgiver man det mest vilkårlige princip med en gådefuld hellighed. Hvad andet kan man kalde den blinde pligt til at adlyde lastefulde eller svage mennesker, blot fordi de fulgte et stærkt instinkt? Den naturlige, gensidige pligt mellem forælder og barn kan defineres kort: Den forælder, som viser det hjælpeløse spædbarn ordentlig omsorg, har ret til den samme omsorg, når alderens svaghed rammer. Men at underkaste et fornuftsvæsen en andens blotte vilje, efter at det er gammelt nok til at stå samfundet til ansvar for sin egen adfærd, er et grusomt og uretmæssigt magtmisbrug. Det er måske lige så skadeligt for moralen som de religionssystemer, der kun lader ret og uret eksistere i Guds vilje.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I never knew a parent who had paid more than common attention to his children, disregarded (Dr. Johnson makes the same observation.); on the contrary, the early habit of relying almost implicitly on the opinion of a respected parent is not easily shaken, even when matured reason convinces the child that his father is not the wisest man in the world. This weakness, for a weakness it is, though the epithet AMIABLE may be tacked to it, a reasonable man must steel himself against; for the absurd duty, too often inculcated, of obeying a parent only on account of his being a parent, shackles the mind, and prepares it for a slavish submission to any power but reason.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har aldrig kendt en forælder, som viste sine børn mere end almindelig omsorg, blive tilsidesat. Dr. Johnson gør samme iagttagelse. Tværtimod er den tidlige vane med næsten ubetinget at stole på en respekteret forælders mening svær at bryde, selv når den modne fornuft overbeviser barnet om, at faren ikke er verdens klogeste mand. Denne svaghed — for en svaghed er det, selv om man kan kalde den ELSKELIG — må det fornuftige menneske ruste sig imod. Den urimelige pligt, man så ofte indprenter, til at adlyde en forælder alene af den grund, at han er forælder, lænker sindet og forbereder det på slavisk underkastelse under enhver anden magt end fornuften.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I distinguish between the natural and accidental duty due to parents.
danishChanges.after: Jeg skelner mellem den naturlige pligt mod forældrene og den, der alene skyldes tilfældige forhold.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The parent who sedulously endeavours to form the heart and enlarge the understanding of his child, has given that dignity to the discharge of a duty, common to the whole animal world, that only reason can give. This is the parental affection of humanity, and leaves instinctive natural affection far behind. Such a parent acquires all the rights of the most sacred friendship, and his advice, even when his child is advanced in life, demands serious consideration.
danishChanges.after: Den forælder, der ihærdigt forsøger at forme sit barns hjerte og udvide dets forstand, giver udførelsen af en pligt, som er fælles for hele dyreverdenen, den værdighed, kun fornuften kan give. Det er menneskelig forældrekærlighed, som langt overgår den instinktive naturlige hengivenhed. En sådan forælder vinder alle det helligste venskabs rettigheder. Selv når barnet er langt henne i livet, kræver forælderens råd alvorlig overvejelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: With respect to marriage, though after one and twenty a parent seems to have no right to withhold his consent on any account; yet twenty years of solicitude call for a return, and the son ought, at least, to promise not to marry for two or three years, should the object of his choice not entirely meet with the approbation of his first friend.
danishChanges.after: Hvad ægteskab angår, synes en forælder ikke at have nogen ret til at nægte sit samtykke efter barnets enogtyvende år, uanset grunden. Alligevel kræver tyve års omsorg noget til gengæld. Hvis valget ikke helt godkendes af denne barnets første ven, bør sønnen i det mindste love at vente to eller tre år med at gifte sig.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, respect for parents is, generally speaking, a much more debasing principle; it is only a selfish respect for property. The father who is blindly obeyed, is obeyed from sheer weakness, or from motives that degrade the human character.
danishChanges.after: Men respekten for forældre bygger som regel på et langt mere fornedrende princip: Den er blot egoistisk respekt for ejendom. Den far, der adlydes blindt, adlydes enten af ren svaghed eller af motiver, der nedværdiger menneskets karakter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A great proportion of the misery that wanders, in hideous forms around the world, is allowed to rise from the negligence of parents; and still these are the people who are most tenacious of what they term a natural right, though it be subversive of the birth right of man, the right of acting according to the direction of his own reason.
danishChanges.after: Man anerkender, at en stor del af den elendighed, som vandrer gennem verden i hæslige skikkelser, udspringer af forældres forsømmelighed. Alligevel holder netop disse forældre mest stædigt fast ved det, de kalder en naturlig ret, selv om den undergraver menneskets fødselsret: retten til at handle efter sin egen fornuft.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I have already very frequently had occasion to observe, that vicious or indolent people are always eager to profit by enforcing arbitrary privileges; and generally in the same proportion as they neglect the discharge of the duties which alone render the privileges reasonable. This is at the bottom, a dictate of common sense, or the instinct of self-defence, peculiar to ignorant weakness; resembling that instinct, which makes a fish muddy the water it swims in to elude its enemy, instead of boldly facing it in the clear stream.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har allerede ofte haft anledning til at bemærke, at lastefulde eller dovne mennesker altid ivrigt søger fordel ved at håndhæve vilkårlige privilegier. Som regel er de desto ivrigere, jo mere de forsømmer de pligter, som alene gør privilegierne rimelige. I bund og grund er det en tilskyndelse fra den sunde fornuft eller den uvidende svagheds særlige selvforsvarsinstinkt. Det ligner instinktet, der får en fisk til at grumse vandet for at undslippe fjenden i stedet for modigt at møde den i den klare strøm.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: >From the clear stream of argument, indeed, the supporters of prescription, of every denomination, fly: and taking refuge in the darkness, which, in the language of sublime poetry, has been supposed to surround the throne of Omnipotence, they dare to demand that implicit respect which is only due to His unsearchable ways. But, let me not be thought presumptuous, the darkness which hides our God from us, only respects speculative truths-- it never obscures moral ones, they shine clearly, for God is light, and never, by the constitution of our nature, requires the discharge of a duty, the reasonableness of which does not beam on us when we open our eyes.
danishChanges.after: Alle slags forsvarere af hævd flygter netop fra argumentationens klare strøm. De søger ly i det mørke, som den ophøjede poesis sprog har forestillet sig omkring den Almægtiges trone, og vover at kræve den ubetingede respekt, som kun tilkommer hans uransagelige veje. Men lad mig ikke blive regnet for formastelig: Det mørke, der skjuler Gud for os, gælder kun spekulative sandheder, aldrig moralske. De lyser klart, for Gud er lys. Med den natur, han har givet os, kræver han aldrig, at vi opfylder en pligt, hvis rimelighed ikke stråler os i møde, når vi åbner øjnene.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The indolent parent of high rank may, it is true, extort a show of respect from his child, and females on the continent are particularly subject to the views of their families, who never think of consulting their inclination, or providing for the comfort of the poor victims of their pride. The consequence is notorious; these dutiful daughters become adulteresses, and neglect the education of their children, from whom they, in their turn, exact the same kind of obedience.
danishChanges.after: En doven forælder af høj stand kan ganske vist aftvinge sit barn en ydre respekt. Især kvinder på kontinentet underkastes familiens planer, uden at nogen tænker på deres ønsker eller på lykken for de stakkels ofre for familiens stolthed. Følgen er velkendt: Disse pligtopfyldende døtre bliver utro hustruer og forsømmer deres børns opdragelse, mens de til gengæld kræver samme slags lydighed af dem.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations. Parent review: restore parental pride as cause of victimization.

danishChanges.before: Females, it is true, in all countries, are too much under the dominion of their parents; and few parents think of addressing their children in the following manner, though it is in this reasonable way that Heaven seems to command the whole human race. It is your interest to obey me till you can judge for yourself; and the Almighty Father of all has implanted an affection in me to serve as a guard to you whilst your reason is unfolding; but when your mind arrives at maturity, you must only obey me, or rather respect my opinions, so far as they coincide with the light that is breaking in on your own mind.
danishChanges.after: Kvinder er ganske vist i alle lande alt for stærkt underlagt deres forældre. Få forældre tænker på at tale sådan til deres børn, selv om himlen synes at lede hele menneskeheden på netop denne fornuftige måde: Det er til dit eget bedste at adlyde mig, indtil du selv kan dømme. Alles almægtige far har lagt en kærlighed i mig, som skal beskytte dig, mens din fornuft udvikler sig. Men når dit sind er modent, skal du kun adlyde mig — eller rettere respektere mine meninger — i det omfang, de stemmer med det lys, der bryder frem i dit eget sind.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A slavish bondage to parents cramps every faculty of the mind; and Mr. Locke very judiciously observes, that "if the mind be curbed and humbled too much in children; if their spirits be abased and broken much by too strict an hand over them; they lose all their vigour and industry." This strict hand may, in some degree, account for the weakness of women; for girls, from various causes, are more kept down by their parents, in every sense of the word, than boys. The duty expected from them is, like all the duties arbitrarily imposed on women, more from a sense of propriety, more out of respect for decorum, than reason; and thus taught slavishly to submit to their parents, they are prepared for the slavery of marriage. I may be told that a number of women are not slaves in the marriage state. True, but they then become tyrants; for it is not rational freedom, but a lawless kind of power, resembling the authority exercised by the favourites of absolute monarchs, which they obtain by debasing means. I do not, likewise, dream of insinuating that either boys or girls are always slaves, I only insist, that when they are obliged to submit to authority blindly, their faculties are weakened, and their tempers rendered imperious or abject. I also lament, that parents, indolently availing themselves of a supposed privilege, damp the first faint glimmering of reason rendering at the same time the duty, which they are so anxious to enforce, an empty name; because they will not let it rest on the only basis on which a duty can rest securely: for, unless it be founded on knowledge, it cannot gain sufficient strength to resist the squalls of passion, or the silent sapping of self-love. But it is not the parents who have given the surest proof of their affection for their children, (or, to speak more properly, who by fulfilling their duty, have allowed a natural parental affection to take root in their hearts, the child of exercised sympathy and reason, and not the over-weening offspring of selfish pride,) who most vehemently insist on their children submitting to their will, merely because it is their will. On the contrary, the parent who sets a good example, patiently lets that example work; and it seldom fails to produce its natural effect--filial respect.
danishChanges.after: Slavisk underkastelse under forældrene hæmmer alle sindets evner. Locke bemærker meget fornuftigt, at »hvis børns sind tøjles og ydmyges for meget, hvis deres mod sænkes og knækkes af en for streng hånd, mister de al deres kraft og flid«. Denne strenge hånd kan til dels forklare kvinders svaghed. Piger holdes af forskellige grunde mere nede af forældrene end drenge, i enhver betydning af ordet. Den pligt, man forventer af dem, bygger ligesom alle vilkårligt pålagte kvindepligter mere på sømmelighed og hensyn til det passende end på fornuft. Når de lærer slavisk at underkaste sig forældrene, forberedes de på ægteskabets slaveri. Man kan indvende, at mange kvinder ikke er slaver i ægteskabet. Sandt, men så bliver de tyranner. Den magt, de skaffer sig med nedværdigende midler, er ikke fornuftig frihed, men lovløs magt som den, enevældige monarkers yndlinge udøver. Jeg antyder heller ikke, at drenge eller piger altid er slaver. Jeg fastholder blot, at blind lydighed mod myndighed svækker deres evner og gør deres temperament enten bydende eller krybende. Jeg beklager også, at forældre dovent udnytter et formodet privilegium og slukker fornuftens første svage glimt. Dermed gør de den pligt, de så ivrigt vil håndhæve, til et tomt navn. De vil ikke lade den hvile på det eneste sikre grundlag: kundskab. Uden den får pligten ikke styrke nok til at modstå lidenskabens stormstød eller selvkærlighedens stille undergravning. Men det er ikke de forældre, der sikrest har vist deres kærlighed, som heftigst kræver, at børnene følger deres vilje, blot fordi den er deres. Eller mere præcist: Det er ikke dem, der ved at opfylde deres pligt har ladet en naturlig forældrekærlighed slå rod i hjertet, født af udøvet omsorg og fornuft, ikke af egoistisk stoltheds overmod.
