Tværtimod lader den forælder, der viser et godt eksempel, tålmodigt eksemplet virke. Det frembringer sjældent andet end sin naturlige følge: barnets respekt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Children cannot be taught too early to submit to reason, the true definition of that necessity, which Rousseau insisted on, without defining it; for to submit to reason, is to submit to the nature of things, and to that God who formed them so, to promote our real interest.
danishChanges.after: Børn kan ikke for tidligt lære at følge fornuften. Det er den rette definition af den nødvendighed, Rousseau insisterede på uden at definere den. At underordne sig fornuften er nemlig at følge tingenes natur og den Gud, som formede dem sådan for at fremme vores sande bedste.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Why should the minds of children be warped as they just begin to expand, only to favour the indolence of parents, who insist on a privilege without being willing to pay the price fixed by nature? I have before had occasion to observe, that a right always includes a duty, and I think it may, likewise fairly be inferred, that they forfeit the right, who do not fulfil the duty.
danishChanges.after: Hvorfor skal børnenes sind fordrejes, netop som de begynder at udfolde sig, blot for at tjene dovne forældre, der kræver et privilegium uden at ville betale naturens pris for det? Jeg har tidligere bemærket, at en rettighed altid rummer en pligt. Jeg mener, man lige så rimeligt kan slutte, at den, der ikke opfylder pligten, mister rettigheden.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is easier, I grant, to command than reason; but it does not follow from hence, that children cannot comprehend the reason why they are made to do certain things habitually; for, from a steady adherence to a few simple principles of conduct flows that salutary power, which a judicious parent gradually gains over a child's mind. And this power becomes strong indeed, if tempered by an even display of affection brought home to the child's heart. For, I believe, as a general rule, it must be allowed, that the affection which we inspire always resembles that we cultivate; so that natural affections, which have been supposed almost distinct from reason, may be found more nearly connected with judgment than is commonly allowed. Nay, as another proof of the necessity of cultivating the female understanding, it is but just to observe, that the affections seem to have a kind of animal capriciousness when they merely reside in the heart.
danishChanges.after: Det er lettere at befale end at begrunde, det indrømmer jeg. Men det betyder ikke, at børn ikke kan forstå, hvorfor de skal vænne sig til bestemte handlinger. Den gavnlige myndighed, en fornuftig forælder gradvis får over barnets sind, udspringer af en fast overholdelse af få enkle adfærdsprincipper. Den bliver virkelig stærk, når den mildnes af en jævn kærlighed, som barnet mærker i sit hjerte. Som almindelig regel må man efter min mening anerkende, at den hengivenhed, vi vækker, ligner den, vi selv dyrker. De naturlige følelser, som man næsten har regnet for adskilt fra fornuften, kan derfor vise sig nærmere knyttet til dømmekraften, end man normalt indrømmer. Som endnu et bevis på nødvendigheden af at udvikle kvinders forstand er det rimeligt at bemærke, at følelserne synes at have en slags dyrisk lunefuldhed, når de kun bor i hjertet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is the irregular exercise of parental authority that first injures the mind, and to these irregularities girls are more subject than boys. The will of those who never allow their will to be disputed, unless they happen to be in a good humour, when they relax proportionally, is almost always unreasonable. To elude this arbitrary authority, girls very early learn the lessons which they afterwards practise on their husbands; for I have frequently seen a little sharp-faced miss rule a whole family, excepting that now and then mamma's anger will burst out of some accidental cloud-- either her hair was ill-dressed,* or she had lost more money at cards, the night before, than she was willing to own to her husband; or some such moral cause of anger.
danishChanges.after: Det er den ustadige udøvelse af forældremyndigheden, der først skader sindet, og piger er mere udsat for den end drenge. Viljen hos dem, der aldrig tåler indsigelser, medmindre de tilfældigvis er i godt humør og slækker tilsvarende på kravene, er næsten altid urimelig. For at omgå denne vilkårlige myndighed lærer piger meget tidligt de kneb, de senere bruger over for deres mænd. Jeg har ofte set en lille frøken med spidse ansigtstræk styre en hel familie, bortset fra de gange, hvor mammas vrede bryder frem fra en tilfældig sky: Hendes hår er måske sat forkert,* eller hun tabte flere penge ved kortbordet aftenen før, end hun vil indrømme over for sin mand, eller hun har en lignende moralsk grund til vrede.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: (*Fodnote. Jeg har selv engang hørt en lille pige sige til en tjenestepige: »Min mor har skændt grundigt på mig i morges, fordi hendes hår ikke var sat efter hendes hoved.« Selv om denne bemærkning var næsvis, var den rammende. Og hvilken respekt kunne en pige opnå for en sådan forælder uden at gøre vold på fornuften?)
danishChanges.after: (*Fodnote. Jeg hørte engang selv en lille pige sige til en tjenestepige: »Mamma har skældt mig grundigt ud i morges, fordi hendes hår ikke var sat, som hun ville have det.« Bemærkningen var næsvis, men rigtig. Hvordan skulle pigen kunne få respekt for sådan en forælder uden at gøre vold på fornuften?)
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: After observing sallies of this kind, I have been led into a melancholy train of reflection respecting females, concluding that when their first affection must lead them astray, or make their duties clash till they rest on mere whims and customs, little can be expected from them as they advance in life. How, indeed, can an instructor remedy this evil? for to teach them virtue on any solid principle is to teach them to despise their parents. Children cannot, ought not to be taught to make allowance for the faults of their parents, because every such allowance weakens the force of reason in their minds, and makes them still more indulgent to their own. It is one of the most sublime virtues of maturity that leads us to be severe with respect to ourselves, and forbearing to others; but children should only be taught the simple virtues, for if they begin too early to make allowance for human passions and manners, they wear off the fine edge of the criterion by which they should regulate their own, and become unjust in the same proportion as they grow indulgent.
danishChanges.after: Når jeg har set den slags udbrud, er jeg blevet ledt ind i triste overvejelser om kvinder. Hvis deres første hengivenhed må føre dem på afveje eller bringe pligterne i konflikt, indtil de blot hviler på luner og skik, kan man kun vente lidt af dem senere i livet. Hvordan skal en lærer overhovedet afhjælpe det? At lære dem dyd på et fast grundlag bliver jo at lære dem at foragte deres forældre. Børn kan og bør ikke lære at undskylde forældrenes fejl. Enhver sådan undskyldning svækker fornuftens kraft i deres sind og gør dem endnu mere overbærende med egne fejl. Det er en af modenhedens højeste dyder at være streng mod sig selv og overbærende mod andre. Men børn bør kun lære de enkle dyder. Begynder de for tidligt at gøre indrømmelser til menneskers lidenskaber og adfærd, slider de skarpheden af den målestok, de bør styre deres egen adfærd efter, og bliver uretfærdige i samme grad, som de bliver overbærende.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The affections of children, and weak people, are always selfish; they love others, because others love them, and not on account of their virtues. Yet, till esteem and love are blended together in the first affection, and reason made the foundation of the first duty, morality will stumble at the threshold. But, till society is very differently constituted, parents, I fear, will still insist on being obeyed, because they will be obeyed, and constantly endeavour to settle that power on a Divine right, which will not bear the investigation of reason.
danishChanges.after: Børns og svage menneskers hengivenhed er altid egoistisk. De elsker andre, fordi de andre elsker dem, ikke på grund af deres dyder. Men indtil respekt og kærlighed forenes i den første hengivenhed, og fornuft gøres til den første pligts grundlag, vil moralen snuble allerede på tærsklen. Før samfundet bliver helt anderledes indrettet, frygter jeg dog, at forældre fortsat vil kræve lydighed, fordi de vil adlydes. De vil bestandigt forsøge at bygge den magt, der ikke tåler fornuftens undersøgelse, på en guddommelig ret.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The good effects resulting from attention to private education will ever be very confined, and the parent who really puts his own hand to the plow, will always, in some degree be disappointed, till education becomes a grand national concern. A man cannot retire into a desert with his child, and if he did, he could not bring himself back to childhood, and become the proper friend and play-fellow of an infant or youth. And when children are confined to the society of men and women, they very soon acquire that kind of premature manhood which stops the growth of every vigorous power of mind or body. In order to open their faculties they should be excited to think for themselves; and this can only be done by mixing a number of children together, and making them jointly pursue the same objects.
danishChanges.after: Den omhu, man lægger i opdragelsen i hjemmet, vil altid kun have begrænset virkning. Den forælder, der selv lægger hånden på ploven, vil i nogen grad blive skuffet, indtil uddannelse bliver en stor national opgave. Man kan ikke trække sig ud i en ødemark med sit barn, og selv hvis man kunne, kunne man ikke vende tilbage til barndommen og blive en passende ven og legekammerat for et lille eller større barn. Når børn kun omgås voksne, får de meget hurtigt en for tidlig voksenhed, der standser enhver kraftfuld udvikling af krop og sind. Skal deres evner åbnes, må de opmuntres til selv at tænke. Det kan kun ske, når flere børn færdes sammen og arbejder mod fælles mål.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A child very soon contracts a benumbing indolence of mind, which he has seldom sufficient vigour to shake off, when he only asks a question instead of seeking for information, and then relies implicitly on the answer he receives. With his equals in age this could never be the case, and the subjects of inquiry, though they might be influenced, would not be entirely under the direction of men, who frequently damp, if not destroy abilities, by bringing them forward too hastily: and too hastily they will infallibly be brought forward, if the child could be confined to the society of a man, however sagacious that man may be.
danishChanges.after: Et barn får hurtigt en sløvende åndelig dovenskab, som det sjældent har kraft nok til at ryste af sig, hvis det blot stiller spørgsmål i stedet for selv at søge viden og derefter ubetinget stoler på svarene. Blandt jævnaldrende ville det ikke ske. De voksnes indflydelse kunne påvirke, men ikke fuldstændig styre, hvad børnene undersøgte. Voksne dæmper ofte evnerne, hvis de ikke ødelægger dem, ved at drive dem for hurtigt frem. Og det vil uundgåeligt ske, hvis barnet begrænses til én voksens selskab, hvor indsigtsfuld denne end er.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, in youth the seeds of every affection should be sown, and the respectful regard, which is felt for a parent, is very different from the social affections that are to constitute the happiness of life as it advances. Of these, equality is the basis, and an intercourse of sentiments unclogged by that observant seriousness which prevents disputation, though it may not inforce submission. Let a child have ever such an affection for his parent, he will always languish to play and chat with children; and the very respect he entertains, for filial esteem always has a dash of fear mixed with it, will, if it do not teach him cunning, at least prevent him from pouring out the little secrets which first open the heart to friendship and confidence, gradually leading to more expansive benevolence. Added to this, he will never acquire that frank ingenuousness of behaviour, which young people can only attain by being frequently in society, where they dare to speak what they think; neither afraid of being reproved for their presumption, nor laughed at for their folly.
danishChanges.after: Desuden bør frøene til enhver hengivenhed sås i ungdommen. Den respektfulde kærlighed til en forælder er meget forskellig fra de følelser mellem ligemænd, som senere skal skabe livets lykke. De bygger på lighed og på en udveksling af tanker og følelser, som ikke hæmmes af den ærbødige alvor, der forhindrer diskussion, selv om den ikke direkte kræver underkastelse. Hvor meget et barn end elsker sin forælder, vil det længes efter at lege og tale med andre børn. Selve respekten — barnets agtelse rummer altid lidt frygt — vil, hvis den ikke lærer barnet at være snu, i det mindste hindre det i at fortælle de små hemmeligheder, der først åbner hjertet for venskab og tillid og siden for en videre menneskekærlighed. Barnet vil heller ikke få den åbne ligefremhed, unge kun lærer ved ofte at være blandt nogen, hvor de tør sige, hvad de tænker, uden frygt for at blive irettesat for selvsikkerhed eller leet ad for tåbelighed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Forcibly impressed by the reflections which the sight of schools, as they are at present conducted, naturally suggested, I have formerly delivered my opinion rather warmly in favour of a private education; but further experience has led me to view the subject in a different light. I still, however, think schools, as they are now regulated, the hot-beds of vice and folly, and the knowledge of human nature, supposed to be attained there, merely cunning selfishness.
danishChanges.after: Synet af skolerne, som de drives nu, gjorde så stærkt indtryk på mig, at jeg tidligere ret varmt talte for opdragelse i hjemmet. Men mere erfaring har fået mig til at se anderledes på sagen. Jeg regner dog stadig skolerne, som de nu er indrettet, for arnesteder for last og dårskab. Det kendskab til menneskenaturen, man angiveligt får dér, er blot snu egoisme.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: At school, boys become gluttons and slovens, and, instead of cultivating domestic affections, very early rush into the libertinism which destroys the constitution before it is formed; hardening the heart as it weakens the understanding.
danishChanges.after: I skolen bliver drenge frådsere og sjuskehoveder. I stedet for at udvikle kærligheden til hjemmet kaster de sig meget tidligt ud i udskejelser, der ødelægger kroppen, før den er færdigudviklet, og hærder hjertet, mens de svækker forstanden.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I should, in fact, be averse to boarding-schools, if it were for no other reason than the unsettled state of mind which the expectation of the vacations produce. On these the children's thoughts are fixed with eager anticipating hopes, for, at least, to speak with moderation, half of the time, and when they arrive they are spent in total dissipation and beastly indulgence.
danishChanges.after: Jeg ville faktisk være imod kostskoler alene på grund af den uro i sindet, som forventningen om ferierne skaber. Mindst halvdelen af tiden, forsigtigt anslået, er børnenes tanker ivrigt rettet mod ferien. Og når den kommer, går den med rene adspredelser og dyrisk selvforkælelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, on the contrary, when they are brought up at home, though they may pursue a plan of study in a more orderly manner than can be adopted, when near a fourth part of the year is actually spent in idleness, and as much more in regret and anticipation; yet they there acquire too high an opinion of their own importance, from being allowed to tyrannize over servants, and from the anxiety expressed by most mothers, on the score of manners, who, eager to teach the accomplishments of a gentleman, stifle, in their birth, the virtues of a man. Thus brought into company when they ought to be seriously employed, and treated like men when they are still boys, they become vain and effeminate.
danishChanges.after: Opdrages børnene derimod hjemme, kan de følge en mere ordnet studieplan end dér, hvor næsten en fjerdedel af året tilbringes i lediggang og lige så meget med savn og forventning. Men hjemme får de for høje tanker om deres egen betydning, fordi de får lov at tyrannisere tjenestefolkene, og fordi de fleste mødre er så bekymrede for manererne. I deres iver efter at lære barnet en gentlemans færdigheder kvæler de menneskets dyder i fødslen. Drengene bringes således i selskab, når de burde arbejde alvorligt, og behandles som mænd, mens de stadig er drenge. Det gør dem forfængelige og blødagtige.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The only way to avoid two extremes equally injurious to morality, would be to contrive some way of combining a public and private education. Thus to make men citizens, two natural steps might be taken, which seem directly to lead to the desired point; for the domestic affections, that first open the heart to the various modifications of humanity would be cultivated, whilst the children were nevertheless allowed to spend great part of their time, on terms of equality, with other children.
danishChanges.after: Den eneste måde at undgå disse to lige skadelige yderligheder ville være at finde en forening af fælles skolegang og opdragelse i hjemmet. To naturlige skridt kunne dermed føre direkte mod målet om at gøre mennesker til borgere. Hjemmets hengivenhed, som først åbner hjertet for menneskelighedens mange former, ville blive udviklet, mens børnene samtidig fik lov at tilbringe en stor del af tiden på lige fod med andre børn.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I still recollect, with pleasure, the country day school; where a boy trudged in the morning, wet or dry, carrying his books, and his dinner, if it were at a considerable distance; a servant did not then lead master by the hand, for, when he had once put on coat and breeches, he was allowed to shift for himself, and return alone in the evening to recount the feats of the day close at the parental knee. His father's house was his home, and was ever after fondly remembered; nay, I appeal to some superior men who were educated in this manner, whether the recollection of some shady lane where they conned their lesson; or, of some stile, where they sat making a kite, or mending a bat, has not endeared their country to them?
danishChanges.after: Jeg husker stadig med glæde landsbyens dagskole, hvor drengen traskede hen om morgenen i regn og sol med bøgerne og, hvis der var langt, sin middagsmad. Ingen tjener førte den unge herre ved hånden. Når han først havde fået jakke og bukser på, måtte han klare sig selv og vende alene hjem om aftenen for ved forældrenes knæ at fortælle om dagens bedrifter. Farens hus var hans hjem og blev siden altid mindet med kærlighed. Jeg spørger nogle af de fremragende mænd, der blev opdraget sådan: Har mindet om en skyggefuld vej, hvor de lærte lektien, eller en stente, hvor de sad og lavede en drage eller reparerede et bat, ikke gjort hjemlandet kært for dem?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But, what boy ever recollected with pleasure the years he spent in close confinement, at an academy near London? unless indeed he should by chance remember the poor scare-crow of an usher whom he tormented; or, the tartman, from whom he caught a cake, to devour it with the cattish appetite of selfishness. At boarding schools of every description, the relaxation of the junior boys is mischief; and of the senior, vice. Besides, in great schools what can be more prejudicial to the moral character, than the system of tyranny and abject slavery which is established amongst the boys, to say nothing of the slavery to forms, which makes religion worse than a farce? For what good can be expected from the youth who receives the sacrament of the Lord's supper, to avoid forfeiting half-a-guinea, which he probably afterwards spends in some sensual manner? Half the employment of the youths is to elude the necessity of attending public worship; and well they may, for such a constant repetition of the same thing must be a very irksome restraint on their natural vivacity. As these ceremonies have the most fatal effect on their morals, and as a ritual performed by the lips, when the heart and mind are far away, is not now stored up by our church as a bank to draw on for the fees of the poor souls in purgatory, why should they not be abolished?
danishChanges.after: Men hvilken dreng har nogensinde med glæde husket årene i tæt indespærring på en skole nær London? Måske mindes han tilfældigvis den stakkels fugleskræmsel af en hjælpelærer, han plagede, eller kagesælgeren, fra hvem han snuppede en kage og fortærede den med egoismens katteagtige appetit. På alle slags kostskoler består de yngres adspredelse i drengestreger og de ældres i last. Og hvad kan på de store skoler skade den moralske karakter mere end det system af tyranni og krybende slaveri, som findes mellem drengene? Dertil kommer slaveriet under formerne, som gør religionen værre end en farce. Hvad godt kan man vente af den unge, som går til nadver for ikke at miste en halv guinea, der bagefter sandsynligvis bruges på sanselig nydelse? De unge bruger halvdelen af deres energi på at undgå gudstjenesten, og det kan man godt forstå. Den evige gentagelse må være en meget trættende begrænsning af deres naturlige livlighed. Når disse ceremonier skader moralen så dybt, og vores kirke ikke længere gemmer et ritual udført med læberne, mens hjerte og sind er langt borte, som en bank at trække på til betaling for de arme sjæle i skærsilden, hvorfor afskaffer man dem så ikke?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But the fear of innovation, in this country, extends to every thing. This is only a covert fear, the apprehensive timidity of indolent slugs, who guard, by sliming it over, the snug place, which they consider in the light of an hereditary estate; and eat, drink, and enjoy themselves, instead of fulfilling the duties, excepting a few empty forms, for which it was endowed. These are the people who most strenuously insist on the will of the founder being observed, crying out against all reformation, as if it were a violation of justice. I am now alluding particularly to the relicks of popery retained in our colleges, where the protestant members seem to be such sticklers for the established church; but their zeal never makes them lose sight of the spoil of ignorance, which rapacious priests of superstitious memory have scraped together. No, wise in their generation, they venerate the prescriptive right of possession, as a strong hold, and still let the sluggish bell tingle to prayers, as during the days, when the elevation of the host was supposed to atone for the sins of the people, lest one reformation should lead to another, and the spirit kill the letter. These Romish customs have the most baneful effect on the morals of our clergy; for the idle vermin who two or three times a day perform, in the most slovenly manner a service which they think useless, but call their duty, soon lose a sense of duty. At college, forced to attend or evade public worship, they acquire an habitual contempt for the very service, the performance of which is to enable them to live in idleness. It is mumbled over as an affair of business, as a stupid boy repeats his task, and frequently the college cant escapes from the preacher the moment after he has left the pulpit, and even whilst he is eating the dinner which he earned in such a dishonest manner.
danishChanges.after: Men frygten for fornyelse omfatter alt her i landet. Det er blot en skjult frygt, dovne snegles ængstelige skyhed. De beskytter deres lune plads ved at dække den med slim og betragter den som arvet ejendom. De spiser, drikker og nyder livet i stedet for, bortset fra nogle tomme former, at udføre de pligter, pladsen blev forsynet med midler til. Netop de kræver ivrigst, at stifterens vilje respekteres, og råber mod enhver reform, som om den krænkede retfærdigheden. Jeg tænker især på de katolske rester i vores kollegier, hvor de protestantiske medlemmer synes så ivrige for den etablerede kirke. Men deres nidkærhed lader dem aldrig glemme det bytte fra uvidenheden, som grådige præster fra overtroens tid skrabede sammen. Nej, kloge i deres slægt ærer de den hævdvundne ejendomsret som en fæstning og lader stadig den sløve klokke ringe til bøn, som dengang messens opløftelse af hostien skulle sone folkets synder. De frygter, at én reform fører til en anden, og at ånden slår bogstavet ihjel. Disse romerske skikke har den værste indflydelse på præsteskabets moral. De ledige snyltedyr, der to eller tre gange om dagen sjusket udfører en gudstjeneste, de finder nytteløs, men kalder deres pligt, mister snart pligtfølelsen. På kollegiet tvinges de til at overvære eller undvige gudstjenesten og lærer dermed en indgroet foragt for netop den tjeneste, der senere skal give dem et liv i lediggang. Den mumles igennem som en forretning, ligesom en dum dreng remser lektien op. Ofte slipper kollegiets indforståede jargon ud af prædikanten straks efter prædikestolen, endda mens han spiser den middag, han har tjent på så uhæderlig vis.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Nothing, indeed, can be more irreverent than the cathedral service as it is now performed in this country, neither does it contain a set of weaker men than those who are the slaves of this childish routine. A disgusting skeleton of the former state is still exhibited; but all the solemnity, that interested the imagination, if it did not purify the heart, is stripped off. The performance of high mass on the continent must impress every mind, where a spark of fancy glows, with that awful melancholy, that sublime tenderness, so near a-kin to devotion. I do not say, that these devotional feelings are of more use, in a moral sense, than any other emotion of taste; but I contend, that the theatrical pomp which gratifies our senses, is to be preferred to the cold parade that insults the understanding without reaching the heart.
danishChanges.after: Intet kan faktisk være mere respektløst end domkirkegudstjenesten, som den nu udføres her i landet, og ingen gruppe er svagere end de mænd, der er slaver af denne barnlige rutine. Et frastødende skelet af den tidligere tilstand vises stadig frem, men al den højtidelighed, der greb fantasien, selv hvis den ikke rensede hjertet, er fjernet. En højmesse på kontinentet må fylde ethvert sind, hvor blot en gnist af fantasi gløder, med den højtidelige vemodighed og ophøjede ømhed, der er så nært beslægtet med fromhed. Jeg siger ikke, at disse religiøse følelser er moralsk nyttigere end andre æstetiske følelser. Men den teatralske pragt, der glæder sanserne, er bedre end en kold opvisning, som fornærmer forstanden uden at nå hjertet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Amongst remarks on national education, such observations cannot be misplaced, especially as the supporters of these establishments, degenerated into puerilities, affect to be the champions of religion. Religion, pure source of comfort in this vale of tears! how has thy clear stream been muddied by the dabblers, who have presumptuously endeavoured to confine in one narrow channel, the living waters that ever flow toward God-- the sublime ocean of existence! What would life be without that peace which the love of God, when built on humanity, alone can impart? Every earthly affection turns back, at intervals, to prey upon the heart that feeds it; and the purest effusions of benevolence, often rudely damped by men, must mount as a free-will offering to Him who gave them birth, whose bright image they faintly reflect.
danishChanges.after: Sådanne betragtninger er ikke malplacerede i en drøftelse af national uddannelse, især fordi forsvarerne for disse institutioner, der er forfaldet til barnagtighed, udgiver sig for religionens forkæmpere. Religion, du rene kilde til trøst i denne tåredal! Hvor er din klare strøm blevet grumset af de fuskere, som formasteligt vil tvinge det levende vand ind i én smal kanal, selv om det evigt strømmer mod Gud, tilværelsens ophøjede hav! Hvad ville livet være uden den fred, som kun kærligheden til Gud kan give, når den bygger på menneskelighed? Enhver jordisk hengivenhed vender sig fra tid til anden og fortærer det hjerte, der nærer den. Og menneskekærlighedens reneste udbrud, ofte brutalt dæmpet af andre, må stige op som et frivilligt offer til ham, der skabte dem, og hvis klare billede de svagt spejler.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In public schools, however, religion, confounded with irksome ceremonies and unreasonable restraints, assumes the most ungracious aspect: not the sober austere one that commands respect whilst it inspires fear; but a ludicrous cast, that serves to point a pun. For, in fact, most of the good stories and smart things which enliven the spirits that have been concentrated at whist, are manufactured out of the incidents to which the very men labour to give a droll turn who countenance the abuse to live on the spoil.
danishChanges.after: På de store skoler antager religionen imidlertid sit mest utiltalende udseende, når den blandes sammen med trættende ceremonier og urimelige begrænsninger. Det er ikke den alvorlige strenghed, der kræver respekt og vækker frygt, men et latterligt præg, der giver stof til ordspil. De fleste gode historier og vittigheder, der liver op efter whistspillets koncentration, fremstilles faktisk af hændelser, som netop de mænd giver en komisk drejning, der støtter misbruget for at leve af dets udbytte.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: There is not, perhaps, in the kingdom, a more dogmatical or luxurious set of men, than the pedantic tyrants who reside in colleges and preside at public schools. The vacations are equally injurious to the morals of the masters and pupils, and the intercourse, which the former keep up with the nobility, introduces the same vanity and extravagance into their families, which banish domestic duties and comforts from the lordly mansion, whose state is awkwardly aped on a smaller scale. The boys, who live at a great expence with the masters and assistants, are never domesticated, though placed there for that purpose; for, after a silent dinner, they swallow a hasty glass of wine, and retire to plan some mischievous trick, or to ridicule the person or manners of the very people they have just been cringing to, and whom they ought to consider as the representatives of their parents.
danishChanges.after: Der findes måske ingen mere skråsikker eller luksusvant gruppe i riget end de pedantiske tyranner, der bor på kollegierne og leder de store skoler. Ferierne skader både lærernes og elevernes moral. Lærernes omgang med adelen fører den samme forfængelighed og ødselhed ind i deres familier, som fordriver hjemmets pligter og glæder fra herregården. Dens pragt efterabes kejtet i mindre målestok. De drenge, der dyrt indlogeres hos lærerne og deres medhjælpere, bliver aldrig del af hjemmet, selv om det er formålet. Efter en tavs middag sluger de hastigt et glas vin og trækker sig tilbage for at planlægge en drengestreg eller gøre nar af udseendet eller manererne hos netop dem, de lige har krøbet for, og som de burde betragte som deres forældres stedfortrædere.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Can it then be a matter of surprise, that boys become selfish and vicious who are thus shut out from social converse? or that a mitre often graces the brow of one of these diligent pastors? The desire of living in the same style, as the rank just above them, infects each individual and every class of people, and meanness is the concomitant of this ignoble ambition; but those professions are most debasing whose ladder is patronage; yet out of one of these professions the tutors of youth are in general chosen. But, can they be expected to inspire independent sentiments, whose conduct must be regulated by the cautious prudence that is ever on the watch for preferment?
danishChanges.after: Kan det da overraske, at drenge bliver egoistiske og lastefulde, når de udelukkes fra almindeligt samvær? Eller at en bispehue ofte pryder en af disse flittige hyrders pande? Ønsket om at leve som klassen lige ovenover smitter enhver person og enhver stand. Smålighed følger denne uædle ambition. Men mest nedværdigende er de erhverv, hvor forbindelser er stigen opad, og fra netop et af disse erhverv vælges ungdommens lærere som regel. Hvordan kan man vente, at de vækker selvstændige følelser, når deres egen adfærd må styres af den forsigtige omtanke, der altid holder øje med forfremmelse?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: So far, however, from thinking of the morals of boys, I have heard several masters of schools argue, that they only undertook to teach Latin and Greek; and that they had fulfilled their duty, by sending some good scholars to college.
danishChanges.after: Langt fra at tænke på drengenes moral har jeg hørt flere skoleledere sige, at de kun påtog sig at undervise i latin og græsk, og at de havde opfyldt deres pligt ved at sende nogle dygtige elever videre til universitetet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A few good scholars, I grant, may have been formed by emulation and discipline; but, to bring forward these clever boys, the health and morals of a number have been sacrificed.
danishChanges.after: Kappestrid og disciplin kan ganske vist have dannet nogle dygtige elever. Men for at fremme disse begavede drenge har man ofret manges sundhed og moral.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The sons of our gentry and wealthy commoners are mostly educated at these seminaries, and will any one pretend to assert, that the majority, making every allowance, come under the description of tolerable scholars?
danishChanges.after: De fleste sønner af landadelen og det velhavende borgerskab opdrages på disse skoler. Vil nogen for alvor hævde, selv med alle forbehold, at flertallet kan kaldes rimeligt lærde?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is not for the benefit of society that a few brilliant men should be brought forward at the expence of the multitude. It is true, that great men seem to start up, as great revolutions occur, at proper intervals, to restore order, and to blow aside the clouds that thicken over the face of truth; but let more reason and virtue prevail in society, and these strong winds would not be necessary. Public education, of every denomination, should be directed to form citizens; but if you wish to make good citizens, you must first exercise the affections of a son and a brother. This is the only way to expand the heart; for public affections, as well as public virtues, must ever grow out of the private character, or they are merely meteors that shoot athwart a dark sky, and disappear as they are gazed at and admired.
danishChanges.after: Det gavner ikke samfundet at frembringe nogle få strålende mænd på de manges bekostning. Store mænd synes ganske vist, ligesom store omvæltninger, at opstå med passende mellemrum for at genoprette orden og blæse de skyer væk, der fortætter sig over sandheden. Men herskede mere fornuft og dyd i samfundet, var sådanne stormvinde ikke nødvendige. Enhver form for fælles uddannelse bør sigte mod at danne borgere. Men vil man skabe gode borgere, må man først øve sønnens og brorens følelser. Det er den eneste vej til at udvide hjertet. Følelser for fællesskabet og offentlige dyder må altid vokse ud af den private karakter. Ellers er de blot meteorer, som farer over en mørk himmel og forsvinder, mens man ser på dem og beundrer dem.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Few, I believe, have had much affection for mankind, who did not first love their parents, their brothers, sisters, and even the domestic brutes, whom they first played with. The exercise of youthful sympathies forms the moral temperature; and it is the recollection of these first affections and pursuits, that gives life to those that are afterwards more under the direction of reason. In youth, the fondest friendships are formed, the genial juices mounting at the same time, kindly mix; or, rather the heart, tempered for the reception of friendship, is accustomed to seek for pleasure in something more noble than the churlish gratification of appetite.
danishChanges.after: Jeg tror, få har næret stor kærlighed til menneskeheden uden først at elske deres forældre, brødre, søstre og selv de husdyr, de først legede med. Ungdommens øvelse i medfølelse former det moralske sindelag. Minderne om de første følelser og interesser giver liv til dem, som senere styres mere af fornuften. De varmeste venskaber dannes i ungdommen, hvor de livgivende safter stiger samtidig og blandes harmonisk. Eller rettere: Hjertet gøres modtageligt for venskab og vænnes til at søge glæde i noget ædlere end driftens selviske tilfredsstillelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In order then to inspire a love of home and domestic pleasures, children ought to be educated at home, for riotous holidays only make them fond of home for their own sakes. Yet, the vacations, which do not foster domestic affections, continually disturb the course of study, and render any plan of improvement abortive which includes temperance; still, were they abolished, children would be entirely separated from their parents, and I question whether they would become better citizens by sacrificing the preparatory affections, by destroying the force of relationships that render the marriage state as necessary as respectable. But, if a private education produce self-importance, or insulates a man in his family, the evil is only shifted, not remedied.
danishChanges.after: Vil man vække kærlighed til hjemmet og dets glæder, bør børn altså opdrages hjemme. Tøjlesløse ferier lærer dem kun at holde af hjemmet for deres egen skyld. Ferierne, som ikke nærer hjemmets hengivenhed, forstyrrer bestandigt studierne og ødelægger enhver udviklingsplan, der omfatter mådehold. Men blev de afskaffet, ville børnene blive helt adskilt fra forældrene. Jeg tvivler på, at de blev bedre borgere ved at ofre de forberedende følelser og ødelægge de bånd, som gør ægteskabet både nødvendigt og respektabelt. Men skaber opdragelse i hjemmet selvvigtighed eller lukker mennesket inde i familien, flyttes ondet blot i stedet for at blive afhjulpet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This train of reasoning brings me back to a subject, on which I mean to dwell, the necessity of establishing proper day-schools.
danishChanges.after: Denne tankegang fører mig tilbage til det emne, jeg vil dvæle ved: nødvendigheden af at oprette ordentlige dagskoler.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But these should be national establishments, for whilst school-masters are dependent on the caprice of parents, little exertion can be expected from them, more than is necessary to please ignorant people. Indeed, the necessity of a master's giving the parents some sample of the boy's abilities, which during the vacation, is shown to every visiter, is productive of more mischief than would at first be supposed. For they are seldom done entirely, to speak with moderation, by the child itself; thus the master countenances falsehoods, or winds the poor machine up to some extraordinary exertion, that injures the wheels, and stops the progress of gradual improvement. The memory is loaded with unintelligible words, to make a show of, without the understanding's acquiring any distinct ideas: but only that education deserves emphatically to be termed cultivation of mind, which teaches young people how to begin to think. The imagination should not be allowed to debauch the understanding before it gained strength, or vanity will become the forerunner of vice: for every way of exhibiting the acquirements of a child is injurious to its moral character.
danishChanges.after: De bør være offentlige institutioner. Så længe lærerne afhænger af forældrenes luner, kan man kun vente den indsats, der er nødvendig for at tilfredsstille uvidende mennesker. Kravet om, at læreren skal give forældrene en prøve på drengens evner, som i ferien vises til enhver gæst, gør faktisk mere skade, end man først skulle tro. Sådanne arbejder er sjældent, mildt sagt, helt barnets egne. Læreren støtter dermed løgn eller spænder den stakkels maskine op til en usædvanlig anstrengelse, der skader hjulene og standser den gradvise fremgang. Hukommelsen fyldes med uforståelige ord til fremvisning, uden at forstanden får klare forestillinger. Men kun den undervisning, der lærer unge at begynde at tænke, fortjener virkelig navnet åndsdannelse. Fantasien må ikke fordærve forstanden, før den har fået styrke, ellers bliver forfængeligheden lastens forløber. Enhver fremvisning af et barns færdigheder skader nemlig dets moralske karakter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: How much time is lost in teaching them to recite what they do not understand! whilst, seated on benches, all in their best array, the mammas listen with astonishment to the parrot-like prattle, uttered in solemn cadences, with all the pomp of ignorance and folly. Such exhibitions only serve to strike the spreading fibres of vanity through the whole mind; for they neither teach children to speak fluently, nor behave gracefully. So far from it, that these frivolous pursuits might comprehensively be termed the study of affectation: for we now rarely see a simple, bashful boy, though few people of taste were ever disgusted by that awkward sheepishness so natural to the age, which schools and an early introduction into society, have changed into impudence and apish grimace.
danishChanges.after: Hvor megen tid går ikke tabt med at lære børn at fremsige noget, de ikke forstår! Imens sidder mødrene på bænke i deres fineste tøj og lytter forbløffede til den papegøjeagtige plapren, fremført i højtidelige rytmer med al uvidenhedens og dårskabens pomp. Sådanne opvisninger lader kun forfængelighedens rødder brede sig gennem hele sindet. De lærer hverken børn at tale flydende eller at optræde yndefuldt. Tværtimod kunne man samlet kalde disse overfladiske øvelser et studium i påtagethed. Nu ser vi sjældent en ligefrem, genert dreng, selv om få mennesker med smag nogensinde har været frastødt af den kejtede forlegenhed, der er så naturlig for alderen. Skolerne og den tidlige indførelse i selskabslivet har forvandlet den til frækhed og abelignende grimasser.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Yet, how can these things be remedied whilst schoolmasters depend entirely on parents for a subsistence; and when so many rival schools hang out their lures to catch the attention of vain fathers and mothers, whose parental affection only leads them to wish, that their children should outshine those of their neighbours?
danishChanges.after: Men hvordan skal det ændres, når lærernes levebrød helt afhænger af forældrene, og så mange konkurrerende skoler lægger lokkemad ud efter forfængelige fædre og mødre, hvis kærlighed blot får dem til at ønske, at deres børn overstråler naboens?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Without great good luck, a sensible, conscientious man, would starve before he could raise a school, if he disdained to bubble weak parents, by practising the secret tricks of the craft.
danishChanges.after: Uden stort held ville en fornuftig og samvittighedsfuld mand sulte, før han kunne få en skole på benene, hvis han nægtede at narre svage forældre med fagets hemmelige kneb.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In the best regulated schools, however, where swarms are not crammed together many bad habits must be acquired; but, at common schools, the body, heart, and understanding, are equally stunted, for parents are often only in quest of the cheapest school, and the master could not live, if he did not take a much greater number than he could manage himself; nor will the scanty pittance, allowed for each child, permit him to hire ushers sufficient to assist in the discharge of the mechanical part of the business. Besides, whatever appearance the house and garden may make, the children do not enjoy the comforts of either, for they are continually reminded, by irksome restrictions, that they are not at home, and the state-rooms, garden, etc. must be kept in order for the recreation of the parents; who, of a Sunday, visit the school, and are impressed by the very parade that renders the situation of their children uncomfortable.
danishChanges.after: Selv på de bedst ordnede skoler, hvor børnene ikke stuves sammen i sværme, må de få mange dårlige vaner. På almindelige skoler hæmmes krop, hjerte og forstand lige meget. Forældrene søger ofte blot den billigste skole, og læreren kunne ikke leve, hvis han ikke tog langt flere børn ind, end han selv kan klare. Den sparsomme betaling for hvert barn giver ham heller ikke råd til nok hjælpelærere til den rutinemæssige del af arbejdet. Desuden får børnene ikke glæde af huset eller haven, hvor godt de end tager sig ud. Generende begrænsninger minder dem hele tiden om, at de ikke er hjemme. De fine værelser og haven skal holdes i orden for forældrenes fornøjelse, når de besøger skolen om søndagen og imponeres af netop den opvisning, der gør børnenes ophold ubehageligt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: With what disgust have I heard sensible women, for girls are more restrained and cowed than boys, speak of the wearisome confinement which they endured at school. Not allowed, perhaps, to step out of one broad walk in a superb garden, and obliged to pace with steady deportment stupidly backwards and forwards, holding up their heads, and turning out their toes, with shoulders braced back, instead of bounding, as nature directs to complete her own design, in the various attitudes so conducive to health. The pure animal spirits, which make both mind and body shoot out, and unfold the tender blossoms of hope are turned sour, and vented in vain wishes, or pert repinings, that contract the faculties and spoil the temper; else they mount to the brain and sharpening the understanding before it gains proportionable strength, produce that pitiful cunning which disgracefully characterizes the female mind--and I fear will ever characterize it whilst women remain the slaves of power!
danishChanges.after: Hvor har det frastødt mig at høre fornuftige kvinder fortælle om den trættende indespærring, de udholdt i skolen! Piger begrænses og kujoneres jo mere end drenge. Måske måtte de ikke forlade én bred gang i en prægtig have, men skulle tåbeligt gå frem og tilbage med rolig holdning, hovedet løftet, tæerne udad og skuldrene tilbage. De måtte ikke springe omkring i de mange bevægelser, naturen kræver for at fuldende sit værk og styrke sundheden. Den rene livskraft, som får krop og sind til at vokse og åbner håbets spæde blomster, bliver sur og får afløb i tomme ønsker eller næsvis beklagelse. Det indsnævrer evnerne og ødelægger humøret. Eller kraften stiger til hjernen og skærper forstanden, før den har fået tilsvarende styrke, så den frembringer den ynkelige snuhed, der skæmmer kvinders sind. Jeg frygter, at den altid vil præge det, så længe kvinder er magtens slaver!
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The little respect which the male world pay to chastity is, I am persuaded, the grand source of many of the physical and moral evils that torment mankind, as well as of the vices and follies that degrade and destroy women; yet at school, boys infallibly lose that decent bashfulness, which might have ripened into modesty at home.
danishChanges.after: Jeg er overbevist om, at mændenes ringe respekt for kyskhed er hovedkilden til mange af de fysiske og moralske onder, som plager menneskeheden, og til de laster og tåbeligheder, der nedværdiger og ødelægger kvinder. Men i skolen mister drenge uundgåeligt den anstændige generthed, som hjemme kunne være modnet til blufærdighed.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I have already animadverted on the bad habits which females acquire when they are shut up together; and I think that the observation may fairly be extended to the other sex, till the natural inference is drawn which I have had in view throughout--that to improve both sexes they ought, not only in private families, but in public schools, to be educated together. If marriage be the cement of society, mankind should all be educated after the same model, or the intercourse of the sexes will never deserve the name of fellowship, nor will women ever fulfil the peculiar duties of their sex, till they become enlightened citizens, till they become free, by being enabled to earn their own subsistence, independent of men; in the same manner, I mean, to prevent misconstruction, as one man is independent of another. Nay, marriage will never be held sacred till women by being brought up with men, are prepared to be their companions, rather than their mistresses; for the mean doublings of cunning will ever render them contemptible, whilst oppression renders them timid. So convinced am I of this truth, that I will venture to predict, that virtue will never prevail in society till the virtues of both sexes are founded on reason; and, till the affection common to both are allowed to gain their due strength by the discharge of mutual duties.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har allerede kritiseret de dårlige vaner, piger og kvinder får, når de lukkes sammen. Bemærkningen kan med rette udvides til det andet køn, indtil vi når den naturlige slutning, jeg hele tiden har haft for øje: Skal begge køn forbedres, må de opdrages sammen, både i familierne og i de fælles skoler. Er ægteskabet samfundets bindemiddel, bør alle opdrages efter samme mønster. Ellers vil kønnenes samvær aldrig fortjene navnet fællesskab. Kvinder vil heller aldrig opfylde deres særlige pligter, før de bliver oplyste borgere og frie ved at kunne tjene deres eget underhold uafhængigt af mænd — i samme forstand, for at undgå misforståelser, som én mand er uafhængig af en anden. Ægteskabet bliver aldrig regnet for helligt, før kvinder opdrages sammen med mænd og forberedes på at være deres ledsagere frem for elskerinder. Snuhedens smålige omveje vil altid gøre dem foragtelige, mens undertrykkelsen gør dem frygtsomme. Jeg er så overbevist om dette, at jeg vover at forudsige, at dyden aldrig vil herske i samfundet, før begge køns dyder bygger på fornuft, og deres fælles følelser får den rette styrke gennem opfyldelsen af gensidige pligter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Were boys and girls permitted to pursue the same studies together, those graceful decencies might early be inculcated which produce modesty, without those sexual distinctions that taint the mind. Lessons of politeness, and that formulary of decorum, which treads on the heels of falsehood, would be rendered useless by habitual propriety of behaviour. Not, indeed put on for visiters like the courtly robe of politeness, but the sober effect of cleanliness of mind. Would not this simple elegance of sincerity be a chaste homage paid to domestic affections, far surpassing the meretricious compliments that shine with false lustre in the heartless intercourse of fashionable life? But, till more understanding preponderate in society, there will ever be a want of heart and taste, and the harlot's rouge will supply the place of that celestial suffusion which only virtuous affections can give to the face. Gallantry, and what is called love, may subsist without simplicity of character; but the main pillars of friendship, are respect and confidence--esteem is never founded on it cannot tell what.
danishChanges.after: Fik drenge og piger lov at studere sammen, kunne de tidligt lære den yndefulde hensynsfuldhed, der skaber blufærdighed uden de kønsskel, som besmitter sindet. Lektioner i høflighed og det regelsæt for passende opførsel, der følger lige efter løgnen, ville blive overflødige gennem vanemæssig anstændighed. Den skulle ikke tages på til gæster som høflighedens hofdragt, men være den rolige virkning af et rent sind. Ville oprigtighedens enkle elegance ikke være en kysk hyldest til hjemmets følelser, langt bedre end de falsk strålende komplimenter i det mondæne livs hjerteløse omgang? Men før forstanden får større vægt i samfundet, vil der altid mangle hjerte og smag. Skøgens rouge vil erstatte den himmelske glød, som kun dydige følelser kan give ansigtet. Galanteri og såkaldt kærlighed kan findes uden en ligefrem karakter, men venskabets vigtigste søjler er respekt og tillid. Respekt bygger aldrig på noget, den ikke selv kan sætte ord på.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: A taste for the fine arts requires great cultivation; but not more than a taste for the virtuous affections: and both suppose that enlargement of mind which opens so many sources of mental pleasure. Why do people hurry to noisy scenes and crowded circles? I should answer, because they want activity of mind, because they have not cherished the virtues of the heart. They only, therefore, see and feel in the gross, and continually pine after variety, finding every thing that is simple, insipid.
danishChanges.after: Smag for de skønne kunster kræver stor dannelse, men ikke mere end smag for dydige følelser. Begge forudsætter den udvidelse af sindet, der åbner så mange kilder til åndelig glæde. Hvorfor skynder folk sig til larmende steder og tætte selskaber? Jeg ville svare: Fordi de mangler åndelig aktivitet og ikke har dyrket hjertets dyder. Derfor ser og føler de kun groft, længes uophørligt efter forandring og finder alt enkelt kedeligt.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: This argument may be carried further than philosophers are aware of, for if nature destined woman, in particular, for the discharge of domestic duties, she made her susceptible of the attached affections in a great degree. Now women are notoriously fond of pleasure; and naturally must be so, according to my definition, because they cannot enter into the minutiae of domestic taste; lacking judgment the foundation of all taste. For the understanding, in spite of sensual cavillers, reserves to itself the privilege of conveying pure joy to the heart.
danishChanges.after: Dette argument kan føres længere, end filosofferne aner. Har naturen især bestemt kvinden til hjemmets pligter, har den også gjort hende særlig modtagelig for de følelser, der hører til. Kvinder er notorisk glade for fornøjelser og må ifølge min forklaring naturligt være det, fordi de ikke kan værdsætte hjemmelivets finere glæder. De mangler dømmekraft, grundlaget for al smag. Trods sanselighedens kværulanter forbeholder forstanden sig nemlig retten til at formidle ren glæde til hjertet.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: With what a languid yawn have I seen an admirable poem thrown down, that a man of true taste returns to, again and again with rapture; and, whilst melody has almost suspended respiration, a lady has asked me where I bought my gown. I have seen also an eye glanced coldly over a most exquisite picture, rest, sparkling with pleasure, on a caricature rudely sketched; and whilst some terrific feature in nature has spread a sublime stillness through my soul, I have been desired to observe the pretty tricks of a lap-dog, that my perverse fate forced me to travel with. Is it surprising, that such a tasteless being should rather caress this dog than her children? Or, that she should prefer the rant of flattery to the simple accents of sincerity?
danishChanges.after: Jeg har set et vidunderligt digt blive smidt til side med et sløvt gab, skønt et menneske med ægte smag vender tilbage til det igen og igen med henrykkelse. Mens musik næsten fik åndedrættet til at standse, har en dame spurgt mig, hvor jeg købte min kjole. Jeg har også set et blik glide koldt hen over et udsøgt maleri og derefter hvile funklende af glæde på en groft tegnet karikatur. Og mens et ærefrygtindgydende naturtræk fyldte min sjæl med ophøjet stilhed, er jeg blevet bedt om at se på de søde kunster hos en skødehund, min vrangvillige skæbne tvang mig til at rejse med. Er det underligt, at et så smagløst væsen hellere kæler for hunden end for sine børn eller foretrækker smigerens svulstige tale frem for oprigtighedens enkle ord?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To illustrate this remark I must be allowed to observe, that men of the first genius, and most cultivated minds, have appeared to have the highest relish for the simple beauties of nature; and they must have forcibly felt, what they have so well described, the charm, which natural affections, and unsophisticated feelings spread round the human character. It is this power of looking into the heart, and responsively vibrating with each emotion, that enables the poet to personify each passion, and the painter to sketch with a pencil of fire.
danishChanges.after: For at belyse dette vil jeg bemærke, at de største genier og mest dannede sind synes at have haft størst glæde ved naturens enkle skønhed. De må stærkt have følt det, de beskriver så godt: den ynde, som naturlig hengivenhed og ligefremme følelser giver menneskets karakter. Netop evnen til at se ind i hjertet og klinge med på hver følelse lader digteren give enhver lidenskab skikkelse og maleren tegne med en glødende pensel.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Ægte smag er altid forstandens værk, anvendt på iagttagelsen af naturlige virkninger; og før kvinder får mere forstand, er det forgæves at vente, at de skal besidde huslig smag. Deres livlige sanser vil altid arbejde på at forhærde deres hjerter, og de følelser, der slås ud af dem, vil vedblive at være levende og flygtige, medmindre en passende uddannelse fylder deres sind med kundskab.
danishChanges.after: Ægte smag skabes altid af forstanden, når den iagttager naturens virkninger. Før kvinder får mere forstand, er det forgæves at vente smag for hjemmelivet hos dem. Deres livlige sanser vil bestandigt arbejde på at hærde hjertet, og de følelser, de vækker, vil fortsat være stærke og flygtige, medmindre en ordentlig uddannelse fylder sindet med kundskab.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: It is the want of domestic taste, and not the acquirement of knowledge, that takes women out of their families, and tears the smiling babe from the breast that ought to afford it nourishment. Women have been allowed to remain in ignorance, and slavish dependence, many, very many years, and still we hear of nothing but their fondness of pleasure and sway, their preference of rakes and soldiers, their childish attachment to toys, and the vanity that makes them value accomplishments more than virtues.
danishChanges.after: Det er manglen på smag for hjemmet, ikke tilegnelsen af kundskab, der fører kvinder bort fra familien og river det smilende spædbarn fra det bryst, der burde nære det. Kvinder har fået lov at blive i uvidenhed og slavisk afhængighed i mange, mange år. Alligevel hører vi kun om deres trang til fornøjelse og magt, deres forkærlighed for libertinere og soldater, deres barnlige optagethed af legetøj og den forfængelighed, der får dem til at sætte selskabelige færdigheder højere end dyder.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: History brings forward a fearful catalogue of the crimes which their cunning has produced, when the weak slaves have had sufficient address to over-reach their masters. In France, and in how many other countries have men been the luxurious despots, and women the crafty ministers? Does this prove that ignorance and dependence domesticate them? Is not their folly the by-word of the libertines, who relax in their society; and do not men of sense continually lament, that an immoderate fondness for dress and dissipation carries the mother of a family for ever from home? Their hearts have not been debauched by knowledge, nor their minds led astray by scientific pursuits; yet, they do not fulfil the peculiar duties, which as women they are called upon by nature to fulfil. On the contrary, the state of warfare which subsists between the sexes, makes them employ those wiles, that frustrate the more open designs of force.
danishChanges.after: Historien fremlægger en frygtelig liste over de forbrydelser, kvinders snuhed har frembragt, når de svage slaver har været dygtige nok til at overliste deres herrer. I Frankrig, og i hvor mange andre lande, har mændene ikke været de luksuselskende despoter og kvinderne de snedige ministre? Viser det, at uvidenhed og afhængighed gør dem hjemlige? Gør libertinerne, der slapper af i deres selskab, ikke konstant nar af deres tåbelighed? Og beklager fornuftige mænd sig ikke bestandigt over, at overdreven optagethed af tøj og fornøjelser holder familiens mor væk fra hjemmet? Deres hjerter er ikke blevet fordærvet af kundskab, og videnskabelige interesser har ikke ført deres sind på afveje. Alligevel opfylder de ikke de særlige pligter, naturen pålægger dem som kvinder. Tværtimod får krigstilstanden mellem kønnene dem til at bruge kneb, som forpurrer magtens mere åbne planer.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: When, therefore, I call women slaves, I mean in a political and civil sense; for, indirectly they obtain too much power, and are debased by their exertions to obtain illicit sway.
danishChanges.after: Når jeg kalder kvinder slaver, mener jeg det derfor politisk og borgerligt. Indirekte får de for megen magt og nedværdiges af forsøget på at opnå en uretmæssig indflydelse.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Let an enlightened nation then try what effect reason would have to bring them back to nature, and their duty; and allowing them to share the advantages of education and government with man, see whether they will become better, as they grow wiser and become free. They cannot be injured by the experiment; for it is not in the power of man to render them more insignificant than they are at present.
danishChanges.after: Lad da en oplyst nation prøve, hvad fornuften kan gøre for at føre dem tilbage til naturen og pligten. Lad dem dele uddannelsens og styrets fordele med mænd, og se, om de bliver bedre, når de bliver klogere og frie. Forsøget kan ikke skade dem. Mænd kan nemlig ikke gøre dem mere ubetydelige, end de allerede er.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: To render this practicable, day schools for particular ages should be established by government, in which boys and girls might be educated together. The school for the younger children, from five to nine years of age, ought to be absolutely free and open to all classes.* A sufficient number of masters should also be chosen by a select committee, in each parish, to whom any complaint of negligence, etc. might be made, if signed by six of the children's parents.
danishChanges.after: For at gøre det muligt bør staten oprette dagskoler for bestemte alderstrin, hvor drenge og piger undervises sammen. Skolen for de yngste, fra fem til ni år, bør være helt gratis og åben for alle klasser.* Et særligt udvalg i hvert sogn bør vælge et tilstrækkeligt antal lærere. Klager over forsømmelse og lignende kan indgives til udvalget, hvis seks af børnenes forældre har skrevet under.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: (*Fodnote. I behandlingen af denne del af emnet har jeg lånt nogle vink fra et meget fornuftigt skrift, forfattet af den afdøde biskop af Autun om offentlig opdragelse.)
danishChanges.after: (*Fodnote. I denne del af emnet har jeg lånt nogle ideer fra et meget fornuftigt skrift om offentlig uddannelse af den tidligere biskop af Autun.)
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Ushers would then be unnecessary; for, I believe, experience will ever prove, that this kind of subordinate authority is particularly injurious to the morals of youth. What, indeed, can tend to deprave the character more than outward submission and inward contempt? Yet, how can boys be expected to treat an usher with respect when the master seems to consider him in the light of a servant, and almost to countenance the ridicule which becomes the chief amusement of the boys during the play hours?
danishChanges.after: Hjælpelærere ville da være overflødige. Jeg tror, erfaringen altid vil vise, at denne underordnede myndighed er særlig skadelig for unges moral. Hvad kan fordærve karakteren mere end ydre underkastelse og indre foragt? Men hvordan kan man vente, at drenge respekterer en hjælpelærer, når skolelederen synes at betragte ham som en tjener og næsten opmuntrer den latterliggørelse, der bliver drengenes vigtigste fornøjelse i frikvartererne?
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: But nothing of this kind could occur in an elementary day-school, where boys and girls, the rich and poor, should meet together. And to prevent any of the distinctions of vanity, they should be dressed alike, and all obliged to submit to the same discipline, or leave the school. The school-room ought to be surrounded by a large piece of ground, in which the children might be usefully exercised, for at this age they should not be confined to any sedentary employment for more than an hour at a time. But these relaxations might all be rendered a part of elementary education, for many things improve and amuse the senses, when introduced as a kind of show, to the principles of which dryly laid down, children would turn a deaf ear. For instance, botany, mechanics, and astronomy. Reading, writing, arithmetic, natural history, and some simple experiments in natural philosophy, might fill up the day; but these pursuits should never encroach on gymnastic plays in the open air. The elements of religion, history, the history of man, and politics, might also be taught by conversations, in the socratic form.
danishChanges.after: Intet af den slags kunne ske i en grundlæggende dagskole, hvor drenge og piger, rige og fattige, mødtes. For at undgå forfængelighedens skel skulle alle være klædt ens og følge samme regler eller forlade skolen. Omkring skolebygningen burde der være et stort areal, hvor børnene kunne bevæge sig på nyttige måder. I den alder bør de ikke sidde stille med nogen opgave mere end en time ad gangen. Men alle disse pauser kunne indgå i grundundervisningen. Mange ting udvikler og underholder sanserne, når de vises frem, selv om børn ville vende det døve øre til deres tørt fremlagte principper: for eksempel botanik, mekanik og astronomi. Læsning, skrivning, regning, naturhistorie og enkle fysiske forsøg kunne fylde dagen, men måtte aldrig fortrænge bevægelseslege i det fri. Grundtræk af religion, historie, menneskets historie og politik kunne også undervises gennem sokratiske samtaler.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: After the age of nine, girls and boys, intended for domestic employments, or mechanical trades, ought to be removed to other schools, and receive instruction, in some measure appropriated to the destination of each individual, the two sexes being still together in the morning; but in the afternoon, the girls should attend a school, where plain work, mantua-making, millinery, etc. would be their employment.
danishChanges.after: Efter niårsalderen burde piger og drenge, som var bestemt til husligt arbejde eller håndværk, flyttes til andre skoler med undervisning, der i nogen grad passede til den enkeltes fremtid. Kønnene skulle stadig være sammen om formiddagen. Om eftermiddagen skulle pigerne gå på en skole, hvor de beskæftigede sig med almindelig syning, kjolesyning, hattefremstilling og lignende.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: The young people of superior abilities, or fortune, might now be taught, in another school, the dead and living languages, the elements of science, and continue the study of history and politics, on a more extensive scale, which would not exclude polite literature. Girls and boys still together? I hear some readers ask: yes. And I should not fear any other consequence, than that some early attachment might take place; which, whilst it had the best effect on the moral character of the young people, might not perfectly agree with the views of the parents, for it will be a long time, I fear, before the world is so enlightened, that parents, only anxious to render their children virtuous, will let them choose companions for life themselves.
danishChanges.after: De unge med større evner eller formue kunne nu på en anden skole lære døde og levende sprog, videnskabernes grundtræk og fortsætte historie og politik i større omfang, uden at skønlitteraturen blev udeladt. Stadig piger og drenge sammen? hører jeg nogle læsere spørge. Ja. Jeg ville ikke frygte andre følger end nogle tidlige forelskelser. De kunne have den bedste virkning på de unges moralske karakter, selv om de måske ikke helt passede til forældrenes planer. Jeg frygter, at der går lang tid, før verden er så oplyst, at forældre kun ønsker at gøre børnene dydige og lader dem selv vælge livsledsager.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Besides, this would be a sure way to promote early marriages, and from early marriages the most salutary physical and moral effects naturally flow. What a different character does a married citizen assume from the selfish coxcomb, who lives but for himself, and who is often afraid to marry lest he should not be able to live in a certain style. Great emergencies excepted, which would rarely occur in a society of which equality was the basis, a man could only be prepared to discharge the duties of public life, by the habitual practice of those inferior ones which form the man.
danishChanges.after: Desuden ville det sikkert fremme tidlige ægteskaber, som naturligt har de gavnligste fysiske og moralske virkninger. Hvor anderledes er ikke den gifte borger end den egoistiske laps, der kun lever for sig selv og ofte er bange for at gifte sig, fordi han måske ikke kan bevare en bestemt levestil! Bortset fra store nødsituationer, som sjældent ville opstå i et samfund bygget på lighed, kan en mand kun forberedes på det offentlige livs pligter ved vanemæssigt at øve de mindre pligter, der former mennesket.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: In this plan of education, the constitution of boys would not be ruined by the early debaucheries, which now make men so selfish, nor girls rendered weak and vain, by indolence and frivolous pursuits. But, I presuppose, that such a degree of equality should be established between the sexes as would shut out gallantry and coquetry, yet allow friendship and love to temper the heart for the discharge of higher duties.
danishChanges.after: Med denne uddannelsesplan ville drengenes kroppe ikke blive ødelagt af de tidlige udskejelser, som nu gør mænd så egoistiske. Pigerne ville heller ikke blive svage og forfængelige af lediggang og overfladiske interesser. Men jeg forudsætter en lighed mellem kønnene, der udelukker galanteri og koketteri, samtidig med at venskab og kærlighed får lov at forberede hjertet på højere pligter.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: These would be schools of morality--and the happiness of man, allowed to flow from the pure springs of duty and affection, what advances might not the human mind make? Society can only be happy and free in proportion as it is virtuous; but the present distinctions, established in society, corrode all private, and blast all public virtue.
danishChanges.after: Det ville være moralens skoler. Hvilke fremskridt kunne menneskesindet ikke gøre, hvis lykken fik lov at strømme fra pligtens og hengivenhedens rene kilder? Samfundet kan kun være lykkeligt og frit i det omfang, det er dydigt. Men de nuværende samfundsskel udhuler al privat dyd og svider al offentlig dyd bort.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: I have already inveighed against the custom of confining girls to their needle, and shutting them out from all political and civil employments; for by thus narrowing their minds they are rendered unfit to fulfil the peculiar duties which nature has assigned them.
danishChanges.after: Jeg har allerede angrebet skikken med at binde piger til nålen og udelukke dem fra alt politisk og borgerligt arbejde. Ved sådan at indsnævre deres sind gør man dem nemlig uegnede til at opfylde de særlige pligter, naturen har givet dem.
danishChanges.reason: Original-led full modern Danish translation and fidelity review; retain original argument, notes and quotations.

danishChanges.before: Only employed about the little incidents of the day, they necessarily grow up cunning. My very soul has often sickened at observing the sly tricks practised by women to gain some foolish thing on which their silly hearts were set.
